action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

read_montage.summary: Read montage: sections, slot tracks and notifies. Each notify and notify state carries objectPath (the placed instance) and properties (its editable reflected properties as export text), so an existing one can be edited in place with editor(set_property, objectPath, propertyName, value). notifyStates lists the windowed notifies the way add_notify_state reports them.

read_sequence.summary: Read anim sequence: length, rate scale, frames, root motion, curves and notifies. Each notify carries triggerTime and duration in seconds, trackIndex and trackName, and for a notify state its notifyStateClass and endTime. Resolves the same path forms asset(read) does. Batch: pass assetPaths (up to 1000) or directory (with recursive? and nameFilter?, a case-insensitive substring or * ? wildcard on the asset name) instead of assetPath to get one row per sequence in 'sequences', paged (default 50, max 200). A sequence that fails to load is its own row with success false and error; the call still succeeds and reports failedCount. Also reports interpolation (linear|step), retargetSource (the skeleton's named retarget pose, empty for none) and retargetSourceAsset (the mesh whose pose the clip's bone lengths are retargeted from, empty for none). fields selects the columns (assetPath is always kept); batch rows default to name, sequenceLength, rateScale, numberOfFrames, samplingFrameRate, rootMotionEnabled, notifyCount.

add_blend_sample.summary: Append a sample to a BlendSpace (#248).

set_blend_sample.summary: Move an existing BlendSpace sample, swap its animation (#272), or set its per-sample rateScale (#1663). Runs ResampleData and PostEditChange, so the grid is rebuilt; read_blendspace reports each sample's rateScale.

list.summary: List anim assets (AnimSequence, AnimMontage, AnimBlueprint, BlendSpace). directory scopes the read to one folder and is now honoured; it was advertised and ignored, so a scoped call used to get the whole project back.

author_montages_batch.summary: Batch-author montages in one call: idempotent create, slot name, blend/rate/length properties, sections and notifies, then save. Every item reports success plus the failing stage (validate|create|slot|properties|sections|notifies|save) and error, so one bad item does not hide the rest. Newly created montages come back as a delete_asset_batch rollback. Each montage still holds the single segment create_montage builds.

populate_blendspace.summary: One-call axis params + samples authoring for BlendSpace 1D/2D. Axis params come from axis (with axisIndex), the per-axis blendspaceAxes list, or the flat create_blendspace keys (#459).

add_notify.summary: Add notify. For PlayMontageNotify the notifyName is also written onto the spawned notify object so OnPlayMontageNotifyBegin broadcasts it (not 'None'), and montage branching-point markers refresh (#528/#880). On a montage the PlayMontageNotify classes are added as BRANCHING POINT notifies, which is the only tick type UAnimNotify_PlayMontageNotify::BranchingPointNotify runs at, so OnPlayMontageNotifyBegin broadcasts without a montage reload; pass branchingPoint to force it either way, and read branchingPointMarkerCount in the response to see what the montage cached. notifyProperties writes EditAnywhere fields onto the spawned notify object and therefore requires a notifyClass that resolves.

remove_notify.summary: Remove notify(s) by name and/or class (#471). Pass at least one of notifyName/notifyClass; both filters AND. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true if no match.

get_skeleton_info.summary: Read a skeleton from a SkeletalMesh or the Skeleton asset itself: bones (name, index, parentIndex), virtualBones (name, sourceBone, targetBone) and slotGroups (name, slots).

list_skeletal_meshes.summary: List skeletal meshes. directory scopes the read to one folder and is now honoured; it was advertised and ignored, so a scoped call used to get the whole project back.

get_physics_asset_constraints.summary: Read every constraint template of a PhysicsAsset: constraintName, bone1 (child) and bone2 (parent); linear x/y/z motion and limit; swing1/swing2/twist motion (Free|Limited|Locked) with limit degrees; per-limit soft flag, stiffness and damping; whether the linear and angular drives are enabled; parentDominates and disableCollision; and frame1/frame2, the constraint frame's position and rotation in each body's space. get_physics_asset lists only body bone names and asset(read_properties) shows ConstraintSetup as opaque object paths, so diagnosing a contorted ragdoll used to need Python. Pass the PhysicsAsset path, or the SkeletalMesh it is assigned to. boneName keeps the constraints touching one bone; limit caps the rows and total still counts every match. Also reports bodyCount, constraintCount and the preview skeletal mesh path.

set_physics_asset_constraint_limits.summary: Write the angular limits of a PhysicsAsset's constraint templates: swing1/swing2/twist motion (Free|Limited|Locked), limit degrees (0 to 180), and whether the cone and twist limits are soft or hard. Shared values go to constraintNames, or every constraint when it is omitted; constraints[] carries per-joint values and is applied after them. A degree value is written only where that axis is Limited, so locked and free axes keep theirs and are listed in skippedLimits. Each template's serialized profile is updated, so the edit survives a save. Unknown names are refused before anything changes. Pass the PhysicsAsset or the SkeletalMesh it is assigned to. Saves by default (save=false to skip) and returns a rollback that restores every touched constraint.

set_physics_asset_body_material.summary: Set the simple-collision PhysicalMaterial of a PhysicsAsset's bodies. physicalMaterialPath goes to boneNames, or every body when it is omitted; bodies[] carries per-bone materials and is applied after it. An empty path clears the override. Unknown bones and a path that is not a PhysicalMaterial are refused before anything changes. Pass the PhysicsAsset or the SkeletalMesh it is assigned to. Saves by default (save=false to skip) and returns a rollback that restores each body's previous material.

bake_keyframes_batch.summary: Bake per-bone keyframe arrays for many bones into an AnimSequence in one call. Auto-creates each bone track first (set_bone_keyframes silently leaves a T-pose if the track is missing), wraps the batch in one transaction, and raises if any bone fails instead of reporting hollow success (#540).

reverse_sequence.summary: Create a time-reversed copy of an AnimSequence, or reverse it in place with inPlace=true. Bone tracks are rewritten through the animation data controller, float and transform curves are mirrored with their tangents, notifies move to length - time (a notify state to length - time - duration) and sync markers mirror the same way. A blendspace sample with RateScale -1 is not a substitute: it freezes under the non-legacy sample length calculation. cycleOffsetFrames or cycleOffsetSeconds (rounded to whole frames) then rotates the reversed loop so it starts that far in; the last key is rewritten to repeat the new first key. The destination is destinationPath, or name (default <Source>_Reversed) in packagePath (default the source's folder). onConflict=skip (default) returns an existing destination untouched, error refuses; it never overwrites. Returns path, numFrames, numKeys, frameRate, the applied cycle offset, reversed counts {boneTracks, floatCurves, transformCurves, notifies, notifyStates, syncMarkers}, and a delete_asset rollback, or for inPlace a reverse_sequence replay that restores it (#1162).

get_bone_transforms.summary: Read reference pose transforms for one, many, or ALL bones. Omit boneNames to return every bone with index/parentIndex/location/rotation/scale; rotation is a quaternion {x,y,z,w}. With boneNames, returns only the named bones (#245). space=component composes the parent chain. A SkeletalMesh path reads the mesh's own bind pose, a Skeleton path the Skeleton's; poseSource and poseSourcePath say which was read (#1451).

inspect_anim_nodes.summary: Deep-dump the FAnimNode_* struct of anim graph nodes (PoseDriver PoseTargets/PoseAsset/RBF params/source bones, etc.) that read_anim_graph omits because it skips the 'Node' property (#657).

compare_curves_to_morph_targets.summary: Compare an AnimSequence/PoseAsset's curve names against a SkeletalMesh's morph target names. Returns curves[], morphTargets[], matched[], curvesWithoutMorph[], morphsWithoutCurve[] - verify authored curves drive morphs without Python (#656).

set_montage_sequence.summary: Replace the animation sequence in a montage slot. With segmentIndex, replaces only that one segment; without it, replaces every segment in the slot (#626).

add_state.summary: Add state to a state machine.

add_transition.summary: Add directed transition between states. blendDuration and blendLogic are applied to the new transition as set_transition_blend applies them, and the result echoes the effective blendDuration and blendLogic. An existing transition is returned unchanged, with a warning when the requested blend differs.

set_transition_condition.summary: Set a transition's 'can enter transition' condition from a bool variable, keyed by transition (not graph name - every rule graph is named 'Transition' so blueprint graph tools can only reach the first). Wires VariableGet(bool) -> bCanEnterTransition, replacing any prior condition. Identify the transition by transitionGuid (from add_transition/read_state_machine) OR fromState+toState (#707).

set_state_machine_entry.summary: Point the state machine's ENTRY node at a state, which is the only thing that gives a machine an initial state. create_state_machine and add_state never wired it, so a machine authored through the bridge compiled with no entry and produced the reference pose at runtime. There is no property behind this: it is the pin link from UAnimationStateMachineGraph::EntryNode to the state's input pin. An omitted or empty stateName clears the link instead, so set and clear are one pair. Reports previousEntryState, and unchanged=true on a replay.

remove_state.summary: Remove a state from a state machine, together with every transition that touched it and the graphs they own - a transition whose endpoint is gone fails the blueprint compile. Returns removedTransitions so they can be replayed, and warns when the removed state was the entry state. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the state is not there.

remove_transition.summary: Remove a transition and its rule graph. Address it by transitionGuid (from add_transition or read_state_machine) or by fromState plus toState, which can match several and removes all of them. A rule graph SHARED with another transition is left in place and counted in sharedRuleGraphsKept. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when nothing matched.

remove_state_machine.summary: Remove a state machine node and everything inside it: its states, its transitions, each of their bound graphs, and the machine's own graph. Leaving a bound graph behind after its node is gone is what makes the next compile assert, so the teardown is explicit rather than left to the node. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the machine is not there.

read_anim_graph.summary: Read AnimBP AnimGraph nodes with properties & pins.

remove_curve.summary: Remove a float curve from an AnimSequence through the animation data controller, so the model, the compressed data and the editor stay in step. Reports removedKeyCount, which is what the rollback cannot restore: add_curve puts back an empty curve of the same name and the keys have to be replayed with set_anim_curve_keys. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when there is no such curve, and the miss lists the curves that do exist.

set_anim_curve_keys.summary: Set float-curve key VALUES on an AnimSequence (add_curve only creates an empty named curve - it cannot set keyframe values). Adds the curve if missing, then replaces its keys. Use for authoring Distance/Speed/any float curve directly (#712).

read_anim_curve_keys.summary: Read float-curve keys on an AnimSequence: per curve its name, keyCount, defaultValue and every key as {time (seconds), value, interp}, the shape set_anim_curve_keys takes, so a read replays as a write. curveName narrows to one curve (case-insensitive) and a miss lists the curves that exist; omit it for every curve (#1644).

apply_animation_modifier.summary: Instantiate a UAnimationModifier subclass and run it on an AnimSequence. Headline use: modifierClass='DistanceCurveModifier' bakes a Distance curve from the clip's root motion for distance matching (needs root motion baked first - see bake_root_motion_from_bone). Registers the modifier on the sequence so it re-applies on reimport. props sets the modifier's EditAnywhere fields (e.g. DistanceCurveModifier: {CurveName, Axis:'XY'|'X'|..., bStopAtEnd, StopSpeedThreshold, SampleRate}). Note: DistanceCurveModifier ships in the 'Animation Locomotion Library' plugin (off by default) - enable it first (#712).

set_montage_slot.summary: Set slot name on a montage track.

remove_montage_section.summary: Remove a composite section from a montage through UAnimMontage::DeleteAnimCompositeSection, then clear every OTHER section whose next-section link pointed at it, because a montage that jumps to a section which no longer exists stops dead. The cleared ones come back in clearedNextLinks so they can be re-pointed with asset(set_property) on CompositeSections[i].NextSectionName. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when there is no such section, and the miss lists the sections that exist.

add_notify_state.summary: Add a windowed notify (a UAnimNotifyState) to a sequence or montage: the form that spans a duration and fires NotifyBegin, NotifyTick and NotifyEnd, which is what a combo window, a hit window or a timed particle effect is built from. add_notify only ever writes the instant form, so this was unreachable. notifyStateClass takes a class name, a bare suffix ('TimedParticleEffect' resolves AnimNotifyState_TimedParticleEffect), or a full path, and an unresolved one is refused rather than silently dropped. notifyProperties are validated against the class before anything is written. Returns objectPath for further editor(set_property) writes, and the full notifyStates list on the asset.

remove_notify_state.summary: Remove windowed notifies by name and/or class; both filters apply together and at least one is required. This is a separate action rather than a flag on remove_notify because that handler's class filter only ever inspects FAnimNotifyEvent::Notify, so a notify STATE is invisible to it. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when nothing matched.

set_sync_markers.summary: Author an AnimSequence's sync markers: apply the list, refresh the sequence's marker index, register the names on the skeleton, then read back what actually landed. A plain property write reaches AuthoredSyncMarkers and leaves it inert, because the runtime reads UniqueMarkerNames and the index built by RefreshSyncMarkerDataFromAuthored, and the editor only offers marker names the skeleton has seen. markerMode 'replace' (default) makes the array the whole list, so an empty array clears them; 'merge' adds or moves only the named ones. The whole batch is validated against the clip length before anything is written.

add_montage_section.summary: Add composite section to montage. Pass segmentIndex (with slotName or slotIndex) to anchor the section to a specific segment: its startTime is taken from that segment and it stays linked, so inserting a segment ahead of it moves the marker with its animation. Without segmentIndex the section is a bare absolute-time marker (#826).

add_montage_segment.summary: Append (or insert) an animation segment into a montage slot's anim track. This is the only way to get more than one animation into a montage: create_montage builds exactly one segment, set_montage_sequence replaces rather than appends, and add_montage_section only writes a time marker with no animation behind it. Creates the named slot when it does not exist. Validates that the source shares the montage's skeleton and matches the track's additive type, then relays out the segments, refreshes linked sections and notifies, and rewrites the montage length (#826).

remove_montage_segment.summary: Remove a segment from a montage slot by index, then relay out the remaining segments and rewrite the montage length. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the slot already holds no segments (#826).

list_montage_segments.summary: List every slot's segments on a montage so a caller can address them by index: animation path, startPos/endPos trim, playRate, loopCount, track position and length per segment, plus the sections with the slot and segment each one links to (#826).

create_ik_rig.summary: Create IKRigDefinition asset, optionally with retargetRoot + chains[].

read_ik_rig.summary: Read an IK Rig's preview mesh, skeleton roots/bones, ancestry-validated chains and goal assignments, concrete goals, exclusions, and structured solver/FBIK effector state.

configure_ik_rig.summary: UE 5.8+. Author an existing IK Rig through UIKRigController with strict bone, ancestry, goal, and setting validation, native readback, one transaction, and checked save; older engines return unsupported_engine_version. autoSetup='retarget' installs the native retarget definition; 'full_body' installs the retarget definition then Full Body IK before requested desired-state upserts.

create_control_rig.summary: Create a Control Rig Blueprint from a skeletal mesh or a skeleton through the engine's Control Rig factory, the same path as the Content Browser's Create Control Rig: the source's bone hierarchy is imported and the preview mesh set. Pass exactly one source. name defaults to '<Source>_CtrlRig' and packagePath to the source's folder. onConflict=skip (default) returns the existing asset, error refuses; it never overwrites. Returns a delete_asset rollback (#1133).

set_control_rig_preview_mesh.summary: Set the preview SkeletalMesh of an EXISTING Control Rig Blueprint, which generic property writes do not reach (#1369). Reads the mesh back, saves, and returns previewMesh, previousPreviewMesh and the mesh's skeleton, with a rollback to the previous mesh.

read_control_rig_graph.summary: Read a Control Rig's RigVM models: every graph with its nodes (name, node path, class), each node's pins (name, pin path, cppType, direction, execute flag, default value, nested sub-pins) and the links between them, plus full member-variable metadata (type, subtype, array-ness, default, public/read-only). list_control_rig_variables only ever reported a node COUNT, which is not enough to verify solver wiring (#774).

read_control_rig_hierarchy.summary: Read a Control Rig's per-element hierarchy metadata: each element's name, type (Bone|Control|Null|Curve...), index, and parent (#619).

begin_control_rig_edit.summary: UE 5.8+. Create a Sequencer Control Rig editing session over a source AnimSequence; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines. Baseline first: before this call, reuse or create a Control Rig for the target character, bind/import the exact target skeleton, add the intended controls, author Forward Solve, add Backward/Inverse Solve, verify it with read_control_rig_hierarchy/read_control_rig_graph, and pass an unchanged source round-trip. For a new baseline, the Unreal 5.8 ControlRig toolset (wrapped on this category, or through epic(call_tool)) creates the rig, imports the skeleton bones, adds controls and adds a backward solve graph; a newly created rig alone is not usable. There is no silent fallback to raw bone-key authoring. rigMode='fk' uses UFKControlRig only when generated FK controls are sufficient; rigMode='asset' requires the verified controlRigPath and rejects rigs without inverse execution. bindingTag is the stable natural key for replay. onConflict is skip|error (default error); existing sessions are never modified. layered defaults false. startFrame is inclusive and endFrame is exclusive. Returns the resolved bindingTag/binding GUID, rig, frame range, controls and created/existed status.

read_control_rig_edit.summary: UE 5.8+. Read transform, bool, float/scale-float, and integer/enum controls from a Control Rig editing session without changing editor state; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines and has no silent fallback. Scalar samples return value instead of transform. Control metadata includes native controlType, animatable, and enum path/options where applicable. Returns session identity, layered mode, range/rate, filtered control metadata, and requested frame samples.

capture_control_rig_pose.summary: UE 5.8+. Capture current live local UControlRig values without opening, scrubbing, refreshing, or evaluating Sequencer; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines and has no silent fallback. The addressed LevelSequence must already be focused. Omit controlNames to capture the current Control Rig selection. Returns an immutable captureVersion=1 snapshot with sequence, binding, track, section, rig-object, current-frame, selection, control-type, and typed-value identity for later propagate_pose validation.

apply_control_rig_edits.summary: UE 5.8+. Apply typed Control Rig edits in one transaction; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines. There is no silent fallback to raw bone tracks. set_keys writes strictly ordered full per-frame transforms from normalized quaternions and preserves shortest-arc quaternion continuity. A set operation writes one full absolute transform at frame or frames. An offset operation applies translation/rotation/scale deltas across an inclusive frame range with optional edge blends. propagate_pose validates caller-held baseline and accepted live snapshots from the same session, exact rig instance, frame, and complete control set, then keys only controls whose values changed across each control's explicit original donorFrames. Snapshot selection is provenance metadata; the explicit propagation controls are authoritative. mode='fixed' copies the accepted changed channels; mode='local_delta' preserves donor motion while applying the captured local delta. Bool, enum, and int controls support fixed only. contact_lock densely constrains a translatable driver control, or an optional driven bone/socket reference, to a fixed component-space target with smooth edge blends and optional pole/control stabilization. Driver and stabilizer keys are read back transactionally. A drivenReference or targetReference contact returns verification='bake_and_analyze_required' without passed=true; bake it and analyze every constrained frame before accepting the bone/socket result. set_bool, set_float, and set_int key matching scalar controls; enum controls use set_int with one of the integer values reported in enumOptions. Sequencer's current interpolation mode is retained. Operations are keyed in order, each sampled after the ones before it land, so batched control offsets compose like separate calls: a component-space offset on a child adds to an earlier offset on its parent. Contacts using targetReference, or drivenReference without the FK rotation-chain solver, require a fresh session without earlier rig edits because those references sample the source animation; bake prior edits and begin a new session first. They must also be first in the batch, otherwise contact_lock_reference_batch_unsupported refuses it. Final readback checks stored control/driver poses; it does not re-evaluate target-reference motion after later edits. Driven contacts also check their final FK end-control or asset-driver pose before saving; bone/socket results still require bake and analysis. Returns per-operation counts, affected controls/frames and changedChannels; a failed key/readback batch is undone.

bake_control_rig_edit.summary: UE 5.8+. Bake the evaluated Control Rig session to a new AnimSequence asset; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines and has no raw-track fallback. The source LevelSequence remains unchanged. outputAssetPath is the output natural key; onConflict is skip|error (default error), never overwrite. Key reduction and Sequencer links are not supported yet, so reduceKeys/createLink must be false or omitted. The output names the bound mesh as its retarget source asset unless setRetargetSourceAsset=false, so a mesh whose proportions differ from the skeleton's reference pose is not retargeted twice on playback. interpolation defaults to the session source clip's, so a Step clip bakes as Step. Takes the rest of the Sequencer bake options (curves, world space, include/exclude names, warm-up, delay, timecode, custom startFrame/endFrame). Returns output asset metadata, frame/rate counts, retargetSourceAsset, interpolation, status, and delete-created-asset rollback.

bake_sequence_animation.summary: UE 5.8+. Bake one skeletal mesh binding of any LevelSequence to a new AnimSequence with the full set of Sequencer bake options, which the engine's own anim sequence export tool does not take. Pick the binding with exactly one of bindingTag, bindingGuid or bindingName. setRetargetSourceAsset defaults true: the output names the bound mesh as its retarget source asset, so its recorded bone lengths are not retargeted again on playback. interpolation is linear|step (default linear). The LevelSequence is never modified; onConflict is skip|error (default error), never overwrite. Returns output asset metadata, frame/rate counts, retargetSourceAsset, interpolation and delete-created-asset rollback.

analyze_animation.summary: Cross-version, data-driven AnimSequence inspection using the native animation APIs available in the compiled engine. Samples an AnimSequence and reports deterministic numeric motion diagnostics without Python or viewport inference. Returns source/rate/range metadata, sampled local/component transforms, root-motion and continuity metrics, and any written analysis artifacts. facingBones samples the component-space vector from boneA to boneB at every sampled frame, rotates it into the root bone's frame, and reports its yaw per sample (facingYawDegrees; 0 is root +X, 90 is root +Y) and over the clip in summary.facing: averageYawDegrees (circular mean), minYawDegrees, maxYawDegrees, spreadDegrees, resultantLength and degenerateSampleCount for samples where the vector is vertical.

set_root_motion.summary: Set root motion settings on AnimSequence.

begin_skeleton_edit.summary: Open a batched bone-editing session over a skeletal mesh's reference skeleton. NOTHING is written until commit_skeleton_edit: a per-edit commit would re-derive the reference skeleton once per change and can leave a half-edited hierarchy, which is why this mirrors the begin/apply/bake lifecycle the Control Rig actions already use. sessionTag is the stable key every later call addresses and defaults to Skel_<MeshName>; reopening the same tag on the same mesh is idempotent. Returns the current bone list, the baseline bone count, and how many bones have skinned vertices.

edit_skeleton_bones.summary: Apply a whole batch of hierarchy edits to an open session, validating every entry against the state its predecessors leave BEFORE mutating anything, so a bad entry at position nine does not leave the first eight applied. Removing a bone that has children, or that mesh sections skin vertices to, is refused with the dependents listed unless removeChildren or force says otherwise; a reparent that would form a cycle names the offending bone. op normalize_scale sets scale 1 on a bone and every descendant while keeping each one's component-space location and rotation, the fix for a 100x root scale inherited by metre-scale children; its row reports bonesNormalized, maxLocalScaleBefore and maxComponentDrift (#1201). Returns a per-edit changed/alreadyApplied row and an inverse-edit rollback.

commit_skeleton_edit.summary: Write the session's batched edits into the skeletal mesh and its skeleton in one transaction, and save both packages. This is the ONLY call that touches the assets. A session with no pending edits closes without dirtying anything. The rollback is flagged lossy on purpose: skin weights and dependent-asset fix-ups cannot be reversed by replaying inverse edits.

cancel_skeleton_edit.summary: Discard an open session's working copy without writing; the assets on disk are untouched. Cancelling a session that is not open reports alreadyClosed rather than failing, so replaying a rollback is safe. Returns the discarded edits so they can be re-sent after a fix.

set_bone_retargeting.summary: Set each bone's translation retargeting mode, which lives in the skeleton's private BoneTree and has no addressable UPROPERTY, so set_property cannot reach it. Omitting bones applies to every bone; includeChildren uses the engine's own recursive setter. Returns the prior and new mode per bone, and a per-bone restore rollback that replays through this same action.

author_blend_profile.summary: Create a blend profile if it is absent and write its per-bone scales. A UBlendProfile is a per-skeleton subobject, so asset(set_property) can neither create it nor address the per-bone map. remove deletes the profile and reports every entry it destroyed, so the inverse can rebuild it. Returns the full entry list plus the skeleton's profile names.

edit_curve_metadata.summary: Author the skeleton curve metadata that compare_curves_to_morph_targets could only read, including the material and morph-target flags that drive curves into materials and morphs. The whole batch validates first, and every operation is idempotent: adding an existing curve or removing an absent one reports rather than errors. Returns the full curve metadata table after the edit.

register_compatible_skeleton.summary: Register, or with remove=true unregister, another skeleton as compatible, so its animations are usable on this one. This closes the loop asset(diff) opens: diff two skeletons for the hierarchy delta, then act on it. The engine call has been exercised in this repo's tests for a long time and was simply never shipped as an action. Returns the compatible list before and after and, per entry, whether the engine's own editor compatibility check agrees plus the source's bone count.

add_virtual_bone.summary: Add a virtual bone from sourceBone to targetBone. name picks its name (the engine's 'VB ' prefix is added when missing) and is refused when a bone or virtual bone already has it; omitted, the engine generates one. Returns virtualBoneName.

create_ik_retargeter.summary: Create IKRetargeter asset and (default) initialize the UE 5.7 ops stack: assigns sourceRig+targetRig to all ops, runs AutoMapChains. Returns chainsMapped count (#246).

read_ik_retargeter.summary: Read an IK Retargeter's source/target rigs and preview meshes, flattened and per-op chain mappings, typed op stack, and all named/current pose offsets when the compiled engine exposes them. Each op now carries its `settings` object in full, reflected off the op's own settings struct: the Root Motion op's RootMotionSource, the Pelvis Motion op's alphas and offsets, and the FK Chains op's per-chain RotationMode and TranslationMode. Those settings decide what a retarget actually does, and they were the part only Python could see (#1000) (#246).

configure_ik_retargeter.summary: UE 5.8+. `ops` writes the per-op settings that decide what a retarget does and that nothing else could reach: pass {name or index, enabled?, settings?, chainSettings?}. `settings` writes properties on the op's own settings struct; `chainSettings` merges per-chain FK properties into the chain you name rather than replacing the whole ChainsToRetarget list, so setting one chain's RotationMode leaves the others alone. Every op write is validated before the transaction opens and applied inside it, so a bad property name changes nothing (#1000/#1034). Configure an existing IK Retargeter through UIKRetargeterController with the correct default-op and per-op rig assignment order, auto/manual chain mappings, named pose authoring, processor validation, native readback, transaction rollback, and checked save; older engines return unsupported_engine_version. Whole-pose auto-align resets that pose first: create a new pose or pass pose.reset=true to acknowledge replacement, then manual offsets are applied.

set_ik_rig_mesh.summary: Set the preview/source skeletal mesh on an EXISTING IK Rig (#701).

set_ik_retargeter_rig.summary: Set the source or target IK Rig on an EXISTING IK Retargeter (#703).

auto_align_retarget_pose.summary: Auto-align all bones of the source/target retarget pose (chain-to-chain) - fixes a retargeter that outputs a static reference pose (#701).

reset_retarget_pose.summary: Reset the current retarget pose (all bones) to the reference pose (#701).

remove_retarget_pose.summary: UE 5.7+. Remove a named retarget pose from the source or target side of an IK Retargeter through IKRetargeterController, e.g. scratch poses left by auto-align (#1288). The default pose is refused; a pose that is already gone reports alreadyRemoved. Returns wasCurrent, the resulting currentPose and the remaining poses; on 5.8 the rollback re-creates the pose with its offsets.

rename_retarget_pose.summary: UE 5.7+. Rename a retarget pose on the source or target side of an IK Retargeter (#1288). The default pose is refused as either name, and a newName already taken on that side is refused. Returns currentPose, the poses and a rename-back rollback.

batch_retarget_animations.summary: Bake validated source AnimSequences onto the target skeleton through an IK Retargeter (RunBatchRetarget), save every output, and roll back newly created outputs if the batch is incomplete or unsavable. Overwrite is rejected. Returns mapping completeness and every unmapped target chain so partial retargets are explicit; pass requireCompleteMapping=true only when the target should have no intentional extra chains (#701).

read_bone_track.summary: Read bone transform samples from AnimSequence: the raw track, or the reference pose for a bone without one (hasTrack says which). rotationFormat=quaternion returns the exact stored quaternion, which an Euler readback loses near gimbal lock; space=component composes the parent chain.

compose_pose_sequence.summary: Author a new AnimSequence from poses sampled out of other sequences (#1230). sources[0] at its frame or time is the base pose and sets the skeleton; layers blend chosen bones (exact names, nameContains, excludeContains, includeDescendants) toward another source by weight, slerping rotation and lerping translation and scale, in order. With easeToSource the keys ease from that composed pose at frame 0 to the named source's pose at the last frame (linear or smooth); otherwise every key holds the composed pose. Writes a track for every skeleton bone and saves; returns the matched bones per layer and a delete_asset rollback.

transform_bone_tracks.summary: Read-modify-write raw bone tracks across many AnimSequences in one call, one transaction and save per sequence (#1227). trackOps apply in order to every key: rotate (a quaternion or rotator, pre-multiplied in parent space or post-multiplied in bone space, optionally rotating translation too), offset (add a translation), copy_from_donor (hold a donor clip's frame rotation on the bones, keeping each key's own translation and scale unless told otherwise), reference_delta (targetBone = targetRef * (sourceRef^-1 * source), with source from a donor frame or from the sequence's own sourceBone per key). Every sequence, bone and donor is validated before anything is written. Each row reports frame 0 of every written track before and after as quaternions.

create_pose_search_database.summary: Create a PoseSearchDatabase asset (motion matching). Pass skeletonPath and it authors the matching PoseSearchSchema (<name>_Schema, default channels) alongside it, which is what makes the database indexable at all; pass schemaPath to reuse an existing one. A schema that cannot index (no skeleton, or no feature channels) is refused rather than assigned, because the editor then reports the DATABASE as the invalid asset. Without either, the database is created empty and unindexable and says so in note (#833).

set_pose_search_schema.summary: Set the Schema on an existing PoseSearchDatabase.

add_pose_search_sequence.summary: Append an AnimSequence/AnimComposite/AnimMontage/BlendSpace to a PoseSearchDatabase, with optional per-clip flags (#684).

set_pose_search_clips.summary: Author the whole clip list of a PoseSearchDatabase in one call (the 'duplicate a stock PSD, swap its clips' pipeline step). Replaces the list by default. Each clip carries per-entry flags. Follow with build_pose_search_index (#684).

read_pose_search_database.summary: Inspect a PoseSearchDatabase: schema, animation entries, cost biases, tags.

set_pose_search_database_settings.summary: Tune a PoseSearchDatabase: cost biases, KD-tree neighbours, search mode, PCA components, normalization set.

create_pose_search_schema.summary: Create a PoseSearchSchema (the feature definition a database indexes against). Binds a skeleton (and optional mirror table) and, by default, adds Trajectory+Pose default channels so the schema is immediately buildable. Refine with add_pose_search_schema_*_channel.

add_pose_search_schema_pose_channel.summary: Add a Pose feature channel to a schema (samples named bones for velocity/position/rotation/phase) (motion matching).

add_pose_search_schema_trajectory_channe.summary: Add a Trajectory feature channel to a schema (past/future motion samples).

read_pose_search_schema.summary: Inspect a PoseSearchSchema: skeleton(s), mirror table, sample rate, feature channels.

create_mirror_data_table.summary: Create a MirrorDataTable for a skeleton (needed for mirrored poses in motion matching / mirror nodes). Auto-derives bone-pair rows from find/replace expressions (defaults to UE mannequin _l/_r suffix swap).

read_mirror_data_table.summary: Inspect a MirrorDataTable: skeleton and bone-pair rows (name -> mirroredName).

create_pose_search_normalization_set.summary: Create a PoseSearchNormalizationSet grouping databases so they normalize their cost space together (consistent blending across a locomotion set). Assign it via set_pose_search_database_settings(normalizationSetPath) (motion matching).

add_motion_matching_node.summary: Add a Motion Matching node to an AnimBP AnimGraph and point it at a PoseSearchDatabase (the runtime node that searches the database each frame). Connects its output to the Output Pose by default. For chooser-driven database selection, bind an anim-node function that calls SetDatabasesToSearch.

add_pose_history_node.summary: Add a Pose History (PoseSearchHistoryCollector) node to an AnimBP AnimGraph - the Motion Matching node needs it in the graph to query pose/trajectory history. Defaults to self-generated trajectory (no external trajectory pin needed) and inserts itself into the pose chain feeding the Output Pose.

set_motion_matching_chooser.summary: Drive the Motion Matching node's Database from a ChooserTable so the database is selected at runtime by character state. Wires a thread-safe EvaluateChooser (result typed to PoseSearchDatabase) into the MM node's Database pin. contextSource selects what the chooser reads its columns from: 'self' (default, the anim instance - choosers branching on AnimBP variables) or 'pawn' (the owning pawn via TryGetPawnOwner - choosers branching on character/pawn state).

create_skeleton.summary: Create a real USkeleton from a SkeletalMesh through the Unreal skeleton factory. The factory assigns the new skeleton to that mesh, then both packages are saved. An existing destination is an onConflict=skip idempotency hit only when the mesh already points at it and the reference skeleton has exactly the same bone count, names in index order, and parent indexes; reference-pose transforms are not compared. Otherwise the action refuses to repurpose it. If either save fails, it restores and saves the mesh's previous skeleton reference, then deletes the new skeleton when safe; an incomplete cleanup returns a machine-readable recovery descriptor. Returns the previous skeleton and a lossy rollback that restores the mesh association; delete the created skeleton separately only after confirming nothing references it.

add_sequence_evaluator.summary: Add a Sequence Evaluator node (explicit-time player) to an AnimBP graph - the node distance matching drives by setting its ExplicitTime each frame. graphName can be the top-level AnimGraph or a state's inner graph (pass the state name). Defaults bTeleportToExplicitTime=false so time advances and root motion extracts. Connects to the Output Pose by default. Returns nodeGuid for bind_anim_node_function (#713).

bind_anim_node_function.summary: Bind a thread-safe anim-node function to an anim graph node's update slot - the mechanism distance matching uses to advance a Sequence Evaluator's explicit time each frame (function calls AnimDistanceMatchingLibrary::DistanceMatchToTarget / AdvanceTimeByDistanceMatching). The function must already exist on the AnimBP (create it as a BlueprintThreadSafe function first). Identify the node by nodeGuid (from add_sequence_evaluator / add_*_node) (#713).

set_sequence_properties.summary: Batch-set properties on AnimSequence assets: loop, root motion and the additive settings (additiveAnimType, refPoseType, refPoseSeq, refFrameIndex). Keys match case-insensitively; an unknown key or value refuses the whole call before any sequence is written. Each result carries properties (read back after the write) and previousProperties. If a path is a Montage and resolveFromMontages is true (default), resolves to its first AnimSequence.

bake_root_motion_from_bone.summary: Bake delta translation from a source bone (e.g. pelvis) onto the root bone across the whole sequence; compensates the source bone so world-space position is unchanged.

get_bone_transform.summary: Read a bone or socket transform on a live actor's SkeletalMeshComponent. Wraps GetBoneTransform / GetSocketTransform. Returns location, rotation, scale (#420).

list_bones.summary: List bones in a live actor's SkeletalMeshComponent ref skeleton (name, index, parent), in reference-skeleton order so parents precede children (#420).

rebind_leader_pose.summary: Re-bind every secondary SkeletalMeshComponent on an actor to a body component (default CharacterMesh0 / Mesh). One-call fix for the 'character explodes after rotating the actor' failure mode (#419).

sample_pose.summary: Evaluate an AnimSequence (or a BlendSpace at a blend position) and return COMPOSED bone transforms, which read_bone_track (raw local space) and get_bone_transforms (reference pose only) cannot give. Returns samples:[{frame, time, bones:[{name, location, rotation, scale}]}]; rotationFormat=quaternion returns rotation as {x,y,z,w}. A montage is refused with a pointer to its segments, because a montage has no pose of its own (#923/#926/#922).

get_live_bone_transforms.summary: Read the EVALUATED pose off a live SkeletalMeshComponent in the editor world or PIE, for many bones at once. This is the read that tells 'standing' from 'prone' when the reference pose cannot (#922). Also returns componentTransform and an evaluation block (animationMode, animInstanceClass, componentSpaceTransformCount) so a clean component transform sitting on a dead anim instance is visible in one call (#922/#926).

measure_natural_speed.summary: Measure a locomotion clip's planted-foot speed, in cm/s, by evaluating the pose and tracking the lowest foot's horizontal travel while it is in contact. Every retarget changes natural speed by the target skeleton's leg-length ratio, so a BlendSpace built on retargeted clips has to re-measure per clip per character (#923). Returns naturalSpeed, plantedDistance, plantedTime, contactThreshold, per-foot breakdown.

preview_animation.summary: Toggle bUpdateAnimationInEditor + VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption=AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones on every SkeletalMeshComponent of an actor. Bypasses the 'cannot be edited on templates' guard for level instances (#419/#420).

set_live_post_process_anim_blueprint.summary: Set or clear a transient post-process AnimBP override on one live SkeletalMeshComponent in the editor world or PIE. Pass the AnimBlueprintGeneratedClass object path (for example /Game/Animations/ABP_Name.ABP_Name_C), not the AnimBlueprint asset path; pass clear=true to remove the component override and fall back to the skeletal mesh asset setting. Incompatible skeletons and the component's main AnimBP class are refused before mutation. Reads back the override, effective class, and live post-process instance. Repeating the active override is a no-op. This never edits or saves a mesh, Blueprint, or component template.

epic_add_actors.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Add actors from the level to the currently open sequence. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_add_actors__level_sequence_editor_s.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Add existing actors to Sequencer. Tracks will be automatically added based on default track settings. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_actors_by_name.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Add actors to the sequence by their names in the level. Finds actors by label in the current level and adds them to the currently open sequence as possessable bindings. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_add_actors_by_name__level_sequence_.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Add all actors in the Sequencer playback world whose labels match the supplied names. Raises an error when no actors match. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_actors_to_binding.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Add actors to an existing binding. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_add_actors_to_binding__level_sequen.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Assigns the given actors to the binding Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_anim_layer_from_selection.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Add an anim layer containing the controls and objects selected in Sequencer, adding the Base layer first if the sequence has no layers. With nothing selected it adds an empty layer named "Empty Layer <N>". Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_auto_bake.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set up auto-bake recorders for the linked anim sequences on the given bindings. Equivalent to the "Add AutoBake" context-menu entry in the Sequencer UI. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_auto_bake_with_anim_sequences.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Same as AddAutoBake, but links pre-created anim sequences instead of prompting for new ones. No asset creation or export options dialogs are shown. Everything is validated first: if anything is invalid an error is raised and nothing is changed. That includes a binding that already has a linked anim sequence, a null, incompatible, repeated or already linked anim sequence, or an anim sequence the editor's asset reference filter refuses to link (as in UEFN). The anim sequences are only linked, not baked here: like AddAutoBake the level sequence is dirtied and the auto-bake runs when the linked track is toggled to, overwriting each anim sequence. The current export options are recorded on the link. To undo this for a binding, call DeleteLinkedAnimTrack, which removes the recorder, the link and the linked track. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_backward_solve_graph.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Create a backward solve graph with InverseExecution event.

epic_add_binding_to_folder.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Add a binding into a folder for organization. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_add_bone.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Add a bone to the Control Rig hierarchy.

epic_add_bool_key.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Add a bool key to the unique matching bool channel, including an unnamed one. Replaces a key already at Frame. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_channel_override.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Override the named channel with a new override of OverrideClass, replacing any existing override. The channel's keys are kept. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_child_folder.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFolderExtensions] Add a child folder to the target folder. The child must belong to the target folder's movie scene. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_child_object_binding.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFolderExtensions] Add a guid for an object binding to this folder Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_child_track.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFolderExtensions] Add a track to this folder. The track must belong to the folder's movie scene. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_comment.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] AddComment Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_component_binding.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Adds a binding to another component of the actor than the one the deformer is applied to. Link a "ComponentBinding/<Name>" node to data interface nodes to read from it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_constraint.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Add a constraint. When a level sequence is open in Sequencer the constraint is keyed active at the current time, otherwise it is added as a static constraint. Raises a script error if a handle is null or invalid, the child is the parent, or the parent is constrained to the child, directly or through a chain of constraints. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_constraint_between.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Add a constraint between two objects, creating their transformable handles; the constraint owns the handles. Each object is a Control Rig with a control name as its attachment, a scene component with an optional socket, or an actor (its root component, optional socket). When a level sequence is open in Sequencer the constraint is keyed active at CreationTime, as the Constraints panel's creation options do; otherwise it is added as a static constraint. Raises a script error if an object is null or not transformable, a control or socket does not exist, a control's type cannot be constrained (Bool, Float, ScaleFloat, Integer), the child is the parent, the parent is constrained to the child, directly or through a chain of constraints, or the constraint cannot be added. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_control.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Add a control to the hierarchy.

epic_add_control_rig_available_space.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Add a space to the end of a control's space picker list, as the level editor's Add Space does. Raises a script error if the Control Rig is null, the control or space does not exist in the rig, or the space is world or the control's default parent. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_double_key.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Add a double key and return its identity. InTime is in display-rate frames unless TimeUnit is TickResolution. SubFrame is clamped to [0, 1) and ignored for tick-resolution frames. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_element.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Add a bone or null element to the Control Rig hierarchy.

epic_add_empty_binding.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions] Add a binding that resolves to nothing, to be assigned an object later, as Sequencer's New Empty Binding does. An empty Name gives "EmptyBinding"; either way a number is appended if a binding already has the name. The binding holds one empty locator, except in sequences without a binding reference table (such as Day Sequences), where it is a plain possessable with no locator. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_event_graph.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Create a new graph with the specified event type.

epic_add_event_key.summary: [Epic AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset] Author a complete event key end-to-end on an Event track section. Equivalent of the three-step manual flow: 1. SequencerToolsFunctionLibrary::CreateQuickBinding to create an endpoint on the Director Blueprint that calls FunctionName on BoundObject (or its class). 2. SequencerToolsFunctionLibrary::CreateEvent to wrap the endpoint in a FMovieSceneEvent bound to the event section. 3. Find the event channel on the section and add a key at Frame carrying the FMovieSceneEvent value. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_event_node.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Add an event node to the graph.

epic_add_integer_key.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Add an integer key to the unique matching integer channel, including an unnamed one. Replaces a key already at Frame. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_key_string.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.keyframing.SequencerKeyframingTools] Add a string key to a channel on a section. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

The new pin is an input if the source is an output, and the reverse. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_loop_binding.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Adds a value carried through the loop: an input and an output pin on both loop nodes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

Raises, changing nothing, when the editor's asset reference filter refuses a reference from the level sequence to the rig (as in UEFN). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_blend_values_on_selected.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Perform a blend operation on selected keys or controls. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_blend_values_on_selected__control_r.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Perform the specified blend operation on the selected keys in the curve editor, or on the selected Control Rig controls at the current time. TimeOffset, BlendToNoise and BlendToWave need keys selected in the curve editor; they do not fall back to selected Control Rig controls. BlendToMirror blends the curve editor key selection, falling back to a Sequencer key selection and then to the selected Control Rig controls at the current time, toward their mirrored pose. epic_create_condition_endpoint.summary: [Epic AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset] Create a Director Blueprint Condition function endpoint on the sequence's Director Blueprint and bind it to a director-blueprint condition on the given host (a section, a whole track, or a single track row), so the host only evaluates at runtime when the function returns true. If the host has no condition, a Director Blueprint Condition is created on it; if it already has one, that condition is reused. A host carrying a different condition type (e.g. a platform or group condition) is rejected - clear it first via MovieSceneConditionExtensions.ClearSectionCondition or ClearTrackCondition. Generates a function graph named after FunctionName whose entry node takes an FMovieSceneConditionContext and returns a bool. The body is left empty by design - author it via BlueprintToolset, then call BlueprintToolset.CompileBlueprint on the Director BP so the condition's CompiledFunctionName is populated; without that the condition is skipped at runtime. The returned UK2Node_FunctionEntry is the new function's entry node. Scope, CheckFrequency, bEditorForceTrue and payload variables are EditAnywhere on the condition; set them via set_editor_property on the condition UObject, obtained from the native accessor (e.g. section.get_section_condition()). Retrieve the condition object before editing its properties; a class-path string is not an object reference. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_dynamic_binding_resolver.summary: [Epic AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset] Create a dynamic-binding resolver function endpoint on the sequence's Director Blueprint and wire it to the binding's FMovieSceneDynamicBinding so the binding is resolved at runtime by the generated function. Generates a function graph named after FunctionName whose entry node returns a FMovieSceneDynamicBindingResolveResult. The function body is left empty by design - callers author it via BlueprintToolset (e.g. drop a "GetPlayerPawn" node, connect its return to the entry's Object pin via a MakeStruct FMovieSceneDynamicBindingResolveResult). The returned UK2Node_FunctionEntry is the entry-point node of the new function graph; pass it by name lookup to BlueprintToolset calls that take node references. After authoring the body, call BlueprintToolset.CompileBlueprint on the Director BP to populate FMovieSceneDynamicBinding's CompiledFunctionName. Otherwise the resolver will be silently skipped at runtime. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

Raises a script error if the track is not a writable Control Rig track, the rig is already on it or on another track, one is layered and the other is not, or the editor's asset reference filter refuses a reference from the track's sequence to the rig's asset (as in UEFN). The new rig is constructed with the track's settings and rotation order overrides, and the controls selected on the old rig are selected on it. When the track's sequence is focused in Sequencer, the new rig is bound to the track's skeletal mesh and replaces the old one in Sequencer and Animation Mode, so it can be read and keyed at once. One undoable step. Raises a script error if the track is not a writable Control Rig track, the reference is not a Control Rig class or asset, the track is layered and the new rig is not an FK rig and has no backwards solve event, or the editor's asset reference filter refuses a reference from the track's sequence to the rig (as in UEFN).
