epic_select_bindings__level_sequence_edi.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary] Adds bindings of the focused sequence to the selection without clearing it. Raises an error when no Sequencer is open, or without selecting anything when any binding is invalid or foreign. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_channels.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.keyframing.SequencerKeyframingTools] Set the channel selection in the Sequencer editor. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_select_channels__level_sequence_edi.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary] Adds channels to the selection without clearing it. A channel name matches a channel of the section or the label of the outliner node that contains it. Raises an error when no Sequencer is open, or without selecting anything when any section is foreign or any name matches nothing. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_control.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Select or deselect a control on a Control Rig. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_select_control_rig_controls.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Select or deselect controls on a Control Rig. Selection drives the selection-based functions such as TweenControlRig, BlendValuesOnSelected, MirrorSelectedControls, ZeroTransforms, and AddAnimLayerFromSelection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_control_rig_pose_asset_contr.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Select the controls stored in a pose asset, as the Pose Library's Select Controls does. Raises a script error if the pose asset or Control Rig is null, or none of the pose's controls exist on the rig. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_control_rig_pose_clipboard_c.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Select the controls in Animation Mode's pose clipboard, as Select Pose and Select Mirror Pose do. Raises a script error if Animation Mode is not active or the clipboard is empty. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_curve_editor_keys.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Add the specified key indices to the active Curve Editor selection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_folders.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the folder selection in the Sequencer editor. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_select_folders__level_sequence_edit.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary] Adds folders from the focused sequence to the selection without clearing it. Raises an error when no Sequencer is open, or without selecting anything when any folder is invalid or foreign. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_mirrored_controls.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Select the mirrored counterparts of the currently selected controls. Replaces the current selection with mirrored controls. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_select_mirrored_controls__control_r.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Replace the selection with the mirrored counterparts of the selected controls. Requires Animation Mode to be active. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_sections.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the section selection in the Sequencer editor. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_select_sections__level_sequence_edi.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary] Adds sections from the focused sequence to the selection without clearing it. Raises an error when no Sequencer is open, or without selecting anything when any section is invalid or foreign. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_selection_set.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Select or deselect a selection set's controls and actors on the actors sets act on, as clicking the set does. Raises a script error if no level sequence is open in Sequencer or the set does not exist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_tracks.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the track selection in the Sequencer editor. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_select_tracks__level_sequence_edito.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary] Adds tracks from the focused sequence to the selection without clearing it. Raises an error when no Sequencer is open, or without selecting anything when any track is invalid or foreign. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_actor_world_transform.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Key an actor's world transform at a frame in the level sequence focused in Sequencer. The key is expressed in the actor's attach parent and, where the actor is the child of an active constraint, in that constraint's space, so the actor reaches the transform. Raises a script error for the cases SetActorWorldTransforms raises for. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_actor_world_transforms.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Key an actor's world transforms at frames in the level sequence focused in Sequencer, adding a Transform track and section if needed. Each key is expressed in the actor's attach parent and, where the actor is the child of an active constraint, in that constraint's space, so the actor reaches the transform. Location, rotation and scale are keyed. Raises a script error if the sequence is not the one focused in Sequencer, the actor is null or not bound in it, or the counts differ. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_actor_world_transforms_async.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] SetActorWorldTransforms as an async operation. See SetActorWorldTransforms for the parameters. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_anim_layer_key.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Key an anim layer's current values at the current Sequencer time, on the layer's selected controls and objects or, if none are selected, on all of them. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_anim_layer_passthrough_key.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set a passthrough key on an anim layer at the current Sequencer time, on the layer's selected controls and objects or, if none are selected, on all of them. A passthrough key makes the layer contribute nothing at that time: additive layers key zero and override layers key the value of the layers below. On the Base layer this keys the inverted input pose instead. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_anim_layer_properties.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set an anim layer's name, mute, lock, weight, type and keyed state; only the properties that differ from the layer's are applied, in one undo step. Raises a script error, changing nothing, if no level sequence is open in Sequencer, Index is out of range, the name is empty, the type is not Base for the Base layer or is Base for another layer, or bKeyed is false on the keyed layer. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_anim_mode_gizmo_scale.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Set the editor's transform gizmo size. Writes UTransformGizmoEditorSettings::TransformGizmoSize. The CR-specific gizmo scale was removed in UE 5.8 in favor of this editor-wide setting. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_anim_mode_hide_manips.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Toggle whether Animation Mode hides all manipulators. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_anim_mode_hierarchy.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Toggle the Animation Mode hierarchy lines/dots display. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_anim_mode_local_spaces.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Toggle multi-select transforms acting in each control's own space. When True, transforming multiple selected controls respects each control's own local space. When False, all use a shared reference. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_anim_mode_nulls.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Toggle the Animation Mode nulls display. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_anim_mode_only_rig_sel.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Toggle Animation Mode restricting viewport selection to rig controls. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_animation_mode_settings.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set every Animation Mode preference and save them to the user's config. Open viewports update immediately. To change some preferences only, read them with GetAnimationModeSettings, edit those fields, and pass the result back. Raises a script error, changing nothing, if TransformGizmoSize is outside -10 to 150, AxisScale or AxisThickness is negative, or a tween setting is not finite. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_animation_mode_tool_open.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Open or close one of Animation Mode's tools, as its toolbar button or command does. Raises a script error if Animation Mode is not active. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_binding_data_domain.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Sets the data domain of a binding and its pins, which removes the links the new data domain is incompatible with. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_binding_data_type.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Sets the data type of a binding and its pins, which removes their links. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_binding_name.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the display name of a binding. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_blend_type.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set a blend type supported by the section's track. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_blender_system.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTrackExtensions] Set the system that blends the track's overlapping sections. Must be one of GetSupportedBlenderSystems. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_bool.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Set a bool control value at a specific frame. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_bound_actor_class.summary: [Epic TemplateSequenceEditor.TemplateSequenceEditorSubsystem] Rebind the sequence to ActorClass by replacing its root spawnable, moving the tracks and component bindings under the old root to the new one. Component bindings resolve by component name, so those ActorClass lacks no longer bind. Camera animation sequences only accept ACameraActor and its subclasses, and a sequence with more than one spawnable is rejected since its root is ambiguous. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_byte_track_enum.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Configure a byte track to use a specific enum type. Byte tracks can animate enum properties. Call this after adding the track and before setting property_name_and_path. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_byte_track_enum__movie_scene_pr.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieScenePropertyTrackExtensions] Set this byte track's enum Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_camera_cut_auto_arrange_section.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTrackExtensions] Set whether camera cut sections auto-arrange. Enabling it on a single-row track closes gaps between sections, as the editor does. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_camera_cut_binding.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set which camera a camera cut section uses. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_camera_cut_binding__movie_scene.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Assign a camera binding. Supply RootSequence for a binding in another sequence; instances must be unique in that hierarchy. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_camera_cut_can_blend.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTrackExtensions] Set whether overlapping camera cut sections blend. Disabling it removes section overlaps and easing, as the editor does. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_camera_lock.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Lock or unlock the camera cut to the viewport. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_clock_source.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the clock source for the sequence. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_clock_source__movie_scene_seque.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions] Set the clock source for this sequence Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_comment.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Set Comment Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_completion_mode.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set how the section's animated state is handled after evaluation. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_component_binding_source.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Changes the kind of component a binding reads from. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_constraint_active_key.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set the constraint active key in the current open Sequencer Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_apply_mode.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set the FK Control Rig to apply mode Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_available_spaces_or.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Reorder a control's space picker list, as moving spaces up and down in the level editor does. Raises a script error if the Control Rig is null, the control does not exist, or Spaces is not the listed spaces in some order. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_controls_visible.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Show or hide a Control Rig's control shapes in the viewport, as Toggle Controls Visibility does for the selected rigs and Toggle Module Controls Visibility for modules; hiding all shapes at once is SetAnimationModeSettings' bHideControlShapes. Raises a script error for the cases GetControlRigControlsVisible raises for. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_layered_mode.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Convert the control rig track into absolute or layered rig. This is destructive: non-FK rigs reset their control values and every section clears its animation and is recreated, and the track is renamed to the rig's class name. Converting to layered requires a backwards solve event unless the rig is an FK rig. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_override.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Override a control setting on a Control Rig instance, as Anim Details' override view does: with an empty Value the setting's current value is captured (Add Override), otherwise the setting takes Value (Edit Override Value). The override goes in the rig's last linked override asset, creating one in the developer folder when it has none, and the rig is reconstructed so it applies. PropertyPath is a control setting path such as TopologyControlSettings->DisplayName, TopologyControlSettings->bShapeVisible, ShapeName, ShapeColor or ShapeTransform; Anim Details' names DisplayName, Shape->bVisible, Shape->Name, Shape->Color and Shape->Transform are accepted too. Raises a script error if overrides are disabled (ControlRig.Overrides), the Control Rig is null, the control does not exist, the path is not a setting of the control, Value cannot be read as that setting, the override asset to edit is read-only, or an override asset must be created and the rig has no asset or the developer folder is not visible or not writable in this editor (as in UEFN). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_priority_order.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set the Control Rig track's priority order; tracks with a higher priority evaluate first. Raises a script error if PriorityOrder is negative. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_rotation_order_over.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Override a control's rotation order, as the Anim Details rotation order dropdown does: its keys are re-baked into the new order so the rotations stay the same, and the rig evaluates in that order. Layered (additive) Control Rigs do not support overrides. Raises a script error for the cases GetControlRigRotationOrder raises for, or when the Control Rig is layered. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_section_transform_m.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set which transform and weight channels a Control Rig section animates (its Active Channels). Disabled channels stop animating and are not keyed; their keys are kept. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_space.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Key the Control Rig Space for the Control at the specified time, compensating so the control keeps its world transform. If the control has no space channel and the space is its current parent, nothing is keyed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_world_transform.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set ControlRig Control's World Transform at a specific time Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_control_rig_world_transforms.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set ControlRig Control's World Transforms at a specific times. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_controls_mask.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Set the visibility mask for the specified controls on a section. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_controls_mask__control_rig_sequ.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set whether the section animates the given controls (bVisible true) or masks them out (false). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_curve_editor_view_mode.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Set how the active Sequencer's Curve Editor lays out its curves. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_custom_clock_source.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions] Drive the sequence's playback from ClockSource, as the Custom clock source picker does: an asset or actor that implements MovieSceneCustomClockSource, or an actor with a component that does. Sets the clock source to Custom. Raises if the source is hidden in this editor or may not be referenced from this sequence. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_custom_time_warp.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTimeWarpExtensions] Replace a section's time warp with a new custom time warp of TimeWarpClass, initialized the way the editor does. Its curve then appears among the section's channels ("PlayRate" for a play rate curve, "TimeWarp" for a time warp curve). PlayRate values are play rate multipliers. TimeWarp values are warped times in tick resolution frames, keyed against unwarped time measured from the section start, so the initial keys map 0 to 0 and the section length to itself. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_data_interface_setting.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Sets a setting of a data interface node, as listed in FDeformerGraphNodeInfo::Settings. The node's pins are recreated if the setting defines them, which removes the links of pins that no longer exist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_default_value.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.keyframing.SequencerKeyframingTools] Set the default value of a channel. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_display_name.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneBindingExtensions] Set this binding's name Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_display_name__movie_scene_track.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTrackExtensions] Set this track's display name Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_display_rate.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the display frame rate of a sequence. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_display_rate__movie_scene_seque.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions] Sets this sequence's display rate Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_double_default.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set the double channel default value. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_double_key_value.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set a live double key's value at double precision. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_ease_in_duration.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionEasingExtensions] Set manual ease-in duration in tick-resolution frames (not display-rate frames), enabling the manual override Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_ease_out_duration.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionEasingExtensions] Set manual ease-out duration in tick-resolution frames (not display-rate frames), enabling the manual override Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_edit_pivot_tool_active.summary: [Epic SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary] Turn the Edit Pivot tool on or off in the level editor, as the Animation Mode "Temporary Pivot" button does. It works on the selected actors and Control Rig controls, so select them first; it turns itself off when the selection changes. It shares the level editor's tool slot with motion trails: turning it on stops motion trails, and SetMotionTrailsVisible(true) turns it off. Raises when no level sequence is open in Sequencer, or the tool does not start. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_emulated_network_mask.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Set the network mode the active Sequencer's root sequence emulates during playback and recompile to match. Raises when no Sequencer is open or the mask is None. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_emulated_network_mask_async.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Set the network mode the active Sequencer's root sequence emulates during playback and wait for evaluation. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_end_frame_bounded.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set end frame bounded Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_enum_track_enum.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieScenePropertyTrackExtensions] Set the enum whose values an enum track animates, including on its existing sections. Keys are entry values, set through the sections' byte channels. A byte track with SetByteTrackEnum animates an enum property the same way. Raises if the enum is hidden in this editor or may not be referenced from this sequence. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_euler_transform.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Set an EulerTransform control value at a specific frame. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_evaluation_type.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Set the evaluation type of a sequence. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_evaluation_type__movie_scene_se.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions] Set the evaluation type for this sequence Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_film_overlay.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Show one of GetFilmOverlayNames in a Cinematic Viewport, or None for no composition overlay. Raises when the viewport is not open or the name is unknown. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_film_overlay_frame_enabled.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Enable or disable a frame overlay, which every Cinematic Viewport shows while it is enabled. Raises when the name is unknown. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_film_overlay_frame_tint.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Set the color a frame overlay draws with. Raises when the name is unknown. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_film_overlay_tint.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Set the tint a Cinematic Viewport applies to the composition overlay it shows, like the Film Overlay menu's tint control. Raises when the viewport is not open. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_fkcontrol_rig_controls_active.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Set whether an FK Control Rig animates controls, as its Select Bones To Animate dialog does: inactive controls stop driving their bones and are masked out of the rig's sections in the focused level sequence. Raises a script error if the sequence is not the one focused in Sequencer, the Control Rig is not an FK Control Rig, or a control does not exist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_float.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Set a float control value at a specific frame. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_float_default.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set the float channel default value. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_float_key_value.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions] Set a live float key's value. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_folder_color.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFolderExtensions] Set the display color of the given folder Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_folder_name.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFolderExtensions] Set the name of the given folder Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_function_settings.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Set Function Settings Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_global_transform.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools] Set global transform of a hierarchy element.

epic_set_int.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Set an integer control value at a specific frame. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_set_kernel_additional_sources.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Sets the shader source assets the kernel includes before its own source, e.g. to share HLSL functions between kernels. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_kernel_binding_options.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] Sets the options of an output binding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_kernel_execution_domain.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] SetKernelExecutionDomain Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_kernel_group_size.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] SetKernelGroupSize Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_kernel_name.summary: [Epic OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem] SetKernelName Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_tag_binding__movie_scene_binding_ta.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneBindingTagExtensions] Attach a tag to the given binding. If the tag name has not been seen before, it is registered in the MovieScene's tag list automatically. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_time_pose_control_rig_world_transfo.summary: [Epic SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary] Key a Control Rig control's world transform at a frame and spread the change across the Time Posing window by weight, as moving the control with Time Posing on does; the keys go to the control's section to key, so Anim Layers apply. One undoable step. Raises when Time Posing is off, the frame is not strictly inside the far anchors, or SetControlRigWorldTransform raises. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_transform_actors_about_pivot.summary: [Epic SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary] Key actors transformed about a pivot at each frame, as the Edit Pivot tool does in Pose mode: the new world transform is World * Pivot^-1 * Delta * Pivot. With bKeepOrientation the actors orbit the pivot and keep their rotation and scale, as Shift does in the tool. Keys the actors in one undoable step. An actor that cannot be keyed (not bound in the sequence, or its Transform track has no Absolute section) is skipped and the reason is logged as an error. Raises when the sequence is not focused or is read-only, Actors or Frames is empty, an actor is null, or no actor can be keyed; nothing is keyed then. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_transform_controls_about_pivot.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Move, rotate or scale Control Rig controls about a pivot, keying them at each frame. At every frame a control's new world transform is World * Pivot^-1 * Delta * Pivot: Delta is applied in the pivot's space, so a 90 degree yaw turns the controls about the pivot's up axis. Controls are keyed with SetControlRigWorldTransforms, so constraints and spaces are compensated. Raises a script error if the sequence is not focused, a control does not exist, Frames is empty, or PivotObject names more than one object. Every control is checked for being driven by the rig at the first frame before any is keyed; if keying still fails partway, the controls keyed before the failure stay keyed, in the call's single transaction, so one undo reverts the whole call. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_transform_controls_about_pivot_asyn.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] TransformControlsAboutPivot as an async operation. See TransformControlsAboutPivot for the parameters. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_tween_control_rig.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Perform a tween operation on a Control Rig at the current Sequencer time. The tween blends between the previous and next keyframe values. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_tween_control_rig__control_rig_sequ.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Perform a Tween operation on the Control Rig's selected controls at the current Sequencer time. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_ungroup_section.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions] Remove a section from its group. Raises when the section is not grouped. A group left with one section is dissolved. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_unlink_anim_sequence.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Remove the link between a binding and one linked Anim Sequence, on both assets. epic_unpin_all_motion_trails.summary: [Epic SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary] Unpin every actor, control and socket trail. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_unpin_motion_trail.summary: [Epic SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary] Unpin a motion trail; it stays drawn while its actor or control is selected. Raises when the trail is not pinned. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_unpin_selected_motion_trails.summary: [Epic SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary] Unpin the pinned trails of the selected actors and controls, as Alt-clicking Motion Paths does. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_untag_binding.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools] Remove a tag from a binding. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_untag_binding__movie_scene_binding_.summary: [Epic SequencerScripting.MovieSceneBindingTagExtensions] Remove a tag from the given binding. Removing its last association also unregisters the tag. No-op if the binding lacks the tag. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_update_control_rig_pose_asset.summary: [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Replace a pose asset's pose with a Control Rig's current values, as the Pose Library's Update Pose does. Raises a script error if the pose asset or Control Rig is null, or bUseAllControls is false and no control is selected. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_validate_sequence.summary: [Epic SequenceValidator.SequenceValidatorSubsystem] Run validation rules on Sequence and its subsequences, as the Sequence Validator window does. The sequence is not modified. Findings in, or reached through, subsequences hidden in this editor are left out. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_wait_for_evaluation_async.summary: [Epic LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem] Wait for a complete editor world tick after this call. TimeoutSeconds must be positive. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_zero_transforms.summary: [Epic animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools] Reset Control Rig transforms to their default (usually zero) values. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

Applies at the current time only. Requires Animation Mode to be active. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

list.summary: List assets through the Asset Registry, including mounted plugin roots. Filter by classPaths (including subclasses), classFilter, nameRegex and skeletonPath. includeMetadata adds animation skeleton and playLength in seconds from registry tags without loading assets. Cursor-paginated with totalMatched, hasMore and nextCursor; maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit.

read_properties.summary: Read asset properties with values. Blueprint paths resolve to the generated-class CDO (#568). propertyName accepts dotted/indexed paths into nested structs, array elements, and instanced subobjects (e.g. `Config.Traits[1].Params.Field`), and keyed paths that pick the one array element whose field equals a value (`Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Offset.Scale3D`, reported back as indexedPath and resolvedPropertyName); landing on an array of subobjects also lists each element's index+class (#527). expandDepth inlines the properties of subobjects OWNED by this asset, so a data asset's nested payload comes back in ONE call instead of a reference you have to chase (#755); references to OTHER assets are marked expandable rather than followed, unless expandExternal=true. Capped by maxExpandedObjects with expansionTruncated reported. Find an array element by field value in a data asset without reading the whole array, e.g. `Profiles[Id=Primary].Presentation.Mesh` reads exactly one matching element. A nested key such as `[Meta.Id=Foo]` also works; no match or several matches are refused with the count and sample values.

list_properties.summary: List reflected properties on any asset.

get_properties.summary: Read property values on any asset; the same read as read_properties with includeValues on by default. propertyName accepts dotted/indexed/keyed paths into nested structs, array elements, and instanced subobjects, so one leaf of one element reads without dumping the array: `Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Offset.Scale3D`. valueFormat='json' returns structured values. resolvedPropertyName reports the numeric path matched; indexedPath is also returned for keyed paths.

duplicate.summary: Duplicate any asset, including an Enhanced Input InputAction with independent copies of its instanced triggers, modifiers and PlayerMappableKeySettings. sourcePath and destinationPath name the assets; onConflict=error refuses an existing destination. Verify with gameplay(read_input_action). Rollback deletes the copy.

rename.summary: Rename asset: pass assetPath and newName, or sourcePath and destinationPath. World Partition levels are detected and their __ExternalActors__/__ExternalObjects__ packages migrate atomically alongside the .umap, source-side redirectors get fixed up, and the active editor world is swapped to blank if it matches the source (#409). Refuses if any package is dirty - save first. If a prior rename left externals orphaned at the old path, re-running reconciles them. Rollback descriptor is emitted even on partial failure so the inverse rename can recover. `force=true` lets the call merge into a destination with pre-existing externals (used by rollback). For batches of 3+ scene-referenced non-world assets use bulk_rename instead.

bulk_rename.summary: Batched rename using IAssetTools::RenameAssets. Each renames[] item is exactly one of {sourcePath, destinationPath (full package path with the asset name)}, {assetPath, newName} or {sourcePath, newPackagePath, newName}; an unknown or mixed key, or a destinationPath naming an existing folder, refuses the whole batch with invalidItems before anything moves (#1291). It runs as a single transaction with one redirector-fixup pass (matches Content Browser drag). Use this over looped rename for scene-referenced assets. World assets are rejected (status=rejected_world); use rename_asset which handles WP externals atomically (#409). The fix-up pass cannot see a referencer that is not loaded, so each renamed item reports redirectorLeft and the result carries redirectorsLeft/redirectorsRemoved plus redirectorPackages, which feeds straight into fixup_redirectors (#908). A batch that would leave another object of a multi-object package at the old path is refused with reason=package_objects_left_behind and splitPackages naming each one; nothing moves (#1137).

fixup_redirectors.summary: Clean up ObjectRedirectors left at the old paths after a move, bounded to exactly the packages you name. Preflights each redirector, its destination, and its hard AND soft referencers, then reports packagesToLoad/packagesToSave before touching anything; dryRun=true stops there. The real run loads only those referencers (a soft reference in an unloaded package is what the rename's own fix-up pass misses), rewrites them, saves them, RE-QUERIES the asset registry, and deletes a redirector only when nothing references it any more, reporting kept vs deleted per package with the referencers that survived. Naming a whole content root is refused unless allowProjectWide=true, so this can never turn into a project-wide resave. Protected mounts are refused outright. Runs unattended: it never calls the editor's interactive fix-up, so no 'No referencing assets found' message or Redirector Update Report modal can block it, and the result summarises fixed (redirectors whose referencers were all repointed), deleted, and noReferencers (#1266). dryRun is the way to preview; save=false repoints the referencers in memory without writing them and keeps every redirector they reference (#908). deleteRedirectors=false saves the repointed referencers and keeps the redirector stubs, reported as kept (#1828).

move.summary: Move asset: pass sourcePath and destinationPath. The same call as rename.

delete.summary: Delete asset. force defaults to false and is a REAL guard: the bridge asks the Asset Registry for referencers first and refuses with success=false, reason='has_referencers' and the full referencers list rather than destroying an asset other packages point at (#976). force=true takes the force-delete path, which also auto-closes open asset editors (#278). On a delete the editor attempted and could not finish, the reason is open_in_editor / has_referencers / in_memory_referenced / package_read_only / package_dirty / unknown, with referencers, inMemoryReferencers, packageReadOnly and packageDirty diagnostics (#601).

delete_batch.summary: Batch-delete assets. Per-path status is deleted | absent | protected | refused | failed, plus reason+referencers on refused and failed entries. A referenced asset is refused per entry with force=false and the rest of the batch still runs, so one guarded asset never hides behind a bare failed count (#976, #278). Result carries deleted/absent/refused/failed/protected/total.

create_data_asset.summary: Create UDataAsset instance of custom class. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix (UMyConfig and MyConfig both resolve), a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a loaded class name; a failed lookup lists the spellings tried and the closest matches (#823).

create_asset_by_class.summary: Create an asset of ANY concrete UObject class (not just UDataAsset) - physical-material subclasses, curves, settings objects. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix, a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a loaded class name (#823). Actors/components and specialized assets (Blueprint/Material) have dedicated actions (#726).

read_graph.summary: Read the NODE GRAPH of any EdGraph-backed asset: every graph in it, every node, and every node's pins with what each pin is connected to. Reflection cannot reach topology: UEdGraphNode declares its Pins array with no UPROPERTY, and UEdGraphPin is a plain class rather than a UObject, so no set_property, reflect_instance or find_object can read, break or make a connection (#1059). For the EdGraph types with no category of their own, CustomizableObject (Mutable) among them. A Blueprint, a PCG graph or a Material is REFUSED here and pointed at blueprint(read_graph) / blueprint(get_connections) / pcg(read_graph) / material(read_graph), which own those types and address them in their own terms. Each node reports name, path, class, title, position and comment; each pin reports name, pinId, direction, type, defaultValue and linkedTo[] naming the node and pin at the other end. Node settings themselves are read with reflection(action='reflect_instance') on the node path this returns, which already works; this reports what that cannot see. connectionCount is per graph and counts each wire once; nodesReported is how many nodes this call emitted, which maxNodes can cut below a graph's own nodeCount. A node reported with hasNoPins is broken: AllocateDefaultPins never ran for it, so it can never be wired and the editor cannot draw it. Each node also reports nodeGuid. To change the graph use connect_graph_pins, disconnect_graph_pins, add_graph_node and remove_graph_node, which go through the graph's own schema. An asset with no graph answers with an empty list and says so rather than failing.

connect_graph_pins.summary: Connect two pins in any EdGraph-backed asset with no category of its own, CustomizableObject (Mutable) among them, through the graph's own schema (TryCreateConnection), so the graph type's rules decide what is legal. A refusal returns the schema's own message with reason='schema_disallowed'. Address each end by node (nodeGuid, node path, name or unique title from read_graph) and pinId, which is the reliable form because pin names repeat on some node types; pin name plus direction also works. A pinId alone needs no node. brokenLinks lists any link the schema replaced. Rollback: disconnect_graph_pins. A Blueprint, Material or PCG graph is refused and pointed at its own category.

disconnect_graph_pins.summary: Break links in an EdGraph-backed asset through its schema. With a target pin, breaks that one link (BreakSinglePinLink); without one, breaks every link on the source pin (BreakPinLinks). Pins are addressed as in connect_graph_pins. A link that does not exist is reported with wasConnected=false and nothing changes. Rollback: connect_graph_pins when exactly one link was broken; otherwise brokenLinks names each one.

add_graph_node.summary: Add a node to an EdGraph-backed asset's graph through the schema's own node action, so its pins are allocated and it is parented to the graph. nodeClass is the class the action spawns (a CustomizableObjectNode class for Mutable, a SoundNode class for a SoundCue); actionName picks a menu entry by name ('category|name' also works) when several actions spawn the same class. When nothing matches, the error lists availableActions. spawnMode=direct constructs nodeClass itself (CreateNewGuid, PostPlacedNewNode, AllocateDefaultPins), and auto does that only for a schema that publishes no node actions. Returns nodeGuid, nodePath and every pin with its pinId. Rollback: remove_graph_node.

remove_graph_node.summary: Remove a node from an EdGraph-backed asset's graph: the schema breaks its links, then the node is destroyed. A node the graph type forbids deleting (a root or output node) is refused. brokenLinks names every link it had so they can be re-made. Rollback: add_graph_node with the same class and position when exactly one schema action spawns it (lossy: a fresh default node); otherwise rollbackPossible=false.

create_customizable_object.summary: Create a Mutable CustomizableObject through Mutable's own factory, so it holds its Source graph with the Base Object node and can be authored with add_graph_node and connect_graph_pins at once. An asset made with create_asset_by_class has no graph. Returns objectPath, graphName, rootNode (nodeGuid and pins with pinIds) and every graph node. onConflict=skip returns an existing CustomizableObject as existed; error refuses. Fails with 'Mutable plugin not available' when the plugin is off. Rollback: delete_asset.

compile_customizable_object.summary: Compile a Mutable CustomizableObject synchronously, without saving or gathering references, and report the outcome: state, compiled, and the LogMutable errors and warnings the compile wrote. A failed compile returns success=false with the first error. Fails with 'Mutable plugin not available' when the Mutable plugin is not enabled.

create_subobject.summary: Create a named subobject OWNED by an existing asset, inside that asset's package, and return its object path for later property writes. This is the missing half of editing a data asset whose payload is named subobjects referenced from a struct array: set_property, bulk_set_properties and append_array_elements can edit the entries, and this makes a new one. Component classes are accepted, unlike create_asset_by_class; Actors are refused because they are spawned into a level. className takes a /Script/Module.Class path, which is how you name a plugin class the Python `unreal` module never exposes. The new object is created RF_Standalone and the package is saved in the same call, so it survives the garbage collection that used to eat a fresh object within one call and is reachable by path from the next one. properties are applied to a throwaway instance first, so a bad path or value creates nothing. outer='asset' (default) gives '<asset>.<name>'; outer='package' puts it beside the asset in the package (#975).

bulk_upsert_data_assets.summary: Create or update up to 500 UDataAsset instances in ONE call. Every descriptor is first applied to a transient copy, so a bad class, property path, or value rejects the whole batch before a package is touched; nothing is half-written by a typo. Per-item status is created | updated | unchanged | skipped | failed (dryRun reports wouldCreate | wouldUpdate | wouldRemainUnchanged | wouldSkip), each with its own error when it failed. Replaying the same request returns unchanged, and only changed packages are saved. Emits a rollback descriptor that restores prior values and deletes what it created.

save.summary: Save one asset, exactly the packages named by assetPaths, or every dirty asset under /Game when both are omitted. assetPaths resolves each asset, object or package path to its loaded package (naming a World Partition actor names its external package), refuses the whole call before writing anything if one names nothing in memory, and reports each package as saved, notDirty or failed with a reason; no other package is written. The save-everything form refuses a call carrying any key it does not take, so a misspelt selector cannot widen it. force=true saves regardless of the dirty flag - several edits (OFPA level actors, some subsystem property writes) never mark their package dirty, so a dirty-only save skipped them and still reported success. Returns the package name plus on-disk file path, size and mtime so the write can be verified rather than trusted (#768). A failed save returns the engine's reason in error and saveDiagnostics, and when the engine refused a reference to a private object, illegalReference names that object, the object and property holding it, and how to clear it (#1120).

save_all_dirty.summary: Flush every dirty package to disk in one call. Reports the packages it attempted, which ones reached disk (with file path, size and mtime) and which are still dirty afterwards, because a bare savedAll boolean has come back true while packages were never written (#768).

read_mesh_materials.summary: Read every mesh material slot, effective shading properties through instance overrides, parent chain, LOD section-to-slot mappings and Nanite state. Read-only.

set_mesh_material.summary: Assign material to static mesh slot.

set_mesh_materials_batch.summary: Assign materials across many meshes and slots in one call, so an N mesh x M slot kit costs one round trip instead of N*M. StaticMesh and SkeletalMesh both work. Address a slot by slotName (survives a reimport reordering slot indices) or by slotIndex (default 0); passing both is rejected when they disagree. Every submitted assignment returns its own index/ok/status/error, status being ok|updated|unchanged|invalid|protected|duplicate|not_found|slot_not_found|failed|skipped. Default is all-or-nothing: any preflight rejection aborts before a mesh is touched. Pass continueOnError to apply the assignments that did pass and keep the rejects reported alongside them. Each mesh is written and saved once no matter how many of its slots the batch names, and the rollback payload restores only the writes that landed (#822).

recenter_pivot.summary: Move static mesh pivot to geometry center. With assetPaths, the first mesh sets the reference pivot for all of them.

import_static_mesh.summary: Import from FBX, OBJ, or GLB/glTF (glTF routes through Interchange) (#549). importUniformScale=100 fixes metre-authored FBX (#687).

import_skeletal_mesh.summary: Import skeletal meshes with scale, replacement, target skeleton or a new skeleton, and optional material/texture import. importer=interchange supplies an explicit pipeline stack so UE 5.8 applies the settings; auto selects it on 5.8 and later. Legacy uses FbxImportUI. dryRun validates first; save defaults false. Returns importedAssets, meshes with bounds, material slots, skeleton and sockets, plus boxExtent, morphTargets and numLODs. Import changes may require backup restoration.

import_animation.summary: Import anim from FBX. importSettings sets any FbxAnimSequenceImportData or FbxImportUI field by UPROPERTY name or dotted path, e.g. {bSnapToClosestFrameBoundary: true} for clips whose length is not frame-aligned; a bool may drop its b prefix. An unknown key fails before anything is imported (#1134). filePaths imports a batch of FBX files into one folder with the same settings, one row per file under files. animations reads back each imported AnimSequence: path, playLength, numberOfFrames, numberOfKeys, frameRate, boneTrackCount, curveCount, enableRootMotion, and hasRootMotion with rootTravel from the root bone track (#1228).

import_file.summary: Import any source file through a chosen factory, unattended. factoryClass names a UFactory subclass by name or /Script path, including one a plugin ships (resolved at runtime; omit it to let the editor pick by extension). factoryProperties sets that factory's properties by UPROPERTY name or dotted path before the import runs, which is how a factory that raises its own options dialog is told to use the supplied options instead, since unattended mode cancels the dialog and the import with it. The file extension is checked against the factory's formats first. An unknown property fails before anything is imported (#1096). Imported assets are saved by default and imported[] reports saved, saveError or dirtyNotSaved per asset; save=false leaves them dirty (#1280). A .csv imports into a DataTable with rowStruct (or the row struct of a DataTable already at the destination) and the dialog's ignoreExtraFields, ignoreMissingFields and importKeyField, never raising the DataTable Options dialog; an unattended .csv import with no row type is refused, and the importer's problems are returned as problems.

import_font.summary: Import a .ttf/.otf (or .ttc/.otc collection) as a FontFace asset, with no import dialog. hinting and loadingPolicy set the face's own options; createFont=true also makes <name>_Font, a runtime Font whose Default typeface is this face. Returns path and the subFaces the file holds. onConflict: skip (default) | error | replace (reimport the bytes) (#1377).

create_font.summary: Create a runtime Font (composite font) whose default typeface has one entry per FontFace: fontFaces[] are FontFace asset paths and typefaceNames[] their entry names in the same order (Regular, Bold, Italic). This is the FTypefaceEntry/FFontData write Python cannot make. onConflict=update rewrites an existing font's default typeface and reports previousTypefaces (#1377).

import_texture.summary: Import image. sRGB/compressionSettings/lodGroup/neverStream are applied at import time (folded in, no second call needed) (#661).

create_render_target_2d.summary: Create and persist a TextureRenderTarget2D asset. Render format is applied before resource initialization.

generate_skeletal_mesh_lods.summary: Generate auto-reduced LODs on one SkeletalMesh, a list, or every SkeletalMesh in a folder, through the engine's RegenerateLOD (#1372). lodCount counts LOD 0; trianglePercentages gives each later LOD its triangle percentage of LOD 0, otherwise the engine's reduction settings apply. Idempotent: a mesh already at lodCount is skipped unless skipExisting=false, and a mesh with more LODs is never trimmed. Imported LODs are kept unless regenerateImported=true. dryRun reports without changing anything. Each mesh row lists every LOD with triangles, vertices, generated and trianglePercentage.

read_skeletal_mesh_build_settings.summary: Read a SkeletalMesh's per-LOD FSkeletalMeshBuildSettings without changing anything. lodIndex and allLods are mutually exclusive. Returns assetPath, lodCount and lods[] of {lodIndex, beforeBuildSettings, afterBuildSettings (identical on a read), beforeOptimizeForInstancing, afterOptimizeForInstancing, changed}, where each settings object carries bRecomputeNormals, bRecomputeTangents, bUseMikkTSpace, bComputeWeightedNormals, bRemoveDegenerates, bUseHighPrecisionTangentBasis, bUseHighPrecisionSkinWeights, bUseFullPrecisionUVs, bUseBackwardsCompatibleF16TruncUVs, bOptimizeForInstancing, thresholdPosition, thresholdTangentNormal, thresholdUV, morphThresholdPosition and boneInfluenceLimit.

set_skeletal_mesh_optimize_for_instancin.summary: Write bOptimizeForInstancing on a SkeletalMesh's LOD build settings, which reorders the skin data so instanced draws of the mesh batch. Only LODs whose current value differs are touched, and the asset is only rebuilt and saved when at least one changes, so a call that asks for the value already set is a no-op. Read the current state with read_skeletal_mesh_build_settings first. lodIndex and allLods are mutually exclusive. Returns assetPath, lodCount and lods[] of {lodIndex, beforeBuildSettings, afterBuildSettings, beforeOptimizeForInstancing, afterOptimizeForInstancing, changed}.

get_static_mesh_build_settings.summary: Read a StaticMesh source model's FMeshBuildSettings (bRecomputeNormals, bRecomputeTangents, bUseMikkTSpace, bRemoveDegenerates, bGenerateLightmapUVs, BuildScale3D and every other field) by its engine property name. lodIndex picks the source model (default 0). Returns settings and sourceModelCount.

set_static_mesh_build_settings.summary: Write FMeshBuildSettings fields on a StaticMesh source model, then rebuild and save it. settings is keyed by engine property name, e.g. {bRecomputeNormals: true}; an unknown name or wrong type refuses the whole call before anything changes. A call that changes nothing skips the rebuild. Returns previous and settings, and rolls back to the previous values. BuildScale3D scales only the render vertices: the editor keeps taking bounds from the unscaled source geometry, so a non-unit BuildScale3D also returns bounds, renderBounds, boundsMatchRender and a warning. To resize a mesh use scale_mesh_geometry.

scale_mesh_geometry.summary: Bake a scale into a StaticMesh's geometry: every source LOD and the hi-res source are transformed (normals and tangents corrected), then render data and bounds are rebuilt, so get_mesh_bounds, actor bounds and the rendered size all follow. factor is a number or {x, y, z}, every component above 0; pivot is the mesh-space point that stays fixed (default origin). Sockets and simple collision move with the geometry unless scaleSockets or scaleCollision is false; a rotated box, sphere or capsule under a non-uniform scale is fitted and counted in collision.approximated. outputPath scales a copy and leaves assetPath untouched. Returns previousBounds, bounds, lods[], socketsScaled and collision. In place, rolls back with the inverse scale; with outputPath, by deleting the copy.

read_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights.summary: Read existing per-vertex skin influences from one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile. The caller must name 1-256 source MeshDescription vertex IDs, so a read cannot dump a whole mesh. Each influence returns boneName, boneIndex, normalized weight and exact uint16 rawWeight. Render data may use 8-bit weights unless high-precision skin weights are enabled. Generated LODs without source geometry are refused.

read_skeletal_mesh_bone_vertex_bounds.summary: Measure where each bone's skinned vertices sit on one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile, so physics bodies, sockets and hit volumes can be sized from the mesh instead of guessed. By default each source vertex counts once, for its dominant bone; minWeight counts it for every bone weighing at least that much. boneNames limits the report to those bones (a named bone with no vertices comes back with vertexCount 0); omitted, every bone that owns a vertex is listed. Each bone returns boneName, boneIndex, parentName, vertexCount, bindPose (its component-space reference transform), componentSpace {min, max, center, extent} in the bind pose and boneSpace {min, max, center, extent} in the bone's own bind-pose frame, the frame a physics body on that bone uses. Also returns vertexCount, unweightedVertexCount and, with minWeight, belowThresholdVertexCount. Read-only.

read_skeletal_mesh_vertices.summary: Read source vertices of one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile in bulk, to analyse a part before moving or reweighting it. Select with boneNames (vertices weighted to any of those bones, includeChildBones adds the bones below them, minWeight sets the least summed weight on them), box {min, max} in the component-space bind pose, both, or neither for every vertex. include picks positions, weights and triangles (default positions and weights). Each vertex returns vertexIndex (the source ID read_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights and set_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights take), position, influences [{boneName, boneIndex, weight}] and, with boneNames, selectedWeight. triangles lists each triangle whose three corners are selected, with triangleIndex, vertexIndices and polygonGroup, once across pages. Pages with offset and limit (default 2000, at most 20000) and returns hasMore and nextOffset; dumpToFile writes the whole selection to outputPath (default under Saved/UE_MCP/SkeletalMeshVertices) and returns only the summary. Always returns vertexCount, selectedVertexCount and selectedBounds. Read-only.

set_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights.summary: Replace skin influences on explicitly selected source MeshDescription vertices in one existing SkeletalMesh LOD/profile. The complete batch is validated before mutation: invalid or duplicate vertices/bones, non-finite/negative/out-of-range weights and all-zero sets fail without a write. Unreal's FBoneWeights normalizes, quantizes to uint16 source weights and prunes ordinary edits to its influence limit; actual before/after values are read back. Other source vertices and source profiles are untouched. Rebuilding may refresh derived render data and dependent generated LODs. A changed mesh is rebuilt and saved; an identical request is a no-op. Rollback payloads use restoreRawWeights with exact uint16 rawWeight values.

transform_skinned_part.summary: Move one rigid part of a SkeletalMesh with its bone: the bone's reference pose and every source vertex skinned to it or to a bone below it, in every LOD, by translation and/or rotation about the bone's origin. space picks the axes: bone (its bind-pose frame, default) or component. A vertex moves by its weight on those bones. Every LOD is read and checked before anything is written, so the edit is all-or-nothing: a LOD without source geometry that is not generated, bones that differ from the reference skeleton, or no LOD 0 vertex on the part refuse the call. A LOD with no vertex on the part is reported with verticesMoved 0, not refused. Vertices move in place in each LOD's source geometry, so hard edges and imported normals are kept (turned with the part on a rotation) whatever the LOD's recompute settings; generated LODs follow their base LOD. Returns per LOD verticesMoved, fullyWeighted, partiallyWeighted, and after the rebuild renderVerticesMoved, maxRenderPositionErrorCm and maxRenderNormalChangeDegrees against where the move should put each drawn vertex. dryRun reports the same plan without writing. Rolls back with the inverse move when every moved vertex moved rigidly.

read_cloth_data.summary: Read Chaos cloth data on a skeletal mesh: per clothing asset, its configs (reflected properties), LOD count, and per-LOD point-weight-map summary (name, target, vertex count, min/max - including the MaxDistances mask). Also reports which render sections each clothing asset is bound to (boundSections, bound), every section of every LOD (sections: lodIndex, sectionIndex, materialIndex, usesCloth, clothingAsset, assetLodIndex) and unboundClothingAssets: an asset bound to no section never simulates (#595/#1139).

bind_cloth_to_section.summary: Bind a clothing asset to one render section so it simulates, as the skeletal mesh editor's section clothing dropdown does. Whatever the section was bound to is unbound first. lodIndex and sectionIndex are validated against the mesh, assetLodIndex against the clothing asset. Saves the mesh; rolls back to the previous binding (#1139).

unbind_cloth_from_section.summary: Remove the clothing asset bound to one render section. The engine unbinds per LOD, so other sections of that LOD bound to the same asset are released too and listed in releasedSections. A section with no binding is a no-op. Saves the mesh; rolls back by rebinding (#1139).

set_cloth_config.summary: Set properties on a clothing asset's Chaos cloth config via reflection (#595).

export_texture.summary: Export a Texture2D to a PNG on disk (for inspection or external diffing) (#697). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger.

compare_textures.summary: Compare two Texture2D assets by dimensions, pixel format, and source-content identity (FTextureSource id) - tells you whether an authored texture actually changed without offline pixel-diffing (#697).

import_texture_batch.summary: Batch import PNGs and other images with per-file preset=normal|masks|color and settings. Normal maps use linear Normalmap compression without green flip; packed masks use linear Masks; color uses sRGB. Per-file lodGroup, maxTextureSize, compressionSettings, sRGB, neverStream and flipGreenChannel override presets. All entries preflight before import; dryRun writes nothing. Saves after applying settings and returns per-item importedAssets, readBack and saved. Rollback deletes new textures only; replaced pixels require a backup.

reimport.summary: Reimport an imported asset from its source file, or from filePath, which is recorded as its new source. A texture keeps its settings: compression, LOD group, sRGB, NeverStream, max size, mip generation, filter and addressing are read before the reimport and any the reimport changed are put back (preserveSettings=false skips that). For a texture the response carries settingsBefore, settingsAfter, restoredSettings (what the reimport changed and was undone) and sourceSizeBefore/sourceSizeAfter, the source pixel dimensions. The package is left dirty and unsaved unless save=true; packageDirty reports it.

read_datatable.summary: Read DataTable rows as structured JSON (struct fields come back as objects). rowNames returns exactly the named rows in the order given, matched like FindRow (case-insensitive), and lists names the table lacks in missingRowNames instead of failing; rowFilter is a substring match instead. columns narrows each row to its Name and the named top-level row-struct fields, which is how one field is read across every row of a wide table; an unknown name is refused with the row struct's field list, and the response echoes the resolved columns. A large table overflows the response inline: pass outputPath to write the rows (after rowNames, rowFilter and columns) to a file as a JSON array instead. The response then carries outputPath (resolved absolute path), rowCount, bytes, rowStruct and totalRowCount, with no rows or rowNames. A relative outputPath resolves under the project's Saved/, missing folders are created and an existing file is overwritten.

create_datatable.summary: Create DataTable. With csvString or a .csv filePath it is filled from that CSV by the engine's CSV importer, with the DataTable Options dialog's ignoreExtraFields, ignoreMissingFields and importKeyField, and no dialog; the importer's problems are returned as problems.

reimport_datatable.summary: Replace a DataTable's rows from JSON (jsonString, jsonPath) or CSV (csvString, a .csv filePath). CSV goes through the engine's CSV importer with the DataTable Options dialog's ignoreExtraFields, ignoreMissingFields and importKeyField, set on the table as the dialog sets them, and never raises the dialog. The importer's problems are returned as problems and fail the call.

clone_datatable_rows.summary: Clone DataTable rows in one call: clones=[{sourceRow, rowName, overrides?}]. Copies native row memory before applying nested or dotted struct overrides, preserving omitted fields and references. All source rows must exist and all destination names must be unused; the full batch is validated before mutation. dryRun returns proposedRows; writes return rows with fields read back, clonedCount, rowCount, saved and persisted. Uses one editor undo transaction; rollback removes the cloned rows with the same save policy and is marked lossy because row change hook side effects cannot be reversed.

set_datatable_row.summary: Append or overwrite a single DataTable row. row carries row-struct fields, and a partial update merges with the existing row. Idempotent; rollback restores the prior row (#437).

update_datatable_row.summary: Alias for set_datatable_row; partial update merges with existing row (#437).

remove_datatable_row.summary: Remove a DataTable row with rowName, or several with rowNames in one transaction. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when all selected rows are absent. save defaults to true; save=false keeps removal in memory, including clone_datatable_rows rollback. Batch or unsaved removal uses editor undo to restore row values; the original single saved removal returns its set_datatable_row inverse.

get_datatable_row.summary: Read one DataTable row's fields without dumping the whole table (#535).

set_datatable_cell.summary: Write a single field on a single existing row (merges, leaves other cells untouched). Errors if the row doesn't exist (#535).

set_datatable_cells.summary: Write many cells across many existing rows in one call, such as relabelling one column on every row. Every cell is validated first (the row exists, the column is a top-level field, the value parses as set_datatable_cell parses it); if any fails, nothing is written and errors[] lists each failing cell. The rest apply in one undo transaction with one Modify/PostEditChange, then every row is re-exported and compared with the export taken before: touched rows may differ only in the requested fields and every other row must be identical, or the write is rolled back and the offending row and field named. Reports changedCells, unchangedCells (already equal), rowsTouched and verified. dryRun validates and reports without writing; save defaults to false; rollback restores the prior values.

rename_datatable_row.summary: Rename a row key, preserving its values (#535).

fill_datatable_from_json.summary: Bulk-upsert rows from a {rowName: {field: value}} object without touching unrelated rows (non-destructive, unlike reimport_datatable) (#535).

import_curvetable.summary: Import CurveTable from JSON/CSV string or file.

remove_curvetable_row.summary: Remove CurveTable row. Idempotent if missing.

get_curvetable_keys.summary: Read keys from one CurveTable row.

set_curvetable_keys.summary: Replace keys on one CurveTable row.

add_curvetable_key.summary: Add or update one key on a CurveTable row.

set_curve_keys.summary: Replace the keys of one channel of a CurveFloat, CurveVector or CurveLinearColor asset. pick it with channel (an index) or channelName (Value, X/Y/Z or R/G/B/A); keys carry time, value and optional interpMode, tangentMode, tangent and tangent weight fields; [] clears the channel. The other channels are left alone. Returns the stored keys and an exact rollback (#1687).

list_textures.summary: List textures, cursor-paginated. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit.

get_texture_info.summary: Read one texture or many via assetPaths: dimensions, MaxTextureSize (maxTextureSize), compressionSettings, lodGroup, sRGB, neverStream, flipGreenChannel, mip count and pixel format.

set_texture_settings.summary: Set one texture or many via assetPaths, with preset=normal|masks|color and explicit settings. Supports MaxTextureSize (maxTextureSize), compressionSettings including Masks, lodGroup, sRGB, neverStream and flipGreenChannel. Validates every texture before mutation; dryRun previews, save defaults false. Returns previousSettings and readBack per texture, saved, and a rollback restoring the previous settings.

read_stringtable.summary: Read StringTable entries and keys: each entry's key, sourceString and metadata ({id: value}).

get_stringtable_entry.summary: Read one StringTable entry: its sourceString and metadata ({id: value}).

set_stringtable_entry.summary: Create or update one StringTable entry. Pass sourceString, or value as a second spelling of it.

remove_stringtable_entry.summary: Remove one StringTable entry. Idempotent (alreadyDeleted=true if missing).

set_stringtable_entry_metadata.summary: Set one metadata value (metaDataId, e.g. Comment, to metaDataValue) on an existing StringTable entry. The same value again reports unchanged; the rollback restores the previous value or removes a new one.

remove_stringtable_entry_metadata.summary: Remove one metadata value from a StringTable entry. Removing one that is not there reports alreadyRemoved; the rollback sets it back.

get_text_localization.summary: Read how a Text property is localized: its text, sourceString, namespace (without the package marker), packageNamespace, key, or the stringTableId and stringTableKey it references, plus isCultureInvariant and isLocalizable. propertyName may dot through structs; widgetName picks a widget in a Widget Blueprint's tree, and a Blueprint asset means its class defaults.

set_text_localization.summary: Set a Text property's namespace, key and/or source string (each defaults to its current value; the package namespace is kept, as the details panel does), or point it at a string table entry with stringTableId (asset path or id) and stringTableKey. Same addressing as get_text_localization. A Widget Blueprint is compiled; the asset is saved. The rollback restores the previous namespace, key and source, or string table reference.

import_stringtable_csv.summary: Import or refresh a String Table from a CSV that is the canonical source, using Unreal's own String Table CSV importer. The CSV is parsed into a throwaway table and checked against expectedKeys FIRST, so a malformed file or a key set that does not match leaves the asset untouched and comes back with missingKeys/unexpectedKeys instead. replaceExisting=true prunes entries the CSV no longer carries, which is what makes the CSV canonical rather than additive; the prune runs after a successful merge so a bad parse can never empty the table. Returns addedKeys, updatedKeys, removedKeys, entry counts and an explicit persisted/saved plus persistError, so a write that did not reach disk is never reported as a success. A relative csvPath is read against the project directory (#978).

add_input_mapping.summary: Append an Enhanced Input key mapping to an InputMappingContext (InputAction + key by name string e.g. 'Mouse2D','LeftMouseButton'). Idempotent on (action,key). For modifiers/triggers use gameplay(set_mapping_modifiers). Same as gameplay(add_imc_mapping) (#525). Returns saved, persisted, packageDirty, packageName, and persistError when not persisted.

remove_input_mapping.summary: Remove an IMC key mapping. Same as gameplay(remove_imc_mapping) (#525). Returns saved, persisted, packageDirty, packageName, and persistError when not persisted.

list_input_mappings.summary: List an IMC's key->action bindings with triggers/modifiers, each with its class and property values (Negate X/Y/Z, SwizzleAxis Order). Same as gameplay(read_imc) (#525).

add_socket.summary: Add socket to StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh. SkeletalMesh writes mesh-local sockets by default; pass a Skeleton asset path to edit skeleton-level sockets. Idempotent on socket name; pass onConflict='update' to overwrite an existing socket's transform with the supplied relativeLocation/relativeRotation/relativeScale (#412).

list_sockets.summary: List sockets on a mesh (StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh). SkeletalMesh results include mesh-local sockets plus assigned Skeleton sockets, each with source='mesh' or source='skeleton'. Every skeletal socket also carries componentTransform {location, rotation, scale}: its transform in component space at the reference pose (the SkeletalMesh's pose for a mesh, including its Skeleton's sockets; the Skeleton's own for a Skeleton asset, named in componentTransformPose), so no actor is needed to see where a socket sits. A socket whose bone is missing from that skeleton returns componentTransformError instead.

set_socket_transform.summary: Update an existing socket's relative transform on StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh. Pass any subset of relativeLocation/relativeRotation/relativeScale; omitted fields stay at their current values. Errors if the socket does not exist (use add_socket to create). Common after FBX import when SOCKET_* empties land with scale=(100,100,100) (#412).

set_property.summary: Assign a different skeleton to an existing SkeletalMesh with propertyName=Skeleton and value set to the skeleton object path; save controls persistence. Use edit_collection_entry to clone a keyed array element or patch one TMap entry. Set a UPROPERTY on any loaded asset (Material, DataAsset, DataTable, SubsurfaceProfile, etc.) using a dotted path. Blueprint paths resolve to the generated-class CDO so you can author its defaults + Instanced sub-object arrays (#568). Walks nested structs, array elements by index (`Rules[1]`) or by key (`Rules[Id=Axe]`: exactly one element's Id must equal Axe, else the error lists the ids), and instanced subobjects internally - no more read-modify-write copies (e.g. `settings.mean_free_path_distance` on a UMaterial, or `Config.Traits[1].Params.Field` on a config asset #527). Value goes through MCPJsonProperty::SetJsonOnProperty so JSON null clears object refs, structs accept {x,y,z}, arrays/maps round-trip. TMap values take { "Key": value } or, for struct keys, [{ key: {...}, value: ... }]; a write that cannot store every entry fails and leaves the old value untouched (#820). The write is saved to the package by default and the result reports persisted plus the package name; a write that could not reach disk (save=false, a protected mount, a read-only file, a refused save) comes back with persisted=false and persistError naming the reason instead of a bare success that reverts on the next editor start (#931) (#420). With save=false, nested array field writes stay in memory, leave the package dirty, and support editor undo; rollback restores the old value with the same save option. An Instanced or EditInlineNew object property takes {instanceClass, properties}: a new subobject of that class is created with the owning object as its outer and its fields set from properties, e.g. RootMotionModifier = {instanceClass: "RootMotionModifier_Scale", properties: {Scale: {x:0,y:0,z:0}}} (#1292). An array of structs is written whole or per element (PropTypes[1].Modes = [{Key, DisplayName, bInCycle}, ...]); struct members match by C++ name, display name, or the Python spelling (display_name, in_cycle) (#1370). For example, `Profiles[Id=Primary].Presentation.Mesh` sets a field on the array element whose Id equals Primary. resolvedPropertyName and the rollback carry the numeric index matched, even when the write changes the key itself. A nested key such as `[Meta.Id=Foo]` also works.

edit_collection_entry.summary: Update or clone one struct array element or TMap entry on a data asset, selected by entryKey. Arrays also need keyField (for example WeaponId); maps use their actual reflected key type. newKey clones to an unused key, while omitting it patches the existing entry. overrides accepts nested objects and dotted struct fields, preserving omitted fields. Validates before mutation; duplicate or missing keys fail. dryRun returns proposedValue; writes return value read back, count, saved and persisted.
