Rollback restores the whole collection, so replay before further collection edits. Instanced subobject cloning is refused.

append_array_elements.summary: Append one or more JSON values to a reflected TArray without replacing existing entries. Supports dotted property paths plus native and user-defined USTRUCT elements. All elements are validated before mutation; returns appended indices and rollback data. The append is saved to the package by default and reports persisted / persistError the same way set_property does (#931); rollback preserves the same save option, so an unsaved append can be restored without writing to disk. Keyed paths such as `Profiles[Id=Foo].Items` select one nested array; resolvedPropertyName and the rollback use its numeric path. unique=true skips a value the array already holds (or an earlier element of the batch adds), compared the way the property type compares, and reports skippedElements; when every value is present nothing is written or saved (#1659). The response carries value, the array read back.

remove_array_elements.summary: Remove elements from a reflected TArray by indices (each must exist) or by elements (every entry matching one of the values goes), keeping the order of the rest. Supports dotted and keyed property paths. Validates before mutation; returns removedIndices, previousValue and value read back, saves by default with persisted / persistError like set_property, and a rollback that restores the whole array with the same save option. A value that matches nothing removes nothing and writes nothing (#1659).

bulk_set_properties.summary: Set dotted UPROPERTY paths (indexed `Rules[1].X` or keyed `Rules[Id=Axe].X`, keys matched once in preflight) on as many as 500 assets in one preflighted batch. Every asset, path, and value is validated before anything is mutated, and every submitted item comes back with its own ok/status/error, so a bad path in item 300 never hides the other 499 verdicts. Default is all-or-nothing: any preflight rejection aborts before a single UObject is touched. Pass continueOnError to apply the items that did pass and keep the rejects reported alongside them. Returns per-property readback, aggregate counts, targeted save results, and a replayable rollback payload covering only the writes that landed. Each property readback reports resolvedPropertyName; apply and rollback use the numeric path matched during preflight.

bulk_read_properties.summary: Read the SAME properties off many assets in one call, filtered and aggregated in the editor. read_properties answers one asset per call, which turns a library-wide question (concurrency settings across 582 sound assets, cull distances across 201 foliage types) into a loop. Select with assetPaths or with directory narrowed by classNames; propertyNames accepts dotted paths into nested structs (e.g. 'CullDistance.Max') and array elements by index or by field value (e.g. 'Profiles[Id=Foo].Mesh'; each row's resolvedPropertyNames gives the index matched and missingReasons says why a selector matched no element or several), and a Blueprint path reads its generated-class CDO. Predicates, groupBy and countBy all evaluate here: filtering happens before anything crosses the wire, with the same operators as level(query_components). Absent and null are reported separately, because 'this class has no such property' and 'this property is unset' are different findings; suspect is true for either, and suspectOnly returns just those rows. Never writes, and reports dirtiedPackages (#909).

set_texture_settings_by_type.summary: Apply the canonical (compressionSettings, sRGB, LOD group) combo to every texture in each group: normal -> Normalmap, grayscale -> Grayscale, baseColor -> Default sRGB, hdr -> HDR (#421).

create_interchange_pipeline.summary: One-call factory for a UInterchangeGenericAssetsPipeline asset with the 15-property mesh-import boilerplate already applied (RecomputeNormals=false, MikkTSpace=true, HighPrecisionTangents=true, BuildNanite=false, CreatePhysicsAsset=false, etc.) (#421).

reload_package.summary: Force reload an asset package from disk.

health_check.summary: Diagnose stuck-unloadable asset. Returns onDisk/inRegistry/isLoaded/canLoad/isStuck flags so an agent can detect the half-shutdown state where load returns null but the file exists (#279).

force_reload.summary: Aggressive reload from disk: closes open editors, reloads the package (rebuilding a Blueprint's class and CDO so container properties come back fresh, not just scalars), and reports objectReplaced. Refuses a dirty package unless discardUnsaved=true, and fails loudly when the editor would not release the old object rather than serving stale values (#279/#820). assetPaths reloads up to 500 assets in one pass, so a material and its instances are re-read together; the whole set is validated first (a missing or unsaved package refuses the call before anything is released) and each asset reports under results (#1645).

export.summary: Export static or skeletal meshes to FBX, Texture2D to PNG, or MaterialInstance parameters to JSON for a DCC round-trip. Material JSON includes parent lineage, scalar/vector/texture overrides and resolved parameter values. DataTable and CompositeDataTable require .json or .csv; format overrides their serializer. Relative outputPath resolves against the project directory; missing folders are created. replaceExisting defaults true; dryRun writes no file. Returns outputPath, assetClass, bytes, and material readBack or table rowCount. Overwritten files require a backup.

search_fts.summary: Ranked asset search (token-scored over name/class/path). Every match is scored and the ranked list is paged, so the top page is a page rather than the whole answer. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit.

reindex_fts.summary: Rescan a content path so newly added assets on disk become searchable by search_fts.

quick_search.summary: Keystroke-speed ranked search over assets, actors in the open level, and files under Source/ and Config/. Every word must match a name, class or path token (exact, prefix, substring, or the letters of the name in order). A leading BP_, M_, DT_ (any short prefix ending in _) keeps names with that prefix; actor:, asset: or file: keeps one kind. Each row has kind, path, name, class, a one-line summary and score; assets also carry objectPath. Assets come from an in-memory index kept current by Asset Registry add, rename and delete events, so no reindex is needed. Returns totalMatched, matchedByKind, indexedAssets, scannedActors, indexedFiles and elapsedMs; paged with cursor and limit.

semantic_search.summary: Natural-language asset search through Epic's Semantic Search plugin (UE 5.8+, experimental, off by default): the query is embedded by the configured provider (Loci or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and matched against the plugin's hybrid vector and keyword index. Returns results ranked by score, each with objectPath, name, class, vectorDistance and keywordScore. directory narrows to one folder; maxDistance overrides the plugin's VectorDistanceCutoff. Refuses with semantic_search_provider_not_configured, naming what is missing, when no provider can answer; check semantic_search_status first.

semantic_search_status.summary: Report whether Epic's Semantic Search can answer: pluginLoaded, provider and providerConfigured (with providerNote saying what is missing), providerRegistered, embeddingDimension, initialized, indexingInProgress, indexedPaths, and index stats (vectorCount, keywordCount, supportedAssetCount, failedCount, indexing). available=false with errorCode and reason when it cannot. Never errors.

semantic_search_index.summary: Queue assets for Semantic Search's index: assetPaths (object or package paths) indexes those, otherwise every asset in the plugin's indexed folders, and force=true clears the index and rebuilds every embedding. Returns at once with started, queuedAssetCount and the index stats; indexing runs in the background (watch semantic_search_status). Requires a configured provider, like semantic_search.

get_referencers.summary: Batch reverse dependency lookup for packages (or one packagePath). includeDetails follows Blueprint referencers up to maxDepth and reports maps, external actor packages, Blueprint paths and one shortest route per package. includeMeshInfo adds bounds, material slots, skeleton, sockets and static mesh collision setup. Returns referencersByPackage and detailsByPackage. Uses saved registry references; runtime-only and unsaved references are outside its scope.

get_dependencies.summary: Forward dependency lookup (what packages this asset references) (#588). Returns {dependenciesByPackage, totalDependencies}.

list_skeleton_bones.summary: List bones (names + rest-pose local and component-space transforms) from a SkeletalMesh or Skeleton asset, no live actor needed (#593). Returns {bones, boneCount, sourceKind, scaleSummary}. scaleSummary covers every bone whatever the page: bonesWithNonUnitLocalScale, min/maxComponentScale, rootScale and up to 32 scaledBones. limit pages the bones and offset starts the page; nextOffset is set while more remain. includeBones=false returns the summary alone (#1201).

get_primary_asset_ids.summary: Enumerate AssetManager-registered FPrimaryAssetIds (verify a primary-asset registration) (#579). Returns {primaryAssetIds:[{primaryAssetId, type, name, assetPath}], count, total}.

set_sk_material_slots.summary: Set materials on a USkeletalMesh by slot name or slotIndex (bypasses the blueprint override-materials path that UE's ICH silently reverts).

diagnose_registry.summary: Scan a content path and compare disk vs AssetRegistry (including in-memory pending-kill entries). Returns onDiskCount, inMemoryIncludedCount, ghostCount and paths.

get_mesh_bounds.summary: Get StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh bounding box. Returns min, max, boxExtent, boxCenter, meshKind (#193/#351).

get_mesh_info.summary: One-call static or skeletal mesh summary: boundsOrigin, boundsExtent, materialSlots (index, slotName, materialPath, isDefaultFallback), sockets (mesh and skeleton sockets), socketCount, skeletonPath, LOD/vertex counts and heightM.

read_import_sources.summary: Read AssetImportData source filenames on an imported asset (StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture, Animation, etc.). Returns sources[] of {relativeFilename, absolutePath, timestamp, fileHash, displayLabelName} (#270).

get_mesh_collision.summary: Inspect StaticMesh collision setup. Returns collisionTraceFlag, hasSimple/ComplexCollision, element counts, the boxes, spheres and capsules as shapes[] in the form set_mesh_simple_collision takes, and bodySetupGuid, the GUID a SplineMeshComponent compares to decide its collision copy is stale (#177).

get_static_mesh_geometry.summary: Capture immutable StaticMesh geometry from an explicit sourceModel or renderData LOD. Page vertices, corners and oriented triangles with all UV channels, normals, tangents, binormal signs, RGBA and material groups; loose vertices and corners are retained. Source data is unbuilt; Nanite render data is its fallback LOD, never cluster geometry. First call returns snapshotId and contentRevision; reuse snapshotId for every table/page. Cached pages describe capturedUtc, not current asset state; omit the ID at offset 0 for a fresh capture after edits. No silent recapture on expiry. Maximum 512 elements per page, 128 MiB per capture, 4 captures/256 MiB cached, 300 seconds idle lifetime. Includes capture-time build, Nanite, collision and material metadata. dumpToFile streams the complete snapshot in one call to a new JSON file (1 GiB export cap), returning only a receipt; outputPath follows the Saved/ dump convention and existing destinations are refused. Omit paging parameters for export.

get_mesh_geometry.summary: Read actual vertex data off a StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh: per-section positions, uvs, normals and triangle indices, from the engine's render data (no ProceduralMeshComponent plugin needed). Triangle indices are section-local, so they index that section's own positions array; add baseVertexIndex for LOD-global indices. Over 20000 vertices inline is refused - pass dumpToFile to write the full data to a JSON file instead, or narrow with sectionIndex (#948/#926/#953).

measure_mesh_geometry.summary: Measure a StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh LOD: bounds, dimensions, surfaceArea, volume, triangleCount, vertexCount, isClosed, isManifold, boundaryEdgeCount, nonManifoldEdgeCount. surfaceArea and volume are NAMED fields, never a positional pair (the engine's get_mesh_volume_area returns them in the order opposite to its name, #938). Vertices are welded by position before topology analysis so a UV seam does not read as a hole (#938/#953).

read_uv_channels.summary: Report every UV channel of a StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh LOD: bounds, UV area, unit-square coverage, overlap fraction and the triangles involved, island count, degenerate islands, seam edges, out-of-range and flipped triangles, plus which channel LightMapCoordinateIndex points at and the LOD's lightmap build settings. This is the verification half of the UV surface: every other UV action reports the same channel block after it writes, so a change can be checked rather than trusted. Overlap and coverage are RASTERISED at rasterSize rather than tested exactly, and the result says so via overlapMethod.

set_uv_channel_count.summary: Add, remove, resize or copy a UV channel. Channel count is a mesh-description attribute with no UPROPERTY, so asset(set_property) cannot reach it. Setting the count it already has returns existed=true and skips the rebuild. Growing has an exact inverse and the rollback restores it; remove and copy-over-existing DESTROY coordinates, so those report rollbackRestoresChannelCountOnly rather than pretending the undo is complete.

unwrap_uvs.summary: Auto-unwrap and pack islands into one channel via Geometry Script, adding the channel if it does not exist. It converts the LOD to a DynamicMesh and back, so the WHOLE LOD is rewritten rather than only its UVs; the result says so. Pass backupToChannel for a lossless rollback, otherwise only the channel count is restorable. Without the Geometry Script plugin it returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable instead of failing opaquely.

transform_uvs.summary: One action for every UV transform: the whole channel, chosen islands, triangles facing a direction, or one material slot, plus flips. The filter is the only thing that varies, so the maths lives in one place rather than in four near-identical actions. Edits the mesh description directly, touching nothing but the UV channel, and emits an EXACT inverse as its rollback. A zero scale component is refused because it has no inverse; an identity transform returns existed=true without rebuilding.

generate_lightmap_uvs.summary: Apply the lightmap build settings AND run UStaticMesh::Build AND read the result back. Deliberately not a setter: bGenerateLightmapUVs, SrcLightmapIndex, DstLightmapIndex and LightMapCoordinateIndex are plain UPROPERTYs that asset(set_property) already writes, and writing them does NOTHING until the mesh rebuilds. That rebuild is the whole point. Returns the channel the build actually produced with its overlap and island report, and fails loudly when the channel did not appear. StaticMesh only. Rollback restores the settings, not the generated coordinates.

export_uv_layout.summary: Render one UV channel to a PNG under Saved/UVLayouts: white wireframe, one hue per island, red where two triangles share a texel, yellow unit-square border. Returns the file path plus the same channel statistics read_uv_channels reports, so the picture and the numbers describe the same rasterisation. Use it to SEE why a lightmap bake is wrong instead of inferring it from counts. inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger.

check_uvs.summary: One-call UV health report, the same idiom as measure_mesh_geometry. Flags a missing lightmap channel, a LightMapCoordinateIndex that disagrees with the build's DstLightmapIndex, overlap in the lightmap channel over budget, lightmap UVs outside 0..1, empty or degenerate channels and islands, and flipped triangles, each with a severity and the action that fixes it. Out-of-range UVs OUTSIDE the lightmap channel are reported as info rather than a fault, because tiling is legitimate there.

apply_mesh_simplify.summary: Reduce a StaticMesh's triangle count while keeping its silhouette, through Geometry Script. Nine strategies because 'simplify' means different things: a target triangleCount or vertexCount, a geometric tolerance (the furthest the surface may drift), an edgeLength, a fast cluster-based edgeLength, a structural collapse of coplanar regions (planar) or of PolyGroup faces (polygroup), and the editor's own reducer (editorTriangleCount, editorVertexCount). NOT reachable through asset(set_property): a StaticMesh's LOD reduction settings build a NEW LOD, they never rewrite LOD 0's source geometry, and no UPROPERTY means 'collapse this mesh to 500 triangles'. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default (outputPath, or '<assetPath>_Simplified'), whose rollback is a complete delete; inPlace=true overwrites the source and reports that its edit has no inverse, with backupPath as the escape. Idempotent: a mesh already at or under the target reports changed=false and is not rewritten. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin, and without it returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable.

apply_mesh_remesh.summary: Rebuild a StaticMesh's triangulation at a uniform or adaptive density. Different from apply_mesh_simplify: simplify only removes triangles, remesh splits AND collapses AND flips edges to reach an even edge length, which is what a mesh needs before deformation, baking, or a convex decomposition that would otherwise follow the original triangulation's bias. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default ('<assetPath>_Remeshed'). Deliberately NOT idempotent and says so in repeatIsIdempotent: remeshing a remeshed mesh keeps moving vertices, so a repeat is a second edit rather than a no-op, which is why the separate-output default matters here more than anywhere else. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin.

apply_mesh_mirror.summary: Reflect a StaticMesh across a plane, optionally cutting away the far side first and welding the seam. This is the 'model half of it and mirror' workflow, and it is real geometry rather than a negative component scale, which inverts the winding and lights wrong; no UPROPERTY on a StaticMesh mirrors its source geometry. Name the plane with axis=x|y|z through planeOrigin, or axis=custom with an explicit planeNormal. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default ('<assetPath>_Mirrored'). NOT idempotent and says so: mirroring a mirrored mesh doubles it again rather than returning the original. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin.

apply_mesh_hole_fill.summary: Close every open boundary loop on a StaticMesh so it becomes watertight, which is what a boolean, a voxel operation, a convex decomposition and a physics conversion all require and the most common reason those fail. WELDS FIRST by default: a great many 'holes' are not holes but duplicated vertices along a seam that no fill can close, and running the fill alone on such a mesh reports zero holes filled while the mesh stays open. Genuinely idempotent: a mesh with nothing left to fill reports existed=true and is not rewritten. Reports filledHoles, failedHoleFills, weldedOpenEdges and the before/after open-border-edge counts, so 'watertight now' can be verified rather than assumed. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin.

set_mesh_simple_collision.summary: Write explicit simple collision shapes onto a StaticMesh: boxes, spheres and capsules by center, rotation and size in the mesh's local space, the half generate_mesh_collision does not cover since it derives shapes from the mesh. A box's extent is the FULL length along each axis (the FKBoxElem X/Y/Z values), not a half extent; a capsule's length is the straight section, so its height is length + 2 x radius. replace=true (default) removes every existing simple shape, convex hulls included, before writing; false appends. Does what the editor's own collision tools do so dependents see the change: Modify, write AggGeom, InvalidatePhysicsData (a NEW BodySetupGuid) and CreatePhysicsMeshes, PostEditChange the mesh, then recreate the physics state of every loaded component using it. The GUID is the point: a SplineMeshComponent keeps its own copy of the mesh's collision and rebuilds it only when the mesh's BodySetupGuid differs from the one it cached, so a direct AggGeom write leaves every spline copy with the old collision. The rebuilt spline copies are not saved; level(resave_mesh_users) saves them. Returns previousShapes and shapes, previousCounts and counts, the previous and new collisionTraceFlag and bodySetupGuid with guidChanged, componentsRefreshed, saved, persisted and packageDirty, and a rollback that writes the previous shapes back; when the mesh carried convex hulls or other shapes shapes[] cannot express, it says so instead. Writing the shapes already there reports existed=true without rewriting. asset(get_mesh_collision) returns shapes in the same form.

generate_mesh_collision.summary: Build simple collision shapes for a StaticMesh from its own geometry, or clear them. Eight solver methods from axis-aligned boxes to a full convex decomposition, plus BoundingBox (one box fitted to the whole mesh). Coincident edges are welded first (weldFirst), so a mesh of unwelded faces fits as one island instead of one shape per face. Writing collision refreshes physics only and never rebuilds render data; the result's renderData reports that the mesh is still drawable and repairs it when it is not. NOT reachable through asset(set_property): UBodySetup AggGeom is a UPROPERTY, but what has to go into it is the OUTPUT of a decomposition solver running over the mesh, and there is no value a caller could supply; the shape count and trace flag stay ordinary property writes and asset(get_mesh_collision) is still the read half. Idempotent: generation from the same mesh with the same options is deterministic, so a repeat reports changed=false without rewriting the asset, compared by a structural signature (shape counts per kind, hull vertex counts, trace flag) rather than byte-for-byte. op='clear' is the remove half and needs no plugin at all. A generation that produces zero shapes is reported as a failure naming apply_mesh_hole_fill, not as a success that quietly left the mesh with no collision.

apply_mesh_fracture.summary: Cut a StaticMesh with planes and write each resulting piece out as its own StaticMesh asset, ready to be placed, simulated or destroyed individually. Three patterns: slice (parallel cuts along one axis), grid (cuts along all three) and random (seeded planes through the bounds). WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not Chaos destruction and produces no UGeometryCollection, because every engine entry point for that carries no UFUNCTION and reflection cannot reach it; the result says so in producesGeometryCollection=false rather than leaving it to be discovered. The source asset is never modified, so the rollback is an exact delete of the pieces it wrote. Seeded, therefore repeatable: onConflict='error' (the default) refuses rather than writing over pieces already there. dryRun lists the cut planes and every path it would write.

audit_hygiene.summary: One read-only sweep answering the questions a project accumulates answers to and never gets asked: what nothing references (unreferenced), what references nothing (brokenReferences), what exists twice (duplicates), what breaks the naming convention (naming), and what renames left behind (redirectors). asset(get_referencers) and asset(get_dependencies) answer the first two for ONE named package; this is the project-wide form, which is the one an agent needs. The unreferenced section carries a caveat to read before acting on it: an asset loaded by name from an INI setting, from C++ with a hardcoded path, or from a soft reference resolved at runtime has no package dependency and appears there while being very much in use, so treat it as candidates to review rather than a delete list. Maps, World Partition external actors and Asset Manager primary assets are already excluded for that reason. Duplicate detection by content matches class, file size and saved package hash, which finds a file copied verbatim but NOT a copy saved under a different name (the name is inside the file); duplicateMethod='name' is what catches an asset imported twice into two folders. Naming rules match on the asset's class name, so WidgetBlueprint and AnimBlueprint carry their own prefixes rather than inheriting Blueprint's, and the effective table comes back in rulesApplied. Counts are always complete; only the listings are capped by maxIssues.

bulk_fix_hygiene.summary: The batched fix-up for the two audit_hygiene findings a machine can act on without deciding something a person should: a name that breaks the convention (fix='naming') and an asset nothing references (fix='unreferenced'). Same preflight shape as bulk_set_properties: every candidate is validated, every candidate gets a status back including the rejected ones, and a failed preflight aborts before anything is touched unless continueOnError. THREE SAFETY RULES that are not the shape: dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE and the dry run names every asset with its exact destination; fix='unreferenced' MOVES assets into quarantineFolder by default rather than deleting them, and that move has an exact inverse this call emits as its rollback; and findings are recomputed here rather than taken from an audit, so an asset that gained a referencer since then is skipped with the referencer named. maxFixes caps the batch far below the audit's scan ceiling. Worlds are refused outright, because moving one without migrating its external-actor packages in the same batch orphans every actor in the level; use asset(rename). fix='redirectors' is refused too and points at asset(fixup_redirectors), which already does it properly.

mesh_boolean.summary: Boolean CSG between two StaticMeshes: union, subtract, intersect, trimInside, trimOutside, newPolyGroupInside, newPolyGroupOutside. The target is the mesh being cut and the tool is what cuts it, each placed by its own optional transform. Writes to a SEPARATE output asset by default (outputPath, or '<targetPath>_<Operation>' when omitted); inPlace=true opts into overwriting the target and is the only destructive form. An existing outputPath is refused unless onConflict='replace'. An empty result is refused and nothing is written unless allowEmptyResult=true, because two meshes that never overlap otherwise report success having deleted everything. Returns triangle and vertex counts for both inputs and the result, plus the written asset's triangles, vertices, LOD count, material slots and bounds, so the operation can be verified rather than trusted. dryRun runs the boolean and reports those counts without writing. Materials and simple collision are copied from the target by default. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin: without it the call returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable, rather than failing opaquely (#916).

move_folder.summary: Move/rename entire content folder with redirector fixup in one transaction. Refused with reason=package_objects_left_behind, before anything moves, when a package in the folder holds an object the move would leave at the old path (#1137) (#192).

create_folder.summary: Create empty content browser folder(s); path and paths combine. Returns per-path created/existed/failed (#212).

delete_folder.summary: Delete content browser folder(s) - counterpart to delete_asset, which leaves the parent directory entry behind as an orphan. Empty folders only by default; pass force=true to also delete any assets still inside (Content Browser 'Delete folder' equivalent). A World Partition map's __ExternalActors__ and __ExternalObjects__ packages for the folder go with it and are counted in externalPackagesDeleted; packages still loaded are kept and reported. Per-path status (deleted/absent/failed) with reason (invalid_path/protected_path/not_empty/delete_failed) and a sample of contained assets on not_empty entries.

create_user_defined_enum.summary: Create a UserDefinedEnum content asset, optionally pre-populated with values (#686).

list_enum_values.summary: List a UEnum's enumerators (index, authored short name, display name, value). Works on native and UserDefinedEnum assets (#686).

edit_user_defined_enum.summary: Author a UserDefinedEnum content asset. op=add_value appends an enumerator (authored name is auto-assigned; pass displayName - or name - to set the editable display text). op=rename_value sets a new displayName on the enumerator resolved by index or name (matches short or display name). op=remove_value deletes it. Recompiles dependents automatically. Native UEnums are not editable (#686).

create_user_defined_struct.summary: Create a UserDefinedStruct content asset, optionally pre-populated with fields (#735).

list_struct_fields.summary: List a UserDefinedStruct's members (index, internal name, friendly/display name, GUID, type label, and typeSpec, which add_field and set_field_type accept back). Use this to find the GUID for a stable rename/retype. Native structs are not editable (#735).

edit_user_defined_struct.summary: Author a UserDefinedStruct content asset. op=add_field appends a member (pass fieldName for its display name; type accepts scalars, structs, enums, object refs and containers such as struct:/Game/S.S[], TArray<int>, Set<Name>, Map<Name,int>, and a field typeSpec from list_struct_fields round-trips). op=rename_field sets a new newDisplayName on the member resolved by fieldGuid or fieldName - the member GUID is preserved so existing Blueprint pins and DataTable rows survive. op=set_field_type changes a member's type. op=remove_field deletes it. add_field, set_field_type and remove_field recompile every loaded Blueprint whose class holds the struct, reinstancing its live instances, and list them in dependentsRecompiled. Native structs are not editable (#735).

rename_struct_field.summary: Rename a UserDefinedStruct field's display name while preserving its member GUID, so Blueprint pins and DataTable rows keyed off it survive. The same edit as edit_user_defined_struct(op=rename_field). fieldName matches the friendly or internal name (#735).

list_locks.summary: List all currently-held asset locks with holder session id, acquiredAt, and ttlSecondsRemaining.

diff.summary: Semantic structural diff between two assets, dispatching on the asset's class. Blueprints: parent class, variables, functions, components, per-graph node and connection deltas. Skeleton and SkeletalMesh: raw bone additions and removals, reparenting (bone, fromParent, toParent), raw-index changes (bone, fromIndex, toIndex), and declared virtual-bone additions and removals, with hierarchyCompatible and editorCompatible reported SEPARATELY. That separation is the point: it answers whether two skeletons are bone-compatible enough to register as Compatible Skeletons or whether a retarget is required, because appending bones (virtual ones especially) leaves the shared hierarchy intact while reparenting an existing bone does not (#879). Deliberately OUT of scope and reported as such: reference-pose transforms (referencePoseCompared=false), export names (exportNamesCompared=false), sockets and retarget sources; structureScope spells the boundary out in the result. Both paths must be the same class. Other asset types report that diffing is not supported yet rather than failing opaquely.

epic_add_enumerator.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Appends a new enumerator to an enum. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_gradient.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Appends a gradient to an atlas as a new final row. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_input_param.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Adds an input-parameter node (a graph-level parameter such as Scalar, Color, or Vector) and returns it. The parameter is exposed on the graph automatically. If ParamName is set it becomes the parameter's name, uniquified against the graph's existing parameters. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_key.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Adds a key to a row. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.AddKey.

epic_add_node.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Adds a node of the given expression type to the graph and returns the new node. Input-parameter and Output expression types are not accepted here; they are created with the dedicated input-parameter and output tools. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_object_variable.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Adds a UObject-reference variable, applying all fields of Spec atomically. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_output.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Adds an Output node and returns it. The output is exposed on the graph automatically. If OutputName is set it becomes the output's name (and its export filename), uniquified against the graph's existing outputs. Configure the output further with the output-settings tool. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_row.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Adds a new row to the curve table with an optional default value. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.AddRow.

epic_add_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Adds new rows with default values to the data table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.AddRows.

epic_add_struct_variable.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Adds a variable of an arbitrary script-struct type, applying all fields of Spec atomically. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_user_asset_tags.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Adds the given User Asset Tags to an asset. Pass tag names without the UAT. prefix; the prefix is added internally. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_variable.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Adds a variable of a primitive or basic struct type, applying all fields of Spec atomically. Supported TypeName values (case-insensitive): bool, int, int64, byte, float, double, name, string, text, Vector, Rotator, Transform, Vector2D, LinearColor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_append_box.summary: [Epic geometry_toolset.geometry_ops.GeometryTools] Appends a box of the given dimensions to the component's mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_append_cone.summary: [Epic geometry_toolset.geometry_ops.GeometryTools] Appends a cone (or truncated cone) to the component's mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_append_cylinder.summary: [Epic geometry_toolset.geometry_ops.GeometryTools] Appends a cylinder of the given radius and height to the component's mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_append_disc.summary: [Epic geometry_toolset.geometry_ops.GeometryTools] Appends a flat disc to the component's mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_append_sphere.summary: [Epic geometry_toolset.geometry_ops.GeometryTools] Appends a sphere of the given radius to the component's mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_append_torus.summary: [Epic geometry_toolset.geometry_ops.GeometryTools] Appends a torus to the component's mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_assign_clothing_to_section.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Binds a clothing asset to a specific LOD and section on the skeletal mesh. Mirrors the SkeletalMesh Editor's "Apply Clothing Data" action. Any clothing already bound to the section is unbound first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_can_edit_asset.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Checks whether an asset can be edited. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_connect_pins.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Connects an output pin on FromNode to an input pin on ToNode. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_convert_clothing_asset_common_to_ch.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Converts a legacy UClothingAssetCommon (the cloth asset created via UChaosClothingSimulationFactory) into a new UChaosClothAsset whose embedded Dataflow graph mirrors the legacy UChaosClothConfig and UChaosClothSharedSimConfig values, with one WeightMap node per legacy weight map. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Creates a new CurveTable asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.Create.

epic_create__data_asset_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_asset.DataAssetTools] Creates a new DataAsset asset in the project. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_create__data_asset_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.DataAssetToolset] Creates a new DataAsset asset in the project. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Creates a new DataTable asset with the specified column schema. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.Create.

epic_create__string_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Creates a new StringTable asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.Create.

epic_create__user_defined_enum_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Creates a new user-defined enum asset with no enumerators. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create__user_defined_struct_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Creates a new user-defined struct asset. The new struct starts with one default bool variable (engine convention). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_atlas.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Creates a new curve atlas asset containing no gradients. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_clothing_asset.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Creates a UChaosClothAssetSKMClothingAsset from a Chaos Cloth/Outfit Asset and adds it to the skeletal mesh's clothing asset array, making it available to assign to sections. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_folder.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Creates a folder at the specified path. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.CreateFolder.

epic_create_gradient.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Creates a new linear color gradient asset, seeded with an opaque black-to-white ramp. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_texture_graph.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Creates a new empty TextureGraph asset. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_delete.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Deletes an asset or folder. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.Delete.

epic_diff.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two CurveTable assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff__data_asset_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.DataAssetToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two DataAsset assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff__data_table_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.DataTableToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two DataTable assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff__string_table_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StringTableToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two StringTable assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_disconnect_pins.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Removes the edge between the specified pins. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_duplicate.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Makes a copy of a folder or asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.Duplicate.

epic_exists.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Determines if a folder or asset exists. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.Exists.

epic_export_png.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.TextureToolset] Exports a Texture to a PNG file on disk. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_export_texture_graph.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Exports every texture output node to a Texture2D asset in the given content folder. Triggers a full graph evaluation internally before writing assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_find_assets.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Searches the project for assets that match specific criteria. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.FindAssets.

epic_find_similar.summary: [Epic SemanticSearchToolset.SemanticSearchToolset] Find assets whose embeddings are semantically similar to the given asset's embedding. Vector-only (no BM25). The source asset must already be indexed by the SemanticSearch plugin. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_fix_up_redirectors.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Fixes up object redirectors at or under a path, rewiring the assets that reference them to point at each redirector's target. A folder also fixes up every other redirector under it, including ones a rename did not create - pass the specific asset path instead when only cleaning up after a move or rename. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_generate_convex_collisions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Generates convex hull collision shapes for a static mesh. Convex hulls provide accurate collision for physics simulation. More hulls improve accuracy but increase runtime cost. Replaces any existing collision. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GenerateConvexCollisions.

epic_generate_lods.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Auto-generates LODs for a static mesh using triangle reduction. Each entry in triangle_percents creates one additional LOD. The value is the fraction of triangles to keep relative to LOD 0, from just above 0.0 (nearly empty) to 1.0 (full detail). For example, [0.5, 0.25] creates LOD1 with 50% of the original triangles and LOD2 with 25%. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GenerateLods.

epic_get_alpha_stops.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Returns the alpha stops of a gradient in time order. Only keys with derived tangents form stops; GetChannelKeys reads any other gradient. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_asset_class.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Gets the class of an asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.GetAssetClass.

epic_get_asset_content_roots.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Returns the known content-browser roots in the current project. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_asset_tags.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Gets the asset registry tags for an asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.GetAssetTags.

epic_get_bounds.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the local-space bounding box of a static mesh. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetBounds.

epic_get_channel_keys.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Returns the raw keys of one channel of a gradient, including tangents. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_collision_complexity.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Returns the collision trace behavior of a static mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_color_stops.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Returns the color stops of a gradient in time order. Only gradients whose red, green and blue curves share key times, interpolation modes and derived tangents form stops; GetChannelKeys reads any other gradient. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_dependencies.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Lists assets that the specified asset depends on. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.GetDependencies.

epic_get_entry.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Returns the source string for a specific key. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.GetEntry.

epic_get_enumerators.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Returns the enumerators of an enum in order. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_gradients.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Returns the gradients of an atlas in row order. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_graph.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Returns every node in the graph, each with its input and output pins and, for a connected input pin, the node feeding it. Input parameters and outputs are ordinary nodes here, identified by their ExpressionClass. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_graph_issues.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Validates the graph and returns every issue it reports: the errors and warnings the engine's validation surfaces (for example missing required inputs, unsupported types, material or subgraph errors, and node warnings). Use it to check a graph's health after editing. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_items.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns cached item data. Items must be loaded in the registry cache to be returned.

epic_get_keys.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Returns all keys for a row. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.GetKeys.

epic_get_live_cloth_simulation_stats.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Returns the live solver counts for every clothing simulation running in PIE - the figures the cloth debug UI shows, without opening it. A simulation only reports counts once it is actually simulating. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_lod_count.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the number of LODs in a static mesh asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetLodCount.

epic_get_lod_thresholds.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the screen-size thresholds at which each LOD becomes active. Screen size is a ratio of the mesh's screen height to the viewport height. A value of 1.0 means the mesh fills the full viewport height; values above 1.0 are valid and mean the mesh must appear larger than the viewport before the next LOD activates. Each LOD activates when the mesh appears smaller than its threshold. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetLodThresholds.

epic_get_material.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the material assigned to a named slot on a static mesh. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetMaterial.

epic_get_material_slots.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the names of all material slots in a static mesh. Material slot names are used when assigning materials to specific parts of the mesh. Use these names with get_material and set_material. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetMaterialSlots.

epic_get_metadata_tags.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Gets the metadata tags for an asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.GetMetadataTags.

epic_get_namespace.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Returns the namespace of a StringTable asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.GetNamespace.

epic_get_plugin_content_paths.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Returns the root content paths for plugins that have content. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_get_quality_level_min_lod.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Returns the per-quality-level Min LOD overrides for a static mesh. Min LOD is the smallest LOD index the mesh may render, forcing lower hardware quality levels to skip its higher-detail, more expensive LODs. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_quality_level_min_lod_default.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Returns the fallback Min LOD for quality levels with no explicit override. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_referencers.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Lists assets that reference the specified asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.GetReferencers.

epic_get_registry_info.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns detailed information about a specific registry.

epic_get_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Returns the column values for one or more rows as a JSON string. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.GetRows.

epic_get_schema.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns the item struct schema as JSON.

epic_get_schema__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Returns the column schema of the data table as a JSON string. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.GetSchema.

epic_get_section_clothing.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Returns the name of clothing bound for a specific LOD section (if any). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_size.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.texture.TextureTools] Returns the dimensions of a Texture2D in pixels. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.TextureToolset.GetSize.

epic_get_table_id.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Returns the table ID for a StringTable asset. The table ID is derived from the asset's package path and is used to reference the string table in text properties and localisation. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.GetTableId.

epic_get_tooltip.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Returns the struct-level developer tooltip. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_triangle_count.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the number of triangles in a specific LOD of a static mesh. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetTriangleCount.

epic_get_user_asset_tags.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Gets the User Asset Tags on an asset. User Asset Tags are user-authored labels stored in the asset's package metadata. They are surfaced by the Manage Tags editor and the Tagged Asset Browser, and are distinct from asset registry tags and metadata tags. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_vertex_count.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the number of vertices in a specific LOD of a static mesh. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.GetVertexCount.

epic_get_virtual_paths.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Converts internal asset/folder paths to their Content Browser virtual path. In most projects this is the same as the input. In UEFN/Valkyrie projects it can differ (e.g. an engine plugin's content grouped under a friendly display path) -- use this only to present a path to the user in conversation. The result may not be a valid input to other tools; pass the original path (e.g. from FindAssets) to other tools instead. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_import_file.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Imports a file from disk as a CurveTable asset. The file's first column is the row name; subsequent columns are sample times and values. interp_mode controls how the imported keys are interpolated between samples. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.ImportFile.

epic_import_file__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Imports a file from disk as a DataTable asset. The file's columns must match the property names in schema. Use search_row_structs to discover usable schema structs. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.ImportFile.

epic_import_file__static_mesh_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Imports a mesh file from disk as a StaticMesh asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.ImportFile.

epic_import_file__string_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Imports a file from disk as a StringTable asset. The file must have a header row with at least 'Key' and 'SourceString' columns. Additional meta-data columns are imported but the namespace is not - the StringTable's namespace is derived from its asset path. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.ImportFile.

epic_import_file__texture_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.texture.TextureTools] Imports an image file from disk as a Texture2D asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.TextureToolset.ImportFile.

epic_is_bitflags.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Returns whether the enum is marked as a bitflags type. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_is_checked_out.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Checks whether an asset is checked out by the current user. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_is_dirty.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Checks whether an asset has unsaved changes. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.IsDirty.

epic_is_nanite_enabled.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns whether Nanite is enabled for a static mesh. Nanite is Unreal's virtualized geometry system that renders highly detailed meshes efficiently. It is most beneficial for meshes with many triangles. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_is_nanite_mesh.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Returns whether this is a Nanite mesh. This reflects the mesh's current state, so it may briefly lag behind a just-changed Nanite setting while a background rebuild finishes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_clothing_assets.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Returns information about all Clothing Assets on a skeletal mesh. Use AssetName with AssignClothingToSection. Check bRequiresMatchingLodIndex to determine how to supply ClothingLodIndex: - true (ChaosClothAsset): pass the same value as LodIndex - false (UClothingAssetCommon): pass any value in [0, NumClothingLods-1] Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_data_sources.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns the editor-defined sources configured on a Data Registry. These are the sources as authored on the registry asset, before any runtime expansion of meta sources.

epic_list_folders.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Lists the folders contained within a folder. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.ListFolders.

epic_list_input_params.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Returns the graph's input-parameter nodes: the graph-level parameters such as Scalar, Color, or Vector. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_items.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns all item names in a Data Registry.

epic_list_keys.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Lists all keys in the string table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.ListKeys.

epic_list_node_types.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Returns every available TextureGraph expression node type, sorted. A returned class identifies the node type to add. Input-parameter and Output types are included but are rejected by the generic add; create those through the dedicated input-parameter and output tools. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_outputs.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Returns the graph's Output nodes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_registries.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns the names of all registered Data Registries.

epic_list_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Lists the names of all rows in the curve table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.ListRows.

epic_list_rows__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Lists the names of all rows in the data table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.ListRows.

epic_list_runtime_sources.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns the runtime sources for a Data Registry. This is the expanded list including transient child sources generated from meta sources. Will equal ListDataSources when the registry has no meta sources.

epic_list_variables.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Returns the variables of a struct in authored order. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_load_asset.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Loads an asset from the project. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.LoadAsset.

epic_move.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Moves or renames an asset or folder. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.Move.

epic_move_enumerator.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Moves an enumerator to a new position, shifting the others to accommodate it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_move_variable.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Moves a variable above or below another variable on the struct. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_read_file.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Reads a text file from disk and returns its contents. Only files under /Game/, an enabled plugin's Content/ directory, or the project Saved/ directory may be read. Only plain text formats are supported. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_read_texture.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.TextureToolset] Reads a Texture and returns it as an image. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_reload_asset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Reloads an asset from disk, discarding any unsaved in-memory changes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_clothing_from_section.summary: [Epic ChaosClothAssetToolset.ChaosClothAssetToolset] Removes the clothing binding from a specific LOD section on the skeletal mesh. Mirrors the SkeletalMesh Editor's "Remove Clothing Data" action. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_collisions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Removes all collision shapes from a static mesh. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.RemoveCollisions.

epic_remove_entry.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Removes an entry from the string table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.RemoveEntry.

epic_remove_enumerator.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Removes the enumerator at the given index, shifting later enumerators down to fill the gap. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_gradient.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Removes a gradient from an atlas, shifting later rows up to fill the gap. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_input_param.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Removes the input-parameter node exposing the named parameter. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_lods.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Removes all auto-generated LODs from a static mesh, keeping only LOD 0. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.RemoveLods.

epic_remove_node.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Removes a node and all its connected edges from the graph. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_output.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Removes the Output node exposing the named output. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_row.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Removes a row from the curve table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.RemoveRow.

epic_remove_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Removes rows from the data table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.RemoveRows.

epic_remove_user_asset_tags.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Removes the given User Asset Tags from an asset. Pass tag names without the UAT. prefix. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_variable.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Removes a variable from a struct. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_rename_row.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Renames a row in the curve table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.RenameRow.

epic_rename_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Renames one or more rows in the data table. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.RenameRows.

epic_rename_variable.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Renames a variable. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_sample_gradient.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Evaluates a gradient with the asset's hue, saturation, brightness, vibrance and alpha-range adjustments applied, so the result can differ from the keyed values. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_save_asset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Saves an asset to disk. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_save_assets.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Saves assets to disk. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_search.summary: [Epic SemanticSearchToolset.SemanticSearchToolset] Run a semantic search over the Content Browser assets indexed by the SemanticSearch plugin. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_search_row_structs.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Finds structs that can be used as a DataTable schema. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.SearchRowStructs.

epic_set_alpha_stops.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Replaces the alpha stops of a gradient, leaving its color keys untouched. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_bitflags.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Sets whether the enum is treated as a bitflags type. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_channel_keys.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Replaces the raw keys of one channel of a gradient, leaving the other channels untouched. Tangents of keys set to an automatic tangent mode are recomputed; authored tangents are kept. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_collision_complexity.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Sets the collision trace behavior of a static mesh. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_color_stops.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Replaces the color stops of a gradient, leaving its alpha keys untouched. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_display_name.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedEnumToolset] Sets the display name of the enumerator at the given index. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_entry.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Adds or updates an entry in the string table. If the key already exists its value is replaced; otherwise a new entry is created. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StringTableToolset.SetEntry.

epic_set_gradients.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.CurveAtlasToolset] Replaces the gradients of an atlas, rebuilding its texture once. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_keys.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Replaces all keys in a row with the provided list. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.CurveTableToolset.SetKeys.

epic_set_lod_thresholds.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Sets the screen-size thresholds at which each LOD becomes active. Screen size is a ratio of the mesh's screen height to the viewport height. A value of 1.0 means the mesh fills the full viewport height; values above 1.0 are valid and mean the mesh must appear larger than the viewport before the next LOD activates. Thresholds must be in strictly descending order (LOD 0 has the largest threshold), and there must be exactly one threshold per LOD. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.SetLodThresholds.

epic_set_material.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Assigns a material to a named slot on a static mesh asset. This affects all instances of the mesh that do not override the slot material. Use set_component_material_override to change materials on a single instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.SetMaterial.

epic_set_nanite_enabled.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Enables or disables Nanite for a static mesh. Changing this setting triggers a mesh rebuild. Nanite is most beneficial for high-polygon meshes. Low-polygon meshes may not benefit from Nanite. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset.SetNaniteEnabled.

epic_set_node_alias.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Renames a node by setting its primary pin's alias name. For Output nodes this additionally syncs OutputSettings.OutputName so the bake's export filename matches the new node name. For other node types, sets the alias on the node's first output pin (or first input pin for input-only nodes like Scalar/Color/Texture). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_output_settings.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Typed shortcut for the most common Output-node configuration. Sets BaseName, FolderPath, and TexturePresetType (cascading preset defaults for Compression/LODGroup/sRGB), then syncs the node's display name and export name to BaseName. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_pin_value.summary: [Epic TextureGraphToolset.TextureGraphTools] Sets one input pin's value on a node, resolving the pin by argument name or alias. For a polymorphic Variant pin (which takes its value from a connected node, not a string) this creates an inline constant node matching the value (a scalar, color, or vector inferred from the value string) and connects it to the pin, replacing any existing source. Re-setting an ordinary pin to the value it already holds is an idempotent success. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_quality_level_min_lod.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Merges per-quality-level Min LOD overrides into a static mesh. Quality levels not listed in Overrides keep their current value; pass -1 to clear a level's override. Leaves the fallback Min LOD unchanged. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_quality_level_min_lod_default.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.StaticMeshToolset] Sets the fallback Min LOD for quality levels with no explicit override. Leaves existing per-quality-level overrides unchanged. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Sets column values for one or more rows. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.DataTableToolset.SetRows.

epic_set_tooltip.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Sets the struct-level developer tooltip. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_variable_default_value.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Sets a variable's default value. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_variable_editable_on_instance.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Sets whether a variable is editable on instances of the struct. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_variable_save_game.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Sets whether a variable participates in SaveGame archives. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_variable_tooltip.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UserDefinedStructToolset] Sets a variable's developer tooltip. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_update_metadata_tags.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Sets or removes metadata tags on an asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.AssetToolset.UpdateMetadataTags.

epic_validate_assets.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.AssetToolset] Validates the given assets and returns the errors and warnings found. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_write_file.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Writes text content to a file on disk. Only files under /Game/, an enabled plugin's Content/ directory, or the project Saved/ directory may be written. Only plain text formats are supported. Overwrites the file if it already exists. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.
