epic_connect_pins.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Makes a connection between source (output) and dest (input) pins. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ConnectPins.

epic_create.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Creates a new Blueprint asset in the project. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.Create.

epic_create_node.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Adds a new node to the graph. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.CreateNode.

epic_delete_node.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Deletes the node from its graph. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.DeleteNode.

epic_diff.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Returns a line diff between two Blueprints' graphs, as DSL, and their class defaults. Empty when they match. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff__blueprint_dsl_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintDslTools] Returns a unified text diff between two Blueprint assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff_blueprint_html.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint_diff.BlueprintDiffTools] Diffs the workspace version of a Blueprint against a depot revision and writes HTML. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff_blueprint_revisions_html.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint_diff.BlueprintDiffTools] Diffs two depot revisions of a Blueprint and writes HTML. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff_changelist_blueprints_html.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint_diff.BlueprintDiffTools] Writes one HTML diff per Blueprint asset that a changelist modifies. Works for submitted and shelved changelists on any branch. The before and after files come from Perforce, so the workspace version is not used. Added, moved, deleted, and non-Blueprint files are skipped, since they have no earlier version at their path. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff_graphs.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Compares two versions of a graph with the same matching the editor's Diff window uses. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_disconnect_pins.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Breaks two connected pins. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_docs.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Returns the common grammar followed by the Blueprint dialect reference. Read it before the first Write or Edit. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_edit.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Applies ordered exact replacements to the latest session text. Revision must come from the latest Read, Write, or Edit for the same asset and scope; otherwise call Read again. The full batch is staged before mutation. The edit fails without a matching session, with a stale Revision, when an OldString is absent or non-unique unless bReplaceAll is true, or when the resulting DSL does not parse. Any failure leaves the asset unchanged. When bDslOmitted is true, apply the replacements to your existing copy. Otherwise Dsl is the authoritative canonical text for later edits. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_find_node_categories.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Retrieves a list of available node categories in a Blueprint graph, optionally filtered by compatible input and/or output pin types On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.FindNodeCategories.

epic_find_node_references.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Returns Graph DSL node references whose palette name, category or reference contains the query (case and spaces ignored), with each one's palette category and name. The reference, not the palette name, is what goes in a Write or Edit call head. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_find_node_types.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Finds node types that can be created in a particular graph meeting the search criteria. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.FindNodeTypes.

epic_find_nodes.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Finds nodes in a graph by title, class, and/or execution role. All filters are optional and ANDed together. Useful for locating specific event chains in large graphs like EventGraph before reading them with get_connected_subgraph. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.FindNodes.

epic_get_comment_box_text.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Returns the text of a comment box. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_connected_subgraph.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Returns detailed information for all nodes connected to the given node. Use this alongside find_nodes to read a single event chain from a large graph (like Event Graph) without reading the entire graph. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetConnectedSubgraph.

epic_get_create_event_function.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Returns the function currently bound to a Create Event node. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetCreateEventFunction.

epic_get_default_object.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Returns the Class Default Object (CDO) for a Blueprint's. ObjectTools list/set/get property will get the CDO automatically, so this should primarily be used before calling tools that want to operate on the object inside the blueprint (like ActorTools). On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetDefaultObject.

epic_get_delegate_signature.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Returns the signature a Create Event node's bound function must implement. Each param is listed on its own line with its type, direction and passing mode, in the terms AddFunctionParam takes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_function_flags.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Returns the detail-panel settings of a Blueprint function. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_graph.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Retrieves a specific graph from a Blueprint asset by name. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetGraph.

epic_get_graph_dsl_docs.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Returns the full syntax reference for write_graph_dsl. Call this before using write_graph_dsl for the first time. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_get_graph_dsl_docs__blueprint_dsl_t.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintDslTools] Returns the full syntax reference for write_graph_dsl. Call this before using write_graph_dsl for the first time. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_node_infos.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Retrieves detailed information for a list of Blueprint graph nodes. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetNodeInfos.

epic_get_node_note.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Returns the note text on a Blueprint node (the small comment bubble shown over an individual node). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_node_type_pins.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Returns the pin names and types for a node type. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetNodeTypePins.

epic_get_nodes_in_comment_box.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Returns the nodes grouped inside a comment box. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_parent.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Returns the parent class of a Blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetParent.

epic_get_pin_value.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Gets the value of a Blueprint graph pin. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetPinValue.

epic_get_variable_category.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Gets the user-defined category of a Blueprint member variable. Categories group variables in the My Blueprint panel. Variables with no explicit category default to the Blueprint's name in the UI. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetVariableCategory.

epic_get_variable_read_only.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Gets whether a member variable is Blueprint Read Only (graphs can read but not write it). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_variable_replication.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Gets the replication mode of a Blueprint member variable. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.GetVariableReplication.

epic_get_variable_tooltip.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Gets the tooltip shown for a Blueprint variable in the editor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_is_node_note_pinned.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Returns whether a node's note bubble is pinned (always visible). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_comment_boxes.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Lists all comment boxes in a Blueprint graph. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_compatible_event_functions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists functions that can be bound to a Create Event node. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListCompatibleEventFunctions.

epic_list_component_events.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists the bindable delegate events available on a component. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListComponentEvents.

epic_list_event_dispatchers.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists all event dispatchers defined on a Blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListEventDispatchers.

epic_list_events.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists all events visible on the Blueprint - locally defined custom events plus inheritable events from the parent class chain and implemented interfaces. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListEvents.

epic_list_functions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists all functions visible on the Blueprint - locally defined plus inheritable ones from the parent class chain and implemented interfaces. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListFunctions.

epic_list_graphs.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists all graphs in the Blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListGraphs.

epic_list_interfaces.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Lists the interfaces implemented by a Blueprint. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_variables.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Lists member or local variables defined on a Blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.ListVariables.

epic_read.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Reads a Blueprint scope as canonical DSL and returns the revision required by Edit. Scope is empty for the whole asset, GraphName for one graph, or GraphName/EntryName for one entry. Backtick-quote a segment containing spaces, syntax characters, or `/`; `` `A/B` `` is one segment. Set bIncludePositions only when node positions are needed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_read_graph_dsl.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Reads a Blueprint graph and returns a DSL script. The returned code uses the same syntax that write_graph_dsl accepts and can be edited and passed back to write_graph_dsl to modify the graph. Call get_graph_dsl_docs() for the full syntax reference. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_read_graph_dsl__blueprint_dsl_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintDslTools] Reads a Blueprint graph and returns a DSL script. The returned code uses the same syntax that write_graph_dsl accepts and can be edited and passed back to write_graph_dsl to modify the graph. Call get_graph_dsl_docs() for the full syntax reference. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_comment_box.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Removes a comment box from its graph. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_function_graph.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Removes a function graph or event dispatcher from the Blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.RemoveFunctionGraph.

epic_remove_function_param.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Removes an input or output from a function or event dispatcher. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.RemoveFunctionParam.

epic_remove_interface.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Removes an implemented interface from a Blueprint. The Blueprint must be recompiled afterward. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_node_pin.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Removes a specific pin from a node that supports dynamic pin removal. Works for Switch nodes (removes one case pin), Sequence nodes (removes one Then output), commutative binary operators like Add/Multiply (removes one input), Make Array nodes, etc. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.RemoveNodePin.

epic_remove_variable.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Removes a member or local variable from a Blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.RemoveVariable.

epic_retarget_node_class.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Replaces a node's baked-in class reference from old_class to new_class in place. If the node's current class reference matches old_class it is replaced with new_class and the node is reconstructed so its pins reflect the new type. If the node already references new_class the call is a no-op. When a Blueprint is duplicated, nodes in the copied graph retain class references pointing to the original Blueprint. Calling this on each node with the original and duplicate classes retargets them without manual delete-recreate-rewire cycles. Handles cast, function call, event, and multicast delegate nodes. The Blueprint must be compiled after all retargeting is complete. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.RetargetNodeClass.

epic_schema.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Returns one node type's schema as a DSL form. Query unfamiliar node types before writing: (node `Type` (in (`Pin` Type) ...) ; data input pins (out (`Pin` Type) ...) ; data output pins (params (`Prop` Type [:over]) ...) ; writable properties, baked as :`Prop` value (determines `Prop` ...)) ; properties whose value changes the pin set (Enum A B ...) lists writable values. :over marks a property with an override input, supplied as :`Prop` (wire Source). Write an (Instanced /Script/Pkg.Base) property with a concrete class-headed value: (class:/Script/Pkg.Concrete :`Field` value ...). Empty sections are omitted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_comment_box_text.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Sets the text on a comment box. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_create_event_function.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Binds a function to a Create Event node. Use list_compatible_event_functions to find valid function names. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetCreateEventFunction.

epic_set_function_flags.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Sets detail-panel settings on a Blueprint function. Only the fields set on Flags are applied; leave a field unset to keep the function's current value for that flag. The Blueprint must be recompiled for the changes to take effect. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_node_note.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Sets the note text on a Blueprint node (its comment bubble). The bubble is made immediately visible in the graph editor when a non-empty note is set. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_node_note_pinned.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Sets whether a node's note bubble is pinned (always visible), vs. only shown on hover. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_node_position.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Sets a new position for the node. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetNodePosition.

epic_set_parent.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Reparents a Blueprint to a new parent class. The Blueprint must be recompiled after reparenting. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetParent.

epic_set_pin_value.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Sets the value of a Blueprint graph pin. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetPinValue.

epic_set_variable_category.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Sets the user-defined category on a Blueprint member variable. Categories group variables in the My Blueprint panel. Pass an empty string to reset to the default (the Blueprint's name). On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetVariableCategory.

epic_set_variable_instance_editable.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Sets whether a member variable is editable per-instance on actors placed in the level. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetVariableInstanceEditable.

epic_set_variable_read_only.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Sets whether a member variable is Blueprint Read Only. A read-only variable can still be read by graphs, but a setter can no longer be created for it. Local variables are not supported. The Blueprint must be recompiled for the change to take effect. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_variable_replication.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Sets the replication mode on a Blueprint member variable. RepNotify will automatically create an OnRep_ function on the Blueprint if one does not already exist. On UE 5.9 it calls BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset.SetVariableReplication.

epic_set_variable_tooltip.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintToolset] Sets the tooltip shown for a Blueprint variable in the editor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_write.summary: [Epic BlueprintToolsets.BlueprintDslToolset] Transactionally applies a DSL document and returns its canonical form and a new revision. A failure leaves the asset unchanged. Use Write for a complete document or a large structural change. Use Edit for a targeted change that can be expressed as exact replacements against text you just read. Top-level entries use upsert semantics: omitted entries remain and produce a warning. Delete an entry with a tombstone such as (event `Foo` :!delete). Deleting a missing entry only warns. Dsl is omitted when bDslOmitted is true because the submitted document is already canonical. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_write_graph_dsl.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools] Populates a Blueprint graph with nodes from a DSL script and compiles the Blueprint. Call get_graph_dsl_docs() for the full syntax reference and examples. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_write_graph_dsl__blueprint_dsl_tool.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintDslTools] Makes a Blueprint graph match a DSL script and compiles the Blueprint. Statements whose DSL is unchanged from the graph's current state keep their existing nodes - positions, wires, and node ids are preserved - and only changed statements are rebuilt. Call get_graph_dsl_docs() for the full syntax reference and examples. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

tools.name: canvas
tools.description:
Unreal Canvas (UE 5.9, the UnrealCanvasBridge plugin): Movie Render Graph renders of the viewport, a Level Sequence or an object reposition, the passes and variables of the render preset, scene snapshots, the raw RGBA viewport stream, stencil, depth and annotation capture settings, and Gaussian splat and cutout actors. Each action runs the Bridge's own MCP tool through epic(call_mcp_tool); they are withheld when the editor does not serve that tool, which is the case until UnrealCanvasBridge is enabled in the .uproject. Render paths are on the editor's machine.

Call canvas(action, args={...}). Actions:
status()
list_passes(presetPath?, variables?:o)
list_variables(presetPath?)
render(cameraSource?:o, captureSceneState?:b, executionMode?, presetPath?, resolution?:o, variables?:o, viewportLook?:o)
render_sequence(cameraSource?:o, presetPath?, resolution?:o, sequencePath?, variables?:o, viewportLook?:o)
render_reposition(sceneStateBlobPath, cameraPose?:s/o, durationSeconds?:n, fps?:n, presetPath?, resolution?:o, saveSequence?:b, variables?:o)
save_scene_snapshot(sceneStateBlobPath, assetName?, destinationPath?, showDialog?:b)
start_viewport_stream(color?:b, depth?:b, exactSize?:b, fps?:n, height?:i, normal?:b, port?:i, sharedMemory?:b, stencil?:b, width?:i)
set_viewport_stream_fps(fps:n)
stop_viewport_stream()
assign_stencil(stencilId:i, one(actorPath; actorLabel))
clear_stencil(one(actorPath; actorLabel))
clear_all_stencils(actorLabels?:[s], actorPaths?:[s])
set_stencil_colors(groups:[o])
set_depth_range(encoding?, farCm?:n, nearCm?:n)
set_capture_stage(stage)
set_capture_annotations(enabled:b)
set_viewport_annotations(enabled:b)
set_annotation_render_mode(edgeThickness:n, fill:b)
spawn_splat(plyPath, actorTag?, label?, location?:[n]/o, replaceExisting?:b, rotation?:[n]/o)
list_splats()
remove_splat(splatId)
spawn_cutout(location:[n]/o, texturePaths:[s], intensity?:n, labels?:[s], rotation?:[n]/o)
spawn_cutout_from_png(location:[n]/o, intensity?:n, label?, one(pngPath; pngBase64), provenancePath?, rotation?:[n]/o)
list_cutouts()
remove_cutout(cutoutId)
add_cutout_variant(cutoutId, label?, one(pngPath; pngBase64))
set_cutout_variant(cutoutId, variantIndex:i)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

status.summary: Whether the Canvas Bridge is ready and an MRG preset is configured, with the preset's pass names. Returns ready, presetConfigured, passes?

list_passes.summary: The render passes (output branches) of the MRG preset and the captures each is expected to produce. Returns passes [name] and captures [{branch, subResource}], which match passName, branchName and subResourceName on render results.

list_variables.summary: The variables the MRG preset defines, with type and default as serialized strings. Pass overrides to the render actions as variables. Returns variables [{name, type, value}].

render.summary: Render the current editor viewport through Movie Render Graph. executionMode PlayInEditor (default) starts a PIE session so physics and Blueprint logic run; EditorWorld renders the loaded editor world at once, as a draft. captureSceneState takes a whole-world Level Snapshot first, for render_reposition and save_scene_snapshot (slow on a large level). Takes 30 to 120 seconds; renders run one at a time.Returns images [{path, passName, branchName, subResourceName, camera}], one PNG per capture under the project's Saved folder; rawDepth [{path, camera}] for a depth capture (float centimetres as .npy); and sceneStateBlobPath when captureSceneState was set.presetPath defaults to the preset in Editor Preferences > Plugins > Unreal Canvas; variables is {name: serialized value} (see list_variables); resolution is {size: preset|1080p|1440p|2160p|custom, width?, height?, matchAspect?}; cameraSource is {mode: viewport|sequence|actor, actorId?, actorName?}; viewportLook is {visibility?, showFlags?, viewMode?}.

render_sequence.summary: Render a Level Sequence through Movie Render Graph to PNG frames. sequencePath omitted renders the sequence open in Sequencer (only the focused shot when Sequencer is drilled into one); an explicit path renders all of it. cameraSource defaults to the sequence's own Camera Cuts. May take minutes.Returns passes [{directory, passName, branchName, subResourceName, frameCount, fps, filePattern, startFrame, firstFrame, lastFrame, sequenceName}], one directory of PNG frames per capture under Saved/UnrealCanvasSequenceRender. presetPath, variables, resolution, cameraSource and viewportLook are as for render.

render_reposition.summary: Render the move from a captured scene state to the current one: loads the Level Snapshot a render with captureSceneState wrote (sceneStateBlobPath), builds a transient sequence that moves each changed actor from its captured pose to its current one (added actors appear and removed ones disappear at the midpoint) while the camera moves from cameraPose to the current viewport, and renders it. A camera-only change is valid.cameraPose is the camera from the original render's result (object or JSON string). durationSeconds defaults to 4 and fps to 24; saveSequence keeps the sequence for Sequencer. Returns passes as render_sequence does.

save_scene_snapshot.summary: Save the Level Snapshot a render captured (its sceneStateBlobPath) as a Level Snapshot asset, which can be inspected or applied to put the captured actor poses back. Saves straight to destinationPath/assetName (default the Canvas generated-content folder's SceneState); showDialog=true opens the editor's save-as dialog instead, which waits for a person. Returns assetPath.

start_viewport_stream.summary: Stream the editor viewport over TCP as raw 8-bit RGBA frames, with optional depth, world-normal and stencil matte passes and the annotation JSON per frame. port omitted uses this editor's assigned stream port, or 9880. width and height default to 512, fps to 30; color, depth and normal default on, stencil off. Returns streaming, port, width, height, fps, format, exact_size, shared_memory_name?

set_viewport_stream_fps.summary: Change the running viewport stream's capture rate (1-120) without restarting it. Refused when no stream runs. Returns fps.

stop_viewport_stream.summary: Stop the viewport stream and disconnect its clients. Returns streaming=false and wasStopped.

assign_stencil.summary: Turn on custom depth for an actor's primitive components and give them a stencil ID (1-254), which the stencil matte pass and stencil color map key on.

clear_stencil.summary: Turn off custom depth on an actor's primitive components and reset its stencil value.

clear_all_stencils.summary: Turn off custom depth and reset the stencil on the given actors, or on every actor in the editor world that has custom depth on when none are given.

set_stencil_colors.summary: Set the stencil-to-color map the viewport stream's matte pass uses: each group maps a stencil ID to an RGB color, and visible=false leaves it out of the matte. At most 32 groups, each {stencilId, r, g, b, visible?}.

set_depth_range.summary: Set the depth pass's near and far cutoffs in centimetres (0 or omitted uses each frame's own min or max) and its encoding (ndc, metric or hilbert).

set_capture_stage.summary: Choose the post-process stage the stream captures scene color and composites stencils at: pre_postprocess, post_tonemap or post_final. A stage whose pass the project does not enable cascades to the one before it.

set_capture_annotations.summary: Turn the 3D annotations pass (the annotations-only image the stream and renders carry) on or off.

set_viewport_annotations.summary: Show or hide the 3D annotation overlay in the editor viewport.

set_annotation_render_mode.summary: Set how 3D annotations rasterize: filled faces or not, and the edge half-width in cube-local units (0 draws no edges).

spawn_splat.summary: Import a Gaussian splat .ply (a path on the editor's machine) as a new GaussianSplat asset and place a GaussianSplatActor for it. An actor with the same actorTag (default UnrealCanvasSplat) is updated in place unless replaceExisting=false. location is [x,y,z] or {x,y,z}; rotation is [pitch,yaw,roll] or {pitch,yaw,roll}. Returns gsplat_id, actor_path, asset_path, actor_tag, label.

list_splats.summary: List the Gaussian splat actors spawn_splat placed in the editor world. Returns gsplats [{gsplat_id, actor_path, label, location, rotation, asset_path}].

remove_splat.summary: Delete a Gaussian splat actor spawn_splat placed, by its gsplat_id. The imported asset stays. Returns actor_path.

spawn_cutout.summary: Place a cutout actor (a textured card) using existing Texture2D assets, one variant per texture, the first active. labels runs parallel to texturePaths; intensity is the emissive multiplier (default 0.3). Returns cutout_id and actor_path.

spawn_cutout_from_png.summary: Place a cutout actor from a PNG image, which becomes its first variant. pngPath is read by this server, so it is a path on the machine ue-mcp runs on. provenancePath is a detached C2PA manifest signed for the image. Returns cutout_id and actor_path.

list_cutouts.summary: List the cutout actors in the editor world. Returns cutouts [{cutout_id, actor_path, location, rotation, variant_count, active_variant_index, labels}].

remove_cutout.summary: Delete a cutout actor by its cutout_id.

add_cutout_variant.summary: Add an image variant to a cutout actor. Returns variant_index.

set_cutout_variant.summary: Show another of a cutout actor's variants, by 0-based index.

tools.name: chooser
tools.description:
Author ChooserTable assets (the data-driven selection layer behind Motion Matching): signature and parameters, columns and their input bindings, rows and their results, cells, the fallback result, auto populate, and nested choosers.

Call chooser(action, args={...}). Actions:
create(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)
describe(table|assetPath, nested?)
add_column(table|assetPath, columnType, inputStruct?, boundProperty?, enumPath?, nested?, insertIndex?:i)
list_rows(table|assetPath, nested?)
add_row(table|assetPath, output?, outputType?, cells?:[*], inputs?:o, nested?, resultType?, insertIndex?:i)
set_row(table|assetPath, index:i, output?, outputType?, disabled?:b, cells?:[*], inputs?:o, nested?, resultType?)
delete_row(table|assetPath, index:i, nested?)
list_object_references(assetPath|path, classFilter?, pathFilter?)
remap_object_references(assetPath|path, from?, to?, fromPrefix?, toPrefix?, dryRun?:b, allowMissing?:b)
list_types(kind:{column,result,parameter,input}, table?, nested?, column?:i)
get_signature(table|assetPath, nested?)
set_signature(table|assetPath, nested?, resultType?:{ObjectResult,ClassResult,NoPrimaryResult}, resultClass?, signatureAsset?)
add_parameter(table|assetPath, nested?, parameterType, properties?:o)
remove_parameter(table|assetPath, nested?, index:i)
get_property(table|assetPath, nested?, target:{column,row,fallback,parameter}, index?:i, propertyPath?)
set_property(table|assetPath, nested?, target:{column,row,fallback,parameter}, index?:i, propertyPath?, value)
delete_column(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i)
move_column(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i, newIndex:i)
duplicate_column(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i)
copy_column(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i, targetTable?, targetNested?, insertIndex?:i)
set_column(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i, disabled?:b, inputType?, parameterIndex?:i, propertyChain?:[s])
delete_rows(table|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i])
move_rows(table|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i], targetIndex:i)
duplicate_rows(table|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i])
copy_rows(table|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i], targetTable?, targetNested?, insertIndex?:i, includeFallback?:b)
get_cell(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i, row?:i, fallback?:b)
set_cell(table|assetPath, nested?, column:i, row?:i, fallback?:b, value)
set_fallback(table|assetPath, nested?, resultType?, output?, outputType?, remove?:b)
auto_populate(table|assetPath, nested?, column?:i, rows?:[i], includeFallback?:b)
create_nested(table|assetPath, nested?, row?:i, name?)
list_nested(table|assetPath)
delete_nested(table|assetPath, name)
rename_nested(table|assetPath, name, newName)
restore_snapshot(table|assetPath, snapshot:o)
remove_disabled(table|assetPath, nested?)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

create.summary: Create an empty ChooserTable asset. Add input columns with add_column, then rows with add_row (#685).

describe.summary: Introspect a ChooserTable: row count, result type, whether it is nested, each column (index, name, columnType, cellType, disabled, randomize, autoPopulates, hasFallbackValue, inputType and its binding) and the fallback result. Read this first to learn the cell text format each column expects (#685).

add_column.summary: Add an input column to a ChooserTable (so rows have a condition to fill). columnType is a Chooser column struct short name, e.g. EnumColumn, BoolColumn, FloatRangeColumn, GameplayTagColumn, ObjectColumn, or an Output* column. Optionally bind its input: inputStruct (parameter struct e.g. EnumContextProperty/BoolContextProperty), boundProperty (context property name to read), enumPath (for enum columns). Placed where the editor places it (before a trailing randomize column) unless insertIndex says otherwise. Sizes the new column's cells to the current rows (#685).

list_rows.summary: List every row: index, disabled flag, output object (resultType + referenced asset path), and each column's cell value as round-trippable text (#685).

add_row.summary: Add a row (appended, or before insertIndex). Set the output via `output` (asset path) + outputType ('asset' hard ref default | 'soft_asset' | 'evaluate' for a nested ChooserTable), or a default result of any type via resultType. Set input-column conditions via `cells` (array aligned to column order) and/or `inputs` (object keyed by column index or name). Cell values are struct text like '(Value=2)' - partial fields are allowed and unspecified ones keep defaults; a bare number/bool works for scalar columns (#685).

set_row.summary: Edit an existing row by index: optionally replace the output (output + outputType) or the result type (resultType, keeping the cells), toggle disabled, and/or update column cells (cells / inputs, same format as add_row) (#685).

delete_row.summary: Delete a row by index (removes its output plus the per-row cell from every column). The rollback puts it back at the same index (#685).

list_object_references.summary: List every leaf object reference reachable from a chooser, descending through nested chooser tables. list_rows renders those as an opaque resultType:NestedChooser with an empty output, so the actual PoseSearchDatabase/asset paths were invisible. Each entry reports the owning table, the exact location (e.g. ResultsStructs[3].Asset), the struct type and the current object path. classFilter matches the referenced object's class, pathFilter is a substring on the path (#754).

remap_object_references.summary: Repoint object references throughout a chooser's nested structure. Either an exact swap (from + to) or a folder rewrite (fromPrefix + toPrefix), which is the 'adopt vendor choosers into our namespace' case. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT - pass dryRun=false to apply. Object-typed targets are class-checked before assignment; the chooser is recompiled and left dirty rather than saved (#754).

list_types.summary: List the type names an authoring call accepts: kind 'column' (add_column), 'result' (resultType on add_row/set_row/set_fallback), 'parameter' (add_parameter), or 'input' (the input types one column accepts for set_column inputType; needs table + column). Full paths, sorted; short names work too.

get_signature.summary: Read a chooser's signature: result type (ObjectResult | ClassResult | NoPrimaryResult), result class, the ChooserSignature asset it inherits from (UE 5.9), and every parameter with its type, class or struct, and full value text. Works on a ChooserTable or a ChooserSignature asset; a nested chooser reports its root's.

set_signature.summary: Set a chooser's result type and/or result class, or point it at a ChooserSignature asset to inherit them and the parameters from (UE 5.9; empty clears the reference). Refused while the signature is inherited, except for clearing the reference. Bindings recompile against the new signature.

add_parameter.summary: Add a parameter (the object or struct a chooser reads from or writes to) of parameterType, e.g. ContextObjectTypeClass with properties {Class: '/Script/Engine.Character'} or ContextObjectTypeStruct with {Struct: ...}. Returns its index, which column bindings use.

remove_parameter.summary: Remove a parameter by index. Column bindings name parameters by index and are not renumbered, so bindings to later parameters need set_column afterwards.

get_property.summary: Read any property by path from a column (target 'column'), a row's result ('row'), the fallback result ('fallback') or a parameter ('parameter'), in Unreal text format. Paths are '.' separated with [index], stepping into instanced structs, e.g. 'InputValue.Binding.DisplayName', 'DefaultRowValue', 'Asset'. An empty path reads the whole struct.

set_property.summary: Write any property by path on a column, a row's result, the fallback result or a parameter (same targets and paths as get_property), in Unreal text format. The value is parsed in full before anything changes. A result change refreshes auto populating columns, as the editor does.

delete_column.summary: Delete a column and its cell in every row.

move_column.summary: Move a column so it ends up at newIndex. A randomize column stays last and cannot be moved, and nothing moves after it.

duplicate_column.summary: Duplicate a column with its cells, inserting the copy right after it.

copy_column.summary: Copy a column with its cells (matched to rows by index) into another table, a nested chooser, or the same table, before insertIndex. The copy's binding keeps its parameter index, so the target needs compatible parameters.

set_column.summary: Change a column: disable or enable it, change its input type (list_types kind 'input'), and/or bind its input to a parameter (parameterIndex) through a property chain, e.g. ['Speed'] or ['MyStruct','MyFloat']; an empty chain binds the parameter itself. The chain is checked under the editor's binding rules before anything changes.

delete_rows.summary: Delete several rows at once, with their cells.

move_rows.summary: Move rows, keeping their order, so they sit before targetIndex (a row index from before the move; rowCount moves them to the end), like dragging rows in the editor. Returns the new index of the first moved row.

duplicate_rows.summary: Duplicate rows (results, disabled flags and cells), inserting the copies after the last of them. A nested chooser result is deep copied.

copy_rows.summary: Copy rows into another table, a nested chooser, or the same table, like copy and paste in the editor: cells go into columns matching by type and input name, and a column is added for cells with no match. Nested choosers are deep copied. includeFallback also copies the fallback result and fallback cells.

get_cell.summary: Read one cell (column + row) or a column's fallback cell (fallback=true, output columns only), with its cell type.

set_cell.summary: Write one cell (column + row) or a column's fallback cell (fallback=true). The value is struct text like '(Min=0,Max=100)' or a bare scalar, parsed in full before anything changes.

set_fallback.summary: Set the fallback result (used when no row passes every filter) from an asset (output + outputType) or a default result of resultType, or remove it (remove=true; output columns keep their fallback cells).

auto_populate.summary: Fill auto populating columns' cells from each row's result: one column (column), some rows (rows, optionally includeFallback), or everything. UE 5.7 and newer.

create_nested.summary: Create a nested chooser inside the table's asset and make it a row's result (row), or add a new row for it. Address it afterwards with `nested` on any table action.

list_nested.summary: List the nested objects of a chooser's asset (nested choosers and column-owned objects) with name, path, class and parent.

delete_nested.summary: Delete a nested chooser or other nested object from the asset, clearing every row's reference to it.

rename_nested.summary: Rename a nested chooser or other nested object; the name must be unique among the asset's nested objects.

restore_snapshot.summary: Put a chooser asset back as a snapshot records it: every table's columns, rows, disabled flags and fallback, recreating nested choosers that were deleted. The snapshot is the rollback payload of the edits that drop data no other action restores (delete_column, delete_rows, a scattered move_rows, auto_populate, delete_nested, remove_disabled).

remove_disabled.summary: Delete every disabled row and column (and any column whose type is not loaded), as the editor's Remove Disabled Data does.

tools.name: conversation
tools.description:
Conversation graphs (UConversationDatabase): dialogue nodes, node connections, sub-nodes, speakers, and entry points. Requires UE 5.8+ with the Conversation toolsets available.

Call conversation(action, args={...}). Actions:

tools.name: datasmith
tools.description:
Datasmith scenes (Revit, SketchUp, CAD exports): inspect a .udatasmith file's options and element counts, import it into a content folder and the level, reimport a scene asset with actor sync, and query level actors by tag with their Datasmith metadata and bounds.

Call datasmith(action, args={...}). Actions:
status()
inspect(filePath)
import(filePath, destinationPath, options?:o)
reimport(sceneAssetPath, filePath?, syncActors?:b, respawnDeleted?:b, options?:o)
query_actors(tagPrefix?, tags?:[s], metadataKey?, metadataValue?, includeMetadata?:b, includeBounds?:b, limit?:i)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

status.summary: Report whether the DatasmithImporter and DatasmithContent plugins are enabled and loaded, and list the DatasmithSceneActors in the editor level with their scene asset and related actor count. Call this first.

inspect.summary: Open a .udatasmith file without importing it and return the exporter header (host, vendor, product, version), element counts (meshes, mesh actors, lights, cameras, materials, textures) and every import options object with its current values. The option names it returns are what import and reimport take in options.

import.summary: Import a .udatasmith file into destinationPath and the current level. Returns the DatasmithScene asset path, the spawned DatasmithSceneActor, the scene's asset counts (static meshes, materials, textures) and actor count, and the source element counts. options sets DatasmithImportOptions fields by dotted path, e.g. {"BaseOptions.bIncludeLight": false}. A failed import is an error that points at LogDatasmithImport. No inverse: it creates the asset set and the actors.

reimport.summary: Reimport an existing DatasmithScene asset from its source (or from filePath when the source moved), updating its actors in the level (syncActors, default true) and optionally respawning deleted ones (respawnDeleted). Returns asset counts before and after and the per-actor changes keyed by Datasmith id: added, removed, moved and kept. No inverse.

query_actors.summary: Find level actors by tag prefix (e.g. Revit.Element.Id.), exact tags, or a Datasmith metadata key/value, and return each one's matched tags, UDatasmithAssetUserData metadata and world bounds, plus the union bounds. Tags and bounds work without the Datasmith plugin; metadata needs it.

tools.name: demo
tools.description:
Neon Shrine demo scene builder and cleanup.

Call demo(action, args={...}). Actions:
step(step|stepIndex?:i)
get_steps()
cleanup()
go_home(discardUnsaved?:b)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

step.summary: Execute demo step. Steps are NOT idempotent: each one spawns unconditionally, so a replay leaves a second set of Demo_ actors, and the result says created rather than a bare success. No inverse is emitted. No step records what it individually created, and demo(cleanup) is not a substitute: it removes the whole demo scene, and on the way it creates /Game/MCP_Home if missing and switches the editor to it, then deletes by label prefix in whatever level is then open. The response names it as guidance with rollbackPossible=false, so the flow runner never invokes it as an undo.

get_steps.summary: List every demo step up front: index, id and description, plus a count. Use this to see what the 19 steps build before running any of them.

cleanup.summary: Remove demo assets and actors. Switches editor to /Game/MCP_Home before deleting so the editor is never left on an Untitled map, dropping unsaved changes to the demo level (which it deletes) and refusing, with nothing deleted, when any other open map has unsaved changes. unchanged=true only when nothing was deleted AND the home level already existed AND the editor was already in it, because anchoring to that level is itself a change this call makes. No inverse of its own - rebuilding means running step 1 through 19 again.

go_home.summary: Switch the editor to /Game/MCP_Home (creating it on first use). Use this before any operation that would leave the editor on an Untitled map. When the open map has unsaved changes (an Untitled map someone edited included) it refuses and names them in dirtyPackages, and the editor stays where it is; pass discardUnsaved=true to drop them, and discardedPackages lists what was dropped. Succeeds only when the home level is the open map afterwards. Reports alreadyOpen=true when the home level was already the open one, and otherwise rolls back by reopening the level that WAS open through level(load) - marked lossy when the home level had to be created, since that package stays on disk. A previously open map with no content path (unsaved or Untitled) has no inverse and the response says so.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

get_shader_compile_status.summary: Read outstanding shader jobs, compiling state, pending material and shader-map counts, and manager availability. waitUntilIdle polls short game-thread snapshots between ticks, leaving the editor free to finish compiling. timeoutMs bounds the wait (default 60000); a timeout returns success=false and state=timed_out with the last counters.

execute_command.summary: Run a console command. world=editor (the default) runs it against the editor world, where Open is refused because it does nothing there; switch maps with level(load) (#1393). world=pie runs it as a PIE player through that player's console (PlayerController::ConsoleCommand, in that instance's context), so cheat-manager and game commands such as slomo, pause or ToggleDebugCamera reach the running game; pieInstance and playerIndex pick the instance and player, a dedicated server with no player runs it against its world, and the command's console output comes back as output. This is the safe route for PIE console commands; calling ExecuteConsoleCommand through invoke_object_function is a known editor crash (#1250).

run_python_file.summary: Run a Python file from disk with __file__/__name__ populated (#142). Pass entryPoint to load the file WITHOUT firing its `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard and then call one named function in it, which is how a Tools/ script holding several stages behind a main() is driven a stage at a time; `args` are then that call's positional arguments rather than sys.argv, `kwargs` its keyword arguments, and its return value comes back as `result` with no resultVariable needed. Pass asMain=true (or runName="__main__") to run the file through runpy as __main__ with sys.argv set to the file plus args, so a main guard that starts a tick callback does fire; runName also sets the module name an entryPoint load uses. captureLog=false drops everything the script logged except its errors, and maxLogChars keeps only the tail: a script that prints a few hundred lines otherwise returns tens of KB to a caller that wanted one value. A script that needs a line trace against the PIE world calls unreal.MCPTraceLibrary.line_trace(start, end, 'pie', pie_instance, 'WorldStatic', trace_complex), which returns hit, impact_point, impact_normal, distance, actor_path, component_name and physical_material without a round trip; the engine's SystemLibrary traces take a TraceTypeQuery, not a CollisionChannel (#1283). (#142/#732/#995)

purge_python_modules.summary: Purge cached embedded-Python modules whose name starts with a prefix, so the editor drops stale code after you edit a Python tool on disk. Returns the purged module names + count (#719).

close_sequence.summary: Close the currently open Level Sequence editor (Sequencer). Do this before bulk-deleting actors a sequence may possess - open sequences re-resolve possessables by name during destruction and can mis-bind. Returns wasOpen + closedSequence (#718).

open_tab.summary: Open a registered editor tab by ID so its UI can be screenshotted as evidence (e.g. 'ProjectSettings', 'OutputLog', 'ContentBrowserTab1') (#727).

open_settings.summary: Open (and navigate) a settings viewer for visual settings evidence. section takes a bare name with category, or a combined 'Engine.Physics' (#727).

show_notification.summary: Show a toast in the editor's notification area (bottom right), the way the editor reports a finished build or a failed save. severity picks the icon and colour (info default, success, warning, error); durationS is how long it stays before fading (default 8). hyperlinkText with hyperlinkUrl adds a link that opens the URL in the default browser; only http and https URLs are accepted. Returns onScreen, read back from the notification windows, so a toast Slate accepted but never drew is visible as onScreen=false.

set_property.summary: Set UObject property. Saves the package to disk by default; pass save=false to leave it dirty in-memory (batch many writes, then editor(save_dirty)/asset(save)) (#674). TMap values take either { "Key": value } or, for struct keys, [{ key: {...}, value: ... }] - exactly what get_property/describe_object return under `value`. A write that cannot store every entry it was given fails and leaves the old value in place; containers report elementCount on success (#820). SkeletalMeshAsset/SkinnedAsset on a skinned mesh component go through SetSkinnedAssetAndUpdate, since a raw write crashes the next pose evaluation; for a placed actor use level(set_component_skeletal_mesh) (#1099). An Instanced or EditInlineNew object property takes {instanceClass, properties}: a new subobject of that class is created with the owning object as its outer and its fields set from properties, e.g. RootMotionModifier = {instanceClass: "RootMotionModifier_Scale", properties: {Scale: {x:0,y:0,z:0}}} (#1292). propertyName accepts dotted paths, array indices and field-value selectors (`Items[Id=Foo].Field`); resolvedPropertyName and the rollback carry the numeric index matched, with indexedPath also returned for keyed paths. A config property on a settings class default (objectPath=/Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings and other Project Settings classes) is written to its ini instead of a package, and the result carries configFile, configSection, configKey and storedValue read back from that file (#1566).

get_property.summary: Read UObject property. propertyName takes the dotted, indexed (`Rules[1]`) and keyed (`Rules[Id=Axe]`) paths asset(set_property) does. `value` is structured JSON and is always safe to write straight back with set_property; `valueText` is UE export text and for a struct-keyed TMap does not read back, so valueTextRoundTrips reports whether it can be reused (#820). resolvedPropertyName reports the numeric path matched; indexedPath is also returned for keyed paths.

describe_object.summary: Describe a UObject and optionally list/read properties. Per property, `value` is the round-trippable structured form and valueTextRoundTrips flags export text that is not (#820).

play_in_editor.summary: PIE control. A start with a session already active fails with alreadyRunning, and a stop with none active fails with alreadyStopped: neither call changed anything, and the marker names the reason. A flow step that expects either outcome carries ignore_failure: true. pieAction defaults to status. A start waits for the AssetRegistry initial scan by default, since PIE silently no-ops during it on a cold editor (#406).

get_runtime_value.summary: Read PIE actor property. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. propertyName supports dotted paths (component.field or component.struct.field) for nested reads on component subobjects (#344/#381).

get_pie_pawn.summary: Resolve the controlled pawn in a PIE world: pieInstance, else the primary world, or the first client world when the primary is a dedicated server. Returns actorLabel/class/path/location/rotation, the controller's controlRotation, velocity, pieInstance, netMode and the map it is in now, so a read after a level change names the new level (#228/#229/#1565).

list_pie_instances.summary: List the running PIE worlds with their instance id, net mode (standalone|listenServer|dedicatedServer|client), player count and whether they own a game viewport. In a multiplayer PIE session every other runtime action resolves the primary world (the server) unless you pass pieInstance, so this is how you discover that a client exists and what id addresses it (#778).

invoke_object_function.summary: Call a UFUNCTION on any UObject, not just a placed actor. Target it with objectPath, or target=gameinstance|gamemode|gamestate|playercontroller|playerpawn|subsystem (subsystem also needs subsystemClass, and resolves world, game instance, LocalPlayer, engine and editor subsystems; a LocalPlayer subsystem such as EnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem is taken from the local player at playerIndex in the selected PIE instance; playercontroller/playerpawn accept playerIndex). The GameInstance, GameMode and subsystems have no actor label, so invoke_function could never reach them. Returns output and return params under returnValues, with a TArray/TSet/TMap return as real JSON and everything else as export text (#885); an unknown function name lists the available ones, and an args name that is not an input of the function is refused with the inputs listed, rather than being dropped and the call run with that parameter at its default (#1548). propertyPath follows a dotted chain of object-reference properties from the selected root to the object actually called, e.g. target=gameinstance with propertyPath='GameSettings.Game Settings' (Details-panel spellings, array indexes and actor component names are accepted) (#1215). Enum arguments take the enumerator or display name. modify={argument, getter, patch} reads a struct from a zero-argument getter on the same object, applies patch (field names or dotted paths to structured JSON, including TMap fields) and passes it as that struct argument, so read-modify-write of a component's settings struct is one call; the result echoes modifiedArgument and modifiedValue (#1203). A target in a running PIE instance is called in that instance's context (callContext=playInstance, callPieInstance), so a client object's UFUNCTION(Server) is sent through that client's net driver instead of running locally (#1217); netCallspace reports the routing. An editor-world target runs under the editor script-execution guard, which forces every actor callspace to Local; the result warns when that happened, and deferToNextTick=true queues the call for the next engine tick where it routes normally, at the cost of returning before it runs (#973). To click a UMG button in PIE, use widget(invoke_runtime_function) (#1140). (#739)

invoke_object_functions.summary: Call 1-64 UFUNCTIONs in order without yielding to the editor tick loop. Each call independently targets a UObject using the same fields as invoke_object_function, so one sequence can span an actor and its components. Calls stop at the first failure; earlier calls are not rolled back. Returns results[] in call order plus completedCalls/requestedCalls, and failedIndex when it stops early, so a retry can resume instead of replaying mutations.

read_bone_transforms.summary: Read live skeletal bone and socket transforms off an actor, once. This is a point-in-time read, NOT a time series - for per-frame capture over a window use a plugin listed in the plugin registry that provides PIE observation. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Pass bones (bone OR socket names) or omit for every bone up to limit. space=world (default) or component; component space is independent of where the actor is standing. Pass relativeTo (bone OR socket name) to express every sample in that live reference frame; relativeTo supersedes space and is calculated in component space. world defaults to auto. Also reports the AnimInstance class/path (#756/#757/#761/#764).

get_object_properties.summary: Read reflected properties off any UObject, with the same targeting as invoke_object_function: objectPath, or target (plus subsystemClass or playerIndex), then propertyPath to follow object references from there (#1215). Blueprint-declared variables are reflected properties, so they read the same way as native ones. Pass propertyNames to filter; entries may use the Details-panel spelling ('World Context Object' finds WorldContextObject, 'Is Active' finds bIsActive), and an entry with a dot or index is a path read into a struct, subobject or, on an actor, a component ('StashWorld.KickRadiusCm', 'CharacterMovement.GroundFriction'), reported under properties and values by the path as written, with pathErrors naming why a path did not resolve (#1212). Names that do not exist come back under missingProperties instead of silently returning nothing. Properties holding a TMap are also reported under `values` in the structured form set_property accepts, because export text cannot carry a struct-keyed map back (#820). world defaults to auto (#739/#802).

set_movement_mode.summary: Set a live PIE character's movement mode and/or velocity on its CharacterMovementComponent. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Modes are named (none|walking|navwalking|falling|swimming|flying|custom) rather than raw enum numbers, because a wrong number reads as success and then behaves as None. Reports previousMode/previousVelocity and reads the mode back afterwards, since SetMovementMode can refuse a mode the character cannot enter (flying with bCanFly off, swimming outside a volume). world defaults to pie (#757).

set_object_property.summary: Write a reflected property on a live UObject instance, with the same targeting as invoke_object_function: objectPath, or target (plus subsystemClass or playerIndex), then propertyPath to follow object references from there (#1215). Use this for a PIE actor, a spawned widget or any runtime instance: editor(set_property) is the asset path and marks the package dirty and saves it, which a live instance has no business doing. propertyName accepts dotted/indexed/keyed paths and the Details-panel spelling. Reports previousValue plus the value read back after the write, so a coerced or clamped write is visible. Export text naming a struct member the target does not have fails the call and leaves the value as it was. Nothing is saved; pass postEditChange=true to fire PostEditChangeProperty. An object inside a saved package (a Widget Blueprint's WidgetTree template, a Blueprint, an editor level actor) is part of that asset: the write marks it dirty, owner reports asset or level, and package, blueprint, compileRequired and saveRequired say what keeps it (#1544). world defaults to auto (#802).

find_object.summary: Resolve or search for a live UObject instance and report the objectPath that addresses it, which is what invoke_object_function / get_object_properties / set_object_property need. Pass objectPath to check one path (returns found/isValid rather than failing when it is gone), or className and/or nameContains to search every loaded object. className takes a short name (StaticMeshActor), a /Script path, a generated class name (WBP_Hud_C) or a Blueprint asset path. This is how you get the path of something spawned at runtime, an editor utility widget or a UMG widget, which no naming convention predicts. The search is paged: pass back nextCursor as cursor to read the next page (#802).

teleport_runtime_actor.summary: Move a live PIE actor and have it STAY moved. A plain SetActorLocation on a Character is undone by CharacterMovement on the next tick, so this stops the movement component, teleports, and stops it again. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Reports actualLocation read back from the actor rather than what was requested. sweep=true moves along the way and stops at the first blocking hit, reported as blocked and hit. world defaults to pie (#770/#777).

set_runtime_visibility.summary: Hide or show live PIE actors and their scene components, capturing an exact rollback snapshot. PIE-only: world must be 'pie' (the default) and pieInstance picks the world when several are running (see list_pie_instances). Provide exactly ONE actor selector - actorLabels[], actorPaths[] (the unambiguous one) or actorClass; a label matching several actors is refused rather than resolved at random. hidden=true hides, hidden=false shows. componentNames[]/componentClasses[] narrow to matching SceneComponents and imply affectComponents; with no component filter the actor itself is the target. affectActor/affectComponents override that split, propagateToChildren (default true) also takes each matched component's descendants, matchSubclasses (default true) widens class matching, and maxTargets bounds how far the expansion may go. dryRun defaults to TRUE: the call reports what it would change and mutates nothing until dryRun=false. Returns hidden, dryRun, mutationPerformed, matchedActors, targetCount, changed, alreadyDesired, worldPath, pieInstance, netMode, targets[], and on a real mutation a rollbackToken to hand to restore_runtime_visibility.

restore_runtime_visibility.summary: Put back the exact visibility state set_runtime_visibility captured, addressed by the rollbackToken from its response. Run set_runtime_visibility with dryRun=false first; a dry run issues no token. The token belongs to one PIE session and expires with it, so restore before play ends. world, if passed, must be 'pie', and pieInstance must match the token's session. Returns restored, rollbackToken, targetCount, changed, alreadyRestored, worldPath, pieInstance, netMode.

invoke_static_function.summary: Call a project static BlueprintCallable editor UFUNCTION by className, functionName and args, returning its result in returnValues. Works on any reflected class, including actor component classes and UBlueprintFunctionLibrary subclasses (no actor instance). invoke_function needs an actor/component target; this targets the library class CDO instead, so it reaches static *_BlueprintOnly libraries (Voxel sculpt/query/stamp), GeometryScript, Kismet math, any function library. world/pieInstance pick WHICH world fills the context param, so a static that looks a GameInstance subsystem up off its context can be exercised against a live PIE session (#971); the result names the world it ran against and the parameter that carried it. Returns return/out params under returnValues, with a TArray/TSet/TMap return as real JSON and everything else as export text (#885). A project library works the same way: className takes the short name with or without its U (or /Script/Module.Class), args are keyed by parameter name, and every non-const reference out-param comes back under its own name in returnValues, an FString unquoted and whole. Example: void UMyLibrary::PlanZone(const FString& ZoneId, bool bDryRun, FString& OutManifestJson, FString& OutError) is className='MyLibrary', functionName='PlanZone', args={ZoneId:'A1', bDryRun:true}, read returnValues.OutManifestJson and returnValues.OutError. Discover libraries + functions with list_function_libraries.

invoke_function.summary: Call a BlueprintCallable / Exec UFUNCTION on a target actor or one of its components. world=editor (the default) runs the function on the actor placed in the level, no PIE session needed, and reports which instance ran it as resolvedActorLabel/resolvedActorPath. actorLabel is matched against placed actors by editor label first, then internal object name, then full object path; a miss is an error naming what was searched (#806). Returns out/return params under returnValues; a TArray/TSet/TMap return comes back as real JSON and everything else as export text (#885). A PIE target is called in its own instance's context with normal RPC routing (callContext=playInstance, #1217). An editor-world target runs under the editor script-execution guard, which forces every actor callspace to Local, so a UFUNCTION(Server) executes locally instead of being sent; the result warns when that happened, and deferToNextTick=true queues the call for the next engine tick where it routes normally, at the cost of returning before it runs (#973). A component redirects the call to that subobject (#382), and actorArgs fills UObject* parameters from actor labels (#383). An args name that is not an input of the function is refused with the inputs listed (#1548). See #228/#229.

list_function_libraries.summary: Enumerate UBlueprintFunctionLibrary subclasses on this build. Filter by name with pattern (case-insensitive substring, e.g. 'GeometryScript' / 'Kismet' / 'Animation'). Returns name, pythonName (the unreal.* class from ScriptName, e.g. unreal.GeometryScript_List for GeometryScriptLibrary_ListUtilityFunctions), module, and (by default) every static BlueprintCallable function on the library with its pythonName, pythonMethod when it is also a ScriptMethod, and tooltip. pattern also matches the Python name. Use to discover what's available for editor.invoke_function (#455).

set_pie_time_scale.summary: Fast-forward PIE game time. Raises WorldSettings caps and calls SetGlobalTimeDilation.

set_pie_paused.summary: Pause or resume a running PIE instance. mode=game (default) is the game's own pause (UGameplayStatics::SetGamePaused, run in that instance's context), so it resumes a game a startup menu paused, which execute_command 'pause' cannot reach because it runs against the editor world. mode=debug is the editor's Pause/Resume play buttons and applies to every PIE world. A refused unpause names the cause; force=true clears the world's pauser. Reports gamePaused/debugPaused read back after the call plus their previous values, and a rollback to the previous state (#1215).

run_stat.summary: Run a stat overlay. name is a bare stat name (e.g. 'unit','fps','game','gpu') prefixed with 'stat '; command is a full console command and wins over name (#722).

set_scalability.summary: Set rendering quality via the Scalability system (actually applies + persists, not just sg.* cvars). Returns appliedLevels (#591).

get_cvars.summary: Read console variables from the running editor by name, names, or pattern (substring match over every registered variable). Each row carries value, defaultValue, isDefault, type, whether it is a cheat, and `setBy`: the priority the current value was written at, which is what separates a variable sitting at its default from one a scalability group or device profile drove there. A variable set at a higher priority ignores later writes from lower ones. Names that do not resolve come back under notFound rather than as an error (#1006).

set_cvars.summary: Bulk-set console variables, from a {name: value} object or a [{name, value}] array. Returns per-cvar old/new values and any notFound names. Use get_cvars to read one back, including which priority its value was set at (#591).

capture_screenshot.summary: Screenshot. target=pie synchronously captures the selected PIE client game viewport with UMG/Slate UI; target=editor captures the level viewport; target=window synchronously captures a whole Slate window via FSlateApplication::TakeScreenshot - pixel-true for ALL Slate/UMG UI, returns after the PNG is written, and works while the window is unfocused. target=pie and target=window refuse a window Slate is not drawing (hidden, minimized, off screen) with the reason, so no readback is left queued (#1450). Multi-instance PIE automatically prefers a world with a game viewport; pass pieInstance or worldPath to select explicitly, which for target=window is what picks the PIE client window instead of the active editor window. Every mode captures at the source viewport/window size - use capture_scene_png for a chosen output size. outputPath is accepted for filename, so the two capture actions take the same name (#966). Returns the resolved PIE instance/world and image dimensions (#226/#724). target=editor reports cameraLock and a warning when the viewport is piloting an actor or locked to a Sequencer camera, since the image then comes from that actor rather than from a pose set_viewport wrote (#1361). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger.

capture_scene_png.summary: Headless PNG via a transient SceneCapture2D (RGBA8 LDR). Returns captureMetadata with the actual camera transform/basis, FOV, resolution, world/PIE identity and resolved focus actor/bounds. Pair this data with this image; get_viewport_state and hit_test_viewport_pixel refer to a different, live editor camera. Without warmupFrames the capture is synchronous and its actor is destroyed before return; old stray capture actors are swept and reported. warmupFrames=1-240 starts one bounded asynchronous capture using normal streaming from the capture camera, then returns captureId and status=warming. Query this same action with captureId only until complete=true, or add cancel=true. Only the latest warm job is retained; another start while it is active is refused. warmupTimeoutSeconds defaults to 60 (1-120), checked between frames and before export. A completed job reports fileWritten, actual warmupFramesRendered, camera metadata, streaming enablement and textureResidencyVerified=false: warmup does not guarantee highest mip residency. Warm captures require fullyLoadTextures omitted or false, retain temporal rendering state, and leave viewport/config/streaming settings alone. Cancel, timeout, world cleanup and module shutdown release the transient rig. focusActorLabel or focusActorPath auto-frames the camera on that actor's bounds (#599/#662). Pending render updates are flushed before the capture so components created at runtime (BeginPlay attachments, retargeted meshes) are drawn, and for immediate PIE captures captureMetadata.runtimeComponents counts the visible runtime primitives and names any the capture still cannot draw (no render state, or bOnlyOwnerSee, which a capture owned by its own actor never shows) (#1203). A synchronous capture keeps a view state and renders settling passes before the exported frame, so Lumen lighting and auto exposure are converged; exposure is metered from the capture camera itself, not copied from the live view, and captureMetadata.exposure reports it (#1549). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger.

get_viewport_state.summary: Full readout of a level viewport: viewMode, viewportType, fov, nearClip, farClipOverride, exposure (fixed or auto, with the EV100), cameraSpeed, gameView, realtime, location and rotation, plus the view modes this engine build supports. get_viewport reports location, rotation and fov only. Call this before a capture to record the conditions it was taken under, so two captures can be compared honestly.

set_view_mode.summary: Pin the viewport's shading mode (Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, LightingOnly, DetailLighting, ShaderComplexity and the rest this build supports). The single biggest determinism lever for screenshot comparison: Unlit takes lighting out of the picture, Wireframe takes shading out. An unknown name is refused with the full list this engine supports rather than silently ignored. Idempotent: setting the mode it already has reports unchanged, and the previous mode comes back as a rollback.

set_buffer_visualization.summary: Show one scene buffer full screen: Velocity (motion vectors), SceneDepth, BaseColor, WorldNormal, Roughness and the rest this engine's BufferVisualizationMaterials define. target=editor (default) sets a level viewport's buffer; target=pie sets r.BufferVisualizationTarget, which every PIE game viewport reads each frame, and puts the game viewport (or the pieInstance one) in VisualizeBuffer, so capture_screenshot(target=pie) records the buffer. buffer=Overview shows the grid of all buffers; buffer=off returns to viewMode (default Lit). An unknown name is refused with availableBuffers. Reports previousBuffer and previousViewMode with a rollback to them (#1645).

render_mesh_studio.summary: Render a list of static or skeletal meshes and assemblies under isolated studio lighting. Uses a disposable preview world, three broad rectangular lights, a cubemap skylight, fixed exposure and no bloom. Fits the camera to union bounds and optional inventory aspect. Waits across real editor frames for registration, shaders and requested texture mips; both combines beauty with an inverse-opacity matte into RGBA. Writes <id>.png and a job-specific outcome manifest. Returns per-item rendered/blocked/error with file, bounds and camera, cleanupComplete and verified dirtyPackagesUnchanged. Refuses PIE and concurrent runs. Cancels on map changes or PIE start. A changed dirty-package set fails the job without clearing dirty flags or saving. Overwrites matching PNG names in outputDir. The call waits for completion; get_mesh_studio_render reads a known job and cancel_mesh_studio_render stops it. inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the first 8 written images as image content, scaled down when larger.

get_mesh_studio_render.summary: Read a studio render's progress or final manifest by jobId. Retains the last 16 jobs; no preview objects remain after a job finishes.

cancel_mesh_studio_render.summary: Cancel a studio render, destroy its preview scene and write outcomes for unfinished items. Returns completed jobs unchanged.

set_viewport_exposure.summary: Pin the editor viewport to a fixed EV100 instead of auto eye-adaptation. Targets the viewport CLIENT, so it is transient, editor-only and does not dirty the level. This does not pin capture_scene_png's separate SceneCapture2D exposure. Post-process volumes remain asset(set_property) territory. Pass ev100 for a fixed value, or mode='auto' to return to eye adaptation.

set_viewport_view.summary: Set fov, nearClip, farClip, viewportType and cameraSpeed in one call. set_viewport writes only location and rotation and does not write the fov it reads back, which is the gap this fills. Reports a per-field changed flag and the previous values, and rolls back to them. nearClip's rollback is marked lossy because the engine reports the effective plane rather than the override.

set_game_view.summary: Toggle game view, which hides editor-only overlays (grid, gizmos, actor icons, volume wireframes) so a viewport capture shows what the game shows rather than what the editor shows. Idempotent: setting the state it already has reports unchanged.

redraw_viewport.summary: Force the viewport to repaint. A bridge write marks the viewport dirty but does not repaint it, so a capture taken immediately afterwards can show the state from before the write. Use set_realtime instead when a ticking simulation also has to advance.

begin_transaction.summary: Open an undo transaction so a run of writes collapses into ONE undo step. General-purpose, unlike material(begin_transaction) which is material-scoped. Nesting is reported rather than refused. Pair with end_transaction to commit or cancel_transaction to discard.

end_transaction.summary: Commit the open undo transaction and return its index in the undo buffer. Ending with nothing open reports that rather than erroring, so a flow that already closed one is safe to replay.

cancel_transaction.summary: Discard the open transaction and restore every object it touched. This is what makes 'do several writes, detect a failure partway, abort, leave the editor unchanged' possible at all; material's begin/end pair had no cancel, so an aborted flow could only ever commit. Cancelling with nothing open reports that rather than erroring.

get_undo_state.summary: Report canUndo and canRedo plus the DESCRIPTION strings of what an undo or redo would actually apply, the queue length, the undo count and the current index. Look before you undo, instead of undoing and reading back a bare boolean.

undo_redo_steps.summary: Undo or redo several steps at once, returning appliedDescriptions: the titles of the transactions actually reversed or reapplied, which is how you confirm you undid what you meant. Stops early with a stated reason rather than silently doing fewer steps, and refuses while a transaction is open.

get_transaction_history.summary: Read the undo buffer itself, newest first: per entry the index, title, id, record count, byte size and primary object, and whether it is applied or undone. currentIndex splits the applied entries from the undone ones. Use it to find the transaction a later cancel or undo should target.

start_trace.summary: Start an Unreal Insights trace. Writes a .utrace and REPORTS WHERE IT LANDED (traceFile, plus the exact UnrealInsights command that opens it); editor(analyze_trace) reads it back once the trace is stopped. Defaults to a timestamped file under <Project>/Saved/Profiling so the path is deterministic rather than invented by the engine. Idempotent in the way that matters here: a trace that is ALREADY running is reported as alreadyTracing rather than quietly starting a second one, because only one connection exists per process. A channels list where nothing resolves is refused with the closest channel names. Rollback: stop_trace.

stop_trace.summary: Stop the running trace and report the finished file: absolute path, byte size, and the UnrealInsights command line that opens it. The destination is only readable while connected, so it is captured before the stop rather than lost by it. Stopping when nothing is running reports wasTracing=false rather than erroring, so a replayed flow is safe. Warns when profiling regions were still open, since those have no end event in the file.
