The rollback is LOSSY and says so: restarting writes a NEW .utrace and cannot reopen this one.

pause_trace.summary: Pause or resume the running trace by muting every active channel, without closing the file. Idempotent: pausing an already-paused trace reports changed=false. Rollback restores the previous state.

get_trace_status.summary: Read the whole trace system: tracing, paused, systemStatus, connectionType, destination, activeChannels, byte and memory statistics, the channel presets start_trace accepts, whether UnrealInsights is on disk, every profiling region still open, and whether a bridge-launched standalone run is alive.

list_trace_channels.summary: Every trace channel this build registers, with its enabled state and, on UE 5.7+, its description, id and read-only flag. This is what makes start_trace's channels parameter discoverable instead of guesswork.

set_trace_channels.summary: Turn named trace channels on and off, including mid-trace. Validates the WHOLE request before applying any of it, so a typo cannot leave a half-configured trace recording something other than what was asked for, and an unknown name comes back with the closest real ones. Each channel reports wasEnabled, enabled and changed read back from the trace system rather than assumed, so a read-only channel refusing at runtime is visible instead of silent. Rollback restores exactly the channels that moved.

begin_profile_region.summary: Open a named bracket around an operation so it can be measured. Times wall clock unconditionally and, on UE 5.7+ with a trace running, also emits an Insights timing region; when it cannot emit one it says so in tracedReason rather than pretending. The name is the key: opening the same name twice reports the existing region rather than nesting two begins under one end. Rollback: end_profile_region.

end_profile_region.summary: Close a named bracket and return what it measured: durationMs and the number of rendered frames it spanned. A region spanning zero frames says so, because a CPU-versus-GPU verdict cannot describe work that ran inside one tick. Ending a region that is not open reports wasOpen=false and lists the ones that are, rather than erroring. No inverse exists and the response says why.

add_trace_bookmark.summary: Drop a named marker on the Insights timeline. Reports recorded=false with the reason when no trace is running or the Bookmark channel is off, instead of returning a success for an event that was dropped. Deliberately NOT idempotent: a bookmark is a point event, so two calls write two markers and the response says so.

get_frame_timing.summary: Frame timings WITH A VERDICT: gameThreadMs, renderThreadMs, rhiThreadMs, swapBufferMs, per-thread wait time, frameMs and fps, and GPU min/avg/max drained from the RHI's own history, then bound = gpu | cpu-game | cpu-render | cpu-rhi | balanced | unknown with the arithmetic that produced it spelled out in verdict. Says unknown when the RHI published no GPU timing rather than guessing. warnings[] names the conditions that make the numbers meaningless and the exact call that fixes each, including the unfocused-editor CPU throttle, which is a plain UPROPERTY and is therefore REPORTED here with its objectPath for editor(set_property) instead of getting a typed setter that would duplicate a working path. sampleWindow states what was actually measured: a handler runs inside one tick and cannot advance frames to build a window.

trigger_hitch.summary: Stall the game thread for a known number of milliseconds, so hitch-detection logic can be tested against a hitch whose size is known in advance. Brackets the stall with a trace region and a bookmark so it is findable in the capture. Capped at 5000ms because this blocks the same thread the bridge answers on. Sleeping consumes no CPU, so it reads as a long frame rather than as game-thread work. No inverse: time does not come back.

analyze_trace.summary: Read a recorded .utrace back and summarise it, through the engine's TraceServices analysis (the module Unreal Insights is built on). Returns frames {count, avgMs, p50Ms, p95Ms, p99Ms, minMs, maxMs, avgFps, framesInTrace}, hitches over hitchThresholdMs (default 50) in time order, worstFrames each with its top CPU timers by exclusive time, topTimers over the window by inclusive (default) or exclusive time with per-frame figures, gpu busy time per frame when the trace carries GPU timing (present=false with the reason otherwise, e.g. a -nullrhi editor), and bookmarks with their time and frame. file defaults to the newest .utrace under Saved/Profiling; startSeconds/endSeconds narrow the window; threads=game (default) aggregates the game thread only, all every CPU thread. Lists are bounded and say when they were cut; dumpToFile writes the whole analysis to JSON and returns the headline numbers with outputPath. A trace still being written is refused: stop it first. Long traces analyse on worker threads and report progress while the call waits. Needs UE 5.7+.

start_csv_profile.summary: Start a named CSV profiler capture (the per-frame stat recorder behind csvprofile start) and wait for it to begin, then return csvPath, the file it is writing. captureName names the file (default <Project>_<timestamp>), folder defaults to Saved/Profiling/CSV, maxFrames ends it by itself after that many frames. A capture already running is reported as alreadyCapturing with its file instead of being queued behind it. Rollback: stop_csv_profile.

stop_csv_profile.summary: End the running CSV capture and wait for the profiler to finish writing it, then return csvPath, csvBytes and capturedFrames. Stopping when nothing runs reports wasCapturing=false (and the last capture's file) rather than erroring. Read the file with editor(summarize_csv_profile). The rollback starts a NEW capture; a finished CSV cannot be reopened.

launch_standalone.summary: Launch the project as a separate -game process, optionally tracing, so frame times come from a real game process rather than from the editor. Passing channels (or traceFile) adds -trace and -tracefile, and the response carries the .utrace path plus the UnrealInsights command that opens it. Idempotent: a bridge-launched run that is still alive is reported as alreadyRunning rather than joined by a second. When the editor runs offscreen, the game is launched offscreen too. The process is detached and its output is not read; poll get_standalone_status. Rollback: stop_standalone.

get_standalone_status.summary: Is the bridge-launched standalone run still alive: running, processId, commandLine, uptimeSeconds, the exit code once it has ended, and its .utrace path with the command that opens it. Only reports runs this bridge started; one launched another way is not tracked.

stop_standalone.summary: Terminate the standalone run this bridge launched, killing its process tree so nothing is left holding the .utrace open. Stopping when nothing is running reports wasRunning=false rather than erroring. Termination is not a graceful quit and the response says what that costs. No inverse: relaunching is a new run.

set_realtime.summary: Toggle realtime update on the level editor viewports so the editor-world sim (Niagara, anims) ticks - otherwise capture_scene_png renders an unticked, empty sim (#537).

hit_test_viewport_pixel.summary: Ray-cast from a screen pixel through the active editor viewport and return the first hit. Builds the ray from the live viewport's projection matrix (no FOV/aspect guessing). width and height override the viewport size when picking from a different-resolution screenshot. Returns hit + actorLabel/actorClass/componentName/componentClass/materialPath/location/impactPoint/normal/distance/faceIndex/boneName/physicalMaterial (#418).

get_runtime_values.summary: Bulk runtime read across the active world. For each actor/component matching classFilter, resolves every path against the (actor|component) root and returns rows of {actorLabel, actorClass, componentName?, componentClass?, values, errors?}. Paths support property hops, sub-object hops, and BlueprintCallable getter calls at any segment (e.g. 'PowerConnector.GetRequired' reaches a UFUNCTION on a UObject sub-object). A getter that takes arguments is written with them inline, 'GetMirroredTallyWeight(overclock)' or 'GetBalance(gold, 2)', which is what makes a keyed accessor readable across every matched instance in one call; the literals are coerced by the same rules invoke_object_function's args use, so FName/FString/int/float/bool/enum all read (#969). classFilter matches actor class OR component class - omit to match everything. An actor whose own class does not match answers with one row per matching component, so two InstancedStaticMeshComponents on one actor are two rows; matched counts rows and matchedActors the actors. componentName roots every path at the component with that instance name (case-insensitive) and skips actors without one, so two components of the same class are addressable apart (#1113). The first segment of a path may also name a component by instance name (case-insensitive) or by class when only one component has it ('CharacterMovementComponent.GroundFriction'); a segment that resolves to nothing lists the actor's components with their classes and the properties it could have been (#1204). To enumerate a live actor's components, use level(query_components, world='pie', actorLabelContains=...). A path whose result is a TArray/TSet/TMap comes back as real JSON rather than one string (#885). World defaults to PIE if running, else editor (#414).

set_viewport.summary: Set the viewport camera, its projection and its orthographic zoom. The projection is switched BEFORE the requested pose is applied, because the viewport keeps a separate transform cache per projection and writing the pose first would hand back the camera from the mode you just left. Every value is validated before anything is written, and the rollback restores the projection and zoom as well as the location and rotation. Acts on the active level viewport (#1029). When the viewport is piloting an actor or locked to a Sequencer camera the pose snaps back on the next tick, so the result carries cameraLock {kind: pilot|cinematic, actorLabel, actorPath} and a warning (#1361).

focus_on_actor.summary: Focus on actor. Pass actorLabel or actorPath (#983).

create_sequence.summary: Create Level Sequence. displayRate sets its display rate up front (#1641).

get_sequence_info.summary: Read sequence: bindings (possessable/spawnable) with their Sequencer tags (#556), each possessable's parentGuid, each spawnable's template class and transform, and each binding's and root tracks with class, name and displayName (the label Sequencer shows, such as the rig on a Control Rig track) and every section's class, range, isActive and rowIndex (#1644), plus a SkeletalAnimation section's animation: clip, offsets and play rate (#1641). includeSectionDetails adds blendType, attach sockets and each channel's key times and default value, which is what a constant transform with zero keys evaluates to. UNITS: playbackRange is reported in TICKS (tick resolution, commonly 24000/s), while MovieSceneScripting*Channel.add_key defaults its time_unit to DISPLAY_RATE. Keys authored with a tick number under the default unit land roughly 800x past the range and the track evaluates to its first key, which presents as transforms that do not work on a structurally perfect sequence (#881).

add_sequence_track.summary: Add an empty track. actorLabel or actorPath binds it to an actor; omit both for a master track (#983). trackType MaterialParameterCollection (MPC) needs materialParameterCollection, the collection asset the track animates (#1407).

add_sequence_section.summary: Add a section to a track (creating the track if needed), set its start/end in seconds, and for a CameraCut track bind it to a camera. actorLabel or actorPath scopes the track to an actor binding. Returns the section index, its range, the channel names to key, and trackCreated. A track that is created with a section of its own gets that section rather than a second overlapping one (reusedDefaultSection) (#548/#983/#1232). On a SkeletalAnimation track, animation sets the clip, startFrameOffset/endFrameOffset trim it in ticks, and playRate scales it; without endSeconds the section spans the clip after those, and the result's animation object reads them back (#1641).

set_sequence_keyframes.summary: Add keyframes to a section channel. Transform channels: Location.X/Y/Z, Rotation.X/Y/Z (or friendly x/y/z, yaw/pitch/roll); Fade/Float: the float channel (#548). interpolation is cubic, linear or constant, and a keyframe's own interpolation field wins (#1232). For any other channel use set_sequence_channel_keys.

get_sequence_channel_keys.summary: Read a section's channels through its channel proxy: every key (tick, displayFrame, seconds, value, interpolation) and the channel default, for one channel or all of them. Works on any section, including the MovieSceneParameterSection of an MPC track, whose channels are named Intensity, Tint.R/G/B/A and so on. The track is chosen by trackType and/or trackName (trackIndex when several match) among the root tracks, or within a binding via bindingGuid, bindingName or actorLabel/actorPath; nothing is created. sampleStartFrame/sampleEndFrame/sampleStep also evaluate the curve at display frames, which replaces baking the channel through Python (#1407).

set_sequence_channel_keys.summary: Write keys and the default value of one named channel on any section, through its channel proxy. keyframes take seconds, frame (display) or tick, a number or boolean value, and an optional per-key interpolation (cubic, linear, constant). clearExisting replaces the whole key set; defaultValue/clearDefault set or remove the default. On an MPC track a name the section does not animate yet is added first, its type read from the collection (parameterType overrides it, and names it on other MovieSceneParameterSection tracks). Validates every key before writing, reads the channel back, and reports keysVerified plus any mismatches. Rollback rewrites the channel with its previous keys and default (#1407).

remove_sequence_section.summary: Remove one section from a track by sectionIndex, using the same track selector as get_sequence_channel_keys. Reports the removed section's class and range and the section count before and after. The rollback is the editor undo of the removal's transaction, valid while it is still the latest on the undo stack (#1232).

resolve_sequence_bindings.summary: What every binding of a Level Sequence resolves to in the editor world right now: bound objects with world transforms, possessedClass, parentGuid, and stale=true for a possessable that resolves to nothing. Filter with bindingGuid or bindingName. Use it to find bindings whose actors were re-created (#1356).

rebind_possessable.summary: Retarget an existing possessable binding to a current level actor without destroying it: the binding guid is kept, so its tracks and every reference to it (camera cuts, attach sections) stay valid. Child component possessables follow the matching components on the new actor (by binding name, then componentMap, then a unique component of the possessed class). Verifies by resolving the binding again and fails when it does not resolve to exactly that actor; children report verified per child. renameBinding renames it to the actor label. The sequence is marked dirty, not saved. Rollback rebinds the previous actor when there was one (#1356).

get_sequence_runtime_bindings.summary: Every LevelSequenceActor in a world (auto: PIE when running, else editor) with its sequence, playback state (isPlaying, isPaused, currentTime), overrideInstanceData and instance-data transform origin, and for each binding of its player the bound objects with world transforms. This maps a PIE actor to the player and binding that own it, which tells it apart from the duplicates an open Sequencer editor spawns (#1232).

get_sequence_binding_components.summary: The components of every Level Sequence binding with their property values, without opening or evaluating the sequence. A spawnable is read off its object template (legacy spawnable or custom binding), a possessable off the actor or component it resolves to in the editor world; a Blueprint class contributes the construction script templates the template holds no instance of. Each component reports name, class, path, source (instance, blueprintClassTemplate, bound) and properties. propertyNames takes C++ or Python spelling and dotted paths, ["*"] reads every editable property, and the default is the primitive rendering flags (CastShadow, bAffectDynamicIndirectLighting, bAffectDistanceFieldLighting, bVisibleInRayTracing, bHoldout, LightingChannels, custom depth and stencil, visibility). Names a component lacks go to missingProperties when asked for. Filter with bindingGuid, bindingName and componentClass (#1640).

set_sequence_playback_range.summary: Set a Level Sequence's playback range in seconds (#548).

set_sequence_display_rate.summary: Set a Level Sequence's display rate, the frame grid Sequencer shows, frame-based scrubbing reads and bakes sample at. displayRate is frames per second (23.976, 29.97 and 59.94 map to the NTSC rates) or {numerator, denominator}. Keys and ranges are stored in ticks and keep their times. Returns the new and previous rate; rollback restores the previous one (#1641).

play_sequence.summary: Play/stop/pause a Level Sequence in Sequencer. Pass sequencePath (or assetPath) to target a specific sequence - it is opened first, because the underlying Sequencer commands act on whatever is currently open. Omit it and the call applies to the open sequence and says so. sequenceAction defaults to play.

scrub_sequence.summary: Park the Sequencer playhead on an exact time and evaluate there, then return. This is what makes scrub-then-capture_scene_png deterministic: play_sequence only offers play/pause/stop and realtime playback races the capture. Pauses first, scrubs, and forces the evaluation before answering, because the playhead move alone does not write possessed-actor transforms. Pass exactly one of seconds or frame. frame is read in timeUnit: display (default, the frame numbers Sequencer shows) or tick (the units get_sequence_info's playbackRange reports). Returns the evaluated time in all three units plus displayRate/tickResolution/playbackRange, and warns when the time is outside the playback range (#881).

render_sequence_frames.summary: Render a Level Sequence to a PNG image sequence in ONE call: for each frame it scrubs, forces the evaluation, and captures through a transient SceneCapture2D (RGBA8 LDR, real PNG), instead of scrub_sequence + capture_scene_png per frame. Camera: the sequence's camera cuts by default (frames with no active cut are skipped and reported), or cameraActorLabel/cameraActorPath for one camera actor, or location/rotation/fov for a fixed camera. The camera's own FOV and post process are used. Range is in display frames: startFrame and endFrame (inclusive), or startSeconds and endSeconds (end exclusive); default is the playback range. frameStep skips frames. More frames than maxFrames is refused. Files are written to outputDir (absolute or project-relative, default Saved/SequenceFrames/<sequence>) as <sequence>.<frame>.png. Refused while PIE runs. The playhead is restored afterwards and playback is left paused. A run that nears the 600s timeout stops, returns truncated=true and nextStartFrame. Returns files[], frames[] with per-frame evaluateMs/captureMs/exportMs/totalMs, and timing totals (#1098). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the first 8 written images as image content, scaled down when larger.

mrq_create_job.summary: Add a job to the editor's Movie Render Queue (needs the Movie Render Pipeline plugin): sequence to render, map to render in (default the open level, which must be saved), and either a preset (a MoviePipelinePrimaryConfig copied into the job) or a graph (a MovieGraphConfig, Movie Render Graph). For a preset job, outputDirectory, fileNameFormat, width+height, format (png | jpg | exr | bmp, replacing the job's other image outputs) and startFrame+endFrame (display frames, end exclusive) are applied to the job's own configuration copy, never the preset asset; a deferred render pass is added when it has none and existing output is overwritten on rerun. A graph job takes those from its graph, so they are refused with a graph. A job name already in the queue reports existed=true and changes nothing. Rolls back through mrq_delete_job.

mrq_list_jobs.summary: List the Movie Render Queue's jobs: name, sequence, map, enabled, consumed, status and progress, configMode (preset or graph) with the graph or preset origin, and for preset jobs the output folder, file name format, resolution, custom range, output formats, render passes and every setting class. isRendering says whether the queue is rendering now.

mrq_delete_job.summary: Delete a Movie Render Queue job by jobName or jobIndex. Refused while the queue renders. A name no job has reports alreadyRemoved=true. Rolls back through mrq_create_job with the job's sequence, map, name, preset or graph and output folder, marked lossy since other edits to its configuration copy are not in the record.

mrq_render.summary: Render Movie Render Queue jobs in the editor through the PIE executor: jobNames, or every enabled job. The chosen jobs render even when consumed by an earlier render, and the queue's enabled flags are put back afterwards. wait=true (default) answers when the render ends, reporting progress while it runs, with render.outputs (the image and video files written since it started), the Movie Render Pipeline's warnings and errors, rendered and cancelled; cancelling the call cancels the render. wait=false answers once it starts; follow it with mrq_get_render_status and mrq_list_outputs. Refused while PIE runs or another render is in progress. No inverse: delete the files listed to undo it.

mrq_get_render_status.summary: Status of the Movie Render Queue render in flight (render) or of the last one (lastRender): jobs with their progress and status message, overall progress, elapsedSeconds, the pipeline's warnings and errors, and once finished its outputs, rendered and cancelled. isRendering reads the queue subsystem directly.

mrq_cancel_render.summary: Cancel the Movie Render Queue render in progress; every job in it stops after the frame in flight and frames already written stay on disk. alreadyStopped=true when nothing was rendering. No inverse: mrq_render starts it again.

mrq_list_outputs.summary: List the image and video files under a Movie Render Queue output folder, newest first: a job's output folder (jobName), any folder (outputDirectory), or by default the folders of the last render, else of every queued job. Tokens other than {project_dir} and {engine_dir} cut the scan at the folder before them. Each file has path, sizeBytes and modifiedUtc.

validate_assets.summary: Run data validation over a directory (default /Game/) or over exact assets named by assetPath or assetPaths, one selector per call.

get_log.summary: Read output log. maxLines selects how far back into the ring buffer to read (default 100, or the whole buffer when filter or category is given); limit pages the lines that match filter/category within that window, and each line carries the sequence number that anchors a cursor.

search_log.summary: Search the captured log. Every match in the 4096-line ring buffer is collected and paged, so a busy log reports how many matched instead of stopping at the first hundred. maxResults caps the search itself and reports cappedAtMaxResults when it was what ended the collection.

run_map_check.summary: Run Map Check on the open level, the same pass as Build > Map Check without its results window, and return the messages it wrote: severity, text, the objects each names and the actorLabel of the first actor, with errors, warnings and total counts. Each run starts a fresh MapCheck page, so the messages are this run's (#1828).

log_map_check_message.summary: Add an error, warning or info message to the MapCheck listing, optionally linked to an actor (UMapCheckSubsystem::LogMapCheckError, LogMapCheckWarning and LogMapCheckInfo on UE 5.9, the same FMessageLog write before it). Read it back with get_message_log logName=MapCheck; the next run_map_check starts a fresh page (#1828).

add_python_path.summary: UE 5.9: put an existing absolute folder on the editor Python's sys.path, optionally under an owner name and with a mountPointRoot that gives generated types stable names (UPythonScriptLibrary::AddAdditionalPath). A path already registered is reported as existed; the rollback removes it. Refused when the path is already on sys.path from another source (#1828).

remove_python_path.summary: UE 5.9: take a registered additional path off sys.path (UPythonScriptLibrary::RemoveAdditionalPath), or with only owner every path that owner registered (RemoveAdditionalPaths). Modules already imported stay loaded. Reports removedPaths, or alreadyRemoved when nothing was registered (#1828).

list_python_paths.summary: UE 5.9: the additional Python paths registered to every owner (UPythonScriptLibrary::GetAllAdditionalPaths), or to one owner (GetAdditionalPaths, with ownerRegistered) (#1828).

get_message_log.summary: Read a Message Log listing (MapCheck, AssetCheck, PIE, LoadErrors, LightingResults...). Call with NO logName to list the registered listings with their error/warning counts, then read one. Counts come from the listing itself; message bodies come from the current page and honour the Message Log tab's severity checkboxes, so when fewer are readable than exist the response says so instead of reading clean. An unknown logName is an error, not an empty log. Blueprint COMPILE results are not here - the compiler makes a listing per Blueprint; use blueprint(compile).

list_crashes.summary: List crash reports, sorted by folder name, which is chronological.

set_dialog_policy.summary: Arm an answer, in advance, for dialogs whose title or message contains a pattern. READ THIS BEFORE USING IT: an armed policy presses the button for you, so from then on a matching prompt is answered and dismissed and the user never sees the question. On a save prompt that means unsaved work can be discarded without anyone reading the warning. Nothing arms a policy on your behalf - the plugin ships none and no other action arms one - so every policy in effect is one somebody typed here deliberately, and this is the only way the bridge ever answers a dialog by itself. Covers the Slate modal windows the editor raises itself (the shutdown "Save Content" prompt among them, whose buttons are Save Selected / Don't Save / Cancel). A response keyword (yes/no/ok/cancel/retry/continue/yesall/noall) resolves to whichever of the dialog's buttons carries that meaning, so response='no' presses "Don't Save"; pass buttonLabel to name a button literally instead. On a plain message dialog buttonLabel answers with the button it names (buttonLabel="Yes" answers Yes); where that dialog has no such button, a label or response answers with the nearest one it offers (yes is OK on an OK/Cancel dialog, no is Cancel), and one with no equivalent there leaves the dialog for a person (#1334). A policy set here answers a matching dialog whoever raised it, and answers one that is already on screen. To read a dialog instead of pre-answering it, use editor(list_dialogs) and then editor(respond_to_dialog).

get_dialog_policy.summary: Get the dialog policies currently armed, each with its response and literal buttonLabel. Every one was armed by a caller through set_dialog_policy: the plugin arms none of its own, so an empty list means nothing will answer any dialog on its own.

list_dialogs.summary: Read the modal dialog blocking the editor, in full: its exact title, its COMPLETE message text (never truncated - messageTruncated is always false), every button label in the order the dialog lays them out, and a `choices` array pairing each button with the exact editor(respond_to_dialog) call that presses it. When the dialog asks a question per row (the "Save Content" prompt is a checkbox per unsaved package), an `items` array reports each tickable row: its index, its label, its cells (asset name, package path, class path) and whether it is currently ticked. `blocks` is the same body in reading order without the title or button labels: paragraphs, and each list as a table {columns, rows, checked, items} (#1891). `combos` reports each drop-down picker (an SComboBox, STextComboBox or SComboButton over a list, such as the DataTable Options dialog's Import As and row type pickers) with its index, the label beside or above it, its current value and its `options`; a picker that builds its menu only on opening has optionsReadable false. `textFields` reports each editable text box with its index, label, value and readOnly. A checkbox labelled from beside it (a details panel's bool property) carries that label as `fieldLabel`. Each choice carries `enabled`: a disabled button, such as Apply before a row type is chosen, is one respond_to_dialog will not press. No button is marked recommended and none is reordered; choosing is yours. Also reports which armed policy matches and which button that policy would press, if any. `blocksGameThread` says whether the editor is actually held: true only for a window on Slate's modal stack, which is what parks the game thread and refuses every other action. A prompt the editor raised without AddModalWindow comes back with `blocksGameThread` false and `detectedBy` parentedWindow - it is reported, because an unanswered question must not be quit out from under, and nothing is refused for it (#1118). `notTreatedAsDialogs` names any window the walk considered and rejected, with the reason: a standalone Message Log or an undocked Output Log is a regular parented window like a dialog is, and used to block every action for the life of the session with no button that could answer it (#1078). A window in that list is NOT blocking anything. Also reports `windows`: every open modal and floating window with the windowId editor(list_windows), press_window_button and close_window take. Runs even while a dialog is blocking the editor, when every other handler times out, so this is the way to see what the editor is asking. A native Windows dialog of the editor process (a GPU device loss, an assert or ensure box, a startup prompt), which the plugin cannot see and which stops the bridge from answering, is read from outside the editor and listed alone, with detectedBy nativeWindow and `native` {hwnd, pid, kind, summary, details}: details carries the GPU state lines from the editor log after a device loss.

respond_to_dialog.summary: Press one named button on the active modal dialog, releasing the game thread. This is the deliberate way to answer a dialog: read it with editor(list_dialogs) first, then name the button you chose. Runs even while the dialog is blocking the editor. ONLY IN auto MODE. The dialog handling mode decides who answers, and it is enforced here: under interactive the question is put to the person in an elicitation form (raised on the call AFTER the one that hands the dialog back, so its text is read somewhere nothing truncates it) and only their button is pressed, under defer they answer it in the Unreal Editor window, and in both this call is refused with the dialog named. editor(list_dialogs) stays available in every mode, so the dialog can always be READ. Pass dialogAction='close' (or 'escape') to destroy the dialog window when no button label fits, which ends the modal without answering the question. It is NOT called 'action': that name is this tool's own dispatch field, so a call writing action='close' selects a nonexistent editor action and never reaches the dialog (#1078). Pass items to tick or untick the dialog's own rows before the button is pressed, which is what makes "Save Selected" mean something: read them from editor(list_dialogs) and send [{index, checked}] for the ones you want changed. The ticks and the press happen in this one call, so a modal is never left holding a selection nobody pressed anything on. Pass combos [{index, option | optionIndex}] to choose a picker's option and textFields [{index, text}] to type into a text box, with the indices list_dialogs reports: pickers are set first (choosing one can change which other fields the dialog shows), then text fields, then items, then the button. Each goes through the widget's own selection and commit handlers, so the dialog's state really changes; a picker that does not end up showing the option is an error and nothing is pressed. combos or textFields may be sent without a button, to set them and read the dialog again before pressing. A disabled button is refused rather than pressed. On a native Windows dialog of the editor process (list_dialogs reports `native`), the named button of that window is pressed by its handle from outside the editor, under the same mode rule; such a dialog is answered with one of its buttons, never closed.

list_windows.summary: Every open modal and floating editor window except the main window, each with a windowId, its title, isModal, isActiveModal, receivesInput, hasParentWindow, hostsDockTabs, isVisible, gatesBridge (true for the window the dialog gate is refusing calls for), its visible texts, and its buttons with index, label, toolTip and enabled state. Reaches what list_dialogs does not: a second prompt behind the first, a floating Message Log or asset editor, a window behind a notification. Served while a dialog is blocking the editor. Pass windowId to describe one window (#1231).

press_window_button.summary: Press one button of an open window, by buttonLabel or buttonIndex from editor(list_windows). Refuses a disabled button, a label matching more than one button, and a window that does not receive input while another window is modal. Served while a dialog is blocking the editor. ONLY IN auto MODE, like respond_to_dialog (#1231).

close_window.summary: Close an open window the way its own close box does: a floating dock area asks its tabs first, and a modal ends unanswered. Served while a dialog is blocking the editor. ONLY IN auto MODE, like respond_to_dialog (#1231).

open_asset.summary: Open asset in its editor. A map opens as the editor world through level(load), so it refuses while the open map has unsaved changes unless saveFirst or discardUnsaved is passed (#1259).

get_open_asset_editors.summary: What the user currently has open in the editor, and which of it holds focus. Returns every open asset editor with its asset path/class, its window and major tab label, and its own tabs - so an open PCG Graph, the Blueprint graph documents someone has open, and the Details panel they are looking at all come back by name. Unreal publishes no single answer to this: the asset editor subsystem knows what is open, the global tab manager knows the active tab, and each tab knows when it was last activated, and nothing joins them. focusedAssetEditor is the editor holding Slate's active tab, activeTab.context says whether that tab is in an asset editor, the Level Editor or elsewhere, and mostRecentlyActiveAssetEditor is where the user last was. Read editorApplicationFocused before trusting the word focused: an agent driven from a terminal has taken OS focus away from Unreal, so Slate's active tab is a record of where the user was rather than where their cursor is, and focusNote says which of the two this answer is. Reads only - it never focuses or opens anything, which editor(open_asset) is for (#1112).

reload_bridge.summary: Hot-reload Python bridge handlers from disk.

save_dirty.summary: Flush every dirty package and return a per-package saved/failed map. Use after multi-step CDO/component edits when set_class_default leaves the asset dirty without persisting (#378). The emptied external package of a deleted World Partition or one-file-per-actor actor is deleted from disk rather than failed, and listed under deleted (#1301). The bridge keeps that package loaded from the delete until a save commits it, so a garbage collection in between no longer loses the delete (#1545). With commitDeletes=true it uses the editor's own dirty-package save instead, which deletes the external package of a deleted World Partition actor rather than failing with 'SavePackage returned false', and reports written, deleted and stillDirty per package (#1156).

configure_pie.summary: Set ULevelEditorPlaySettings - multi-client PIE, net mode, single-process flag, Play-in-New-Window resolution (#384/#671), and multiplayer client window placement: clientWindowWidth/clientWindowHeight size each additional client window, newWindowPosition {x,y} places new PIE windows and turns centerNewWindow off unless it is passed too (#1235). playMode viewport | new_window | standalone sets where the Play button and every bridge PIE launch play; the default is the active level viewport (#1526). Reports every setting read back after the write with its previous value, and a rollback to the previous values. get_pie_config reports the same fields.

get_pie_config.summary: Read current ULevelEditorPlaySettings (numClients, netMode, single-process, separate-server) (#384).

pose_debug_camera.summary: Eject and aim the PIE debug camera (ToggleDebugCamera free camera) for verification shots. Moving the DebugCameraController actor is overridden by its free camera, so this poses what the camera follows: the spectator pawn (moved with its velocity stopped) and the control rotation. location and rotation set the pose, lookAtActorLabel/lookAtActorPath aim at an actor's bounds center, enabled=false returns control to the player. Reports the camera location and rotation read back from the camera manager and a rollback to the previous state (#1250).

set_pie_view_target.summary: Make an actor the running PIE player's view target (PlayerController SetViewTargetWithBlend, run in that instance's context), so a spawned CameraActor frames capture_screenshot(target=pie) even in a map with no possessed pawn, which pie_set_player_view cannot do. Select the actor with actorLabel or actorPath in the PIE world; playerIndex picks the player, blendTime blends instead of cutting. Reports the view target read back, pendingViewTarget while blending, the previous target, and a rollback to it (#1203).

pie_set_player_view.summary: Point the running PIE player's view (control rotation) at a pitch/yaw/roll so a capture frames the intended direction. Requires PIE (#671).

stage_game_input.summary: Stage input for the running game: set input mode (gameOnly|gameAndUI|uiOnly) and mouse cursor so injected/simulated input reaches the pawn. This only sets the mode; pie(inject_input) injects the input. Requires PIE (#671).

run_automation_tests.summary: Run registered Automation tests matching a filter and return per-test pass/fail plus error lines. Runs them synchronously through the test framework rather than the console queue, and suspends the editor's unfocused-CPU throttle for the duration - otherwise an unfocused editor drops to a few FPS and the framework's interactive-frame-rate gate never opens, leaving tests queued forever (#765). A test whose latent commands are still queued when latentTimeoutSeconds runs out is reported as abandoned, with the reason: latent work needs engine frames, and this runs on the game thread, so a test that starts PIE (CQTest multi-client network tests, for instance) belongs in the editor's Automation window or -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests <name>" at launch. Such a test used to terminate the editor outright (#993). Afterwards it clears the dirty flag on /Temp world packages the run dirtied that no world context still uses, so a test that left its world behind does not block level(load) or prompt on shutdown, and lists them in tempWorldsCleared; nothing is saved or deleted (#1488) (#693).

list_dirty_packages.summary: Enumerate currently-dirty content + map packages, read from the editor's own dirty-package lists (the same ones Save All uses). Includes a never-saved /Temp world, because an unsaved new map is exactly the unsaved work a caller needs to see before closing or reloading (#340).

discard_dirty.summary: Clear the dirty flag on the packages named, so closing the editor does not stop on unsaved state nobody wants. Only packages in packages are touched, all or nothing: one refusal clears none. Transient packages and /Engine maps (their built data and external actors too), such as the /Engine/Maps/Entry startup map that cannot be saved, are always allowed. Project and plugin content, never-saved /Temp maps and engine content outside a map are refused unless allowContent=true, because their unsaved edits are lost when the editor closes; code and PIE packages are always refused. Each package is reported as cleared, notDirty, refused (with a reason) or, under dryRun, wouldClear, with its kind, and remainingDirty lists what the editor's close prompt would still ask about. The edits stay in memory until the editor closes. editor(stop_editor, discardTransient=true) runs this for every disposable package before the quit.

get_world_state.summary: One atomic read of which world is open and what is unsaved. Returns editorWorldName, editorWorldPackage, persistentLevelPackage, worldPackageDirty, a sorted dirtyPackages list with counts, and the editor/play/simulate mode. level(get_current) plus editor(list_dirty_packages) is two calls, so the editor can change between them and neither result proves which world the other described; this answers both in one game-thread dispatch. Read-only, and fails closed rather than reporting an empty world as a clean one (#920/#921).

epic_add_assets_to_collection.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Adds assets to the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_call_cheat.summary: [Epic CheatsToolset.CheatsToolset] Runs a cheat on the local player, exactly as if it were typed into the console. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_capture.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Renders offscreen from the given world and camera using the specified mode. Use ListModes for names available in this build and session; DescribeMode supplies interpretation and sub-modes. Unknown or unavailable modes raise a script error. Mode names are case-sensitive. Availability does not validate scene content or every pass prerequisite. Uses world post-process volumes, with no temporal history or camera-specific post-process overrides. This is not a live viewport screenshot. PNG output is an opaque, display-encoded 8-bit visualization, not a raw or HDR buffer export. Capture timings are not representative game-frame timings. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_capture_active_editor_view.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Captures the active editor camera offscreen using the requested mode, without changing the viewport. Repeated calls follow viewport movement; use GetActiveEditorView plus Capture for a fixed camera. Mode, Options, output format and rendering limits are the same as Capture. Does not reproduce temporal history, editor overlays or camera-specific post-processing. This is not a viewport screenshot. Use DescribeMode for diagnostic guidance. Raises a script error if no active editor level viewport is available. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_capture_asset_image.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Renders a thumbnail for the specified asset (e.g. static meshes, skeletal meshes, skeletons, animations, montages, materials, textures).

epic_capture_editor_image.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Captures an image of the entire editor application as the user sees it.

epic_capture_editor_viewport.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Redraws and captures an editor viewport with its view and post-process state: a level viewport or an asset editor viewport such as the Static Mesh or Skeletal Mesh Editor's. Restores camera and show flags on return; temporal history may advance or be affected by camera overrides. Asymmetric projections return the image with a warning and no camera snapshot or image FOV. Raises a script error for an unavailable/unreadable viewport or unsupported HDR encoding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_capture_game_viewport.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Captures the current Game or PIE viewport as Slate draws it, with UMG and any other UI over the viewport, such as the recording border. In PIE it redraws the window that holds the viewport; if that fails, the image shows the scene only, with a warning. Metadata records the world and request time, not the originating GPU frame, camera, mode or internal resolution. Output is an opaque 8-bit PNG, not a raw or HDR buffer export. PQ/scRGB HDR uses the engine screenshot decoder and sRGB8 image conversion. Conversion clips highlights and out-of-gamut channels without an additional tone curve. A warning identifies this conversion. Other HDR output encodings are rejected. Raises a script error if the host cannot render, or if no initialized, readable Game/PIE framebuffer is available. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_capture_viewport.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Captures the level viewport with optional annotations. Annotations rendering overlays a projected 3D world-space grid plus name + position labels on visible actors. The grid is drawn at a configurable ground-plane Z and projected through the camera, with coordinate numbers at intersections (shown in meters). Each labeled actor gets a crosshair at its projected screen position with a leader-line callout placed to avoid overlap. This gives a vision-capable agent spatial awareness: it can reference grid coordinates to direct placement and identify scene contents by label. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_center_view.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Re-centres the Rewind Debugger visible view range on Time, preserving the current view width. Independent of the scrub cursor: pair with SetScrubTime when you want to both move the cursor and bring it into the centre of the visible timeline. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_close_editor_for_asset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Closes every asset editor open for the specified asset. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_collection.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Creates a new static collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_describe_mode.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Describes a mode's purpose, interpretation, limits, registered sub-modes and default. Accepts the same names and aliases as Capture. Unknown names raise a script error. Availability covers capture-path and session prerequisites, not per-world content or pass activation. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_destroy_collection.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Deletes the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_execute_python.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Runs a Python script in the editor's interpreter on the game thread. IMPORTANT: Call `read_me` once per conversation before using this tool, for full usage instructions -- including how to compose other tools and yield control during long-running work. Look up each `unreal` API with search_symbols or get_symbol before calling it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_exit_editor.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Requests a shutdown of the editor application. The request is queued for the next editor tick so this call can return first; the process then exits and no further tool calls are possible. Errors if any level or content package has unsaved changes and bDiscardUnsavedChanges is false. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_focus_on_actors.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Repositions the level editor camera to focus on the specified actors. Cannot be called while PIE is active.

epic_get_active_editor_modes.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the IDs of the currently active editor modes. More than one mode can be active at once; the default placement mode ("EM_Default") is usually present. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_active_editor_view.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Snapshots a level editor viewport's world, camera and clipping planes: ViewportId's, or the active one. Asset editor viewports are refused, since Capture cannot render their preview worlds. Pass World and Camera to Capture. Match SourceDimensions' aspect ratio to retain framing; letterboxing is excluded. The snapshot does not follow viewport movement. Requires an interactive editor session and an active level viewport. Raises a script error if the viewport is unavailable, has zero size or uses an unsupported projection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_asset_editor_selection.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets what is selected inside the asset editor for the given asset (e.g. selected graph nodes in a Blueprint or Material editor, selected widgets in a UMG editor, and objects shown in the editor's details panels). This is distinct from level-actor selection (GetSelectedActors) and content-browser selection (GetSelectedAssets). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_asset_thumbnails.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the assets' existing cached thumbnails (the images the Content Browser shows) without loading or rendering the assets. On success the result's value holds one image per requested path, in request order; an entry is an empty image when the asset has no saved thumbnail or its thumbnail could not be decoded. The call completes with an error instead if any requested path cannot be found. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_camera_transform.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the position and rotation of the level viewport camera.

epic_get_collection_assets.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the assets in the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_content_browser_path.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the current path of the active content browser.

epic_get_csv_info.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Surveys a capture without returning per-frame values. StatGroups (the group histogram) is always populated; individual stat names only when StatNameFilter is set. GroupDepth groups the histogram by the first N segments of the '/'-delimited stat tree: depth 1 buckets under "Exclusive", depth 2 under "Exclusive/GameThread". Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_cvar_value.summary: [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Reads the current value of a console variable as its canonical string representation (e.g. "true"/"false" for bools, "1.5" for floats). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_frame_timings.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Reads the engine's per-frame timing globals once (no smoothing - usually the previous frame). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_frame_tree.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Captures the latest stat frame as a nested tree. Siblings sorted most-expensive first. Top-level entries are typically thread roots (GameThread, RenderThread). On leaves, ExclusiveMs equals InclusiveMs. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_log_categories.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Returns a sorted list of registered log categories. On UE 5.9 it calls ConsoleToolset.LogsToolset.GetLogCategories.

epic_get_log_entries.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Returns log entries from the current session's log file. On UE 5.9 it calls ConsoleToolset.LogsToolset.GetLogEntries.

epic_get_object_events.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns all events that fired on a recorded object within a time range. Events represent discrete occurrences such as Linguine prompt executions. Returns {"Events": []} when no session is active or no events exist in the range. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_object_properties.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the recorded property state of an object at or before a given time. Uses closest-before semantics: returns the most recent snapshot at or before Time. Returns {} when no session is active or no snapshot exists before Time. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_open_assets.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the list of assets currently open in asset editors.

epic_get_pivot_location.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the current location of the editor's transform-gizmo pivot. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_recent_transactions.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Returns transactions from the undo history, newest first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_selected_actors.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the currently selected actors in the level editor.

epic_get_selected_assets.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the list of assets selected in the content browser.

epic_get_selected_object.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the object currently selected in the Rewind Debugger outliner, if any. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_selected_outliner_folders.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the folder paths selected across all open scene outliners. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_session_info.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the current Rewind Debugger session state. Call this first to confirm a session is active before querying object data. Always returns all fields; IsActive is false when no session is loaded. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_show_flag.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Reads whether a named engine show flag is currently enabled on the active level editor viewport. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_stat_counters.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Samples every non-cycle counter in a stat group for a single frame: integer/float counters and memory pool sizes (draw calls, primitive counts, LLM tags, etc). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_symbol.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Returns the documentation of a registered tool, or of a type, function, method, or property in the `unreal` Python API. Pass a toolset or full tool name, a top-level name ('EditorActorSubsystem', 'log'), or a qualified 'Class.member'. A toolset returns its description and the signature of each of its tools. A tool returns its signature, description, and parameters. A function or member returns its signature and full documentation. A type returns its description, then one line for each editor property (inherited ones included), enum value, and method it declares, and how many methods it inherits from each base; get_symbol on 'Type.member' or on a base gives the details. A struct only tools use returns its fields and the tools that use it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_trace_event_details.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the full decoded JSON for a single trace event from a named source. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_transaction_details.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Returns detailed information about a single transaction Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_transaction_recency_index.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Returns how far back a transaction is in the undo history, counted newest-first: 0 is the most recent transaction, 1 the next, and so on. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_verbosity.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Returns the current verbosity level for a log category. On UE 5.9 it calls ConsoleToolset.LogsToolset.GetVerbosity.

epic_get_video_info.summary: [Epic MediaToolset.MediaToolset] Reads container metadata. Windows Media Foundation is required. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_visible_actors.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns all actors in the current level whose bounds intersect the viewport frustum.

epic_is_pierunning.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] True for active PIE or simulation, including online login before world creation. A queued start alone returns false.

epic_list_cheats.summary: [Epic CheatsToolset.CheatsToolset] Lists the cheat commands available on the local player. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_collections.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Lists all collections in the content browser. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_editor_modes.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Lists the IDs of all registered editor modes (e.g. "EM_Default", "EM_Landscape", "EM_Foliage"), ordered by mode priority. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_editor_viewports.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Lists the open level and asset editor viewports, with ids to pass as Options.ViewportId or to CaptureEditorViewport. Only a viewport with bIsVisible set presents frames, so ask the user to bring any other to the front first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_events.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Returns the capture's events with their frame indices. Repeats of the same event name on one frame collapse into a single entry carrying a Count. FrameEnd -1 runs to the end; the defaults return the whole run. At most Count events (the first in frame order) are returned. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_modes.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Lists canonical names of modes that can capture in this build and session. Aliases are not listed separately. Availability reflects capture-path, build, session and project prerequisites, not scene content. Buffer-visualization targets incompatible with the capture output format are omitted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_object_trace_events.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Lists trace events attributed to ObjectId within [StartTime, EndTime], aggregated across every registered IRewindDebuggerToolsetEventDecoder. Returns lightweight rows; call GetTraceEventDetails to decode a specific event in full. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_objects.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Lists all objects recorded in the current session, optionally filtered by class name. Each entry includes an ObjectId for use with GetObjectEvents and GetObjectProperties. Returns {"Objects": []} when no session is active or no objects match the filter. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_show_flags.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Lists every engine show flag with its display name and editor group. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_stat_groups.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Enumerates registered stat groups. Names are STATGROUP_-prefixed and match the argument accepted by GetStatCounters. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_viewport_recordings.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Lists this session's viewport recordings, including the active one. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_views.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Snapshots actors with active camera components and player camera managers in the given world. Preserves custom perspective near planes and explicitly configured orthographic clip planes. A player view whose transform, active lens and clipping match a listed view marks that entry as a player view instead of adding one. Lists player views first, then the remaining actor cameras. Returns empty when no views exist; an invalid world raises a script error. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_worlds.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Lists Editor, PIE and Game worlds in the engine's world contexts, including non-renderable worlds. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_open_editor_for_asset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Opens an asset editor for the specified asset.

epic_read_image_file.summary: [Epic MediaToolset.MediaToolset] Reads up to 64 MiB of encoded PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, or WebP data without re-encoding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_read_me.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Usage instructions for execute_python. Call this once per conversation before using execute_python. Explains the execution environment (namespace, async/await, composing other tools) and, only when relevant, the spatial coordinate-conversion helpers available in the current editor session. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_read_stat_values.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Returns up to Count per-frame values of one stat, starting at FrameStart. An over-large Count clamps to the stat's own length rather than erroring; Count = -1 reads to the end of the column. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_record_viewport.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Records a viewport for DurationSeconds, then completes with the finalized file. Canceling the call stops the recording early and keeps the file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_reduce_stat.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Reduces each requested stat to average, min, max, total, and the P50/P90/P95/P99 percentiles over a frame-index range. FrameEnd -1 runs to the end; the defaults reduce over the whole run. Stats not present in the capture are omitted from the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_assets_from_collection.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Removes assets from the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_run_console_command.summary: [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Executes an arbitrary UE exec command. Output is written to the session log. Python is refused: any command containing "py" as a whole word (the py command, including when wrapped by defer, redirecttofile, etc.) is rejected. Run Python with the Python scripting tool instead. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_sample_frames.summary: [Epic MediaToolset.MediaToolset] Samples midpoint-spaced frames in a time range. Windows only. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_screen_coords_to_world.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Finds the world position of the nearest solid object at a given set of normalized view space coords.

epic_search_console_commands.summary: [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Returns exec commands whose name contains the search string (case-insensitive). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_search_cvars.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Finds all console variables that contain a given name. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_search_cvars__console_toolset.summary: [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Finds all console variables that contain a given name. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_search_symbols.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Searches the registered tools and the `unreal` Python API for types, functions, methods, and properties. Searches what this editor session provides, so every result exists here. Feed a result's qualified_name to get_symbol to read it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_search_transactions.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Searches the undo history by transaction label using a fuzzy (edit-distance) match, closest match first. When two transactions match a query equally well the more recent one is returned first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_actors.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Selects the specified actors in the current scene.

epic_select_asset_editor_objects.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Sets what is selected inside the asset editor for the given asset, replacing the current selection. Supported for Blueprint editors (graph nodes) and Widget editors (widgets and graph nodes); raises for material editors and other asset types whose selection cannot be set. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_assets.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Selects the specified assets in the content browser. Completes once the content browser has applied the selection.

epic_select_object.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Selects a recorded object in the Rewind Debugger panel and opens the details panel so its state and timelines are visible to the user. Use after ListObjects to surface a particular object when reporting findings. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_select_outliner_folders.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Selects the specified folders in every open scene outliner. Replaces the existing folder selection; non-folder selections (e.g. selected actors) are preserved. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_camera_transform.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Sets the position and/or rotation of the level viewport camera. Anything not provided keeps its current value.

epic_set_content_browser_path.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Navigates the active content browser to the specified folder path.

epic_set_cvar_value.summary: [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Sets the value of a console variable. The value is parsed according to the variable's declared type. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_editor_mode.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Activates the specified editor mode. Pass "EM_Default" (or an empty string) to return to the default placement/select mode. Cannot be used during PIE. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_pivot_location.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Sets the location of the editor's transform-gizmo pivot. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_scrub_time.summary: [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Moves the Rewind Debugger scrub cursor to a specific recording time. The engine clamps to the recording's range. Disables auto-scroll-with-recording so the timeline stays put. Does not re-centre the visible view range; pair with CenterView to do that. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_show_flag.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Toggles a named engine show flag on the active level editor viewport (e.g. "Navigation", "Collision", "Grid", "Bounds", "Fog", "Landscape", "Volumes"). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_verbosity.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Sets the verbosity level for a log category. On UE 5.9 it calls ConsoleToolset.LogsToolset.SetVerbosity.

epic_set_viewport_view_mode.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Sets the view mode of the active level editor viewport (e.g. Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, Lighting-only, complexity visualizations). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_show_notification.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Shows a transient editor notification (Slate toast, bottom-right). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_skim_video.summary: [Epic MediaToolset.MediaToolset] Samples midpoint-spaced frames over the video's known duration. Windows only. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_start_pie.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Starts PIE or simulation in the current level, then waits for warmup. Local single-player worlds usually exist at PostPIEStarted; deferred online login delays warmup until a world exists. The whole request has a 30-second timeout. Errors if a session is active or queued.

epic_start_viewport_recording.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Starts recording a viewport to an MP4 as the user sees it and returns at once; StopViewportRecording finishes it. One recording runs at a time, and it also ends on its own at MaxDurationSeconds or when the viewport goes away. The red border at the frame edges is the recording indicator, not scene content. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_stop_pie.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Stops PIE or simulation and waits for shutdown. Normally handled on an editor tick; pending online login defers shutdown until a world exists. Errors if no session is active.

epic_stop_viewport_recording.summary: [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Stops a recording and completes once its file is finalized. A recording that already ended returns its result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_top_stats.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Ranks the capture's stats by a reduced aggregate (average, max, total, or a P50/P90/P95/P99 percentile) over a frame range and returns the top Count, each already reduced. A StatNameFilter wildcard restricts the ranking to a group (e.g. "GPU*"); empty ranks all stats. FrameEnd -1 runs to the end; the defaults rank the whole run. Ranking is by raw aggregate value with no unit normalisation, so an unfiltered ranking mixes unit domains (byte counters rank alongside millisecond timings). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_trigger_gpuprofile.summary: [Epic PerfToolset.GpuProfilerToolset] Captures the next rendered frame's GPU work as a nested tree (2-3 frame latency). Top-level entries are GPU queues (Graphics, Async Compute); each contains its passes as a recursive subtree. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_world_pos_to_screen_coords.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Converts a world-space position into normalized screen space based on the editor viewport camera.

tools.name: epic
tools.description:
Unreal's AI Toolset Registry itself: discovery (status/list_toolsets/describe_toolset), turning toolsets off and on (get_toolset_states/set_toolset_enabled), direct dispatch (call_tool), and the registry's own meta-tooling (agent skills, programmatic tool batching). Also Epic's Unreal MCP plugin's own tools and resources (list_mcp_tools/call_mcp_tool, list_mcp_resources/read_mcp_resource). Toolsets that map to a real editor domain are NOT here - unless nativeTools withholds them, they appear as epic_* actions on that domain's category (GAS in gas, Sequencer in animation, Dataflow in dataflow, and so on), so reach for the domain tool first and use this one to introspect or call the registry directly. A toolset no recorded catalog has (one a launcher plugin or a newer plugin version adds, or a newer engine's) has no epic_* action but is still listed by list_toolsets and runs through call_tool: check here before concluding the editor cannot do something. Requires UE 5.8+ with the ToolsetRegistry plugin enabled - call epic(status) first to check availability. The ai_assistant_* actions drive Epic's in-editor AI Assistant (UE 5.9+ with the AI Assistant plugin): send a message and get the reply, read a conversation, and read its update events; check ai_assistant_status first.

Call epic(action, args={...}). Actions:
status()
list_toolsets(nameFilter?, includeSchemas?:b)
describe_toolset(toolset)
get_toolset_states(nameFilter?)
set_toolset_enabled(toolsets:[s], enabled:b)
call_tool(toolset, tool, input?:o, inputJson?)
list_mcp_tools(nameFilter?, includeSchemas?:b, includeRegistryAdapters?:b)
call_mcp_tool(tool, input?:o, inputJson?)
list_mcp_resources()
read_mcp_resource(uri)
ai_assistant_status()
ai_assistant_send_message(message, conversationId?, hiddenContext?, reply?:b, wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n)
ai_assistant_get_conversation(conversationId?, wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n)
ai_assistant_get_request(requestId:i)
ai_assistant_get_events(sinceSeq?:i, conversationId?)
epic_create_markdown_knowledge_base(alias, description, relativePath)
epic_create_skill(folderPath, assetName, description, details:o)
epic_execute_tool_script(script)
epic_get_docked_context()
epic_get_execution_environment()
epic_get_knowledge_entry(alias, entryId)
epic_get_project_context()
epic_get_skills(skillPaths:[s])
epic_list_knowledge_base_tags(alias, prefix, limit?:i)
epic_list_knowledge_bases()
epic_list_skills()
epic_query_knowledge_base(alias, text, tags:[s], limit?:i)
epic_update_skill(skillPath, description, details:o)
epic_write_knowledge(alias, fileId, summary, tags:[s], bodyJson, entryId)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

status.summary: Report whether Epic's ToolsetRegistry is available and how many toolsets are registered. Never errors (reports available=false with a reason when the plugin is absent).

list_toolsets.summary: List registered toolsets: name, version, description, tool names + count. Strips the verbose per-tool input/output schemas to stay small - use describe_toolset for those (or includeSchemas).

describe_toolset.summary: Full schema for one toolset: every tool with its input/output JSON schema.

get_toolset_states.summary: Every registered toolset with its enabled state, including the disabled ones list_toolsets leaves out: for each, the block and allow patterns that match its name (blockedBy, allowedBy), outsideAllowList, disabledBy (blockList, allowList or noVisibleTools) and toggledHere when set_toolset_enabled wrote its pattern. Also the registry's live blockedNames and allowedNames, the settings' copies, and the config file they are saved to. UE 5.8+ with the ToolsetRegistry plugin, Win64 editor.

set_toolset_enabled.summary: Turn registered toolsets off or on by exact name, effective at once: a disabled toolset leaves list_toolsets and its epic_* actions, and call_tool refuses its tools. Off adds the pattern /^\Qname\E$/ to the registry's block list; on removes it, and adds the same pattern to a non-empty allow list that does not match. Applied to the live registry and saved to UToolsetRegistrySettings (Config/DefaultGame.ini on 5.9, DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini on 5.8), so the next session starts the same way. Unknown names are refused with validNames; a toolset blocked by a pattern this action did not write is refused rather than edited. A toolset already in the asked state reports unchanged. Rollback restores the previous state.

call_tool.summary: Execute a registered Epic tool exactly as its MCP server would. toolset takes the qualified toolset name from list_toolsets and is required, e.g. GASToolsets.AttributeSetToolset; tool takes the tool's name from describe_toolset, bare or qualified, e.g. GASToolsets.AttributeSetToolset.ListAttributeSets; pass the arguments as input, or as inputJson to send raw JSON. Returns the tool's JSON result; images its output schema marks (FToolsetImage) come back as MCP image content. A tool that answers later reports progress while it runs.

list_mcp_tools.summary: List the tools Epic's Unreal MCP plugin serves beside the registry: legacy MCP Tool Library Blueprints (source toolLibrary) and tools other plugins register (source plugin). Its adapters onto the registry are counted, not listed, since list_toolsets covers them; includeRegistryAdapters lists them too. available=false and no tools when the plugin is not enabled.

call_mcp_tool.summary: Run a tool from list_mcp_tools exactly as Epic's MCP server would: input as an object, or inputJson. Text and structuredContent come back as JSON, images and audio as MCP content. A long tool reports progress, and cancelling the call reaches the tool's CancelAsync.

list_mcp_resources.summary: List the resources registered with Epic's Unreal MCP plugin: uri, name, title, description, mimeType. Empty when no provider is registered or the plugin is off. This server also serves them as MCP resources.

read_mcp_resource.summary: Read one resource from list_mcp_resources by uri: contents with its text, or its blob as base64.

ai_assistant_status.summary: Report whether Epic's AI Assistant API (UAIAssistantInstance, UE 5.9+ with the experimental AI Assistant plugin) is loaded: engineVersion, available, and when it is not, errorCode unsupported_engine_version or PLUGIN_NOT_AVAILABLE with the reason. When available, lists its UFUNCTIONs, whether the singleton exists, whether conversation updates are being recorded, and pendingRequests. Never errors.

ai_assistant_send_message.summary: Send a user message to Epic's AI Assistant, as UAIAssistantInstance::SendTextMessageAndGetReply (reply=true, default) or SendTextMessage (reply=false). Empty conversationId starts a new conversation. Opens the assistant panel, which needs the editor's Epic sign-in to answer. Waits (default 300s) and returns state complete with reply (and conversationId: the one the reply names, or on builds whose reply is bare text the first update event's, when none was given) or, with reply=false, the conversationId the message was bound to; wait=false returns state pending and a requestId for get_request. A timeout fails with state timed_out and keeps the requestId. Engines before 5.9 return unsupported_engine_version.

ai_assistant_get_conversation.summary: Read an AI Assistant conversation as Epic serializes it (UAIAssistantInstance::GetConversationJson): conversation is the parsed JSON (conversationJson when it does not parse). Empty conversationId reads the active conversation. Does not open the assistant panel, and fails while it is closed (send_message opens it). Waits like send_message (default 60s).

ai_assistant_get_request.summary: One poll of an AI Assistant request that send_message or get_conversation opened: state pending, complete (with its reply, conversationId or conversation) or failed (errorCode ai_assistant_failed, assistantError). A complete or failed answer releases the request; an unknown or released requestId returns ai_assistant_request_not_found.

ai_assistant_get_events.summary: Conversation updates UAIAssistantInstance::OnConversationUpdated reported (Started, MessagesUpdated, Complete, Stopped), each with seq, conversationId and utc, oldest first; pass the last nextSeq as sinceSeq to read only newer ones. Recording starts once the assistant instance exists (after a send_message or get_conversation, or the panel's own use); listening=false says it has not started. Does not open the panel.

epic_create_markdown_knowledge_base.summary: [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Creates an empty markdown base under the project's Content/KnowledgeBases folder, writes the marker file that lets it be rediscovered on restart, and registers it. An empty base is valid; the first WriteKnowledge creates its first file. Raises an error if the alias is already registered or not a valid identifier, if RelativePath is not one or two plain segments, if the directory already belongs to another base, or if it cannot be written.
