Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_skill.summary: [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Creates a new AgentSkill. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user.

epic_execute_tool_script.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.programmatic.ProgrammaticToolset] Execute a Python script against the toolset APIs. Use this to batch multiple tool calls into a single script execution, reducing round-trips and context usage. IMPORTANT: Available modules and usage instructions are described by the value returned by `get_execution_environment`. You MUST call `get_execution_environment` once in the conversation before using this tool. Read the value in the `instructions` field in the returned environment info prior to calling this function, so that you understand what APIs are available and how to use them. Before writing a script that calls multiple tools, look up the output schemas (if available) for any tools you plan to use. This returns the JSON schema describing each tool's return value, so you know how to parse results and pass data between calls. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_get_docked_context.summary: [Epic AIAssistantEditor.AIAssistantToolset] Returns the UE tab layout and editor context in the window hosting the assistant. Tab information is available for tool windows with no asset editor. The result is empty when the assistant is closed or detached from a window. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_execution_environment.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.programmatic.ProgrammaticToolset] Get details about execution environment. This includes instructions on how to write scripts, and constraints, such as what modules may be imported and the script entrypoint and function signature. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_get_knowledge_entry.summary: [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Returns one entry by id with its full body. Ids are exact, so take them from QueryKnowledgeBase hits rather than composing them; a miss names the nearest ids the base holds. Raises an error if the alias is not registered or no entry has that id. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_project_context.summary: [Epic AIAssistantEditor.AIAssistantToolset] Returns important information about the current project and/or current user. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_skills.summary: [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Returns detailed information about a specific set of AgentSkills.

epic_list_knowledge_base_tags.summary: [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Lists the tags a base's entries carry, most common first, so a Tags filter is spelled from what exists rather than guessed. Tags are exact strings: "simulation" does not match "Simulation". Raises an error if the alias is not registered or the base fails to build. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_knowledge_bases.summary: [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Lists every registered knowledge base. Call this first: aliases are the handle every other tool takes and they vary by project. Choose a base by its Description. A base with a "vocabulary" consumer is the catalogue that tool's input is spelled from, so query it before calling that tool. Builds nothing. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_skills.summary: [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Gets a summary of all AgentSkills in the project.

epic_query_knowledge_base.summary: [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Searches one base. Text is matched as plain words and ranked; Tags keep only entries carrying all of them; both empty lists the whole base. Bodies are truncated; GetKnowledgeEntry returns a hit's full payload. Raises an error if the alias is not registered or the base fails to build. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_update_skill.summary: [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Updates an existing AgentSkill. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user.

epic_write_knowledge.summary: [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Writes a structured entry into a markdown base as a JSON block, preserving the prose and other blocks in the file. An existing EntryId is replaced in the file that holds it, wherever that is; an empty EntryId appends a new entry to the file FileId names, creating the file if absent. Reuse the stem of a hit's Source as FileId so a topic accumulates rather than sprawls. Only markdown bases are writable; check bWritable in ListKnowledgeBases first. Raises an error if the alias is not registered, the base is read-only, BodyJson is not a JSON object, or the file cannot be written. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

tools.name: fab
tools.description:
Fab (Epic marketplace) content in the editor. Searching the Fab catalog and importing listings, free ones included, is what Epic's built-in Fab tools do (the Fab plugin's FabToolset.FabToolset, UE 5.9). They are declared here as epic_* actions from the recorded catalog, and list_epic_tools lists the ones this editor actually has with the call that runs each. ue-mcp's own actions add: plugin/login status, login/logout, syncing your owned library into the Content Browser, downloading and verifying owned UE packs with pause/resume, inspecting/clearing the native cache, installing verified Content safely, importing local source files, and opening the fab.com search page at a query.

Call fab(action, args={...}). Actions:
list_epic_tools(includeSchemas?:b)
status()
login()
logout()
sync_library(batchSize?:i)
list_owned(query?, offset?:i, limit?:i)
download(listingId, engineVersion?, platform?, outputDirectory?, verifyOnly?:b)
download_status(jobId?)
pause_download(jobId)
resume_download(jobId)
cancel_download(jobId)
install_pack(jobId)
remove_installation(jobId)
list_cached()
cache_info()
clear_cache()
import_file(source|sourceFile, destination|destPath)
open_search(query, listingType?, assetFormat?, free?:b, open?:b)
epic_fab_sign_in()
epic_get_fab_listing_details(listingId)
epic_install_fab_listing(listingId, assetFormat, engineVersion?, distributionMethod?, title?, fileId?)
epic_search_fab_listings(keywords?, sortBy?, bFreeOnly?:b, assetFormats?, count?:i, cursor?, listingTypes?, categories?, sellers?, excludedSellers?, licenses?)
epic_search_fab_my_library(keywords?, assetFormats?, sortBy?, count?:i, cursor?, listingTypes?, categories?, sellers?, excludedSellers?, licenses?)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

status.summary: Report Fab plugin state: authenticated (whether a native Fab session is available), whether the plugin is installed and enabled (pluginDir, pluginVersion), whether the module is loaded, whether the native import/cache API is linked in this build, whether the Fab window has been opened this session, the download cache location/size, and librarySync state with pages, snapshotItems, publishedRows and any sanitized failure. The launcher installs Fab as its own 'Fab UE Plugin' item, so an engine can lack it; then errorCode is PLUGIN_NOT_AVAILABLE and note says what is missing and how to install it, the same reason the other Fab actions refuse with. Call this first.

login.summary: Open the native Fab EOS account portal. With a session already active it opens nothing and answers unchanged=true. Returns before authentication completes; finish any prompt, then poll status.authenticated. No inverse: opening a portal does not own the resulting account session. idempotencyObservable=false because this call cannot attribute a later login to itself.

logout.summary: Request native Fab logout and clear this editor's owned-library snapshot. EOS completes asynchronously; poll status.authenticated until false. No inverse: cleared credentials require a person to sign back in.

sync_library.summary: Sync the owned Fab library into the native Content Browser table (UE 5.8+). Requires a native login. Returns immediately; poll status.librarySync until complete or failed. Fetches all pages before replacing the previous snapshot, preserving it on HTTP, JSON, pagination or publication failure. No project files change.

list_owned.summary: Read the current account's synced owned metadata and supported projectVersions, with local title filtering and pagination. Each row adds listingId (what download takes) and availableForThisEditor (this editor's engine and platform are among its projectVersions). Complete sync_library first; before it, errorCode FAB_NOT_SIGNED_IN or FAB_LIBRARY_NOT_SYNCED says which step is missing. Only the owned library: to search the public catalog use Epic's built-in Fab tools (list_epic_tools).

download.summary: Start an owned native UE asset-pack download. engineVersion and platform default to this editor's; a listing without that build answers with the versions it offers. Returns job immediately; poll download_status for complete or failed. Native BuildPatchServices verifies SHA hashes and reuses partial staging. Defaults to the native Fab cache. verifyOnly checks an existing tree without repairing it. Repeat the same listing/version/outputDirectory after an editor restart to resume. No project content changes until install_pack.

download_status.summary: Read asynchronous job state, native phase, progress, required/downloaded bytes and failure code; omit jobId to list this editor session's jobs. No tokens or signed URLs are returned.

pause_download.summary: Stop network/assembly work while keeping native verified files and staging. Wait for paused before resuming. Can pause distribution resolution too.

resume_download.summary: Resume a paused, failed or cancelled job. Reuses the native Fab session and obtains a fresh distribution signature before native verification and repair.

cancel_download.summary: Cancel a job while retaining its verified data for an explicit later resume. Does not delete downloaded or installed content.

install_pack.summary: Copy a completed, SHA-verified pack's native Content packages into this project, preserving package paths. Checks every source and collision first; different existing files are refused. Skips identical files and installs no Config, engine plugins or settings. Records exactly which files it created for remove_installation.

remove_installation.summary: Remove only unchanged, unloaded project files that this session's install_pack job created. Refuses modified or loaded packages before deleting anything; preserves pre-existing identical files.

list_cached.summary: List the entries currently in the local Fab download cache (already-downloaded owned assets).

cache_info.summary: Report the Fab download cache location, total size, and entry count.

clear_cache.summary: Delete the local Fab download cache to reclaim disk. Does not affect assets already imported into the project. Reports unchanged=true when the cache was already empty (where the native Fab API is linked). No inverse: the downloads come back only by downloading them again.

import_file.summary: Import a source file into the project through the Fab Interchange import pipeline. Use for owned assets that are downloaded/cached locally, or any local source file (fbx, textures). Single files import synchronously and report the created asset paths; pack/quixel workflows may run asynchronously. A synchronous import rolls back by deleting exactly the assets it created, taken from the paths the importer reported (a force delete, because the imported set references itself). An ASYNCHRONOUS import emits no inverse: its paths are not known yet, and a record naming the destination folder would delete whatever else already lives there.

open_search.summary: Open fab.com's own search page at a query in the user's default browser. Builds https://www.fab.com/search?q=<query>&listing_types=<listingType>&asset_formats=<assetFormat>&is_free=1, leaving out unset filters. This action itself sends no request to Fab and returns no listing data; to search the catalog and import listings from the editor, use Epic's built-in Fab tools (list_epic_tools). open=false returns the URL without opening it, for showing as a link. Returns url and opened.

epic_fab_sign_in.summary: [Epic FabToolset.FabToolset] Starts Fab sign-in by opening the Epic account portal in the user's system browser. Only needed when another tool reports that nobody is signed in. Sign-in normally persists across editor restarts, so this is usually a one-time step per machine. This does NOT wait for the user to finish. It returns as soon as the browser has been asked to open, with status "browser-opened". Tell the user a browser window has opened and they need to complete sign-in there. Do NOT claim they are signed in - call search_fab_my_library afterwards to find out. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_fab_listing_details.summary: [Epic FabToolset.FabToolset] Reads the full details of one Fab listing: description, tags, licenses and their prices, rating. Use this after search_fab_listings or search_fab_my_library, when the user asks what something actually is or does, or what it costs. The listingId comes from one of those results. Reports description (possibly shortened - descriptionTruncated says so), tags, licenses, assetFormats, free, limitedTimeFree, freeUntil, rating, publishedAt, fabUrl, and mature when it is 18+ content. Each license carries name, licenseId and free and, when Fab prices it, price and priceCurrency - with discountedPrice, discountPercentage, effectiveDiscountPercentage, lowestPriorPrice and discountEndDate during a sale. Rules for reporting this: - Describe what a listing contains only from its description and tags. Never add content they do not name, even when the title or seller suggests it. When descriptionTruncated is true, say the rest was not read rather than guessing at it. - These tools return no images: a search result's thumbnailUrl is a link you have not seen. If you do see a listing's images and they show something the description does not name, tell the user it appears in the images but not in the description, rather than stating it as part of the listing. - limitedTimeFree true means one of its licenses has a discountedPrice of 0 until freeUntil (UTC). free stays false. That license's price is its price without the discount. To install such a listing, the user must first add it to their library from fabUrl, while it is free; then install it from search_fab_my_library. Do not call install_fab_listing for it before that. - It does NOT report supported engine versions. If the user asks about compatibility, read engineVersions from the search_fab_listings result instead. Do not say the listing supports no engine versions, and do not guess. - It does not report ownership either. Use search_fab_my_library for that. - aiTrainingForbidden true means the seller forbids using it to train AI models. Refer to https:www.fab.com/eula and section "Content that May Not be Used As Training Input Into Generative AI Programs." in there for more information about this restriction. - Prices are per license, in the user's Fab account currency, as the Fab website shows them. Fab may add VAT or other tax at checkout in some regions, so do not say whether a price includes tax. Say which license a price is for, and quote it with its priceCurrency. free at the top level means at least one license costs nothing. - A license with free false and no price is one Fab did not price: nobody is signed in, or Fab could not price it. Send the user to fabUrl for the price; do not retry. - During a sale, discountedPrice is what the user pays until discountEndDate. lowestPriorPrice is the lowest price in the 30 days before the sale, and effectiveDiscountPercentage the discount measured from it rather than from price. - fabUrl is the listing's page. Give it, copied exactly, whenever you name the listing. Never build one from listingId; when fabUrl is absent, give no link. - A "no such listing" failure can also mean the listing is no longer public, so do not tell the user it never existed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_install_fab_listing.summary: [Epic FabToolset.FabToolset] Installs a Fab asset into the running editor: one the user owns, or a free one. Returns JSON: { listingId, assetFormat, title, status, message }. "handed-to-editor" adds kind, and engineVersion when one was used; "choose-file" adds files, each { fileId, fileName }. Which search result to install from: - Something the user owns: its search_fab_my_library result. - A free listing (free true) the user does not own: its search_fab_listings result. Free content installs straight into the project in every format, unreal-engine included. Do NOT ask the user to add it to their library first. - The one exception is a listing with limitedTimeFree true in get_fab_listing_details that is not in the user's library. It does not install, in any format, until the user adds it to their library on Fab. Tell them to do that first, from its fabUrl, then install it from search_fab_my_library. You cannot add anything to the library yourself. - Anything else needs a license first, which the user gets on Fab from its fabUrl. Installs these formats: unreal-engine (asset packs and code plugins), glb, gltf, fbx, converted-files and metahuman. Pass listingId and title from that result, and the fields of one of its installOptions - assetFormat always, engineVersion and distributionMethod when the option has them - exactly as returned. Values are checked for form, not for where they came from: a missing required value, a malformed one or an engineVersion newer than this editor is rejected, but any other valid value is used as given, so an edited one installs something other than the option the user saw. Pass title as well: the editor's download notification shows it, and glb, gltf, fbx and converted-files are imported into a folder named after it. CRITICAL - this is fire-and-forget. status is "handed-to-editor", "already-in-progress" or "choose-file", NEVER "installed". A successful result means a download is running, not that the asset is imported and usable. Tell the user the download has begun and that progress appears in the editor. Do NOT tell them it is ready, and do not offer to place or use the asset immediately afterwards. kind says what was started, and the two finish differently: - "content" imports into the project on its own. - "plugin" installs into the project's Plugins directory and then stops. The editor asks to restart, and the plugin does nothing until the user accepts. Warn them about the restart prompt when you report a plugin install, and do not claim the plugin is available. "choose-file" means the format has several files - often quality levels or variants - and nothing was downloaded. Show the user the fileName of each, ask which they want, and call this again with the same arguments plus that file's fileId. Do not pick one yourself unless the user already said which. "already-in-progress" means this asset was already downloading, from an earlier call or from the Fab tab, and this call started nothing. Say so rather than reporting a fresh download, and do not call this again for the same asset. Failure cases worth relaying accurately: - "you don't appear to own a license to this" means exactly that. Fab reports an unowned asset much the same way it reports a missing one, so do NOT tell the user the asset does not exist. - When a free listing the user does not own is refused - "you don't appear to own a license to this" or "no such download" - Fab serves it only to accounts that have it in their library. Give the user its fabUrl to add it there, then install it from search_fab_my_library. - if it reports that nobody is signed in, call fab_sign_in and then try again. - a refusal naming an EULA - the Fab EULA, or the UEM EULA for a Legacy UEM listing - means the signed-in Fab account has not accepted it. Tell the user they need to read and accept that EULA, which governs the use of this asset, and give its link. They accept it for their Fab account; it cannot be accepted from here. Never say it was accepted, and do not retry the install until the user says they have accepted it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_search_fab_listings.summary: [Epic FabToolset.FabToolset] Searches the whole Fab marketplace, as JSON: { query, results: [...], nextCursor }. Use this when the user wants to find or buy something: "is there a X on Fab", "find me a medieval village pack", "what environment packs are there". To search what they already have, use search_fab_my_library, which reads their library directly. Each result carries listingId, title, seller, sellerId, listingType, fabUrl, free, rating, licenses (each a name and licenseId), assetFormats, installOptions, engineVersions, distributionMethod, and mature when it is 18+ content. Pass listingId to get_fab_listing_details for the full description and each license's price. fabUrl is the listing's page on Fab. Rules for reporting these results: - Give every listing you name with its fabUrl, copied exactly. Never build one from listingId; when a result has no fabUrl, give no link for it. - There is no description here, and a title or seller does not say what a listing contains. Do not describe its contents until get_fab_listing_details has reported them; until then, say you have not checked. - There are no prices here. free true means at least one license costs nothing; the others may not. get_fab_listing_details says which license is free and what the rest cost. - This route does not report ownership, so a hit says nothing about whether the user already owns the listing. search_fab_my_library is what answers that. - installOptions is how install_fab_listing would install the listing in this editor, one entry per format, as in search_fab_my_library. Empty means it can use none of its formats - say so when it matters to the user. - A listing with free true installs straight from this result, owned or not: pass one of its installOptions, with listingId and title, to install_fab_listing. Do not ask the user to add it to their library first. - Anything else installs only once the user owns it. Look its title up with search_fab_my_library and install from that result. - discounted true with free false can mean the listing is free only for a limited time; get_fab_listing_details says so with limitedTimeFree. Such a listing does not install from this result: the user must add it to their library first, from its fabUrl. - Only the formats install_fab_listing installs, unless you name others in AssetFormats. That is the useful default in an editor, but it means a "nothing found" result only rules out those formats. - engineVersions is what the listing supports. Assets commonly support older engines than the running editor and still work. - THERE IS NO TOTAL COUNT. Never say how many results Fab has. nextCursor present means more results exist; pass it back as Cursor to continue. Absent means this is the end. - rating is absent when nobody has rated the listing yet. Tell the user it has no ratings yet, the same way you report any other rating. It is not a rating of zero. - The filters take the values results report: sellerId for a seller, never the seller's name. A listing type, category or license Fab does not know fails with an error naming the filter; drop that filter or ask the user, rather than guessing another value. An unknown sellerId matches nothing, so no results can mean a wrong sellerId. - mature true marks 18+ content, and its thumbnail is blurred. Fab applies the user's mature content setting to what get_fab_listing_details returns for it. Before calling get_fab_listing_details for one, tell the user it is mature content and ask whether to continue, as the Fab website does. Respect the user's mature content setting, below, at all times while surfacing mature content. - Which mature listings appear follows the user's Fab mature content setting: Hide, Blur or Show. To change it, the user signs in on fab.com, opens User preferences (the sliders button next to Sort on a search page) and sets Mature content. An account with an age rating restriction cannot change it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_search_fab_my_library.summary: [Epic FabToolset.FabToolset] Searches everything the user has a license to on Fab, as JSON: { query, results: [...], nextCursor }. Only the formats install_fab_listing installs, unless you name others in AssetFormats: to answer a question about other formats, such as what Unity assets the user has, name them there. Use this whenever the user refers to assets they have - "my library", "what I own", "that pack I bought" - and before installing anything that is not free. Each result carries listingId, title, seller, sellerId, listingType, licenses, assetFormats, engineVersions, distributionMethod and installable. An installable result also carries installOptions: one entry per format this editor can install, each holding assetFormat and, where that format needs them, engineVersion and distributionMethod. To install, pick one option and pass its fields unchanged, with listingId and title, to install_fab_listing. These results carry no fabUrl. To link one, take fabUrl from get_fab_listing_details; never build a link from listingId. Rules for reporting these results: - owned is always true. These cost the user nothing further - never quote a price or offer to buy one. - When a result has several installOptions, prefer unreal-engine: it arrives as ready-made Unreal content. The others are imported through Interchange or the MetaHuman importer. If the user asked for a specific format, use that one. - installable false comes with notInstallableReason, which says what install_fab_listing lacks - no format it installs, no build for this engine, an engine installation, a complete project, a listing no longer on Fab. It is a fact about that tool, NOT about the asset: relay the reason, and do not tell the user the asset cannot be used. - distributionMethod says what installing the unreal-engine option will do, so read it before offering to install: asset_pack adds assets to the project, and code_plugin installs an editor plugin that needs an editor restart. Say which of the two it is. complete_project is a whole project, which install_fab_listing does not install. - engineVersions is what the asset supports, which is often below the running editor. That is normal: an option's engineVersion is the newest of them this editor can load. - Results are eventually consistent. Something added to the library moments ago may not appear yet, or may appear not installable because Fab does not offer its download yet. If the user just added it, or insists they own it, say it may still be syncing and suggest trying again shortly. Do not call it a download limitation. - THERE IS NO TOTAL COUNT. nextCursor present means more results; pass it back as Cursor. - The filters take the values results report: sellerId for a seller, never the seller's name. Keywords also match seller names, so to filter by a seller, search with their name first and take the sellerId of every matching seller from the results - one brand can sell under several accounts. A listing type or category Fab does not know fails with an error naming the filter; drop that filter or ask the user, rather than guessing another value. An unknown license or sellerId matches nothing, so no results can mean a wrong value. If this reports that nobody is signed in, call fab_sign_in and then try again. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

tools.name: feedback
tools.description:
Submit feedback when a native tool falls short: a missing action, a wrong result, a crash, or a gap you had to work around with execute_python. A python workaround is a common trigger but is not required. Reports are routed to the tracker that owns the surface - ue-mcp core, or the plugin listed in the plugin registry that provides it - by consulting the published plugin registry.

Call feedback(action, args={...}). Actions:
submit(summary, title, author?, confirmToken?, idealTool?, pythonWorkaround?, repo?)
route(summary, title, idealTool?, repo?)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

tools.name: flow
tools.description:
Run pre-built named sequences for this project. ALWAYS check project(action="get_status") first - its 'flows' field lists what's available. If a flow matches the user's request, run it via flow(action="run", flowName="...") instead of composing the sequence by hand. Config reloads on every call - no restart needed.

Actions:
- run(flowName, params?:o, rollback_on_failure?:b, skip?:[s]): Execute a named flow from ue-mcp.yml. A step whose handler reports success:false FAILS the step and stops the run, and the inverses collected up to and including it are what rollback_on_failure unwinds. A step whose failure is EXPECTED says so itself, in the YAML, with ignore_failure: true - the run walks on, and the step is still recorded as failed with its error and its data, marked ignoredFailure. That is how stop, build, start survives an editor that was already stopped, instead of editor(stop_editor) reporting a success it did not achieve. The failing step's OWN inverse, which a few handlers attach after a partial write, is collected like every other: under rollback_on_failure it is replayed FIRST, ahead of the steps before it, so the partial write is undone before they unwind. It arrives verbatim on steps[i].partialWriteRollback, whose replayed flag says whether the runner ran it or it is yours to run, and in that step's error text. A nested flow's steps arrive on steps[i].nestedSteps, reported on the same terms. Returns a summary, every step's data, and the runId.
- plan(flowName): Show a flow's execution plan without running a step of it. Returns the ordered plan, and the flow as declared under definition: its description and each step's task or nested flow, options and conditions, with ${steps.N...} references left unresolved. inputs lists the params a run may pass: each parameter the step tasks read and the steps leave unset, with its type, required flag and the steps that read it.
- list(): List the flows available to this project, merged from ue-mcp.yml, the user-global config and any loaded plugin.

Step types supported in YAML flows: any MCP action (category.action), nested flows (flow:),
and 'shell' for running shell/exec commands. Per-step options: options, when, retries,
retryDelay, retryOn, and ignore_failure (record this step's failure and carry on).
Example shell step:
  steps:
    1: { task: shell, options: { command: "npm run up:build" } }

omit.description: Drop these result fields (dotted paths, same traversal as select). Runs after select.

params.description: run: runtime options merged into every step's options (highest priority)

rollback_on_failure.description: run: invoke inverse tasks in reverse order on failure

select.description: Keep only these result fields (dotted paths; arrays are traversed, so 'components.name' keeps every component's name). Unmatched paths are reported.

skip.description: run: step names or numbers to skip

tools.name: foliage
tools.description:
Foliage instances, types, procedural spawners, sampling and settings. Every FoliageType tunable (Density, Radius, ScaleX/Y/Z, AlignToNormal, GroundSlopeAngle, CullDistance, CastShadow) is a plain property: use set_settings, batch_set_settings_where or asset(set_property), not a typed action. Grass on landscape layers is authored elsewhere and deliberately has no action here: material(add_expression, expressionType="LandscapeGrassOutput") adds the slot node, material(list_expressions) reads it back, asset(create_asset_by_class, className="LandscapeGrassType") makes the grass type, and asset(set_property) fills its GrassVarieties.

Call foliage(action, args={...}). Actions:
list_types(cursor?, limit?:i)
get_settings(foliageTypePath|foliageTypeName)
sample(center:v, radius?:n)
create_type(meshPath, name?, packagePath?, onConflict?, settings?:o)
set_settings(foliageTypePath|foliageTypeName, settings:o)
batch_set_settings_where(settings:o, where:[o], whereMode?, foliageTypePaths?:[s], directory?, recursive?:b, fromLevel?:b, propertyNames?:[s], dryRun?:b, save?:b, maxTypes?:i)
add_instances(foliageTypePath, transforms?:[o], center?:v, radius?:n, count?:i, seed?:i, projectToGround?:b, traceUp?:n, traceDown?:n, applyTypeRules?:b, skipCollision?:b)
remove_instances(foliageTypePath, instanceIndices?:[i], transforms?:[o], center?:v, radius?:n, all?:b, matchTolerance?:n, actorPath?, dryRun?:b)
get_instances(foliageTypePath?, center?:v, radius?:n, limit?:i, startIndex?:i, includeTransforms?:b)
add_type_to_level(foliageTypePath)
remove_type_from_level(foliageTypePath, force?:b)
read_spawner(spawnerPath)
set_spawner_types(spawnerPath, foliageTypePaths:[s], mode?, save?:b)
simulate_procedural(actorLabel?, actorPath?, spawnerPath?, clearExisting?:b, skipCollision?:b)
clear_procedural(actorLabel?, actorPath?, spawnerPath?)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

list_types.summary: List foliage types in the level, one row per type per InstancedFoliageActor (foliageActorPath says which), sorted by that pair.

sample.summary: Count instances per foliage type inside a sphere.

set_settings.summary: Modify ONE foliage type's settings. For the same edit across every type matching a condition, use batch_set_settings_where instead of calling this in a loop.

batch_set_settings_where.summary: Write settings to every FoliageType whose CURRENT property values match a predicate, with the predicate evaluated in the editor. set_settings is one asset per call and cannot express a condition at all, so 'include_in_hlod=false on every type whose cull distance is set' meant reading 201 assets out, computing the 36 matches client-side, and writing them back one at a time. Candidates come from foliageTypePaths[] (explicit), directory (scan FoliageType assets) or fromLevel=true (types placed in the open level). Predicate fields read the asset's own properties by dotted path, so CullDistance.Max works and a bare name is treated the same as props.<name>; operators are the same vocabulary as level(query_components). dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE because this writes to many assets at once, and the preview still resolves every setting path so an unwritable property is reported before the commit. Written values are read back rather than echoed, so a value the property coerced is visible. The inverse is asset(bulk_set_properties) carrying the previous value of every property on every type written, which is the only action that takes DIFFERENT values per asset - two matched types can have had different previous values for the same setting. It is marked lossy when a matched FoliageType lives inside a level rather than as an asset (no assetPath addresses it), and omitted entirely above that action's 500-item batch limit, with the reason stated rather than a record that would restore part of the write. Pass one of foliageTypePaths, directory or fromLevel (#988).

add_instances.summary: PAINT foliage into the open level. Nothing else on this surface could place a single instance, so create_type produced an asset that never appeared anywhere. Two modes: transforms[] places each entry exactly, center+radius+count scatters uniformly over a disc. Each candidate is traced onto the geometry beneath it (projectToGround, default true) and then run through the FoliageType's OWN placement rules (applyTypeRules, default true) so the random scale between ScaleX/Y/Z, the random yaw and pitch, align-to-normal within AlignMaxAngle, the Z offset and the CollisionWithWorld test all apply - which is what makes a painted instance behave like one painted by hand. A candidate that hits nothing, or that the type's ground-slope or height range rejects, is reported in skippedCandidates with the reason rather than silently dropped. The type is added to the level's palette if it is not there already. Returns the InstancedFoliageActor it wrote to, and rolls back by removing exactly the transforms it placed. Each transforms entry is {location, rotation?, scale?}.

remove_instances.summary: Remove foliage instances by index, by exact transform, inside a sphere, or all of a type. The rollback captures each removed instance's world transform and replays it as an add, so this is recoverable up to 2000 instances; the base component an instance was painted onto is not restored. dryRun reports what would go without touching anything. Scope to one InstancedFoliageActor with actorPath when a World Partition map holds the same type on several.

get_instances.summary: Read placed foliage instances with their world transforms, paged. sample only ever returned counts, so there was no way to verify a paint or find what to remove. Filter by type and/or by a sphere; index is the position inside the named actor's info for that type, which is exactly what remove_instances takes.

add_type_to_level.summary: Put a FoliageType asset into the open level's palette, allocating the instanced component that holds its instances. create_type only makes the asset; until this runs the type is invisible to the level and to the foliage editor. Idempotent: a type already in the level reports existed and allocates nothing.

remove_type_from_level.summary: Take a FoliageType out of the open level's palette. REFUSES while the type still has instances unless force=true, because removing it destroys them and their transforms are not captured - remove them first with remove_instances, whose rollback does capture them. The FoliageType asset itself is untouched; asset(delete) deletes it.

read_spawner.summary: Read a ProceduralFoliageSpawner: its tile settings, the foliage types it will spawn resolved to real asset paths, and every volume in the open level bound to it with its bounds and whether it has produced anything. The volume half is the part nobody can read off the asset and the usual reason a simulation appears to do nothing. Returns objectPath for the scalar tunables, which are plain properties.

set_spawner_types.summary: Set which foliage types a ProceduralFoliageSpawner spawns. This needs an action rather than a property write: FoliageTypes is a private array whose element object pointer is private too, and every write has to be followed by RefreshInstance or the cached type the simulation actually reads stays stale. Validates every path before writing anything, reports unchanged when the list already matched, reads the result back rather than echoing it, and rolls back to the previous list.

simulate_procedural.summary: Run the procedural foliage simulation and place what it generates. Address one volume with actorLabel or actorPath, or every volume in the open level bound to one spawner with spawnerPath. Validates every target first (spawner set, type list non-empty, volume bounds non-zero) so a half-simulated set of volumes is not possible, then generates desired instances and traces and places each one under the same type rules as add_instances. Reports generated, placed and skipped per volume. Place the volume itself with level(spawn_volume, volumeType="ProceduralFoliageVolume"), which builds the cube brush a bare spawn leaves empty.

clear_procedural.summary: Remove every instance a procedural foliage component spawned, matched on the component's own procedural GUID so hand-painted instances of the same type are left alone. Pass one of actorLabel, actorPath or spawnerPath. Reports alreadyRemoved when the component had produced nothing. The inverse re-runs the simulation, which reproduces the cleared content only while the spawner's seed, tile settings and type list are unchanged.
