action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

sample.summary: Read the surface height AND every paint-layer weight at one world XY. Height and weights come from the landscape's own height and weight data (the merged result of every edit layer), the same data landscape(paint_layer) writes, so they are exact and do not depend on built collision. Layers come back with weight (0..1), weight255 (the weightmap byte the editor shows), the LayerInfo path and its physical material, plus dominantLayer and totalWeight - which is what makes reading a paint weight one call instead of rendering the weightmap to a render target and reading that back. Also returns quad, quadExtent and inBounds, so a zero weight OFF the landscape reads as out of bounds rather than as a measured zero, and traceHeight/normal from a confirmation collision trace (absent when collision is unbuilt or the proxy is streamed out). Position accepts x + y, point {x, y}, or worldX + worldY (#939).

sculpt.summary: Raise, lower or flatten terrain with a circular brush. mode=raise|lower|flatten; amount is world centimetres at full strength (raise/lower), and flatten pulls toward the height under the brush centre. falloff (0..1) is the smoothstepped soft edge. Runs in one transaction and leaves the level dirty and unsaved. Writes into an edit layer (editLayer by name, else editLayerIndex, default 0) - required on UE 5.8, where a write without one is regenerated away by the layer system. Idempotent: a brush that rounds to the height already there reports unchanged=true and updated=false rather than claiming it moved ground. The rollback record carries the exact previous heights over the brush rectangle and replays through set_height_region; above rollbackMaxVertices the response says rollbackOmitted with the reason instead of a record that would restore part of the footprint (#742).

paint_layer.summary: Paint a weight layer with a circular brush. The layer must already have a LayerInfo on this landscape (see add_layer_info) - an unregistered name errors and lists the layers that ARE registered instead of silently painting nothing. Weights are written as given - the engine no longer renormalises other layers for you, so set them explicitly if they must sum to 1. Writes into an edit layer (editLayer by name, else editLayerIndex, default 0). Idempotent: a brush that changes no weight reports unchanged=true. The rollback record carries the exact previous weights over the brush rectangle and replays through set_layer_weight_region, with the same rollbackOmitted cap as the region writes (#742).

list_edit_layers.summary: List the landscape's edit layers by name, in stack order, with guid, visible, locked, heightmapAlpha and weightmapAlpha. These names are what sculpt, paint_layer and the region writes take as editLayer (#1156).

merge_edit_layers.summary: Re-merge every edit layer into the landscape's final height and weight maps (ALandscape::ForceLayersFullUpdate), then run the update immediately unless updateNow=false. Use after edits that leave the merged result stale. Changes no authored value, so there is no rollback (#1156).

list_splines.summary: Read every landscape spline network: controlPoints (name, path, location and rotation in world space, halfWidth, sideFalloff, endFalloff, layerName, raiseTerrain, lowerTerrain, connectedSegments, and the owner actor) and segments (start and end points, tangent lengths, layer, raise/lower flags, meshes, meshComponentCount, length). Covers splines on landscape actors and proxies and on World Partition LandscapeSplineActors. x/y/z on a point are its location in spline space, as before.

create_spline_point.summary: Add a landscape spline control point at a world location, with optional rotation, halfWidth, sideFalloff, endFalloff, paint layerName and raiseTerrain/lowerTerrain. On a single landscape it goes into the landscape's own splines component; on a World Partition map it goes into a new LandscapeSplineActor, as the Landscape Mode spline tool does, unless ownerPath names an existing owner. Pass ownerPath (returned as ownerPath) to keep later points in the same network, since a segment only joins points of one owner. name makes the create idempotent. Rolls back through delete_spline_point.

update_spline_point.summary: Move a landscape spline control point or change its rotation, halfWidth, falloffs, paint layer or raise/lower flags. Moving a connected point recomputes its rotation from its segments unless rotation is passed or autoRotate is false. Reports unchanged when nothing moved, and the rollback restores every previous value.

delete_spline_point.summary: Delete a landscape spline control point and every segment connected to it. Idempotent: a point that is not there reports alreadyDeleted. A point with no segments rolls back through create_spline_point with its name and settings; one with segments says why it has no rollback.

connect_spline_points.summary: Join two control points of the same spline owner with a segment. Tangent lengths default to the distance between the points; layerName, raiseTerrain, lowerTerrain, meshes, collisionProfile and castShadow set the segment in the same call. Points already joined report existed. Rolls back through delete_spline_segment.

update_spline_segment.summary: Change a landscape spline segment's tangent lengths, paint layer or raise/lower flags. Reports unchanged when nothing changed; the rollback restores the previous values.

set_spline_segment_meshes.summary: Set the meshes a landscape spline segment deforms along itself (mesh, scale, forwardAxis, upAxis, materialOverrides, centerH, scaleToWidth per entry), its collisionProfile and castShadow. meshes replaces the whole list, and an empty list clears it. Returns meshComponentCount, the spline mesh components the segment built. The rollback restores the previous list.

delete_spline_segment.summary: Delete one landscape spline segment; its control points stay. Idempotent. Rolls back through connect_spline_points with the segment's tangents, layer, flags and meshes.

apply_splines.summary: Apply the landscape's splines to its terrain: raise and lower the heights under each segment and paint each segment's layer. A landscape with a reserved splines edit layer is written there, regenerated from the splines each time; otherwise the deformation goes into editLayer (by name, else editLayerIndex, default 0) and stays when the splines change. The edit layers merge now unless updateNow is false; read the result back with get_height_at_point after merge_edit_layers, since the merge finishes on the GPU.

add_layer_info.summary: Register paint layer (creates LayerInfo asset + binds to active landscape). Idempotent: a layer already registered reports existed and emits no record, so a replay cannot delete a layer it did not create. Rolls back through remove_layer on the parent Landscape actor, which un-registers the layer; marked lossy when the LayerInfo ASSET was created here, because remove_layer deliberately leaves it on disk.

create_layer_info.summary: Standalone LayerInfo asset creation - no landscape required (#251).

create.summary: Spawn a new ALandscape with a flat heightmap. Defaults match the Editor's Landscape Mode 'create new' (8x8 components, 63 quads/subsection, 2 subsections/component = 1016x1016 quads) (#303).

get_material_usage_summary.summary: Per-proxy summary: landscape/hole material paths + component/grass/nanite counts (#150).

list_proxies.summary: Enumerate loaded World Partition LandscapeStreamingProxy actors with per-proxy objectPath and worldBounds (origin/extent), sorted by object path, plus loadedProxies + parentLandscapes counts. Unloaded proxies are not spawned as actors, so only loaded ones appear - use this to confirm a proxy is streamed in before trusting a layer/height readback (#733).

find_proxy_at.summary: Resolve which loaded LandscapeStreamingProxy covers a world X/Y. Returns found/loaded + label, or loaded:false when the covering proxy is streamed out (so a 0-weight readback there is ambiguous, not real) (#733).

get_height_region.summary: Read the raw uint16 heights over a rectangle of landscape vertices, with min/max/mean reported in raw units AND in world Z so the numbers mean something without a second call. Heights come back as a plain array below arrayEncodingLimit and as a little-endian base64 blob above it, and that blob feeds straight back into set_height_region, so a read-modify-write round trip needs no reformatting. Reports hasUnloadedComponentsInRegion, because on a World Partition map an unloaded component reads as absent rather than as flat ground. Reads the merged surface unless editLayer or editLayerIndex names one, in which case it reads that layer's own contribution.

set_height_region.summary: Write heights over a rectangle of landscape vertices. Accepts heightsBase64 (the blob get_height_region hands back), heights as one number per vertex row-major from (minX,minY), or height / rawHeight to fill the whole rectangle with one value; heightSpace picks whether the numbers are raw uint16 (32768 = the actor's own Z) or world centimetres. Idempotent: a write that changes nothing reports unchanged true and updated false rather than claiming an edit. The rollback record carries the exact previous heights, and when the rectangle is above rollbackMaxVertices the response says rollbackOmitted with the reason instead of emitting a record that would restore only part of it. Requires an edit layer, since a write with none is regenerated away by the layer system.

get_height_at_point.summary: Surface height under one world XY, as both the raw uint16 and the world Z, plus the landscape vertex it was read at. Reads the nearest vertex rather than interpolating, so it can differ from a physics trace by up to half a quad of slope, and it says so. Position accepts x + y, point {x, y}, or worldX + worldY.

get_normal_at_point.summary: World-space surface normal under one world XY, computed by central difference over the neighbouring vertices in world centimetres and rotated into world space, so a non-uniform landscape scale is accounted for. Returns the normal, the slope in degrees and the vertex it was read at.

get_slope_at_point.summary: Slope under one world XY in degrees from horizontal, in radians, and as a grade percentage, plus the downhill direction as a unit vector. The downhill direction is what routes a road or a river; a slope number alone never is.

get_slope_map.summary: Per-vertex slope in degrees over a rectangle, plus min/max/mean and a fixed nine-bucket ten-degree histogram. The buckets are fixed on purpose: they are what a caller reasons about (anything under 15 degrees is buildable) and a configurable bin count would make two runs incomparable. The per-vertex array is returned below arrayEncodingLimit and omitted with a reason above it.

sculpt_region.summary: Apply one shaping operator over a rectangle: raise, lower, flatten, smooth, mountain, valley, ridge, plateau, crater or terrace. One action rather than ten, because the region resolution, falloff, strength blend, previous-height capture and rollback record are identical for every shape and only the per-vertex kernel differs. amount is world centimetres at full strength, shape picks a radial (ellipse) or edge-relative (rect) falloff, and sharpness controls how peaked the dome operators are. flatten and plateau take targetHeight in world Z, or flattenTo as mean / center / min / max; smooth takes iterations; terrace takes steps; ridge takes ridgeAngle in degrees; crater takes rimPosition and rimRatio. Reports verticesClampedToHeightRange when the shape ran past the uint16 range, since that is a flat-topped mountain rather than a failure. With more than one edit layer it shapes the merged terrain and writes only the change into editLayer, scaled by that layer's heightmap alpha; terrainBefore/terrainAfter report the ground, heightBefore/heightAfter the layer.

apply_erosion.summary: Run hydraulic or thermal erosion over a rectangle. Hydraulic rains on every vertex, routes water to lower four-neighbours, carries sediment to capacity and deposits the rest, then re-deposits whatever is still suspended so the pass does not quietly remove material every run; thermal slumps anything steeper than talusAngle toward it. This is a CPU grid model over the region on the game thread, not the Landscape Mode erosion tool, and the response says so. Cost is vertices times iterations and is refused above maxWork rather than blocking the editor for an unbounded time. With more than one edit layer it shapes the merged terrain and writes only the change into editLayer, scaled by that layer's heightmap alpha; terrainBefore/terrainAfter report the ground, heightBefore/heightAfter the layer.

import_heightmap.summary: Write a 16-bit heightmap file into a region of the landscape. format is png16 (16-bit greyscale PNG) or raw16 (headerless little-endian uint16), inferred from the extension when omitted; an 8-bit image is refused with its real format rather than stretched, because a 256-step heightmap terraces visibly. A raw16 file carries no dimensions, so width and height are required for it. When the image and the region disagree the call refuses and prints the region that WOULD fit, unless resample is true, which bilinearly fits it and says detail was averaged away. minHeight and maxHeight remap the image's 0 and 65535 onto a world Z band, which is the control a heightmap authored elsewhere actually needs. A relative filePath resolves under the project's Saved directory.

export_heightmap.summary: Write a region's heights out as a 16-bit greyscale PNG or a headerless little-endian uint16 file, for inspection or for a round trip through an external terrain tool. Reports the exact byte count, the region and the height range in raw units and world Z, so the file can be re-imported at the right scale. Exports the merged surface unless editLayer or editLayerIndex names one. No inverse is emitted: the bridge has no delete-file method, and overwriting a file whose previous contents were never read is not undoable, so the response says rollbackOmitted with which of the two cases applied.

analyze_terrain.summary: Height and slope distribution over a region, plus largestFlatArea: the biggest axis-aligned rectangle whose every vertex is within slopeThresholdDegrees, in quad indices AND world coordinates with its mean Z. That last part is the answer to where a building fits, which a flat-vertex COUNT never is - ten thousand scattered flat vertices and one flat plateau report the same number. The height histogram takes histogramBins; the slope histogram is fixed at nine ten-degree bands so two runs stay comparable.

get_layer_weight_region.summary: Read one paint layer's 0..255 weights over a rectangle, with min/max/mean and the painted vertex count and fraction. An unregistered layerName is refused with the layers that ARE registered, so a typo and a landscape whose material never declared the layer read differently. Weights come back as an array below arrayEncodingLimit and as base64 above it, in the exact form set_layer_weight_region takes back.

set_layer_weight_region.summary: Write one paint layer's weights over a rectangle. Accepts weightsBase64 (one uint8 per vertex, the form the getter returns), weights as one number per vertex, or weight / strength as a single 0..1 fraction to fill the rectangle. Idempotent, with the same unchanged/updated reporting as set_height_region, and the rollback record carries the exact previous weights up to rollbackMaxVertices. Weights are written as given: the engine no longer renormalises the other layers for you, so set them explicitly if they must sum to 1.

layer_exists.summary: Is this paint layer registered on the landscape, and does it have a LayerInfo asset to store weights in? Returns exists, hasLayerInfo, its layerInfoPath, and the full layer list. The two flags are separate because a material can declare a layer that has no LayerInfo assigned, which looks present and fails every paint.

add_layer.summary: Register a paint layer on the landscape, creating the ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset that its weight data needs and binding it. The counterpart to remove_layer, and the same handler add_layer_info calls. Idempotent: a layer already registered is reported with its existing asset path rather than duplicated.

remove_layer.summary: Unregister a paint layer and drop its weight data across every component of the landscape. Idempotent: removing a layer that is not there reports alreadyAbsent with the layers that are, rather than failing. NOT undoable through the bridge - the weights are destroyed without being read back first, and the response says so with the reason, so export them with get_layer_weight_region first if they matter. The ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset itself is left on disk, so add_layer brings the layer back empty.

get_holes.summary: Read the landscape visibility mask over a rectangle or at a single world XY, as booleans plus the hole vertex count and fraction. A vertex counts as a hole once its visibility weight passes the engine's own two-thirds threshold, so this action and the renderer agree about what a hole is. A hole only renders, and only stops collision, if the landscape material routes a Landscape Visibility Mask node into opacity mask.

set_holes.summary: Punch or fill the landscape visibility mask over a rectangle or at a single world XY. Accepts hole as a single boolean for the whole target, holes as one boolean per vertex, or weightsBase64 to restore exact previous visibility weights (which is the form its own rollback record carries). Unlike every other region action this one does NOT default to the whole landscape when no target is given: that would punch the entire terrain into a hole on a call that forgot a parameter, so it refuses instead.

plan_real_world.summary: Turn a real-world extent plus a heightmap file into the exact landscape(create) and landscape(import_heightmap) parameters that reproduce it in engine at true scale. Creates nothing: it is arithmetic against engine invariants a caller cannot restate correctly by hand, namely that a landscape's vertex count is componentCount x subsectionSizeQuads x numSubsections + 1 with subsectionSizeQuads restricted to 7/15/31/63/127/255, and that its uint16 heights only mean metres through the actor's Z scale. Size the tile with realWorldSizeMeters {x,y}, or with boundsLatLon {minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon} which is projected on a local tangent plane at the box centre latitude (an approximation, not a datum reprojection, and the response says so). minElevationMeters and maxElevationMeters state what the image's value range means; elevationEncoding full spans 0..65535 across that band, data measures the image's own range and needs sourcePath. Returns the chosen resolution, every legal alternative with its error, the resulting metres per quad, the vertical precision in centimetres, and warnings for resampling, anisotropy, quantisation and exaggeration. Fetching DEM tiles over the network is deliberately NOT part of this: provider APIs, keys and licences change independently of the engine, so that half belongs in a plugin.

project_geo_coordinates.summary: Convert between latitude/longitude and a landscape's world space, in both directions, against the same boundsLatLon the landscape was planned for. Each entry in points is either {lat, lon}, answered with the world X/Y and the sampled surface Z so the point lands ON the terrain, or {x, y}, answered with the geographic coordinate that world position corresponds to - which is what turns analyze_terrain's largestFlatArea back into a real place. northAt says which end of the landscape's Y axis is north, defaulting to minY because a DEM raster's first row is its northern edge and that is how import_heightmap lays one down; getting it wrong mirrors every placement about the middle of the map and nothing about the result looks wrong.

refresh_physical_material_collision.summary: UE 5.8+: safely refresh physical-material collision data in memory on loaded World Partition LandscapeStreamingProxy actors after a LayerInfo PhysMaterial change. Requires complete registered collision coverage and no pending landscape edit-layer work. Preserves and verifies every raw, complex-live, and simple-live height sample, builds material data before one collision recreation, and fails the whole matched batch on any unsafe result. Filters combine: actorLabels[], guids[], and bounds {min,max}; omitting them targets every loaded proxy up to maxActors (default 256, hard max 1024). Unloaded proxies are untouched; pin them first with level(load_actor_descs). Refuses PIE/SIE and non-World-Partition maps. Persistence is deliberately unsupported because Landscape PreSave can mutate edit-layer collision data; this action never saves packages, and save accepts only false. No inverse: this recomputes derived collision and physical-material data from weightmaps it never writes, so nothing restores the previous build and the response says rollbackPossible=false. Returns loaded/matched/refreshed/failed counts and exact affected package paths.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

get_outliner.summary: List actors (each row includes editorHidden - hidden in the viewport but still rendering in game, and folderPath). classFilter is a case-sensitive SUBSTRING over the class name by default; pass exactClass=true to require the exact class instead. folderPath matches one World Outliner folder exactly and folderPathPrefix matches that folder and everything nested under it, so narrowing a folder to a single class no longer needs a get_actor_details round trip per entry (#911) (#717).

set_editor_visibility.summary: Bulk set editor-only visibility (temporarily-hidden-in-editor) on actors. Targets actorLabels[] or all=true (#717).

place_actor.summary: Spawn actor. Pass world:pie to spawn into the running PIE world (#585).

delete_actor.summary: Remove actor. A label matching several actors is refused with the candidates rather than deleting one of them (#983).

get_actor_details.summary: Inspect actor. With includeProperties=true, a UPROPERTY declared as a C-style FIXED ARRAY (int32 Foo[3], one FProperty with ArrayDim 3) comes back as a JSON ARRAY of its elements plus arrayDim, instead of element 0 presented as the whole value. That mattered on RecastNavMesh NavMeshResolutionParams, whose three entries are the Low, Default and High generation tiers, and where reporting only Low sent a user tuning cell sizes against numbers the engine was not using (#927). Containers over 64 entries and values over 16384 characters are cut and marked truncated, with count for a container (#1277).

move_actor.summary: Transform actor. In the editor world the move is one undo transaction and dirties the actor's package, reported as packageDirty, so level(save) persists it (#1261), and it ends with PostEditMove(true) so OnActorMoved listeners such as PCG see it (#1315). Pass world:pie to move a live PIE actor (resolves labels/names from get_outliner {world:pie}) (#586).

aim_actor_at.summary: Rotate an actor so its forward (+X) points at a target (#566/#983). In the editor world the aim is one undo transaction and dirties the actor's package, reported as packageDirty, so level(save) persists it.

nav_project_point.summary: Project a world point onto the navmesh. Returns onNavMesh + projectedLocation (#585).

select.summary: Select actors. A label naming several actors selects all of them; selectedPaths reports exactly which (#983). The level editor never selects a child actor of a ChildActorComponent itself, so naming one selects the actor that owns it and lists the substitution under redirected (#1656).

select_component.summary: Select one component in the level editor, with its owning actor, replacing the selection unless addToSelection=true. componentName is looked up on the actor, then on its child actors. A component on a child actor cannot be selected in the level editor, so the ChildActorComponent that spawned it is selected instead, as a viewport click would do, and the result says so with redirected=true. Returns selectedActorPath and selectedComponent, and unchanged=true when that was already the selection (#1656).

remove_component.summary: Remove instance component from a level actor by name. Idempotent: returns alreadyDeleted=true if no matching component exists (#426).

set_component_property.summary: Set component prop. A C-style FIXED ARRAY element is addressed by index in the dotted path ('Foo[2].Bar'); without an index every write lands on element 0 (#927). Pass value=null to clear a TObjectPtr/SoftObject/WeakObject/UClass/Interface reference (#420). Resolves inherited/SCS components on placed Blueprint instances case-insensitively, and refreshes the scene transform after RelativeLocation/RelativeRotation/RelativeScale3D writes (#539). Pass world='pie' (with optional pieInstance) to write to a LIVE PIE component rather than the editor one (#763). StaticMesh on a static mesh component goes through SetStaticMesh, so the bounds and render state follow the new mesh and it draws; the result reports previousValue, value and changed (#1548).

nudge_component.summary: Adjust an exact named SceneComponent using frame-relative translation, quaternion rotation, or uniform relative scale. frame=parent uses the parent COMPONENT transform; the socket is reported separately. axisRotation and viewRotation are mutually exclusive. An editor-world apply ends with PostEditMove(true) on the owner, so OnActorMoved listeners see it (#1315). viewRotation is observer-relative to the selected frame, not a player camera: clockwise/counterclockwise is resolved using Unreal screen basis and returned as signed degrees. dryRun=false by default; dryRun returns current spatial inspection plus requested world location/rotation and relative scale without a transaction, modification, setter, dirtiness, or rollback. The rollback it emits is a level(restore_component_transform) call.

restore_component_transform.summary: Put an exact named SceneComponent back to a relative transform: the relativeTransform nudge_component records in its rollback, so a nudge can be undone by hand as well as by the flow runner. The quaternion is what is applied. A component already at that transform is reported unchanged.

get_component_details.summary: Read a placed actor's component transforms. With componentName returns that component's relative+world location/rotation/scale, class, and attach parent; without it lists every component. With includeValues=true also dumps arbitrary UPROPERTY values (custom fields, CharacterMovement MaxWalkSpeed, etc.); world='pie' reads the live PIE instance (#539/#584).

get_current.summary: Get current level name and path.

load.summary: Open level or load map: switch the editor to another map as the current editor level (the native load_map). Returns levelPath, levelName, worldPath and previousLevelPath, and refuses a path that does not exist. Refuses while the open map or its external actor packages have unsaved changes, naming them in dirtyPackages: pass saveFirst=true to save them first or discardUnsaved=true to drop them (a never-saved Untitled map included, which has no file to save to), and the result lists savedPackages or discardedPackages (#1259).

clear_level_script.summary: Preview or remove every node and member variable from the currently loaded persistent level's Level Blueprint. Defaults to dryRun=true. Actors are untouched; save=true saves only the current level after a successful compile.

save.summary: Save the level currently being edited, and say what happened to each package. Takes the same package path editor(save_dirty) uses, so the two can no longer disagree about whether one package was written: the old action returned a bare {success:false, error:'Failed to save current level'} on a map that save_dirty then wrote seconds later, and a false failure makes an agent redo work that was already on disk (#964). On a World Partition or one-file-per-actor map the actors live in their own packages, so those are saved too and each is reported separately. A package that was already clean is reported as skipped, not as a failure. The emptied external package of a deleted World Partition or one-file-per-actor actor is deleted from disk, as the editor's own save does, and listed under deleted (#1301). The bridge keeps that package loaded from the delete until a save commits it, so a garbage collection in between no longer loses the delete (#1545). On failure the error names the package, the resolved file, whether that file exists and is read-only, the engine's ESavePackageResult and the error/warning lines the save itself emitted. Saving during PIE is refused by name rather than failing silently. With commitDeletes=true it goes through the editor's own dirty-package save instead, which deletes the external package of a deleted World Partition actor (a direct save fails on it with 'SavePackage returned false') and saves every other dirty map and content package, reporting written, deleted and stillDirty per package (#1156).

list.summary: List levels: the persistent level first, then every streaming level with its loaded and visible state, in the world's own streaming order.

create.summary: Create a new level at a path and open it. levelPath is validated before the engine is asked: an omitted or malformed path is refused outright, because NewLevel("") logs an engine error and lands the editor on an untitled map that cannot then be saved (#833). worldPartition=true makes a blank World Partition level with one file per actor, and the result reports worldPartition and externalActors (#1247). A level made from a World Partition templateLevel is saved and reopened before returning (savedAndReopened), so its actor descriptors point at the new map rather than the /Temp world it was built in (#1284).

list_volumes.summary: List volumes, sorted by actor path so a page boundary is stable.

set_light_properties.summary: Edit a light OR SkyLight (intensity/color now work on SkyLight too, #608).

get_actors_by_class.summary: List actors by class. Matches Blueprint subclasses of a native base via IsChildOf when className resolves to a UClass (short name, /Script path, or BP class path), else falls back to name-substring. Each actor includes location/rotation/scale, live when world=pie. labelPrefix narrows to actors whose editor label starts with it (case-sensitive), and with it className may be omitted to match every class (#1113) (#675).

get_actors_by_component_class.summary: List actors that own a component of a given class (exact or substring match). Returns each actor plus its matchedComponents. For a whole-map question use level(query_components), which filters and counts in the editor instead of returning every candidate (#582).

query_components.summary: Ask one level-wide question about components and get the answer, not the candidates. Selection, projection, predicates, grouping and counts all evaluate in the editor, so a 4,000 actor map costs one call instead of thousands. Computed (not raw) values: shadow.effectiveCastShadow crosses CastShadow with visibility, bHiddenInGame, owner hidden and bCastHiddenShadow, so a hidden debug marker with CastShadow=true is correctly NOT a shadow caster; every mobility and collision enum comes back as a clean name (Movable, QueryAndPhysics), never as EComponentMobility.MOVABLE; navigation.effectiveNavRelevant crosses bCanEverAffectNavigation with collision and custom navigable geometry. Never writes, and reports dirtiedPackages so you can see that. Field groups for 'fields' and for dot paths: transform, bounds, localBounds (unscaled, includes UBoxComponent BoxExtent), shadow, nanite, navigation, tick (tick settings plus componentActive and autoActivate, the transient active state no property read reaches, #1656), materials (per slot: effective path, componentOverride vs meshDefault, slot name/index, isNull, isWorldGrid, materialClass and isDynamic to tell a MaterialInstanceConstant from a MaterialInstanceDynamic, #1303), mesh (adds instanceCount + hierarchical for an ISM/HISM, #986), decal, health (roll-up incl. suspect), attachment (parentComponent, parentActor, socket, relative transform, isRoot, onlyOwnerSee/ownerNoSee and firstPersonPrimitiveType where the engine has it; with world=pie this enumerates a live pawn's components for dual-mesh visibility checks, #1250), customPrimitiveData (runtime: the values SetCustomPrimitiveData* wrote, e.g. from a construction script, and defaults: the serialized array, #1303), physics (simulatingPhysics, gravityEnabled, awake, linearVelocity, angularVelocityDegrees, mass while simulating, physMaterialOverride and the effective physicalMaterial with friction/restitution/density; pass world=pie for live rigid bodies, #1212). A dot path used in where/groupBy/countBy turns its own group on. actorPropertyNames projects the owning actor's properties, Blueprint variables included and dotted paths allowed, under actorProps.* so per-instance BP state can be filtered, grouped and counted with the rest of the row (#1303). Child actors spawned by a ChildActorComponent are scanned like any actor, and their rows carry parentActorLabel, parentActorPath and childActorComponent; includeChildActors=true applies the actor filters (actorClass, labels, tag, folder) to the top-level owning actor instead, so actorLabelContains naming a placed actor also returns the components of its child actors (#1656). propertyNames takes the same dotted paths into the component (AttachEndTo.ComponentProperty, Items[2].Mesh). A name that resolves to nothing is listed with its reason under missingProps / missingActorProps rather than dropped, and a where/groupBy/countBy path props.X or actorProps.X projects X by itself. For one row per actor (a per-instance audit with its attach parent), add where attachment.isRoot isTrue and fields attachment: that row's attachment.parentActor and socket are the actor's own attachment (#1530). groupBy and countBy COUNT COMPONENTS, not instances: one HISM holding 5,000 instances counts as 1, so for per-mesh placement totals use level(summarize_static_mesh_usage), which sums instances and counts distinct actors. duplicateTransformTolerance reports duplicateTransformGroups. levelPath temporarily opens another map: it refuses if anything is dirty and restores the map that was open (#910/#943/#912). includeCollision adds collisionEnabled and objectType plus responseOnChannel for collisionChannel, or non-Block responses capped at 32.

count_actors_by_class.summary: Histogram of actor classes in the level (sorted desc) (#146).

get_runtime_virtual_texture_summary.summary: List RuntimeVirtualTextureVolume actors + their bound VirtualTexture assets (#150).

set_water_body_property.summary: Set a property on an actor's WaterBodyComponent (ShapeDilation, WaterLevel, etc.). Requires Water plugin. For spline edits use level(set_spline_points) (#151). A deprecated property (TessellatedWaterMeshExtent in 5.8) is not serialized: the write comes back with a warning, and TessellatedWaterMeshExtent, which is not on the body at all, is refused with the supported route, level(rebuild_water_zone) (#1156).

rebuild_water_zone.summary: Rebuild a WaterZone's water mesh and water info, repeating until the WaterMesh QuadTreeResolution stops changing. The grid is sized from the extent seen on the previous rebuild, so a single rebuild after a ZoneExtent or TileSize change reports a stale grid. Optionally sets zoneExtent and/or the WaterMesh tileSize first, which is the supported replacement for the deprecated TessellatedWaterMeshExtent. Returns zoneExtent, tileSize, quadTreeResolution, passes and stable per zone. Without actorLabel/actorPath every zone in the world is rebuilt. Requires Water plugin (#1156).

get_water_state.summary: One structured read of every WaterZone and WaterBody. Zones: ZoneExtent, RenderTargetResolution, OverlapPriority, local tessellation settings, OwnedWaterBodies, and waterMesh TileSize, QuadTreeResolution, TessellationFactor, LODScale and the far-distance mesh settings. Bodies: OceanExtents, CollisionExtents, WaterZoneOverride, OwningWaterZone, bAffectsLandscape, ShapeDilation and every water material. Properties absent on the running engine are omitted, and deprecated fields such as TessellatedWaterMeshExtent are flagged under deprecatedProperties. Requires Water plugin (#1156).

get_spline_info.summary: Read a spline component's points, closedLoop, length, and per-point tangents/types, and splineHasBeenEdited (whether a construction script rerun keeps the points). Works in editor or PIE (#553). componentName picks a specific (custom) spline; projectPoint returns the closest location, inputKey, distanceAlongSpline, distanceToSpline, and tangent (#555).

set_spline_points.summary: Set spline points. A point is either a bare {x,y,z} or the typed form, which keeps what a position alone loses: pointType, arriveTangent, leaveTangent, rotation and scale. The whole batch is validated before any existing geometry is cleared, so a malformed request leaves the spline as it was, and the edit goes through an editor transaction so Undo reaches it. componentName picks one spline on an actor carrying several (#1029). markEdited (default true) sets bSplineHasBeenEdited, the flag the spline editor sets, so a Blueprint construction script rerun keeps these points instead of resetting the spline to its defaults; the result reports splineHasBeenEdited, previousSplineHasBeenEdited and creationMethod, and the rollback restores the flag.

create_spline_actor.summary: Spawn an actor whose root is a SplineComponent named Spline through splinePoints (at least two {x,y,z}, world space unless coordinateSpace is local), with closedLoop, one pointType for every point, and tags. label makes it idempotent: an existing label is reported (onConflict skip), refused (error), or has its points rewritten (update, rolled back to the previous points). A new actor rolls back through delete_actor. The spline is marked edited, so the points survive a construction script rerun.

build_spline_meshes.summary: Fill a spline with a chain of SplineMeshComponents from one staticMesh, for roads, fences, pipes and cables. Each piece is spacing long (default the mesh length along forwardAxis times scale), stretched so a whole number of pieces fills the spline unless stretchToFit is false; scale's other two axes set the cross-section, roll turns every piece, startOffset and endOffset leave the ends empty, collisionProfile sets collision. Output is tagged with generatorName (default SplineMeshes) and the parameters are stored on the actor, so running it again replaces the previous pieces rather than adding to them, and rebuild=true reruns the stored parameters with any passed ones on top. Rolls back to the previous run, or through clear_spline_generated when there was none.

scatter_along_spline.summary: Place one or more meshes along a spline every interval centimetres (default 200) or count times, picking among meshes by weights. offset and positionJitter are in the spline's frame (x along it, y to its right, z up), yawJitter and scaleMin/scaleMax randomise rotation and uniform scale, alignToSpline (default true) turns each placement to the spline, and seed makes the result repeatable. mode instances (default) adds one HierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent per mesh to the spline's actor; mode actors spawns StaticMeshActors. Output is tagged with generatorName (default SplineScatter) and a rerun replaces it; rebuild=true reuses the stored parameters. Rolls back like build_spline_meshes.

clear_spline_generated.summary: Remove everything a spline generator made (its tagged components on the actor and its tagged actors) and the parameters it stored. Idempotent: nothing to remove reports alreadyDeleted. Rolls back by running the generator again with the stored parameters.

create_blockout.summary: Place a blockout primitive: shape box, ramp (rises toward the actor's +X), wedge (a gable with its ridge along Y), cylinder (sides) or stairs (steps, climbing toward +X), size centimetres along the actor's axes with location at the bottom centre. It is a StaticMeshActor tagged with tag (default Blockout) and BlockoutShape:<shape>, using a unit shape mesh generated once and saved under meshFolder (default /Game/Blockout/Meshes) with the engine grid material unless material is given. Rolls back through delete_actor; the shape mesh stays for reuse.

list_blockout.summary: List the blockout actors carrying tag (default Blockout): label, path, shape, mesh, transform, size along the actor's own axes, bottomCentre, world bounds and tags, plus a count per shape. includeReplaced adds the actors replace_blockout put in their place, with the record restore_blockout reads.

match_asset_to_blockout.summary: Rank the StaticMeshes under candidateFolder by how well their bounds fit a blockout actor (actorLabel or actorPath) or every blockout carrying tag. Each candidate reports score (the mean of sizeScore and shapeScore, 1 is identical), its size, the yawOffset that fits best when allowRotation tries a quarter turn, and the uniformScale and stretchScale a fit would apply. limit caps the candidates per blockout; maxCandidates caps how many meshes are loaded.

replace_blockout.summary: Swap blockout actors for a StaticMesh fitted to each one's bounds: assetPath for all of them, or the best match under candidateFolder for each. fit uniform (default) scales evenly to fit inside, stretch matches every axis, none keeps scale 1; the asset's bottom centre lands on the blockout's, with its rotation plus yawOffset. The replacement keeps the label and folder and carries BlockoutReplacement and a record of the blockout, and the blockout is removed. Every target is planned before anything is destroyed. Rolls back through restore_blockout.

restore_blockout.summary: Put back the blockout a replace_blockout replacement recorded (mesh, transform, material, tags, label, folder) and remove the replacement. Takes the replacement by actorLabel, actorPath, or actorPaths as replace_blockout returns them. Rolls back through replace_blockout when every swap used the same asset, fit and yaw.

get_world_settings.summary: Read world settings (GameMode, KillZ, gravity, etc.).

get_actor_bounds.summary: Get actor AABB. Returns origin + extent (#188).

get_component_tree.summary: Deep component-tree dump for an actor. Returns per-component: name, class, attachParent, attachSocket, mobility, visibility, relative+world transforms, tags. For PrimitiveComponents adds collisionProfile/collisionEnabled/bounds/castShadow. For StaticMeshComponent adds staticMesh + materials[], and for an ISM/HISM also instanceCount plus instanced{hierarchical,numCustomDataFloats} - the number you need before deciding whether to touch an ISM at all, since a component holding three instances and one holding three hundred thousand were otherwise the same row (#986). For SkeletalMeshComponent adds skeletalMesh + skeleton + materials[]. For NiagaraComponent adds niagara{asset,active,visible} and for AudioComponent audio{sound,playing} - runtime FX state in PIE (#581). With includeProperties, a TArray/TSet/TMap over 64 entries comes back as its first 64 with count and truncated, and any value over 16384 characters is cut and marked truncated, so per-instance ISM data cannot swell the response (#1277). relativeTo names a scene component on the same actor (a camera, a hand) and adds relativeToComponent, each row's transform in that component's space. socketNames lists bones or sockets; every component that has sockets reports, per name, found, kind (bone|socket), componentSpace and world transforms, and relativeToComponent with relativeTo. world also takes a world object path, so a Blueprint editor preview world (/Engine/Transient.World_N, listed by editor(find_object, className=World)) is readable; with world omitted an actorPath in another world reads that world. The response names the world and worldType that answered, and each scene component also reports hiddenInGame (#240/#241/#302/#320/#370/#353/#581).

get_relative_transform.summary: Compute target's transform in reference's local space (location/rotation/scale). Common dungeon/calibration workflow (#386/#387/#983).

resolve_actor.summary: Resolve internal/runtime actor name to editor label. internalName is e.g. StaticMeshActor_141. Returns actorLabel, actorPath, className, location (#178).

set_actor_property.summary: Set per-instance UPROPERTY on a level actor. 'WorldSettings' as the actorLabel targets the world settings actor. propertyName takes dotted paths like 'Foo.Bar', and a C-style FIXED ARRAY element is addressed by index: 'NavMeshResolutionParams[1].CellSize' reaches the Default tier rather than always writing element 0 (#927). value is string/number/bool/object/array; a label string resolves to an AActor* ref, and a JSON array of labels populates a TArray of actor refs (#538) (#202/#230). Blueprint instance variables are addressed by their variable name. The result reads the property back after the write: value and previousValue in export text, plus changed (#1566).

read_actor_motion.summary: Snapshot motion telemetry for one or many actors: location, rotation, velocity, scale, angularVelocity (when simulating physics), grounded + distanceToGround (downward 200u trace). Defaults to the PIE world with editor fallback. Loop at your sample interval for long telemetry probes (#453).

add_hismc_instances.summary: Bulk-add transforms to a HISMC / ISMC component on an actor (Python add_instance crashes on UE 5.7; this is the C++ path). Each transforms entry is {location: {x,y,z}, rotation?: {pitch,yaw,roll}, scale?: {x,y,z}}; componentName defaults to the first ISMC/HISMC found (#434).

get_instance_transforms.summary: Read every instance transform on an actor's ISMC/HISMC; componentName defaults to the first. Returns instances[{index, location, rotation, scale}] (#697).

update_instance_transform.summary: Update a single ISMC/HISMC instance by index; unspecified location/rotation/scale are preserved (#697).

remove_instance.summary: Remove a single ISMC/HISMC instance by index (#697).

set_nanite_settings.summary: Enable/disable + force-build Nanite on a UStaticMesh asset (rebuilds render data immediately, not on next cook) (#696).

get_nanite_info.summary: Read a UStaticMesh's Nanite state (naniteEnabled, positionPrecision, numLODs) (#696).

add_post_process_blendable.summary: Add a material blendable (post-process material or MID, e.g. a toon/outline pass) to a PostProcessVolume's WeightedBlendables (#666).

set_post_process_settings.summary: Write post-process settings AND enable the bOverride_<Name> flag for every key given. Inside FPostProcessSettings each value is gated by its own override bit, so writing AutoExposureMinBrightness through the generic property setter stores the number, leaves the bit off, and the engine keeps using the default while the details panel shows the value you asked for. Nothing errors. That is the trap this closes: the auto-enable IS the action. Works off the struct's reflected fields, so every setting is reachable, not just exposure, and a key that has no override bit (WeightedBlendables) says so instead of implying one was enabled. Every key is resolved BEFORE anything is written, so a typo fails the call rather than half-applying it, and each key reports previousValue, newValue, overrideWasEnabled and overrideEnabled read back from the struct. Finds the settings on the actor or on one of its components; a camera with several camera components needs componentName (or propertyName) and is refused by listing the candidates rather than by picking one. The level is left dirty and is NOT saved (#950).

get_post_process_settings.summary: Read post-process settings with the override bit that decides whether each one applies. onlyOverridden answers 'is this volume actually overriding exposure' directly, instead of dumping the whole FPostProcessSettings as one ExportText blob to parse. Each row is name, type, value, overridden (the bOverride_<Name> bit) and hasOverrideFlag; the bits themselves are not listed as settings of their own, because a caller who writes the bit without the value has changed nothing. Also returns totalSettings and overriddenCount, so 'nothing is overridden here' is a fact rather than an empty list (#950).

set_fixed_exposure.summary: Pin exposure on a post-process volume or camera in one call. Writes the same value to AutoExposureMinBrightness and AutoExposureMaxBrightness, which is how the engine disables eye adaptation, and enables both override flags so the values actually apply (#950).

export_actor_fbx.summary: Export an actor's skeletal/static mesh to FBX and write a metadata sidecar JSON (actor transform, mesh, materials, skeleton) for a downstream bridge (e.g. MetaTailor). Returns fbx + metadata paths (#637).

spawn_skeletal_mesh_actor.summary: Spawn a SkeletalMeshActor for visual/deform verification. Optional per-slot COMPONENT material overrides (they write the component's OverrideMaterials, not the mesh ASSET's slots, which material(build_material) writes) and single-node animation preview (animSequence + loop). Each entry in materials[] comes back with ok, and a path that does not load or a slot index past the mesh's slot count is reported rather than silently dropped, because a silently dropped assignment reads as one that worked. To dress an actor that is already placed, or to put one material on every slot, use level(set_component_materials) (#946). Returns actorLabel + boxExtent + materialSlotCount. The animSequence is written to the component's editable AnimationData, so it persists across a level save/reload instead of only driving the runtime preview and coming back in A-pose (#790) (#679/#677).

delete_actors.summary: Bulk-delete actors. The filter names say exactly what they match, because two level actions taking similar-sounding filters with different semantics is how a caller ends up trusting a wrong zero (#963): labelPrefix is a CASE-SENSITIVE PREFIX over the EDITOR LABEL, labelContains a case-insensitive SUBSTRING over the label, nameContains a case-insensitive substring over the INTERNAL name, className a case-sensitive substring over the class name. get_outliner's nameFilter is looser than any of them (label OR internal name, substring), so a string that selects a set there can select a different set here. When nothing matches, the response explains it rather than returning a bare zero: zeroMatchHint reports how many actors the same string WOULD have matched under the other semantics with samples, and a World Partition map says that only loaded actors were enumerated. classPathContains is a case-insensitive substring of the generated UClass path (e.g. /SurvivalGameKitV2/), so a whole vendor folder can be selected without listing every Blueprint class, and classPathContainsAny is the same match against any of several substrings (#924). folderPath selects one World Outliner folder exactly and folderPathPrefix that folder and everything nested under it, the same folder match get_outliner and query_components use; a folder filter that matches nothing returns similarFolders (#1529). dryRun previews. Returns matched/deleted/labels/classPaths/folderPaths (#220/#924/#963).

delete_exact_labeled_actors_in_levels.summary: Delete actors by EXACT label across several map packages in one call, without leaving the maps open or dirty. Previews by default (dryRun defaults to TRUE, the opposite of delete_actors), and every level is loaded and preflighted before anything is deleted, so a bad label in the last map cannot half-commit the first. Refuses the whole request on duplicate labels, a class that does not match expectedClassPath, actors living in a streaming sublevel, WorldSettings/default brush/level blueprint, World Partition maps, a read-only .umap, or an editor that is already dirty. Saves only the maps it actually changed, then returns to the map that was open. Limits: 16 levels, 256 labels per level. onMissing=ignore makes a replay idempotent.

list_actor_descs.summary: World Partition ONLY: list on-disk actor descriptors, including actors whose cell is not loaded and which every other actor query therefore reports as absent. Returns guid/label/class/package/folderPath/bounds/runtimeGrid/dataLayers plus a loaded flag, and separate loadedMatches/unloadedMatches counts so 'not streamed in' is distinguishable from 'does not exist'. packages[] looks actors up by their external actor package (full path or the XX/YY/NAME tail, as a changelist lists them) and reports the ones no descriptor holds as missingPackages. Needs UE 5.5 or newer (#746).

load_actor_descs.summary: World Partition ONLY: pin matched actors so they become resident and the normal actor actions can reach them, or unpin to release. Pinning is used rather than transient streaming because a transient load is dropped again by the streaming system mid-measurement. Takes the same filters as list_actor_descs (packages[] included, with missingPackages) and refuses to act on more than maxActors (default 256) so an unfiltered call cannot pin a whole map by accident. Reports residentAfter, read back from the world rather than assumed. Unpinning releases pins and nothing else: an actor an editor loaded region or location volume holds stays resident, and list_loaded_regions / unload_loaded_regions release those. Needs UE 5.5 or newer (#746).

list_loaded_regions.summary: World Partition ONLY: list the editor loader adapters that keep actors resident, which load_actor_descs(unpin) cannot release because they are not pins: user loaded regions (the World Partition editor's Load Region from Selection, and the regions the editor restores when a map is reopened), location volumes, and any other loader the engine tracks. Each row has an id that unload_loaded_regions accepts, its kind (userRegion, locationVolume, actor or other), label, bounds, loaded, and actorCount / residentActors / dirtyActorPackages measured over those bounds (the adapter keeps its own reference set private, so the count is the spatially loaded descriptors that meet the box). Unloaded sources are hidden unless includeUnloaded=true. Paged. Needs UE 5.5 or newer.

unload_loaded_regions.summary: World Partition ONLY: unload editor loaded regions and location volumes by id (from list_loaded_regions) and/or by a bounds box, the same as Unload Region in the World Partition editor, which is the only way to make actors a loaded region holds non-resident. Refuses the whole request, unloading nothing, when a region holds actors whose packages are dirty (their unsaved edits would be discarded) unless force=true; refuses more than maxRegions (default 8) so a wide box cannot unload everything; dryRun previews. residentAfter is read back from the world over the unloaded footprint, with residentPinnedAfter and a note when something else (a pin, an overlapping region) still holds actors. Needs UE 5.5 or newer.

load_region.summary: World Partition ONLY: load a box as a user loaded region, the same as Load Region from Selection in the World Partition editor, and return its id for unload_loaded_regions. Refuses a box holding more than maxActors (default 256) actors; a loaded region over the same box is reported as existed. Its rollback is unload_loaded_regions for that id. Needs UE 5.5 or newer.

get_world_partition_settings.summary: World Partition ONLY: the streaming knobs on the open map, plus the runtime cell transformer stack. Returns the world partition and runtime hash classes, whether streaming is enabled, the default HLOD layer, and grids[] with each grid's name, CellSize, LoadingRange and a dotted path rooted at the world partition. Grids are found by REFLECTION rather than against a fixed class, so this answers for the RuntimeHashSet layout and the older spatial hash alike. cellTransformers[] lists each stack entry with its class, its instancePath and the current values of the instanced transformer object's editable properties, which no read exposed (#985).

set_world_partition_settings.summary: World Partition ONLY: write the streaming knobs. cellSize and loadingRange are the shorthand for the primary tuning pair and pick the map's only grid automatically, or name one with grid (its name) or gridPath (the dotted path from get_world_partition_settings). settings takes any dotted path rooted at the world partition, which is how the INSTANCED runtime cell transformer object is configured ('RuntimeCellsTransformerStack[0].Instance.SomeProperty') - that object is read-only through Python and was previously set by hand in the editor UI. Every path is resolved BEFORE anything is written, so a bad path fails the call rather than leaving the map streaming on a mixture nobody asked for, and each write reports previousValue and the value read back. Streaming settings only apply to cells generated after the change, so rebuild the streaming data before measuring. The map package is left dirty and is NOT saved (#985).

add_runtime_cell_transformer.summary: World Partition ONLY: append a WorldPartitionRuntimeCellTransformer to RuntimeCellsTransformerStack and configure its instanced object in the same call. Adding the entry without being able to write the instance would leave the manual editor step exactly where it was, so the instance is created here and properties are applied to it. skipIfPresent (default true) makes a rerun a no-op that reports the existing index instead of stacking duplicates. position inserts at an index rather than appending, because the stack is ordered (#985).

set_world_partition_streaming.summary: World Partition ONLY: turn streaming on or off for the open map (UWorldPartitionSubsystem::SetStreamingEnabled on UE 5.9, UWorldPartition::SetEnableStreaming before it). With streaming off every actor is always loaded. An unchanged state is reported as unchanged; the rollback sets the previous state (#1828).

set_runtime_hash_class.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: convert the open map's runtime hash to another class (WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet, WorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash), keeping what the conversion supports. Refusals quote the engine's reason (#1828).

list_runtime_partitions.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: the runtime hash set's partitions in declaration order, each with its class and HLOD setup names (#1828).

get_runtime_partition.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: one runtime partition's class and editable properties (cell size, loading range...), or with setupName the partition of one of its HLOD setups; hasPartition=false for a setup without one (#1828).

add_runtime_partition.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: add a runtime partition to the runtime hash set (default class RuntimePartitionLHGrid), with default values and no HLOD setups. A name already there is reported as existed; the rollback removes the new partition (#1828).

remove_runtime_partition.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: remove a runtime partition; the last one cannot be removed. Actors still assigned to it stream with the first partition until reassigned. An absent name is reported as alreadyRemoved (#1828).

rename_runtime_partition.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: rename a runtime partition; HLODs must be rebuilt afterwards. The rollback renames it back (#1828).

set_runtime_partition_properties.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: write editable properties of a runtime partition (or, with setupName, of one of its HLOD setup partitions), the way the subsystem documents changing their settings. Every name is checked before anything is written; returns previous and readBack, and the rollback writes the previous values (#1828).

list_hlod_setups.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: a runtime partition's HLOD setups in hierarchy order, each with its partition class and HLOD layers. The non-spatially loaded setup, when present, is last and named None (#1828).

add_hlod_setup.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: add a spatially loaded HLOD setup without layers after the partition's existing ones; its partition is derived from the previous level. The rollback removes it (#1828).

remove_hlod_setup.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: remove a spatially loaded HLOD setup, leaving its layers unassigned (listed in unassignedHlodLayers). The None setup cannot be removed (#1828).

set_hlod_setup_layers.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: assign HLODLayer assets to an HLOD setup, removing them from the partition's other setups; an empty array leaves it without layers. The rollback restores the setup's previous layers (#1828).

build_hlod_actors.summary: World Partition ONLY: build loaded HLOD actors in place, as their details panel's Build HLOD button does (UWorldPartitionSubsystem::BuildHLODActors on UE 5.9, AWorldPartitionHLOD::BuildHLOD before it). Omit actorLabels for every loaded HLOD actor; up to date actors are skipped unless force. Does not save (#1828).

build_world_partition_hlods.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: set up and build the open map's HLODs in an external process, as the Build HLODs menu does (UWorldPartitionSubsystem::BuildHLODs). Every modified package must be saved first. The map is unloaded and reopened, so earlier actor references go stale. hlodLayer builds only that layer's HLODs (#1828).

delete_world_partition_hlods.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: delete every HLOD of the open map in an external process (UWorldPartitionSubsystem::DeleteHLODs). Every modified package must be saved first; the map is unloaded and reopened (#1828).

get_hlod_stats.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: build statistics of every HLOD actor from its saved descriptor, without loading it: name, hlodLayer, spatiallyLoaded, dataLayers and stats (InputActorCount, MeshTriangleCount, MemoryDiskSizeBytes, BuildTimeTotalMilliseconds...). HLOD actors created since the last save are not listed yet (#1828).

get_world_partition_minimap.summary: World Partition ONLY: the open map's minimap actor and its settings, with the world bounds a build would capture and the texture resolution it would produce (UE 5.9). exists=false when the map has no minimap actor (#1828).

create_world_partition_minimap.summary: World Partition ONLY: spawn the minimap actor in the persistent level when the map has none (UWorldPartitionSubsystem::GetMiniMap with bCreateIfMissing). An existing actor is reported as existed; the rollback deletes a new one (#1828).

build_world_partition_minimap.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: build and save the open map's minimap in an external process, as the Build World Partition Editor Minimap menu does, without its prompts. Every modified package must be saved first; the map is unloaded and reopened (#1828).

check_world_partition_errors.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: the map's World Partition problems, as Map Check's World Partition validation and the Scene Outliner's Repair Errors see them: errorType, severity, message and the actor, referenced actor or object each names, with errors and warnings counts (#1828).

repair_world_partition_errors.summary: World Partition ONLY, UE 5.9: repair what check_world_partition_errors reports as NotUsingExternalActors, WorldDataLayersNotSaved and InvalidActorFile, as the Scene Outliner's Repair Errors button does. Saves, deletes invalid actor files and clears the undo history when actors move; not undoable. Reports repairableBefore and repairableAfter (#1828).

replace_actors_with_class.summary: Replace actors with new instances of an actor class, as the editor's Replace Selected Actors With command does (UEditorActorSubsystem::ReplaceActorsWithClass on UE 5.9, the same factory path before it). The class needs an actor factory that works without an asset (lights, empty actors, volumes); asset-backed classes go through replace_actors_with_asset. One undo transaction; returns newActors (#1828).

replace_actors_with_asset.summary: Replace actors with new actors created from an asset (static mesh, Blueprint, particle system), as the editor's Replace Selected Actors With command does (UEditorActorSubsystem::ReplaceActorsWithAsset on UE 5.9). copySourceProperties (default true) copies a replaced actor's values when the asset is a Blueprint sharing its native parent. One undo transaction; returns newActors (#1828).

rebuild_brush.summary: UE 5.9: rebuild a brush or volume's geometry from a brush builder without changing its transform, pivot or visibility (UEditorActorSubsystem::RebuildBrush). builderClass picks a builder (CubeBuilder, CylinderBuilder...), default the brush's own; builderProperties sets its parameters, such as {X, Y, Z} for a cube. The rollback rebuilds with the previous builder and values (#1828).

set_actor_hlod_layer.summary: Assign (or clear) the per-actor HLODLayer override across every actor a selector picks. Assigning one across 295 InstancedFoliageActors was a Python loop. Goes through the engine's own AActor::SetHLODLayer rather than writing the private property directly, so the result behaves like an edit made in the details panel. hlodLayer=null clears the override. An actor already carrying the requested layer is reported as unchanged rather than counted as an update, so a rerun is readable. Optionally sets bEnableAutoLODGeneration in the same pass, since the layer only matters when the actor is allowed to build HLODs at all. On a World Partition map this dirties one package per actor and does NOT save (#985).

set_actor_folder_path.summary: Assign World Outliner folder paths in bulk. Filter with actorLabels (exact), labelPrefix, className or tag; pass an empty folderPath to move actors back to the root. Runs in one transaction so the whole move is a single undo, reads each write back (verified), and reports missingLabels for names that matched no actor. Editor-only organisation: the level is left dirty and is NOT saved (#767).

create_outliner_folder.summary: Create World Outliner folders that hold no actors yet, such as a layout to move actors into later. Pass folderPath, folderPaths, or both; nested paths like Props/Lights are fine. Each path reports created, existed or failed (invalid_path, create_failed), so a replay is readable. Its rollback is delete_outliner_folder over the folders it created (#1529).

delete_outliner_folder.summary: Remove EMPTY World Outliner folders, together with the empty folders nested under them. A folder outlives its actors: emptying one with delete_actors(folderPath|folderPathPrefix) leaves the folder behind, and this is the call that clears it. A folder that still holds an actor anywhere in its subtree is refused as not_empty with the actor count and sample labels, never emptied for you. Each path reports deleted, would_delete (dryRun), absent or failed; deletedFolders lists every folder removed, and the rollback recreates them with create_outliner_folder. On a World Partition map only loaded actors are checked (#1529).

add_actor_tag.summary: Append a tag to an actor's Tags array (#219).

remove_actor_tag.summary: Remove a tag from an actor's Tags array (#219).

list_actor_tags.summary: List an actor's Tags, in the order they are authored on the actor (#219/#983).

rename_actor_object.summary: Rename a placed actor's OBJECT NAME (its FName, the last segment of actorPath), keeping its editor label; set_actor_label and the outliner rename change only the label. Every target is tested first and a name already held in the level is refused, because UObject::Rename onto a taken name is a fatal engine error. A batch is all or nothing: one bad entry renames nothing. newName omitted generates a unique name from the class. renames:[{actorPath|actorLabel, newName?}] renames several in ONE undo transaction. Refuses WorldSettings, the level script actor, the default brush, transient actors and actors in their own external package (World Partition, one file per actor). Returns oldName/newName/oldPath/newPath per actor and dirtiedPackages; the map is NOT saved and no redirector is created, so soft references that stored the old path do not follow. dryRun previews (#1574).

attach_component.summary: Attach an actor root or exact named child SceneComponent to an actor root or exact named parent SceneComponent. A non-root child changes only component hierarchy, not actor parentage. An already-matching attachment is a no-op and does not reapply transform rules. relativeLocation/relativeRotation set a corrective offset in the parent component or socket frame after the attach (or on an existing matching attachment), so a tool-in-hand calibration onto a skeletal socket is one call; the result reports the relative transform read back (#1250). Returns verified resolved component and socket details; native attachment failure is an error.

detach_component.summary: Detach an actor root or exact named child SceneComponent while preserving world transform. Omitted childComponentName selects the actor root. An already-detached component is a verified no-op. Returns previous parent component/socket details plus alreadyDetached and detachmentChanged.

set_current_edit_level.summary: Set the active edit-target sub-level so subsequent spawns land in it (#204).

list_streaming_sublevels.summary: List streaming sub-levels with transform + initially-loaded/visible flags (#206).

batch_translate.summary: Translate a set of actors by an offset (#203/#983).

place_actors_batch.summary: Bulk-spawn StaticMeshActors with per-instance mesh + transform. Mesh loads cached per path. Each entry may carry tags[] and a parentLabel; attaches run after every spawn with the world transform kept, so a parent may come later in the same batch, and each is reported in attachments[] with its refusal reason when it fails. Returns spawned/failedMesh/failedSpawn counts + labels, plus attached/failedAttach when any entry names a parent (#264, #1263).

batch_set_properties.summary: Set the same properties on every actor an editor-side SELECTOR picks. batch_translate needs an explicit label list, which for auto-numbered labels is a payload you have to generate first; this takes tag / classFilter / labelPrefix / labelContains / folderPath instead, so '190 SpotLights tagged LichtTest' is one call. Property writes delegate to set_actor_property, so dotted paths, actor-label object references and TArray-of-actor-labels all behave identically to the single-actor action. The whole batch is ONE undo transaction. dryRun resolves every property against every matched actor's class and reports currentValue without writing. The level is left dirty and is NOT saved. Pass at least one selector: actorLabels, labelPrefix, labelContains, tag, classFilter, folderPath or folderPathPrefix (#984).

bulk_set_component_property.summary: Set one property on the SAME NAMED COMPONENT across every actor a selector picks (the real case: NavModifierComponent.AreaClass on dozens of placed StaticMeshActors). Delegates to set_component_property per actor, so value semantics match exactly, including JSON null to clear an object reference. An actor that has no component of that name is reported as no_such_component rather than counted as a failure or silently skipped. One undo transaction. The level is left dirty and is NOT saved (#941).

remove_components_by_class.summary: Remove every instance component of a class across the actors a selector picks. remove_component takes one name at a time, which cannot reach 230 orphaned SplineMeshComponents whose names are auto-generated (SplineMeshComponent_0, _1, ...). dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE here, unlike delete_actors: this deletes components you cannot enumerate by name, so you see the list first. Only INSTANCE components are removed; a native or SCS component belongs to the class and is reported under skippedNonInstanceComponents rather than destroyed, because destroying it would come back on the next construction rerun. Omitting every actor selector means every loaded actor, which is a legitimate request and the reason for the dryRun default. One undo transaction. Pass componentClass and at least one selector (#907).

spawn_actors_batch.summary: Bulk-spawn actors of ANY class with per-instance properties, from explicit transforms or from positions DERIVED in the editor. place_actors_batch is StaticMeshActor only and spawn_light takes one position. Exactly one source: instances[]; fromComponents, which places one actor per matched component at boundsOrigin + boxExtent*extentFraction + offset; or alongSpline, which scatters by distance. fromComponents defaults to space='local' on purpose: a component's WORLD bounds are axis-aligned, so 'the top of the mesh' computed from them is not on a rotated lamp post, while local bounds carry the component's own orientation. That is what makes 'a SpotLight at 72 percent of each of 190 lamp posts' one call instead of 190 bounds reads and 190 spawns. properties applies to every spawn and per-instance properties win. dryRun returns every computed transform without spawning. maxSpawn (default 500) refuses a plan bigger than you meant. The level is left dirty and is NOT saved (#987).

get_skinned_vertices.summary: Read a placed skinned mesh component's vertices as posed: where they are drawn now, in the editor world or PIE (world, pieInstance). A leader-pose follower (gloves, clothing, heads driven by another component's pose) reads through its leader's pose, as it is drawn. Positions are skinned on the CPU from the render LOD the component draws (lodIndex picks another), with active morph targets applied; cloth simulation and mesh deformers are not included. space picks component (default) or world for positions, box and nearPoint. Select with boneNames (summed render weight on those bones, includeChildBones, minWeight), box {min, max}, nearPoint with radius, any combination, or none for every vertex. include picks positions, weights and triangles (default positions and weights). Each vertex returns vertexIndex (a render vertex index of that LOD, not a source vertex ID), position, influences [{boneName, boneIndex, weight}] and, with boneNames, selectedWeight; triangles lists each fully selected triangle once across pages with triangleIndex, vertexIndices and sectionIndex. Pages with startIndex and limit (default 2000, at most 20000) and returns hasMore and nextStartIndex; dumpToFile writes the whole selection to outputPath (default under Saved/UE_MCP/SkinnedVertices) and returns only the summary. Also returns lodIndex, drawnLodIndex, componentTransform, leaderPoseComponent for a follower, morphTargets applied, vertexCount, selectedVertexCount and selectedBounds. For source vertices in the bind pose use asset(read_skeletal_mesh_vertices). Read-only.

set_component_skeletal_mesh.summary: Swap the mesh on a skinned mesh component of an actor that is already placed, through SetSkinnedAssetAndUpdate. Writing SkeletalMeshAsset or SkinnedAsset as a raw property leaves the pose buffers sized for the old skeleton and crashes the editor on the next pose evaluation, so set_property, set_actor_property and set_component_property route those names through the same setter. Returns previousValue, value, materialSlotCount and materialSlotNames (slot layouts differ per mesh). One undo transaction; the level is dirtied and NOT saved (#1099).

set_component_materials.summary: Set per-slot COMPONENT material overrides on placed actors. This is the other half of material assignment and the half that had no action: material(build_material) and asset(set_property) write the mesh ASSET's slots, while a placed actor usually needs the instance override the details panel edits (OverrideMaterials). set_actor_material does one slot on whichever primitive component it finds first, so dressing a placed skeletal mesh meant a Python loop over get_num_materials(). Exactly one of: materials[] (index = slot; a null or empty entry clears just that slot's override), material (one path applied to EVERY slot), clearOverrides=true (drop every override so the asset's own slots show through). Every slot comes back with its previous and new path AND whether each is a componentOverride or the meshDefault, read back rather than echoed. Every material path is resolved before anything is written, so a bad path fails the call instead of half-applying it. Works on any UMeshComponent (static or skeletal). One undo transaction; the LEVEL is dirtied and NOT saved, the mesh asset is untouched (#946).

spawn_transient_actor.summary: Spawn an actor for VERIFICATION that cannot be saved into the map. Checking anything that only exists on a live actor needs a subject, and spawning a normal one and forgetting to delete it is how a SceneCapture2D ended up committed to source control. So this actor is transient by construction: RF_Transient (the package serializer skips it), bTemporaryEditorActor (an editor preview actor, kept out of the level's persistent actor list), no external actor package on a World Partition map, and its label is set with bMarkDirty=false because SetActorLabel dirties the map by default. It carries a UEMCP_TransientVerification tag so it can be listed and so destroy refuses anything it did not create, and the response reports dirtiedPackages rather than promising nothing was dirtied. initialize controls how far towards a running state it is taken, because the EDITOR WORLD HAS NOT BEGUN PLAY and a spawned actor therefore gets neither InitializeComponent nor BeginPlay: 'none' spawns only, 'construction' (default) reruns construction scripts, 'beginPlay' also registers components and dispatches the begin-play cycle on this actor, which is what a component doing its setup in BeginPlay (a GAS ability system component's attribute-set scan, for one) needs before it can be read. 'beginPlay' also runs InitializeComponent on registered components. Each returned component reports registered, wantsInitializeComponent, initialized (InitializeComponent ran or is not wanted) and hasBegunPlay, read from the component, and while BeginPlay has not run the response carries hasBegunPlay=false, componentsNotBegunPlay and a beginPlayWarning, because a function invoked on such a component can succeed and change nothing (#1480). Destroy it with destroy_transient_actor. properties (propertyName -> value) are written through set_actor_property before construction and BeginPlay, so gameplay tags, tag containers, structs and object references take the same forms they take there; each comes back in properties[] with ok, the value read back after initialization, or its error, and any failure fails the call (#1103) (#956). The lighting cache is invalidated after the spawn, as the editor does on placement, so a stationary light gets its preview shadow map channel and lights the scene without being moved (#1548).

destroy_transient_actor.summary: Destroy an actor created by spawn_transient_actor. It will ONLY destroy an actor carrying the UEMCP_TransientVerification tag and RF_Transient: a label or path that resolves to a real level actor is refused by name rather than deleted, because this is the cleanup call and a mistyped label at cleanup time is how real work disappears. Use delete_actor or delete_actors for a real level actor (#956).
