list_transient_actors.summary: List the verification actors spawned by spawn_transient_actor that are still in the world, so nothing is left behind by accident. They cannot be saved into the map and do not survive a map reload, but they are live until destroyed (#956).

convert_brushes_to_static_mesh.summary: Convert BSP brushes into StaticMeshActors via UEditorActorSubsystem::ConvertActors, generating the static meshes into destinationPath. Finishing a blockout pass otherwise meant doing it by hand. dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE, because conversion DESTROYS the source brushes and there is no way back to a builder brush once the map is saved. Every candidate the selector picked comes back with a verdict, so nothing is silently dropped: the default builder brush, brush shapes, volumes (both derive from ABrush and neither is geometry a player sees) and subtractive brushes (they carve space and have no surface, so converting one yields an empty mesh that looks like success) are all excluded unless you opt in by name. classFilter is EXACT by default here. Reports convertedFrom (recorded before the call, since the actors are gone after it), newActorLabels and newStaticMeshes (#911).

rerun_construction.summary: Re-run the construction script on PLACED actor instances, so an SCS or construction-script change reaches the copies already in the level instead of only new ones. blueprint(run_construction_script) builds a TEMPORARY actor and throws it away, and Python cannot do this at all because Actor.rerun_construction_scripts() is missing from the wrapper. Requires actorLabels or className: this destroys and rebuilds every generated component on each match, so it will not run against a whole level implicitly. Reports reran, failed[], samples[], and how many matches have no user construction script (their generated components are still rebuilt, but a caller expecting a script change to land needs to know). Compares each actor's saved state before and after: changed[] actors leave their packages dirty (dirtiedPackages[]) and are NOT saved (#944); unchanged[] actors whose package was clean before are put back to clean (restoredCleanPackages[]), so a no-op rerun does not rewrite the file on the next save (#1547).

recreate_physics_state.summary: Rebuild the physics and collision state on the components a selector picks, after the mesh data underneath them changed. Stale collision makes line_trace report a MISS through solid geometry, which is the worst kind of wrong answer because nothing about it looks wrong. dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE and is the preflight: it lists which components would be rebuilt and what their collision enabled state and profile are right now. Requires at least one bound and never refreshes a whole world implicitly. Returns per-component before/after collision state plus a post-refresh collisionSummary histogram (#915).

resave_mesh_users.summary: Rebuild the collision of every LOADED component using the given static meshes, then save exactly the packages that own those actors. Use it after a mesh's collision changed. A SplineMeshComponent keeps its own deformed copy of its mesh's collision, saved with the actor, and rebuilds it only when the mesh's BodySetupGuid differs from the one it cached, so an AggGeom edit that left the GUID alone leaves every copy stale in memory and on disk. recreateCollision (default true) calls RecreateCollision on each SplineMeshComponent, rebuilding the copy from the current mesh whatever the GUID says, and RecreatePhysicsState on every match. Components match by mesh object path, case-insensitive, and componentClass narrows them to StaticMeshComponent or SplineMeshComponent (default any). Matches are grouped by the actor's external package (one file per actor) or its level's package, and those are saved through the same targeted save asset(save, assetPaths) uses, so no other dirty package is written. A package holding only StaticMeshComponents has nothing of its own to write and reports notDirty. dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE and lists every package, actor and component with the component's current body setup GUID and bounds, and for a spline whether its cached GUID matches the mesh. Per package: actor labels, componentCount, status saved | notDirty | failed with a reason, wasDirty, and the file's size and mtime before and after with fileChanged. Scans only actors resident in the editor world; on World Partition, load the cells first with level(load_actor_descs). Refuses during PIE and over maxActors.

test_component_overlap.summary: Do two placed components overlap? Returns the boolean plus both sides' local bounds, world bounds and world transforms, and separation (when apart) or penetration depth (when overlapping). For a UBoxComponent it also returns boxExtentUnscaled, the authored BoxExtent the details panel shows, which no other read exposed. method=OBB (default) runs a separating-axis test on the components' oriented local bounds, so a rotated box is tested as a rotated box; method=AABB compares the axis-aligned world bounds and adds a per-axis gap. Deliberately geometric rather than a physics overlap query: a physics answer depends on collision state, and stale collision state is what makes a trace lie (see recreate_physics_state). Omitting a componentName selects that actor's root component (#914).

shape_trace.summary: Sweep a sphere, axis-aligned box or vertical capsule in the editor or PIE world. Uses line_trace channel names and selectors. Returns the first blocking hit plus bStartPenetrating; multi=true returns overlaps through the first blocker, capped at 64 with totalHits and truncated.

line_trace.summary: Line trace. world selects which world is traced: 'editor' (default) or 'pie' for the LIVE running PIE world, which is the only way to check geometry that exists once play has begun (#933). Traces simple collision by default, the same as a gameplay trace, so the result matches what the running game hits; pass traceComplex to trace per-triangle instead. multi=true returns hits[] in distance order, every overlap up to and including the first blocker, capped at 64 with totalHits and truncated; hit stays true only when something blocked. channel picks the collision channel, including channels this project renamed in its collision settings. The response echoes traceComplex, channel and the world that actually answered, and faceIndex is only present on a complex hit. Returns hit + actorLabel/actorClass/componentName/componentClass/location/impactPoint/normal/distance/faceIndex/boneName/physicalMaterial (#420, #807, #933). From inside a run_python_file script the same trace is unreal.MCPTraceLibrary.line_trace(start, end, world, pie_instance, channel, trace_complex) (#1283).

bulk_line_trace.summary: Batch of line traces. Each traces[] item uses the same semantics as line_trace (start + end or direction+distance, simple collision by default, optional traceComplex/channel/ignoreActors). The top-level world applies to the WHOLE batch, so one call cannot straddle the editor and PIE worlds and present the results as comparable. Caps at 256. Returns results[] in traces[] order, one per item, each with the same fields as line_trace (or success=false + error for that item). A per-item multi=true returns that item's hits[] the way line_trace does, so a floor or ceiling height profile is one call (#933, #1564).

actors_in_box.summary: Every actor whose bounds meet a world-space box (min, max). mode=overlap (default) keeps any actor whose bounds intersect the box, touching faces included; mode=contained keeps only actors whose bounds lie fully inside it. Bounds are computed the way get_actor_bounds computes them; an actor with no primitive component counts as its location (bounds.source=location), and onlyColliding drops it. Hidden means hidden in the queried world: editor-hidden for the editor world, hiddenInGame for world=pie; includeHidden keeps them. Each row: label, path, class, folderPath, location, rotation, scale, bounds{origin,extent,min,max,source}, contained, editorHidden, hiddenInGame. Rows are sorted by label; limit (default 200, max 2000) reports total and truncated (#1564).

snap_instances_to_surface.summary: Project ISMC/HISMC instances down onto surface geometry, preserving each instance's rotation and scale. Dry-run by default: preflights every requested instance and reports what would move before anything does, then applies successful projections in one transaction with rollback. Filter the surfaces traced against with surfaceActorClass/surfaceActorLabels so instances do not snap onto each other. onMiss controls whether a miss aborts the batch or is skipped. Does not save packages (#905).

summarize_static_mesh_usage.summary: Read-only inventory of which static meshes are actually placed in the loaded world, aggregated in one game-thread scan instead of walking every actor and component. This is the action for placement counts, and query_components is not a substitute for it: grouping there only increments, so one HISM holding 5,000 instances counts as 1, while this SUMS real ISM/HISM instances and counts distinct actors per mesh, and it sorts every aggregate before truncating so the top N is the true top N with an exact totalUniqueMeshes. Distinguishes actors, components and placements. Results are bounded; full-scan totals are preserved alongside the truncated rows. Loads nothing and saves nothing (#903).

audit_performance.summary: Read-only scene performance audit of the loaded level, or of the box regionMin..regionMax, in one game-thread scan. Ranked, bounded lists with totals: trianglesByMesh (LOD0 triangles x placements, share of the level, Nanite flag), regions (gridSize X/Y cells by triangles and by shadowed-light overlap), instancingCandidates (one static mesh placed as at least instancingMinCount separate components, with the separate draws that costs), dynamicShadowCasters (count, movable count, costliest by triangles), lights (shadowed point/spot/rect lights by how many others their attenuation spheres touch, and stationary lights that may exceed the four stationary shadow channels), texelDensityOutliers and lightmapResolutionOutliers (outlierFactor above or below the median), naniteCandidates (static meshes at or over heavyTriangleThreshold rendering without Nanite, with blockers such as a translucent slot), and translucentOverdraw (translucent primitives that are large or stacked). Static estimates from asset and component data, not measurements; confirm with editor(analyze_trace). Never writes. dumpToFile writes every row to JSON.

snap_actor_to_floor.summary: Snap an actor's bounds-bottom to the first downward line-trace hit. Equivalent of the End-key shortcut, works on arbitrary geometry (not just Landscape). The actor lookup and the downward trace both run in the world named by world, so a PIE snap measures against PIE geometry (#933) (#419, #933). World Partition HLOD actors are skipped, since the editor makes them traceable but the game does not, and listed in skippedHlodActors; with only HLOD below, the call refuses until the cell is loaded. In the editor world the snap is one undo transaction and dirties the actor's package, reported as packageDirty.

epic_add_actors_to_data_layer.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Adds actors to a data layer, creating its instance in the current world if it has none yet. Actors already in the layer are left unchanged. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_component.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Adds a component to an actor instance or blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.AddComponent.

epic_add_cone.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.primitive.PrimitiveTools] Adds a cone-shaped StaticMeshComponent to an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.PrimitiveToolset.AddCone.

epic_add_cube.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.primitive.PrimitiveTools] Adds a cube-shaped StaticMeshComponent to an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.PrimitiveToolset.AddCube.

epic_add_cylinder.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.primitive.PrimitiveTools] Adds a cylinder-shaped StaticMeshComponent to an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.PrimitiveToolset.AddCylinder.

epic_add_sphere.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.primitive.PrimitiveTools] Adds a sphere-shaped StaticMeshComponent to an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.PrimitiveToolset.AddSphere.

epic_add_tag.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Adds a tag to an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.AddTag.

epic_add_to_scene_from_asset.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Creates a new actor in the scene from an asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.AddToSceneFromAsset.

epic_add_to_scene_from_class.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Creates a new instance of the specified object at the specified transform. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.AddToSceneFromClass.

epic_annotate_actor.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Annotate a scene actor, so its meshes are marked in the matte. Annotating it again replaces the prompt. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_are_annotated_actors_always_on_top.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Whether annotated scene actors draw through occluders, which also makes the matte ignore occlusion. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_are_labels_visible.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Whether the viewport draws the prompt labels. Each annotation can also hide its own (bShowLabel). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_can_edit.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Checks whether an actor can be edited. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_commit_level_instance.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Saves or discards edits to a level instance and exits edit mode. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.CommitLevelInstance.

epic_create_data_layer_asset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Creates a new Data Layer asset in the content browser. A Data Layer asset is reusable across levels; assign it to actors in the current world by adding them to the data layer. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_level.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Creates a new empty level asset and opens it in the editor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_level_instance.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Creates a Level Instance actor in the scene referencing an existing level asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.CreateLevelInstance.

epic_delete_folder.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Deletes a folder from the outliner. Actors directly in the folder are moved to the parent folder. Sub-folders and their actors are preserved by re-rooting them under the parent. For example, deleting 'Lighting' with a sub-folder 'Lighting/Spotlights' leaves 'Spotlights' intact under the parent. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.DeleteFolder.

epic_diff.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.ActorToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two actors. Compares the actors' classes, top-level properties, and per-component class and top-level properties. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff__level_toolset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two scene asset packages, each expected to contain a single external actor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_edit_level_instance.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Opens a level instance for editing. While in edit mode, scene tools such as add_to_scene_from_class and remove_from_scene operate within the level instance's sub-level. Only one level instance can be in edit mode at a time. Call commit_level_instance when done to save or discard changes. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.EditLevelInstance.

epic_find_actors.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Searches the scene for actors that match specific criteria. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.FindActors.

epic_find_annotation.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Find an annotation by the id an MCP tool or GetAnnotations reported. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_gather_visible_annotations.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Returns the annotations with their on-screen rects, as the JSON the image pipeline consumes. Each entry carries a `visible` flag that is false when the annotation is out of frustum OR its colour group is hidden - so an isolate/show call shows up there, not by dropping entries. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_active_group.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] The group, 1-8, that new annotations join when no group is given. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_actor_asset_path.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns the content path that identifies this actor on disk. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_actor_bounds.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the bounding box of an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetActorBounds.

epic_get_actor_transform.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the position, rotation, and scale of an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetActorTransform.

epic_get_actors_in_data_layer.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns descriptors for the loaded actors assigned to a data layer. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_actors_in_folder.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Returns the actors in the specified outliner folder. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.GetActorsInFolder.

epic_get_annotations.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] List every annotation in the editor level, proxies and annotated actors alike. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_canonical_actor_state.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.ActorToolset] Returns a JSON-safe canonical form of an actor (or a Blueprint's CDO) for diffing. Captures the actor's class, its top-level properties, and each component's class and top-level properties. References to the actor itself (path or label) are normalized to "<actor>", and for Blueprint CDOs the generated class path is normalized to "<class>" and the reported class becomes the parent native class, so two CDOs from structurally identical Blueprints produce identical output despite their unique generated-class paths. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_capture_stage.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Where in the frame the viewport capture reads colour. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_collision_channels.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Returns all available collision channels for use with find_actors. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.GetCollisionChannels.

epic_get_component_actor.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the actor that owns the specified component. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetComponentActor.

epic_get_component_transform.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.ActorToolset] Returns the position, rotation, and scale of a scene component. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_components.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the components that an actor contains. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetComponents.

epic_get_current_level.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Returns the path to the current level asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.GetCurrentLevel.

epic_get_data_layers.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns the data layer instances in the current world. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_folders.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Returns all folder paths currently in use in the outliner. Includes all intermediate parent paths. For example, if an actor is assigned to 'Lighting/Spotlights', both 'Lighting' and 'Lighting/Spotlights' are returned. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.GetFolders.

epic_get_label.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the actor's human friendly name as it appears in the editor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetLabel.

epic_get_parent_component.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the parent component that this component is attached to, if any. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetParentComponent.

epic_get_parent_level_instance.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns the level instance that directly contains an actor, loaded or not. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_root_component.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the root component of an actor, if any. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetRootComponent.

epic_get_tags.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns the list of tags on an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.GetTags.

epic_get_visible_groups.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] The colour groups shown in the viewport overlay and the matte, in ascending order. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_has_tag.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Returns whether an actor has a specific tag. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.HasTag.

epic_is_actor_hidden.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns whether the actor is hidden in the editor viewport and outliner. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_is_checked_out.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Checks whether an actor is checked out by the current user. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9.

epic_is_level_instance_loaded.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Returns whether a level instance's level is loaded. Level instances created by other tools, or that came with a loaded level, finish loading some time after those tools return. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_is_overlay_visible.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Whether the viewport draws the coloured annotation overlay. The matte and passes do not depend on it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_isolate_annotation_group.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Shows a single colour group and hides the rest, so the annotation guide marks one target. Use this to work through annotations one group at a time; ShowAllAnnotationGroups restores. Also makes Group the active group, so a later PlaceAnnotation without an explicit Group lands in the group you just soloed rather than in a hidden one. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_isolate_group.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Show only this group, 1-8, and make it the active group. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_annotations.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Lists every 3D spatial annotation in the level, with its id, objectId, prompt, colour, colour group (1-8), world location and the actor it is bound to. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_load_actors.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Loads the actors described by the given descriptors into the editor and returns them. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_load_level.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Loads a level in the editor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.LoadLevel.

epic_load_level_instance.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Loads a level instance's level, making its actors available as loaded actors. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_look_at.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Rotates an actor so its forward vector points at a world-space position. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.LookAt.

epic_merge_actors.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Merges multiple StaticMesh actors into a single mesh asset and actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.MergeActors.

epic_persist_annotations.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Save every scratch annotation with the level from now on. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_place_annotation.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Place a proxy region carrying a prompt. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_place_annotation__unreal_canvas_spa.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Places a new 3D annotation proxy box carrying a spatial prompt. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_actors_from_data_layer.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Removes actors from a data layer. Actors not in the layer are left unchanged. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_all_annotations.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] RemoveAllAnnotations Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_annotation.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Remove an annotation. A proxy region is deleted; a scene actor stays and loses its matte marking. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_annotation__unreal_canvas_sp.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Deletes one annotation. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_annotations_from_actors.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationEditorSubsystem] Remove every annotation the actors carry: the inverse of annotating them. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_annotations_from_selection.summary: [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Deletes every annotation on the currently selected actors - the inverse of annotating a selection. epic_remove_component.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Removes a component from an actor instance or blueprint. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.RemoveComponent.

epic_remove_from_scene.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Deletes an actor from the scene. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.LevelToolset.RemoveFromScene.

epic_remove_tag.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools] Removes a tag from an actor. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ActorToolset.RemoveTag.

epic_rename_folder.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Renames a folder in the outliner. Updates the folder path for all actors in the folder and any sub-folders. epic_replace_actors_with_asset.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Replaces actors in the scene with new actors created from an asset (e.g. a static mesh, Blueprint, or particle system), matching the editor's "Replace Selected Actors With..." command. action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

insert_expression_between.summary: Insert an expression between an existing source and an expression input or material property. Preserves the source output and masks. Named inputs include MakeMaterialAttributes and SetMaterialAttributes. Repeating the same target, type and upstream input reports existed. Returns previousSource, expressionName and rollback restoring the original wire. Dirties the material; save explicitly.

restore_expression_insertion.summary: Apply an insert_expression_between rollback record: restore the exact previous source and masks and remove the inserted node. Refuses if the target changed or another wire now uses that node.

read_summary.summary: Read class counts and only nodes matching classes and parameterNames, with parameter names and groups. Without filters returns counts only. propertyChain traces one material property or named expression input upstream with a depth limit and a 2000 node cap; reports truncation. Read-only.

read.summary: Read material structure. Accepts a Material or a MaterialInstance; an instance answers with its lineage, shading setup and resolved parameters instead of a graph (#952).

list_parameters.summary: List a material's parameters. On a MaterialInstance each entry carries the resolved value, the parent's defaultValue and whether this instance overrides it (#952).

set_parameter.summary: Set parameter on MaterialInstance. parameterType (scalar|vector|texture) is auto-detected when omitted. A vector/colour value may be passed as value OR color, shaped {r,g,b,a}, [r,g,b,a] or '(R=..,G=..,B=..,A=..)'. Saves the instance and returns readBack + saved so a set/verify round trip needs no second call (#952).

read_instance.summary: Read any MaterialInstance (Constant or Dynamic): parentChain up to the base material, the overrides it holds, and the effective scalar/vector/texture parameter values it renders with (value, parent defaultValue, overridden). To read the material actually on a placed component, including a transient MaterialInstanceDynamic created at runtime, pass actorLabel or actorPath instead of assetPath; world defaults to auto (PIE when running, else editor) (#1114). assetPaths reads several instances in one call into instances[], each with requestedPath, parentChain and its scalar/vector/texture overrides; a path that is not a MaterialInstance fails that row and the call names it. overridesOnly=true leaves out the effective value of every parameter, which keeps a palette read across many instances small (#1183).

read_mpc.summary: Read a MaterialParameterCollection: every scalar and vector parameter with its stored defaultValue and id. Pass world to also read the live collection instance in that world (liveValue, differsFromDefault), which is what materials sample and what Blueprint writes change (#1116).

batch_set_instances.summary: Assign texture, scalar and vector tint/scale parameters to material instances in one batch. Batch reparent + reassign parameters across many Material Instances in one call. Returns per-instance results (#594).

list_static_switches.summary: List static switch parameters on a Material or MaterialInstance.

set_static_switch.summary: Set a MaterialInstanceConstant static switch parameter. value is a boolean.

set_expression_value.summary: Set a value on an expression node. Common typed knobs: value (constant/param default), texturePath (TextureSample/TextureSampleParameter2D default texture; applied as a native property edit, the material recompiled with its static-permutation instances, and the response reports samplerType, compileErrors on 5.8+ and shaderState, which lists instances left without a shader map, #1441). Constant2Vector/3Vector/4Vector and VectorParameter all take value (or color) as {r,g,b,a}, {x,y,z,w}, [r,g,b,a] or '(R=..,G=..)'; Constant2Vector reads the first two components (#979). Saves the material and reports saved. A TextureCoordinate node takes uTiling, vTiling and coordinateIndex, which are separate top-level keys rather than anything inside `value`. For any OTHER UPROPERTY on the expression (e.g. SamplerType, SamplerSource, Group), pass propertyName + value to hit the generic reflection setter. Reports previousValue and rolls back to it where the previous value can be expressed in this action's own vocabulary. Pass functionPath instead of materialPath to edit a node inside a MaterialFunction (index from list_function_expressions); the function is then updated so every material using it recompiles (#1138, #663).

set_custom_expression.summary: Read/write a MaterialExpressionCustom (HLSL) node: code, named inputs[] (rebuilds input pins; wire them with connect_expressions targetInput=<name>), outputType (float1|float2|float3|float4|materialAttributes), description. Omit code/inputs to read. Add the node first via add_expression expressionType=Custom, or add_function_expression inside a MaterialFunction (then pass functionPath, #1138) (#617).

create_instance.summary: Create an instance of a parameterized master material, then assign BaseColor, Normal and packed RMA textures with set_parameter or batch_set_instances. Create material instance. Idempotent by path: an existing instance is reported rather than replaced.

create.summary: Create material. Idempotent by path: an existing material is reported rather than replaced.

add_function_expression.summary: Add an expression node to a MaterialFunction graph. inputName and inputType apply to a FunctionInput, outputName to a FunctionOutput (#463). name labels any node, so connect_function_expressions can address it by that name.

connect_function_expressions.summary: Wire two expressions inside a MaterialFunction; each expression is named or indexed. The result lists sourceOutputs (the source node's output names by index; an empty name is the default output an omitted sourceOutput selects) and connectedOutputName (#463).

list_function_expressions.summary: List expression nodes inside a MaterialFunction (#463).

build_material.summary: Build a PBR material from a texture set in one call: creates a TextureSample per entry, picks each sampler type FROM THE TEXTURE (a virtual/UDIM texture silently loses its material connection on recompile unless it samples through the Virtual* variant), wires them, recompiles, saves, and reports which connections survived the recompile. name (+ packagePath) creates the material; materialPath builds into an existing one. assignToMesh puts the result on a StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh (#946). A parameterized master and its instances in the same call (#1229): textureParameters=true makes the samples TextureSampleParameter2D nodes named after their keys; parameters[] adds scalar/vector/texture parameter nodes {name, type, default?, group?}; nodes/connections/propertyConnections add math nodes exactly as build_graph does, where a connection can name a texture key (orm), a parameter name (Tint) or a node; instances[] creates one MaterialInstanceConstant per piece {name, parameters: {Tint: {r,g,b}, ORM: '/Game/T_Piece_ORM'}, assignToMesh, slotName} and assigns it to that slot. textures is optional when parameters or nodes say what to build.

create_simple.summary: Single-call simple material with optional constants and usages[] (e.g. InstancedStaticMeshes, Nanite, NiagaraSprites). Recompiles + saves in one shot (#225).

get_usage.summary: Read the EMaterialUsage flags on a material. `usages[]` carries every flag this engine build defines with its `enabled` state and the bUsedWith* `propertyName` behind it, and `enabled[]` is just the ones that are on. Pass a material INSTANCE and the flags come from the base material it resolves to, which is the shader map it renders through: `materialPath` names that material and `inherited` is true (#1004).

set_usage.summary: Turn on EMaterialUsage flag(s) for a material, then recompile and save. Flag names come from this engine own EMaterialUsage reflection, so every usage the build defines is accepted (VolumetricCloud, Voxels, MeshDeformer and the rest included) and `unknown` names only what it truly could not resolve. This only ever turns flags ON: it routes each one through UMaterial::SetMaterialUsage, which is an ensure rather than a write, so a replay also repairs a material whose bit is set but whose shaders were never built. `applied` names the flags this call turned on and `alreadySet` those that were on already. To CLEAR a flag, write its reflected property with editor(set_property): every usage this action recognises is backed by a bUsedWith* UPROPERTY on the material, and the response returns the exact {objectPath, propertyName, value} arguments per flag under `clearCalls`. Clearing a flag does not discard the shader permutations that were compiled for it (#225).

set_domain.summary: Set material domain. Required for post-process / decal / UI authoring (#299/#356).

add_expression.summary: Author parameterized master materials with TextureSampleParameter2D (BaseColor, Normal, packed RMA), ScalarParameter, VectorParameter (tint), TextureCoordinate and Multiply nodes. parameterName names texture/scalar/vector parameters; set_expression_value assigns default textures and SamplerType. Add expression node (#318). properties sets any other UPROPERTY on it in the same call, e.g. {ConstB: 12.92} on Divide, {ConstExponent: 2.4} on Power (#1461). Returns expressionIndex, the node's position as set_expression_value and set_custom_expression take it, and expressionName, its unique engine name.

connect_expressions.summary: Wire two expressions. sourceOutput and targetInput take a pin name or an index; a single-input node such as Sine, ComponentMask or BlackBody takes targetInput Input (or 0), and the graph editor's short labels (UVs, Tex, Exp) are accepted too. An unknown pin fails and lists the node's pins by index.

list_expressions.summary: List expression nodes, in the material's own stored order, which is what nodeId indexes into. Set includeInputs to include each node's input wiring (default false). Paged with cursor/limit.

read_graph.summary: Read the stored material expression graph without creating an editor graph. Returns the same paged expressions as list_expressions, with inputs carrying inputIndex, inputName, connectedExpressionIndex, connectedOutputIndex, connectedExpressionClass and connectedExpressionDescription, plus every root material input under connections (expressionIndex, outputIndex, expressionClass, expressionDescription; null when disconnected). MaterialAttributes is listed only when the material uses material attributes. Pass expressionIndex (a nodeId) to read just that node and the source expressions its inputs link to, unpaged. A Custom node's row also carries custom {code, description, outputType, inputNames, additionalOutputs, additionalDefines, includeFilePaths}, so the whole graph, HLSL included, can be checked against source in one read (#1645).

delete_expression.summary: Remove expression. expressionName matches a description, class, parameter name, FunctionInput/FunctionOutput name, index or engine name. Pass functionPath instead of materialPath to remove it from a MaterialFunction (#1138).

list_expression_types.summary: List available expression types, in the curated order they are grouped in. Paged with cursor/limit.

recompile.summary: Recompile material. Pass recompileChildren=true to cascade to every MaterialInstanceConstant whose parent chain reaches this material (#421).

validate.summary: Validate material graph - find orphans, broken refs. An orphan is a node no material output or custom output node reaches; delete_orphans removes exactly those.

delete_orphans.summary: Delete every expression no material output or custom output node reaches (the orphans validate reports), then recompile and save. dryRun=true lists them without deleting. Returns orphans[] and deletedCount.

export_graph.summary: Export material graph as JSON in build_graph's shape: nodes[], connections[] and propertyConnections[], so the result imports back.

import_graph.summary: build_graph under another name: adds the nodes, connections and propertyConnections it is given (an export_graph result imports as is).

build_graph.summary: Add a whole node graph in one call. nodes[]: {name, class, posX?, posY?, parameterName?, group?, defaultValue?, value?, channels?, texturePath?, properties?:{UPROPERTY: value}}; name is yours and becomes the node description. connections[]: {from, fromOutput?, to, toInput?} between node names (or expressions already in the material), pins by name or index; a single-input node such as Sine takes toInput Input. propertyConnections[]: {property, from, output?}. removeExpressions[]: existing expressions to delete once the new nodes are wired, so a Custom node is replaced in one call (#1461). Every class, property and pin is checked first and a failure keeps nothing. Returns nodes[] mapping each name to its expressionName and expressionIndex.

render_preview.summary: Render preview PNG. inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger.

create_rvt.summary: Create a RuntimeVirtualTexture asset. materialType is validated against RuntimeVirtualTexture::IsMaterialTypeSupported, which is the reason it is a parameter rather than a follow-up property write: a project can disable individual material types to cut shader permutations, and set_property would happily store one that then compiles to nothing. Everything else (tileCount, tileSize, tileBorderSize, compression, adaptive/private/packed page table, continuous update, LOD group) is a plain UPROPERTY: write it with asset(set_property) at the returned objectPath. Reads back the DERIVED layout - size, pageTableSize, layer count and per-layer pixel format and colour space - which no property read produces. Idempotent by path; rollback deletes the asset.

read_rvt.summary: Read a RuntimeVirtualTexture and its whole reference graph: the derived layout (size, pageTableSize, per-layer pixel format, sRGB and YCoCg), every volume bound to it with its transform, every primitive and landscape that writes into it, and every material sample node that reads it. problems[] names the failures that otherwise only show up visually - no volume (so no world bounds), no writer (so every page renders empty), a disabled material type, and the classic one: a sample node whose materialType disagrees with the asset, which decodes the wrong channels and still compiles. level(get_runtime_virtual_texture_summary) answers the level-side question; this answers the asset-side one.

add_rvt_volume.summary: Spawn the RuntimeVirtualTextureVolume that gives an RVT its world bounds, bind the asset through the engine's SetVirtualTexture (which re-registers the render state, unlike a raw property write), and fit the volume to what actually writes into the texture. An unfitted volume sits at the origin at unit scale and renders a 100cm cube of the world, so the fit is the point. Idempotent BY BINDING rather than by label: two volumes on one RVT is a real misconfiguration (one wins, the other renders nothing) and an existing binding is reported rather than duplicated. When nothing writes into the RVT yet there is nothing to fit to, and the response says so in boundsFitNote rather than reporting a fit that did not happen. Rollback deletes the actor.

set_rvt_volume_bounds.summary: Refit an RVT volume to the world, which is the Set Bounds button and is not a property write: it DERIVES a transform from what is in the level. boundsMode='writers' covers every primitive whose RuntimeVirtualTextures array names this RVT; boundsMode='alignActor' matches one actor's box and rotation, which is what a landscape wants because the volume's axes have to be the terrain's axes. The volume's own local extent is read back through CalcBounds and solved against the target box rather than assumed to be a unit cube, so the fit survives engine changes. Honest limitation: it does NOT perform the landscape texel snap (that lives in a module the bridge does not link) and says so when bSnapBoundsToLandscape is set. Rollback restores the previous transform exactly.

add_rvt_sampler.summary: Add or rebind the RuntimeVirtualTextureSample node that READS an RVT in a material, then call the engine's InitVirtualTextureDependentSettings, which is the one step add_expression + set_expression_value cannot do: it copies the asset's material type and packed/adaptive page-table flags onto the node and rebuilds its output pins. Setting VirtualTexture alone leaves those stale, which compiles cleanly and decodes the wrong channels. Optionally connects each output pin to the material property of the same name and reports the pins that have no counterpart (WorldHeight, Mask, Mask4, Displacement) rather than dropping them silently. Idempotent by expressionName. MipValueMode, TextureAddressMode and bEnableFeedback stay editor(set_property) territory at the returned expressionObjectPath.

add_rvt_output.summary: Add the RuntimeVirtualTextureOutput node that makes a material WRITE into an RVT, and mirror the material's existing BaseColor / Normal / Roughness / Specular / Opacity connections into it, which by hand is one connect_expressions call per channel with each source expression and output index looked up by eye. Reads the node's inputs by NAME through the same GetInput/GetInputName pair connect_expressions uses, so a channel added by an engine version is picked up rather than mis-wired. Inputs with no material counterpart are reported with the call that wires them. Idempotent by expressionName. Note this does not choose WHICH RVT: that is the primitive's RuntimeVirtualTextures array (assign_rvt_to_landscape, or editor(set_property) on a mesh component).

assign_rvt_to_landscape.summary: Assign RVTs to a landscape across EVERY proxy that shares its ULandscapeInfo, not just the actor named. A streaming or World Partition landscape is many ALandscapeStreamingProxy actors, and writing RuntimeVirtualTextures on one of them with set_property leaves the rest rendering nothing into the RVT, which is invisible until the pages come back empty. Also calls PostEditChange plus MarkComponentsRenderStateDirty per proxy, without which the change does not take effect, and checks the two things that make an assignment useless anyway: a landscape material with no RuntimeVirtualTextureOutput node, and an RVT whose material type is disabled for the project. assignMode='set' with an empty list clears the assignment. Rollback replays the named landscape's previous list, with previousPerProxy carrying the exact per-proxy state.

create_designer.summary: Create a Material Designer material: a DynamicMaterialInstance asset WITH its Material Designer model, through the plugin's own DynamicMaterialInstanceFactory (asset(create_asset_by_class) leaves the model empty). Seeds a Base Color slot when the new model has none, requests a build and saves. Returns path, modelPath, slotCount and a delete_asset rollback. Needs the Material Designer plugin (#1131).

read_designer.summary: Read a Material Designer (DynamicMaterial) model: material settings (domain, blend mode, shading model, flags), materialProperties with their enabled state and designerSlot, and every slot's layer stack. Each layer carries name, bEnabled, MaterialProperty, blendMode, effectStack and its stages (stageType Base or Mask) with sources, inputs, sub-stages, values, texture UVs and text renderers described recursively; every component reports objectPath, componentPath and writableProperties for set_designer_value. Target a Motion Design shape with actorLabel/actorPath (the first material slot holding a DynamicMaterialInstance, or componentName?/slotIndex?/slotName?), or pass assetPath (a DynamicMaterialInstance, a DynamicMaterialModel, or any object inside one). designerSlot and layerIndex narrow the read. Needs the Material Designer plugin (#1131).

set_designer_value.summary: Set one property on a Material Designer component (a layer, stage, value, texture UV, text renderer, the editor-only data's settings) by reflection. Uses the component's own setter when it has one (SetValue, SetOffset, SetTiling, SetText, SetEnabled, SetLayerName) so the model updates the way the Material Designer UI does; otherwise writes the property, calls PostEditChangeProperty and Update, and requests a material build. Address the component by objectPath or componentPath (both reported by read_designer), or by designerSlot? + layerIndex/layerName (+ stage? base|mask|index); componentPath and the layer forms also need assetPath or actorLabel/actorPath. Returns previousValue and a rollback (#1131).

add_designer_layer.summary: Add a default layer to a Material Designer slot through UDMMaterialSlot::AddDefaultLayer, optionally naming it, then request a material build. Returns the new layer as read_designer describes it; its stages are then set with set_designer_value. designerSlot defaults to the slot mapped to materialProperty (#1131).

remove_designer_layer.summary: Remove a layer from a Material Designer slot through UDMMaterialSlot::RemoveLayer, after CanRemoveLayer agrees (a slot keeps its base layer). Address it by objectPath, or by layerIndex or layerName in a target's slot. Runs in an editor transaction; the rollback is one editor undo (#1131).

epic_add_expression.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Adds a new expression node to a Material or MaterialFunction graph. Use list_expression_classes to discover available types. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.AddExpression.

epic_clear_parameters.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Clears all parameter overrides on a material instance, reverting to parent defaults. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.ClearParameters.

epic_connect_expressions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Connects an expression node's output pin to another expression node's input pin. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.ConnectExpressions.

epic_connect_to_output.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Connects an expression node's output to one of the material's output properties. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.ConnectToOutput.

epic_create.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Creates a new MaterialInstanceConstant asset derived from a parent material. Material instances expose the parent's parameters without triggering a full shader recompile when parameter values change. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.Create.

epic_create_function.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Creates a new empty MaterialFunction asset. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.CreateFunction.

epic_create_material.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Creates a new empty Material asset. Warning: Each new Material increases shader compile times. Prefer creating a MaterialInstance from an existing Material where possible. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.CreateMaterial.

epic_create_parameter_collection.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Creates a new empty MaterialParameterCollection (MPC) asset. An MPC holds named Scalar and Vector parameters with default values that materials can reference at runtime without recompiling shaders. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.CreateParameterCollection.

epic_delete_expression.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Removes an expression node from a Material or MaterialFunction graph. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.DeleteExpression.

epic_delete_parameter_group.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Removes a parameter group, ungrouping all parameters that belong to it. The parameter expressions themselves are not deleted - only their group assignment is cleared. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.DeleteParameterGroup.

epic_delete_unused_expressions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Deletes all expression nodes not connected to any material output. Useful for cleaning up a material graph after reorganising or after the AI has added experimental nodes that were later abandoned. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.DeleteUnusedExpressions.

epic_diff.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two MaterialInstanceConstant assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff_function.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two MaterialFunction assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_diff_material.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two Material assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_disconnect_expressions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Disconnects the input pin of an expression node, removing whatever is connected to it. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.DisconnectExpressions.

epic_disconnect_from_output.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Disconnects the expression currently connected to a material output property. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.DisconnectFromOutput.

epic_get_expression_input_names.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the names of all input pins on a material expression node. Use these names as to_input_name when calling connect_expressions. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.GetExpressionInputNames.

epic_get_expression_inputs.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the current wiring of each input pin on a material expression. Use after building or modifying a graph to verify the wiring matches expectations. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.GetExpressionInputs.

epic_get_expression_output_names.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the names of all output pins on a material expression node. Use these names as from_output_name when calling connect_expressions or connect_to_output. The empty string represents the default (first) output of nodes that expose only an unnamed output. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.GetExpressionOutputNames.

epic_get_expressions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns all expression nodes in a Material or MaterialFunction graph. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.GetExpressions.

epic_get_property_input.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the expression and output pin feeding a material output property. Use to inspect what drives MP_EmissiveColor, MP_Opacity, MP_BaseColor, etc. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.GetPropertyInput.

epic_get_referencing_materials.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns asset data for all Materials that reference this MaterialFunction. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.GetReferencingMaterials.

epic_get_scalar_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the current value of a scalar parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.GetScalarParameter.

epic_get_static_switch_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the value of a static switch parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.GetStaticSwitchParameter.

epic_get_statistics.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialToolset] Returns compiled shader statistics for a Material or MaterialInstance on the current shader platform: instruction counts, texture-sample counts, and sampler usage. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_texture_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the texture assigned to a texture parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.GetTextureParameter.

epic_get_vector_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the current value of a vector parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.GetVectorParameter.

epic_layout_expressions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Automatically arranges all expression nodes in a Material or MaterialFunction graph. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.LayoutExpressions.

epic_list_expression_classes.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns MaterialExpression subclasses valid for the given context. Use the results with add_expression. Pass a search string to filter by name, e.g. 'Multiply' or 'Parameter'. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.ListExpressionClasses.

epic_list_parameter_groups.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the unique parameter group names defined in a Material or MaterialFunction. Parameters are organised into groups in the Material Instance editor. This returns the distinct set of group names found across all parameter expressions in the graph. The empty string represents parameters that have not been assigned to a named group. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.ListParameterGroups.

epic_list_parameters.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Returns all parameters exposed by a material or instance, with their names and types. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.ListParameters.

epic_recompile.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Recompiles a Material or MaterialFunction after edits. For Materials, raises if the shader fails to compile. For MaterialFunctions, also recompiles any Materials that reference the function. Call this once after a set of graph modifications is complete - after adding or deleting expressions, making connections, or changing expression properties such as parameter names or default values. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.Recompile.

epic_rename_parameter_group.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Renames a parameter group across all parameter expressions in a Material or MaterialFunction. All parameters currently in old_name will be moved to new_name. If new_name already exists, the parameters are merged into it. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialToolset.RenameParameterGroup.

epic_set_parameter_override.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Enables or disables a parameter override on a material instance. Enabling sets the override to the current effective value. Disabling reverts to the parent. For non-static parameter types, disabling also discards the prior override value; re-enabling later restores the parent value, not the prior override. Static switches and static component masks preserve their value across toggle. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.SetParameterOverride.

epic_set_parent.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Changes the parent of a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.SetParent.

epic_set_scalar_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Sets the value of a scalar parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.SetScalarParameter.

epic_set_static_switch_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Sets the value of a static switch parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.SetStaticSwitchParameter.

epic_set_texture_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Assigns a texture to a texture parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.SetTextureParameter.

epic_set_vector_parameter.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Sets the value of a vector parameter on a material instance. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset.SetVectorParameter.

tools.name: metahuman
tools.description:
MetaHuman Creator characters: create a MetaHumanCharacter, read its body constraints, wardrobe and texture state, set parametric body constraints, dress wardrobe slots, request the cloud auto-rig and texture sources, and assemble it into skeletal meshes and a blueprint.

Call metahuman(action, args={...}). Actions:
status()
create_character(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)
read_character(assetPath|characterPath, includeBody?:b)
set_body(assetPath|characterPath, constraints:o)
set_wardrobe(assetPath|characterPath, items:o)
request_rig(assetPath|characterPath, rigType?, blocking?:b)
request_textures(assetPath|characterPath, blocking?:b)
assemble(assetPath|characterPath, pipelineType?, quality?, nameOverride?, commonFolderPath?)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

status.summary: Report whether the MetaHumanCharacter plugin is enabled and its editor subsystem loaded, and list the MetaHumanCharacter assets under /Game. The Epic cloud login state is reported as unknown with the reason: no reflected API exposes it. Call this first.

create_character.summary: Create a MetaHumanCharacter asset through the plugin's own factory. Idempotent by name (onConflict skip). Rollback deletes the asset.

read_character.summary: Read a MetaHumanCharacter: template type, texture state (hasHighResolutionTextures, synthesized face and body texture counts, hasFaceDNABlendshapes), and with includeBody (default) the body constraints (name, active, target, min, max), wardrobe slot selections and canBuild. Opens the character for editing to read those and closes it again if it was not open. The rig state is not reflected and is reported as unknown with the reason.

set_body.summary: Set parametric body constraints by name, {Height: 180, Muscularity: 0.9} or {Height: {target: 180, active: true}}, and commit the body state. Writes the whole constraint array back, so edits are not lost to the copy the engine hands out, refuses unknown names with the list of real ones, and returns each constraint before and after. Rollback restores the previous targets and active flags.

set_wardrobe.summary: Dress wardrobe slots: {"Top Garment": wardrobeItemPath}. Each item is added to the character's collection and selected in its slot, then the preview is rebuilt. Returns per-item applied/error and the slot selections before and after. No inverse.

request_rig.summary: Request auto-rigging from the MetaHuman cloud service (rigType JointsOnly or JointsAndBlendshapes), blocking by default. This is the step that opens the Epic login, so run it before request_textures. A refusal for want of a login is an error with loginState not-logged-in. Returns the texture/rig state and canBuild afterwards plus the MetaHuman log warnings. No inverse.

request_textures.summary: Request high-resolution texture sources from the MetaHuman cloud service, blocking by default. Needs the Epic login request_rig opens; a refusal for want of it is an error with loginState not-logged-in. Returns texture state before and after. No inverse.

assemble.summary: Assemble the character (pipelineType Cinematic, Optimized or UEFN; quality such as Medium) as one tracked long call of up to 15 minutes. Checks CanBuildMetaHuman first and returns its logged reason when it refuses. Returns the created skeletal meshes, blueprints and other asset paths, the elapsed seconds and the MetaHuman log warnings. No inverse.

tools.name: networking
tools.description:
Networking and replication: actor replication, property replication, net relevancy, dormancy.

Call networking(action, args={...}). Actions:
set_replicates(blueprintPath, replicates?:b)
set_property_replicated(blueprintPath, variableName|propertyName, replicationType?, replicated?:b, repNotify?:b)
configure_net_frequency(blueprintPath, netUpdateFrequency?:n, minNetUpdateFrequency?:n)
set_dormancy(blueprintPath, dormancy)
set_net_load_on_client(blueprintPath, loadOnClient?:b)
set_always_relevant(blueprintPath, alwaysRelevant?:b)
set_only_relevant_to_owner(blueprintPath, onlyRelevantToOwner?:b)
configure_cull_distance(blueprintPath, netCullDistanceSquared?:n)
set_priority(blueprintPath, netPriority?:n)
set_replicate_movement(blueprintPath, replicateMovement?:b)
get_info(blueprintPath)
audit_replication(path?, className?, includeNative?:b, includeBlueprints?:b, includeEngine?:b, requireServerValidation?:b, onlyWithFindings?:b, maxBlueprints?:i, limit?:i, dumpToFile?:b, outputPath?)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

set_replicates.summary: Enable or disable actor replication on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value. Rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost.

set_property_replicated.summary: Mark a Blueprint variable as replicated. replicationType is 'None' | 'Replicated' | 'RepNotify'; repNotify=true is shorthand for RepNotify and replicated=true for Replicated (#768). Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the variable already had that type. Rolls back through this same action with the type it had; marked lossy when the variable carried a ReplicationCondition other than COND_None, because making a variable replicated resets that and this action has no parameter to restore one.

configure_net_frequency.summary: Set update frequency. Reports unchanged=true when both frequencies already held these values, and otherwise rolls back to the pair that was there - the record carries both regardless of which one was asked for, so an inverse cannot leave the two inconsistent.

set_dormancy.summary: Set net dormancy on a Blueprint's CDO: DORM_Never | DORM_Awake | DORM_DormantAll | DORM_DormantPartial | DORM_Initial. An unrecognised spelling is REFUSED and the valid five are named, where it used to leave the value alone and still report success. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had that dormancy. Rolls back through this same action with the previous one, with nothing lost.

set_net_load_on_client.summary: Control whether the actor is loaded on clients (bNetLoadOnClient). A class with no such property reports a warning and unchanged=true rather than the existed it used to claim for a write that never happened. Reports existed=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag.

set_always_relevant.summary: Set bAlwaysRelevant on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost.

set_only_relevant_to_owner.summary: Set bOnlyRelevantToOwner on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost.

configure_cull_distance.summary: Net cull distance. Reports unchanged=true when the value is already set, and otherwise rolls back to the previous NetCullDistanceSquared read off the CDO before the write. A class with no writable NetCullDistanceSquared reports a warning rather than a silent success.

set_priority.summary: Set NetPriority on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the value is already nearly equal to the one asked for, and otherwise rolls back to the float the property held, with nothing lost.

set_replicate_movement.summary: Set replicated movement on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost.

audit_replication.summary: Project-wide replication audit over native and Blueprint classes. Each class row lists its replicated properties (lifetime condition, push-based, RepNotify function and its REPNOTIFY condition, read from the class's own GetLifetimeReplicatedProps), its RPCs (Server / Client / NetMulticast, reliable, validated) and, for actors and components, the replication settings on its defaults (replicates, netDormancy, netCullDistanceSquared, update frequencies, priority, relevancy). findings name each problem visible from the class alone: repNotifyFunctionMissing, onRepWithoutReplicatedProperty, replicatedPropertyNotRegistered, replicatedPropertyOnNonReplicatingClass, reliableMulticast, and serverRpcWithoutValidation when requireServerValidation=true. Native scope is the project's modules and project plugins unless includeEngine=true; Blueprints come from path (default /Game). Classes with findings sort first; totals stay complete when rows are cut at limit, and dumpToFile writes every row to a JSON file.
