action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

list.summary: List Niagara assets: every NiagaraSystem and NiagaraEmitter as one row tagged with its `type`, sorted by object path within each type, plus systemCount/emitterCount for the whole listing. Lists the whole project; page through it with cursor/limit.

list_dynamic_inputs.summary: Report the authored override map per module: which inputs carry a plain value, which are wired to a dynamic-input script, and which hold an inline HLSL expression, with nested dynamic inputs one level down under nestedOverrides. This is a graph walk, so no property read produces it. Pair with list_module_inputs, which shows the inputs that have no override at all.

set_dynamic_input.summary: Wire a dynamic-input NiagaraScript into a module input's override pin, creating the pin if needed and replacing whatever was there. A dynamic input is a graph node, not a property, so set_property cannot do this. Returns dynamicInputName, which is the module name to pass to set_module_input when setting the dynamic input's OWN inputs. Errors list the module's real input names and the modules present.

remove_dynamic_input.summary: Unwire a dynamic input, delete the nodes that fed only it, and drop the override pin so the module's own default comes back. An input with no dynamic input returns alreadyRemoved rather than an error, so a rollback replays safely.

add_simulation_stage.summary: Create a simulation stage on an emitter: the stage object AND the backing NiagaraScript, its output node with a fresh usage id, and a parameter-map input node, so the stage actually compiles. set_property cannot create a graph, which is why this is a handler. Returns simulationStageObjectPath; set IterationSource, NumIterations, ExecuteBehavior and the ElementCount bindings on it with asset(set_property).

remove_simulation_stage.summary: Remove a simulation stage, its script, and the graph nodes that fed only its output node, leaving nodes shared with another stack alone. A missing stage returns alreadyRemoved with the stages that do exist. Reports removedModules, which the rollback cannot restore, rather than pretending the undo is complete.

add_event_handler.summary: Create an event handler on an emitter, with its event script, output node and usage id, so the handler's struct fields point at something real. Returns eventHandlerPropertyPath; set ExecutionMode, SpawnNumber and MaxEventsPerFrame through asset(set_property) on emitterObjectPath with that prefix.

remove_event_handler.summary: Remove an event handler by its script's usage id and delete the graph chain that fed only it. A missing handler returns alreadyRemoved listing the handlers present. Echoes the ExecutionMode and SpawnNumber the rollback will not restore.

get_custom_hlsl.summary: Read every CustomHLSL node in a graph: the source body, and the pins Niagara parsed out of it. Omit nodeIndex to list them all. This is what makes HLSL iterable rather than write-once, since nothing else can read the body back. stackContext and the emitter apply when addressing a system.

set_custom_hlsl.summary: Overwrite a CustomHLSL node's body and reconstruct the node, so the returned pins are the ones the new source actually declares. A bare property write would leave stale pins and an uncompiled script, which is why this is a handler. A body identical to the current one returns alreadySet and skips the recompile. stackContext and the emitter apply when addressing a system.

remove_module.summary: Remove a module from an emitter stack: unwire its node group, close the parameter-map chain over the gap, and delete the module with its override node and dynamic inputs. add_module had no inverse below UE 5.8, where only the Epic toolset covers this. Returns remainingModules in stack order and echoes the removedOverrides the rollback will not restore.

set_module_enabled.summary: Enable or disable a module in place. A disabled module keeps its node, its inputs and its stack position and is skipped at compile time, which makes this the reversible way to test whether a module is causing a behaviour. Already in that state returns alreadySet.

compile.summary: Force a real compile of a system and report what the translator said, per script: scriptName, usage, status (NCS_UpToDate | NCS_UpToDateWithWarnings | NCS_Error | ...), errorMsg and every compile event with its severity and the node and pin guid that produced it, plus a top-level compiled boolean and a flat errors[]. This is the assertion a graph edit has to survive. validate answers whether the system EMITS, which a malformed script can still pass, and get_compiled_hlsl returns success without compiling anything at all on a CPU-sim emitter. The call blocks until the compile settles, because an asynchronous one hands back the previous compile's status. force (default true) recompiles even when nothing looks dirty, which is the case a graph edit that left change tracking untouched produces.

validate.summary: Verify gate: does this system actually emit? Reports per emitter whether it is enabled and has a spawn module + an enabled renderer. valid=false means empty shell.

spawn.summary: Spawn VFX on a new NiagaraActor host of its own, never on an existing actor. The rollback deletes that host by actorPath and nothing else. Scale is three separate keys, scaleX/scaleY/scaleZ, not a vector object; autoDestroy=true destroys the host when the system finishes (default false). spawn_actor is the same host without scale or autoDestroy.

spawn_actor.summary: Spawn a PERSISTENT, labeled NiagaraActor in the editor world (findable, re-activatable, survives capture - unlike spawn). Assigns the system and activates unless activate=false (#537).

reactivate.summary: Reset + reactivate the NiagaraComponent on a placed actor (replay a burst before capturing) (#537/#983).

set_parameter.summary: Set a user parameter on the NiagaraComponent of a placed actor. parameterType selects how the value is read: float, int and bool take `value`; vector takes valueX/valueY/valueZ, which are separate keys rather than a `value` object because that is what the handler reads. Reports previousValue and rolls back to it.

create.summary: Create system. Idempotent by path: an existing system is reported rather than replaced.

create_emitter.summary: Create a Niagara emitter asset. templatePath copies an existing emitter as the starting point (the content browser's create-from-template path); omit it for the default empty emitter with the standard modules and a sprite renderer. inherit=true makes it a child that tracks the template instead, which then refuses local edits to inherited modules.

remove_emitter.summary: Remove an emitter from a system (CRUD delete), addressed by emitterName or emitterIndex.

set_emitter_property.summary: Set emitter property. propertyName 'enabled' toggles the emitter and 'name' renames it (its Emitter.* parameters follow; the result's newEmitterName is the name it landed on); anything else is an FVersionedNiagaraEmitterData property.

list_modules.summary: List Niagara module scripts, sorted by object path. pathFilter narrows the whole set rather than only the first page, which is what it always claimed to do.

get_emitter_info.summary: Inspect an emitter: a standalone emitter asset by assetPath, or an emitter inside a system by systemPath plus emitterName or emitterIndex. Returns sim target, renderers, every emitter-data property with its value, and the module stack per context. Module input values such as SpawnRate or the EmitterState loop settings come from list_module_inputs.

set_renderer_property.summary: Set any renderer property. Bools, numbers and strings are taken directly; object properties (a sprite/mesh renderer's Material, the mesh on a mesh renderer) take an asset path and are class-checked; structs, enums, names and arrays go through the shared JSON property setter, so there is no longer a type whitelist to fall off (#783).

create_system_from_spec.summary: Declaratively create a system + emitters: emitters=[{path}].

get_compiled_hlsl.summary: Read GPU compute script info for an emitter.

list_module_inputs.summary: List an emitter's modules in stack order (stackContext, stackIndex, moduleName, enabled) with the inputs you can actually SET - Spawn Rate, Lifetime, Colour, Sprite Size - each with its name, qualifiedName, type, a settable flag, its current value and valueSource: local (authored on this emitter), moduleDefault (the module script's default), or linked (driven by a dynamic input, described by list_dynamic_inputs). Compile-time switches and enums are reported separately under switchPins; note that 'inputs' now means override-map inputs, NOT the function-call node pins it meant before (those are switchPins) (#784).

set_module_input.summary: Set a module input value. Override-map-bound inputs (the numeric/colour values that matter) are written through the stack override map, the same path the Niagara stack editor uses; others fall back to the pin default. Reports writePath ('overrideMap'|'pinDefault'). On the overrideMap path previousValue cannot be read back (NiagaraEditor does not export the binder's reader), so it reports '(unread: override map)' and NO rollback is offered - re-set the value explicitly instead. The pinDefault path reports a real previousValue and is rollback-safe (#769). value accepts a scalar, [x,y,z], {x,y,z[,w]} or {r,g,b[,a]} (alpha defaults to 1); anything the input's type cannot parse is REJECTED rather than written, including gapped component objects and non-finite numbers.

add_module.summary: Add a stock /Niagara/Modules script to an emitter stack (the modules that make an emitter actually do anything). Then set_module_input to tune it.

list_static_switches.summary: List static switch inputs on a module.

set_static_switch.summary: Set static switch value on a module's function call node.

create_module_from_hlsl.summary: Create a NiagaraScript module backed by a custom HLSL node. inputs/outputs are [{name,type}].

create_scratch_module.summary: Create empty Niagara scratch module. inputs/outputs are [{name,type}] (#185).

capture_sim_cache.summary: Record per-frame particle attributes off a placed actor's NiagaraComponent into an in-memory NiagaraSimCache, GPU emitters included, in the editor world or PIE. Returns simCachePath, frames, and per emitter its numInstancesPerFrame and attributeNames (bare names: Position, Velocity, Age). frames > 1 advances the simulation one tickDelta between frames. The component must be active. Read the values with read_sim_cache.

read_sim_cache.summary: Read particle attributes from a captured sim cache frame. Returns numInstances for the frame and the emitter layout; per attribute found, count, components, the first `limit` values and per-component min/max/avg over every instance. Names may be bare (Age) or qualified (Particles.Age). A name not in the layout fails the call and names the readable ones; an attribute in the layout on a zero-instance frame reports count 0 with a note, so an empty frame and a wrong name never look the same.

epic_add_emitter.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds an emitter to a Niagara System. The new emitter will be based on the template emitter, inheriting its configuration and modules. Returns the full emitter topology (no input values - call GetEmitterInputValues for values).

epic_add_module.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a module to a script stack. The module will be inserted into the specified script's execution stack. Returns the module topology with all inputs walked (no input values - call GetModuleInputValues for values).

epic_add_renderer.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a renderer to an emitter. Creates a new renderer of the specified type and adds it to the emitter's renderer list. Returns an FNiagaraExt_RendererRef with the new renderer's Index and RendererClass, usable directly with SetRendererData / GetRendererData without a follow-up topology call.

epic_add_set_parameter_entry.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a single parameter to an existing SetParameters module. The module referenced by ModuleRef must be a SetParameters (UNiagaraNodeAssignment) module. Use bIsSetParametersModule in the module topology to confirm before calling.

epic_add_set_parameters_module.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a SetParameters module to a script stack. Unlike AddModule which requires a script asset, a SetParameters module dynamically assigns values to named parameters and generates its own internal script. Use this when you need to set one or more particle/emitter/system parameters directly in the stack.

epic_add_user_variables.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds or updates user variables on a system. If a variable with the same name already exists, it will be replaced with the new definition.

epic_apply_stack_issue_fix.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Applies a Fix-style stack issue fix identified by IssueId and FixId. Link-style fixes are rejected. The fix is undoable via the editor undo stack. Applying a fix may trigger a recompile; the result waits for that compile to complete so post-fix state is valid.

epic_construct_niagara_bpwrapper_from_co.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Blueprint] Creates a Blueprint actor wrapper from a Niagara Component. This generates a new Blueprint actor and preserves all component property values and user variable overrides.

epic_construct_niagara_bpwrapper_from_sy.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Blueprint] Creates a Blueprint actor wrapper around a Niagara System. This generates a new Blueprint actor with a Niagara component configured to use the specified system.

epic_create_niagara_system.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Creates a new Niagara System asset. The new system will be based on the template system, inheriting its configuration and emitters.

epic_find_niagara_scripts.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Searches for UNiagaraScript assets matching the given filters.

epic_get_asset_discovery_info.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Returns the project's configured asset discovery groups.

epic_get_available_dynamic_inputs.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all available Dynamic Input Module assets compatible with the given type. Dynamic inputs provide procedural value generation for module parameters.

epic_get_data_interface_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for a specific Data Interface class. Describes all available properties and their types for the given data interface type.

epic_get_dynamic_input_chain.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the full recursive chain for a dynamic input: topology metadata and resolved values at every level. The starting input must have value mode Dynamic; an error is surfaced otherwise. The schema expands one full level and emits a typed recursion stub at deeper levels; the wire format recurses to arbitrary depth matching the underlying chain.

epic_get_dynamic_input_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a dynamic input module in the stack. Describes the inputs and configuration for a procedural value generator.

epic_get_dynamic_input_schema_from_asset.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a dynamic input asset. Standalone function that doesn't require a system context - useful for browsing available dynamic inputs.

epic_get_emitter_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns emitter property values as a single JSON-string blob in PropertyValues. The blob contains the full FVersionedNiagaraEmitterData (SimTarget, bLocalSpace, RandomSeed, FixedBounds, etc.) - fields use C++ PascalCase, must be parsed to read individual values. For typed access to common metadata (SimTarget, EmitterName, bEnabled, RendererClasses) prefer GetEmitterSummary - it returns those as named fields directly and avoids a JSON parse step. Use this endpoint when you need the full property set or a less-common field.

epic_get_emitter_input_values.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all resolved input values for every module across all four emitter script stacks. One FNiagaraExt_ModuleInputValues entry per module, each carrying all its resolved input values. Call this in parallel with GetEmitterTopology to get both structure and values in two passes.

epic_get_emitter_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for Niagara Emitter. Describes all available properties and their types that can be set on a Niagara Emitter.

epic_get_emitter_summary.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns lightweight emitter metadata: name, enabled state, sim target, renderer classes. Use this when you only need to check metadata without walking the full emitter structure.

epic_get_emitter_topology.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns full emitter topology: four script stacks with all modules and inputs, renderer references. All fields always populated. The returned topology carries no input values; call GetEmitterInputValues in parallel.

epic_get_module_input_values.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns resolved input values for a single module. Use when you need values for one specific module without walking the whole emitter.

epic_get_module_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a module and all its inputs. Call this after seeing a module in topology to understand what inputs it exposes.

epic_get_module_schema_from_asset.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a module asset. Standalone function that doesn't require a system context - useful for browsing available modules.

epic_get_module_topology.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns module topology: metadata and all inputs (name/type/visibility only, no values). All fields always populated.

epic_get_niagara_script_digest.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Returns the decoded asset-registry tag metadata for a Niagara script asset.

epic_get_renderer_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns renderer property values. Retrieves the current values of all configurable renderer properties.

epic_get_renderer_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for a specific Renderer class. Describes all available properties and their types for the given renderer type.

epic_get_script_stack_input_values.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all resolved input values for every module in the given script stack. One FNiagaraExt_ModuleInputValues entry per module.

epic_get_script_stack_topology.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns script stack topology: all modules and their inputs in execution order. All fields always populated.

epic_get_stack_input_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the value of a stack module input. Retrieves the current value and configuration for a specific module input parameter.

epic_get_stack_input_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a single module input in the stack. Describes the type, metadata, and configuration options for a specific input parameter.

epic_get_stack_input_topology.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns stack input topology: name, type, visibility, editability. No value payload. For the resolved value call GetStackInputData. For a dynamic-input chain call GetDynamicInputChain.

epic_get_stack_issues.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all stack issues (errors, warnings, info) from the Niagara module stack, including dismissed ones. Waits for any in-flight compile to complete before collecting.

epic_get_system_compile_state.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the current compile state of a Niagara System: aggregate status, per-script compile events, and summary flags. Waits for any in-flight compile to complete before collecting.

epic_get_system_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns system property values. Retrieves the current values of all configurable system-level properties.

epic_get_system_dependencies.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the four Used* sets (renderers, data interfaces, modules, dynamic inputs) gathered across all emitters and system scripts. These sets are not included in topology structs; call this endpoint separately when needed.

epic_get_system_schema.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for Niagara System. Describes all available properties and their types that can be set on a Niagara System.

epic_get_system_summary.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns lightweight system metadata: name, user variables, and one summary entry per emitter. Use this for first contact with an unfamiliar system. For full structural detail call GetEmitterTopology per emitter.

epic_get_user_variables.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Returns all user variable values currently set on the component. This retrieves the current values of all user-exposed parameters that can be overridden at the component level.

epic_get_user_variables__niagara_toolset.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all user variables defined on the system. User variables are parameters exposed for external control and can be overridden per component instance.

epic_get_variable.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Gets the current value of a specific user variable on the component. This retrieves the current value of a user-exposed parameter, including any component-level overrides.

epic_remove_emitter.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes an emitter from a system. Deletes the specified emitter and all its associated scripts, modules, and renderers.

epic_remove_module.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes a module from a script stack. Deletes the specified module and all its inputs from the script's execution stack.

epic_remove_renderer.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes a renderer from an emitter. Deletes the specified renderer from the emitter's renderer list.

epic_remove_set_parameter_entry.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes a parameter from an existing SetParameters module by name. The module referenced by ModuleRef must be a SetParameters (UNiagaraNodeAssignment) module. Use bIsSetParametersModule in the module topology to confirm before calling.

epic_remove_user_variables.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes user variables from a system. Deletes the specified user variables from the system's user parameter collection.

epic_set_emitter_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets property values on a Niagara Emitter. Applies new values to emitter-level properties based on the provided data structure.

epic_set_module_enabled.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets whether a module is enabled. Disabled modules remain in the stack but don't execute. Current state is visible in module topology.

epic_set_niagara_script_description.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Sets the Description field on a Niagara script's FVersionedNiagaraScriptData. Does not checkout or save the asset but will update the asset registry tags. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_renderer_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets property values on a Niagara Renderer. Applies new values to renderer properties based on the provided data structure. Payload shape varies with the concrete renderer class; call GetRendererSchema for the renderer's class to inspect valid properties before writing.

epic_set_stack_input_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets the value of a stack module input and returns the resulting stored value. Updates the value and configuration for a specific module input parameter.

epic_set_system.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Sets the Niagara System for a component. Use this instead of setting the Asset property directly to ensure proper initialization.

epic_set_system_data.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets property values on a Niagara System. Applies new values to system-level properties based on the provided data structure.

epic_set_variable.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Sets the value of a user variable on the component. This overrides the default value of a user-exposed parameter on a specific component instance.

epic_uenum_info.summary: [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Info] Returns information about a UEnum and all its values. ALWAYS call this when working with a UEnum type to see valid values.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

list_graphs.summary: List PCG graphs, sorted by object path. Lists the whole project; page through it with cursor/limit.

read_graph.summary: Read graph structure: every node with its name, title, inputPins and outputPins (the pin labels connect_nodes takes), the graph's inputNode and outputNode, and edges.

read_node_settings.summary: Read node settings. An instanced subobject (a spawner's MeshSelectorParameters or InstanceDataPackerParameters) is expanded under instanced {class, properties}, and a weighted mesh selector also lists meshEntries [{mesh, weight, materialOverrides}] (#1303).

get_component_details.summary: Inspect PCG component (#983). Reports blueprintOwned with a warning when the Blueprint's construction script builds the component (edits on the placed actor can be lost on reconstruction; use set_component_parameters with blueprintPath), isGenerating, isCleaningUp, generated, partitioned (with local component counts) and lastRun {id, state generating|generated|cancelled|cleaned|not_started, startedUtc, finishedUtc}; to wait for a run, use wait_for_generation or wait=true on execute.

create_graph.summary: Create graph in packagePath (or path), default /Game/PCG. Idempotent by path: an existing graph is reported rather than replaced.

add_node.summary: Add node. The engine assigns its name unless name is given; either way nodeName in the result is what connect_nodes and remove_node take. A name already in the graph with the same class is reported as existed; another class is refused (#1331).

connect_nodes.summary: Wire nodes. Returns edgeVerified=true after confirming the UPCGEdge persisted; surfaces an error if AddEdge succeeded but no edge object was instantiated (#304). A pin label the node does not have is refused with reason pin_not_found and validPins, the labels it does have. An edge the graph refuses says why: connectionResult (InvalidNode, InvalidPin, IncompatibleTypes, RequiresFilter, RequiresConversion, CycleDetected) and connectionReason; validate_edge asks the same question without connecting (#1828).

validate_edge.summary: Ask whether an edge can be added without touching the graph (UPCGGraph::ValidateEdge on UE 5.9, the same node, pin, cycle and type checks before it). Pins default as connect_nodes defaults them. Returns valid, connectionResult (Success, InvalidNode, InvalidPin, IncompatibleTypes, RequiresFilter, RequiresConversion, CycleDetected), reason and alreadyConnected (#1828).

get_custom_hlsl.summary: Read a Custom HLSL node's kernel: sourceText, functionsText, the generated declarationsText, and readOnly with kernelSourceOverride when a compute source asset supplies the kernel (#1828).

set_custom_hlsl.summary: Write a Custom HLSL node's sourceText and/or functionsText, as the HLSL Source Editor does (UPCGCustomHLSLSettings::SetSourceText and SetFunctionsText on UE 5.9). Refused while a Kernel Source Override makes the node read-only. Saves the graph; returns the node's pins as they now stand, and the rollback writes the previous text (#1828).

disconnect_nodes.summary: Remove a wired edge between two PCG nodes. Omitted pins match any pin; a pin label the node does not have is refused with validPins. Returns removedEdges count (#346).

set_node_settings.summary: Set node params. Pass a settings object of {propertyPath: value} (dotted paths and nested structs supported), or propertyName + propertyValue for a single write. Reports previousProperties and rolls back to them. Writing a spawner's MeshSelectorType or InstanceDataPackerType recreates its selector or packer (listed in recreatedInstancedParameters). Fields of an instanced subobject the node owns are written with a dotted key (MeshSelectorParameters.AttributeName) or a field object ({MeshSelectorParameters: {AttributeName: 'Mesh'}}), in the same call as the type that selects its class; a path for an instanced subobject, or a dotted key into an object the node does not own, is refused. Addresses the graph's DefaultInputNode and DefaultOutputNode too: writing their Pins changes the graph's own pins and those of every Subgraph node calling it. An attribute selector (TargetAttribute, InputSource1, OutputTarget...) takes the PCG editor's syntax as a string: MyAttr, $Density, @Last, $Position.Z (#1275); a selector given as an object replaces the whole selector, so fields left out (ExtraNames) reset. Returns resolvedSelectors with each written selector as stored, and removedEdges for edges a pin-changing write dropped, with a warning (#1298). readBack holds each written property as stored; struct text that left fields out (which keep their old values) adds a warning naming the property (#1299).

set_static_mesh_spawner_meshes.summary: Populate weighted MeshEntries on a PCGStaticMeshSpawner node (#145). entries=[{mesh, weight?}]; replace defaults to true. Refuses a selector the node's settings do not own; reports selectorOuterIsSettings.

remove_node.summary: Remove node. The graph's input and output nodes are refused.

unwrap_instance_nodes.summary: Give instance nodes (UPCGSettingsInstance wrappers, read-only in the PCG editor's details panel) their own settings object, keeping every value and edge. Settings from a shared asset are copied into the node. Nodes that already own their settings are left alone. Omit nodeName for every node in the graph (#1087).

execute.summary: Regenerate PCG. A seed is written to the component before generating, and the old one reported back as previousSeed (#983). Returns at once with runId, or with wait=true only once that run finishes, adding wait {state generated|cancelled|cleaned|not_started|timed_out, durationMs}; a timed-out wait is a warning, not a failure (#1365). When Generate defers its start to a later tick, the run follows that generation (lastRun.deferredStart) instead of settling as not_started; a run that started nothing reports alreadyGenerated, lastFinishUtc and a note saying the output was already up to date. Refused with generation_in_progress while a run is active.

force_regenerate.summary: Force a stuck PCG component to regenerate (clears graph ref, re-sets, cleanup+generate) (#146/#983). Cancels active generation before resetting; returns runId like execute, including when the component was busy, and takes wait=true the same way (#1365).

get_generation_state.summary: One poll of a PCG component's generation: busy (generating, cleaning up, or local components generating), finishCount and lastFinishState for generations that ended since the bridge started watching the component (whoever started them), and lastRun. wait_for_generation polls this for you (#1365).

cleanup.summary: Cleanup a PCG component (remove spawned content) (#146).

toggle_graph.summary: Toggle a PCG component's graph assignment to force reinit (no generate) (#146).

add_volume.summary: Place PCG volume. Idempotent by editor label when one is given. transform {location, rotation, scale|scale3D} is honoured; reports the placed location, rotation, scale, extent and scaledExtent.

import_graph.summary: Bulk-author a PCG graph from JSON: nodes=[{name,class,posX?,posY?,settings?,subgraph?:{path,parameters}}], connections=[{from,fromPin?,to,toPin?}], replace defaults to false. Without replace, a name the graph already has is that node: the same class updates it in place (counted in nodesUpdated and listed in updatedNodes) and edges naming it land on it; another class, or a name given twice, refuses the call before anything changes (#1262). removeNodes and removeConnections run first, without replace. The rollback of an import without replace removes the nodes it created, cuts the edges it added and restores the values it overwrote; only replace=true carries a full graph snapshot (#1331). One call replaces N add_node + M connect_nodes + K set_node_settings (#213). A path for an instanced subobject is refused before anything changes, while its fields are written as set_node_settings writes them (MeshSelectorParameters.AttributeName or a field object); failed nodes, settings or connections make the result a failure; name-collision warnings are informational. Attribute selectors in settings take the PCG editor's syntax as a string ($Position.Z, @Last). A Get Graph Parameter node (PCGUserParameterGetSettings) takes parameter: '<name>' and binds to that graph parameter; export_graph emits it the same way (#1264).

export_graph.summary: Export a PCG graph as JSON; includeSettings defaults to true. Each node carries inputPins and outputPins, its pin labels; import_graph ignores them. Round-trip safe with import_graph (#213). Subgraph assignments and parameter overrides are preserved as subgraph {path,parameters}; other instanced subobjects (a spawner's mesh selector) are left out and listed in omittedInstancedProperties. Attribute selectors export in editor syntax ("$Position.Z"), extra names included (#1267).

export_level_to_asset.summary: Export a saved level to a PCG data asset (a PCG Assembly), the Content Browser's 'Create PCG Assets from Level(s)' without its dialog. Default name <LevelName>_PCG beside the level; an existing asset is overwritten. assetPath takes the asset's own path (object path, or an existing asset's package path) as well as a folder for assetName, and an existing asset of another class is refused (#1296). Reports points per output pin (Root, Points). UE 5.5+ (#1244).

update_level_assets.summary: Re-export PCG data assets from the levels they were exported from ('Update PCG Assets'). Reports points per output pin. UE 5.5+ (#1244).

set_subgraph.summary: Point a Subgraph node at a PCGGraph or PCGGraphInstance through the engine's SetSubgraph, so its pins and user-parameter bag are built (a write to SubgraphInstance.Graph builds pins but no parameters). "" clears it. Returns the node's pins and every parameter with its value and override state (#1253).

set_subgraph_parameters.summary: Override a Subgraph node's user parameters: parameters={name: value}; null clears an override. A name the subgraph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and rolls back to them (#1253).

set_graph_pins.summary: Add, update, replace or remove the graph's own pins on its input or output node (side), matched by label: append (default) adds a pin or updates the one with that label, replace makes the pins exactly the list, remove deletes the labels given. Fields left out keep an existing pin's values, so its edges stay wired. Every Subgraph node calling the graph gets the same pins. Returns the resulting pins and removedEdges for edges a removed or retyped pin dropped. Rolls back to the previous Pins through set_node_settings (#1318).

set_graph_parameters.summary: Add, change, retype or remove a graph's user parameters (the Graph Parameters a Get Graph Parameter node and a Subgraph or Graph Instance override read). graphParameters=[{name, type?, typeObject?, default?}]: a new name needs a type; an existing one keeps its type unless another is given; default is JSON or export text. removeParameters=[names]. Every entry is checked on a scratch copy first, so one bad entry refuses the call with nothing changed. Returns the parameters and previousParameters; the rollback removes what was added and restores changed defaults (#1264).

create_graph_instance.summary: Create a PCG Graph Instance asset running graphPath, with optional parameter overrides={name: value}; an override for a name the graph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, sets none and fails with the asset path in createdWithoutOverrides. Idempotent by path. Returns every parameter with its value and override state (#1264).

set_graph_instance_overrides.summary: Set a PCG Graph Instance asset's parameter overrides: overrides={name: value}; null clears one. A name the graph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and rolls back to them (#1264).

set_component_graph.summary: Assign a PCG graph to a PCGComponent through UPCGComponent::SetGraph, on a Blueprint's component template (blueprintPath; compiled and saved, so every placed instance rebuilds with it) or on a placed actor (actorLabel or actorPath). graphPath is a PCGGraph or PCGGraphInstance; "" clears it. componentName picks one when there are several. On a placed actor whose Blueprint's construction script builds the component, the call reruns the construction script and fails with reason discarded_by_reconstruction if the assignment did not survive. Returns graph, previousGraph and the new graph's parameters with their override state; rolls back to the previous graph (lossy when the component held overrides).

get_component_parameters.summary: Read a PCG component's graph and each graph parameter's value and override state ({name, type, value, overridden}), on a placed actor (actorLabel or actorPath) or on a Blueprint's component template (blueprintPath). componentName picks one when there are several. A placed actor's component that its Blueprint's construction script builds reports blueprintOwned and a warning: values written to the placed actor can be discarded on reconstruction, so write them to the Blueprint.

set_component_parameters.summary: Set a PCG component's graph parameter overrides: overrides={name: value}, null clears one. With blueprintPath it writes the Blueprint's component template (a child Blueprint gets its own override of an inherited one), compiles and saves, so every reconstruction keeps the overrides; this is the write for a PCGComponent inside a Blueprint actor. With actorLabel or actorPath it writes the placed component; when the Blueprint's construction script builds that component, the call reruns the construction script as the editor does and fails with reason discarded_by_reconstruction, naming the lost overrides and the Blueprint write to use, if they did not survive (persistedThroughReconstruction). A name the graph does not declare or a value of the wrong type refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and every parameter's value and override state, and rolls back to the previous values.

read_generated_output.summary: Read the data a PCG component generated, for any actor's PCG components (not only PCGVolumes): per tagged data its pin, tags, dataClass, kind (points | attributeSet | other), count, and a page of entries with the requested attributes (selectors such as $Position, $Density, $Position.Z or a metadata attribute; default the point properties plus every metadata attribute). offset/limit page the entries, and nextOffset says there are more. A partitioned component's local components are read too. Each component row also lists what the graph spawned, which a spawner does not hand to the output node: spawnedComponents [{name, class, owner, mesh, instanceCount}], spawnedInstanceCount and spawnedActors, with totals spawnedComponentCount and spawnedInstanceCount on the result. With nodeName it reads that node's output from the component's inspection instead (UE 5.8+): the first call turns inspection on and asks for a regenerate, later calls return each execution stack's data (#1309).

epic_add_comment_box.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Adds a comment box around the given nodes.

epic_add_comment_box__pcgeditor_subsyste.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Adds a comment box around the given nodes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_node.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Adds a native node to the graph.

epic_add_node__pcgeditor_subsystem.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Adds a native node to the graph. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_subgraph_node.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Adds a subgraph node to the graph.

epic_add_subgraph_node__pcgeditor_subsys.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Adds a subgraph node to the graph. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_collapse_nodes_to_subgraph.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Collapses at least two nodes into a subgraph. Empty AssetPath creates an embedded graph; otherwise creates a new unsaved asset named Name in the folder specified by AssetPath. Nodes must belong directly to Graph; input/output nodes are rejected. Comment boxes containing selected node positions and no unselected node positions move to the subgraph too. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_connect_node_pins.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Add an edge between two nodes connected to the specified pins.

epic_connect_node_pins__pcgeditor_subsys.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Add an edge between two nodes connected to the specified pins. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_graph.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Creates a new saved PCG graph asset.

epic_create_graph__pcgeditor_subsystem.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Creates a new unsaved PCG graph asset with a unique name. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_delete_embedded_subgraph.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Deletes an embedded graph. Referenced graphs raise a script error unless bAllowReferenced is true, which clears references and leaves missing-subgraph nodes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_disconnect_node_pins.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Removes the edge between two nodes connected to the specified pins.

epic_disconnect_node_pins__pcgeditor_sub.summary: [Epic PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem] Removes the edge between two nodes connected to the specified pins. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

view_trace.summary: Trace the live PIE player viewpoint. Returns viewLocation, viewRotation, viewDirection and line; sweepRadius also returns a sphere sweep. Each hit includes component collision state, channel response, blocksVisibility and owner label/class. Ignores the viewing pawn by default; requires running PIE.

inject_input.summary: Inject one frame of an Enhanced Input action into a PIE player. client 1..N relays to a remote player.

inject_input_start.summary: Start holding an input action every frame until inject_input_stop, PIE end, or duration_seconds of game time; control_rotation pins the controller's aim every frame while it runs. Hold several actions at once with one call each. Returns injection_id. Rolls back with inject_input_stop.

inject_input_update.summary: Change the value or control_rotation of a running hold.

inject_input_stop.summary: Stop a hold or tape by id; alreadyStopped when it had ended.

inject_input_tape.summary: Play a per-frame value array through an input action; returns injection_id.

drive_pawn.summary: Walk the PIE player's pawn: movement input every frame along direction or toward targetLocation, or mode=navigate for a navmesh move to targetLocation. Ends as completed, arrived, timeout, no_path, nav_ended, map_changed (stopOnMapChange), stopped or pie_ended. The pawn is found again every frame, so a drive carries on through a level change. With wait (default true) answers once it ends with a sampled track of location, rotation, controlRotation, velocity and map, plus mapChanges, distanceTravelled and the navPath taken; wait=false returns driveId at once.

drive_status.summary: A pawn drive's state and sampled track; includeSamples=false for the summary only.

drive_stop.summary: End a pawn drive now and return its track; alreadyStopped when it had ended.

clients.summary: List a networked PIE session's players: client 0 is the editor's own player, 1..N remote players in join order with ready and log_file.

console.summary: Run a console command in a remote player's own process (client 1..N). The editor's own PIE player is editor(execute_command, world="pie").

remote_result.summary: Whether a request relayed to a remote player ran: reported, ok, finished, error.

uat_run.summary: Run a multiplayer acceptance scenario unattended: opens its map, starts PIE with its players, drives each step, judges it from the host and client logs, stops PIE and writes report.md and report.json. Poll uat_status.

uat_status.summary: State of the current or last acceptance run: per-step results, verdict and report_dir.

uat_abort.summary: End the acceptance run early; it stops PIE and reports what it reached.

record_arm.summary: Arm the PIE recorder; it starts on BeginPIE and finalizes on EndPIE into Saved/MCPRecordings/<id>. Rolls back with record_disarm.

record_status.summary: Recorder state, id, frame, elapsed time and pie_active. While waiting_for_pawn: waiting_for (what is missing) and pie_worlds (each PIE world's pie_instance, net_mode, players and pawns).

record_read.summary: Read a recording artifact: manifest, sequence, csv, drift or tracked.

mark.summary: Insert a labelled marker into the recording in flight.

replay_arm.summary: Arm the replayer for the next PIE session: re-injects a recording's input and records drift. Rolls back with replay_disarm.

replay_run.summary: Unattended replay: arm and start PIE in one call, auto-stop PIE and write drift.json. Poll replay_status until pie_active=false.

replay_status.summary: Replayer state and the last result: drift report, frames and contact sheet paths.

replay_analyze.summary: Read a finalized drift.json as a lead: first divergence, top channels, errors during the run, bracketing images.

replay_state.summary: Deterministic state replay: the recorded pawn pose at a time or frame, interpolated; apply=true teleports the live PIE pawn there.

test_scaffold.summary: Write a reproduction test.json beside a recording: drift and error assertions plus derived predicates.

test_run.summary: Run a reproduction test: replay the recording when needed, then check drift, errors and predicates. Returns passed and failures.

assert_eval.summary: Evaluate predicates over a finished run's per-frame series, errors and markers; writes verdict.json. Ops eq|ne|lt|lte|gt|gte|approx|between|changed|increased|decreased|crossed under hold always|never|eventually|at_end|once_then_always.

record_diff.summary: Diff two recordings frame by frame against drift thresholds.

scenario_scaffold.summary: Write a declarative scenario.json (arrange, act, assert) from a recording.

scenario_validate.summary: Validate a scenario's structure and predicates without running it.

profile_create.summary: Create an observation profile asset: tracked values, actors and widgets, pawn and montage sampling, drift thresholds.

profile_update.summary: Update an observation profile; lists given replace the stored ones.

observe_arm.summary: Arm the observer with a profile; it samples every frame of the next PIE session into Saved/MCPObservations/<run>. Rolls back with observe_disarm.

observe_read.summary: Read an observation artifact; file=series returns per-channel time series.

anim_state.summary: A PIE actor's anim instance: active montage and state machine states.

anim_properties.summary: UPROPERTY values on a PIE actor's anim instance.

session_errors.summary: Deduped errors and warnings logged during a PIE session, with Blueprint exceptions.

session_log.summary: Paged Output Log lines captured during a PIE session, with filters.

perf_summary.summary: A recording's frametime avg/p50/p99/max, game/render/gpu ms, peak memory and worst hitches.

script_create.summary: Create a test script asset: steps of {instruction, judge auto|manual, arrange, act, expect {value, op decreasing|increasing|eq|gt|lt|visible|exists|triggered, target, within_ms, client}}. arrange takes a scenario's spawn|set|call entries and act takes uat_run's step actions (place, press, inject, hold, tape, console, capture, wait_ms); they run in that order before the expect window, which counts from the end of act. op triggered waits for the person playing to fire the Input Action value names (e.g. /Game/Input/IA_Interact) on player client (0 or absent the editor's own player, 1..N a remote player): only a fresh trigger after act ends counts, not input still held when the window opens, the evidence records triggered_at_ms and action_value, and within_ms 0 or absent waits with no timeout until it fires or script_stop. Always saves, returning what the check finds as warnings [{step, field, message, candidates}]: an expect.value the level, player pawn and profile do not resolve, an op or target the value's type cannot meet, an actor, actor class or Input Action arrange, act or a triggered expect name that does not exist, or no auto step without manual_only=true. resolve_in_pie=true on a step defers a value that only exists in PIE. Refused (INVALID_SCRIPT_STEPS, errors in the same shape) only when the script cannot be written: no steps, a step that does not parse, or a map (e.g. /Game/Maps/L_Arena) that is not a level.

script_update.summary: Update a test script; steps given replace the stored ones. Checks the result like script_create when steps, profile, map or manual_only change, and saves with its findings as warnings; refuses only what cannot be written.

script_validate.summary: Check steps the way script_create does without saving anything: valid, and errors [{step, field, message, candidates}] for every finding script_create would return as a warning or refuse.

script_values.summary: What a script can name in the open level: the player pawn's readable value paths with kind and type, pawn_channels read off the sampled pawn with no profile (pos_x, vel_z, rot_yaw, speed2d, ...), level actors, classes the game mode spawns, Widget Blueprints and the profile's tracked values. target adds which actors are of that class and whether it is the player pawn.

script_list.summary: List test scripts, each with map and last_run: its newest run's run_id, state, started_at, ended_at, summary and results_path, or null.

script_run.summary: Run a test script in PIE: opens the script's map first when another level is open, refusing when that level has unsaved changes or PIE is running elsewhere; arms the observer and, unless record=false, the recorder; mode=manual instead starts no PIE, observer or recording, leaves auto steps unchecked and puts every manual step up for its verdict at once; evaluates auto steps live and marks each pass or fail; waits on manual steps for verdicts, asked through an elicitation form when the client supports one, otherwise through verdict. Writes results.json beside the observation. wait=true returns once the run finishes.

script_status.summary: A script run's state, steps and events since since_seq. wait=true blocks until it finishes or needs a verdict.

script_stop.summary: End a script run now; unsettled steps stay pending and results.json is written.

verdict.summary: Record a manual step's verdict: pass, fail or skip, with a note. source=agent marks the calling agent's own judgement and needs evidence {note, captures?}; a step with agent_judgeable=false takes only a person's verdict.

script_runs.summary: List script runs newest first, the active one included: run_id, script, started_at, ended_at, state, summary, per-step results and results_path. script narrows to one script's runs.

script_replay.summary: Replay a finished run's recording in the level it ran in and re-evaluate its auto steps at their recorded offsets; manual steps keep their verdicts. Reports regressions.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

epic_add_additional_plugin_directory.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Adds a directory the project searches for plugins, saves the .uproject file, and rescans so plugins in the directory are discovered without a restart. No-ops if the directory is already listed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_disallowed_plugin.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Adds an entry to a plugin's DisallowedPlugins array in its .uplugin file, or updates its comment if the entry already exists. The disallowed plugin does not need to be currently discovered. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_plugin_dependency.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Adds a dependency entry to a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file. No-ops if a dependency with that name already exists with matching settings. The dependency plugin does not need to be currently discovered.

epic_create_plugin.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Creates a new plugin from a template and loads it into the editor. Use GetPluginTemplateDescriptions to obtain a valid TemplateInfo.

epic_get_additional_plugin_directories.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Lists the extra directories the project searches for plugins (the .uproject's AdditionalPluginDirectories). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_capabilities.summary: [Epic AgentPluginToolset.AgentPluginToolset] Returns details for specific capabilities. Discovery fails after 60 seconds. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_configured_additional_metadata_.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Lists the additional metadata keys the GameFeatures subsystem is configured to read from each .uplugin (UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys), sorted. These are the only keys SetGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue and RemoveGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue will accept. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_disallowed_plugins.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the entries from a plugin's DisallowedPlugins array in its .uplugin file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_game_feature_plugin_details.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Reads the editable metadata on a Game Feature Plugin's .uplugin descriptor. Returns the BuiltInInitialFeatureState and the configured additional metadata keys (UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys) with their values rendered as JSON literals. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_game_feature_state.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Gets the current state of a Game Feature Plugin.

epic_get_plugin_dependencies.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the dependency entries from a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file.

epic_get_plugin_dependents.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the names of all discovered plugins that declare a dependency on the given plugin.

epic_get_plugin_descriptor.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Gets the editable descriptor fields for a discovered plugin.

epic_get_plugin_for_asset.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the name of the enabled plugin whose content mount point contains the given asset path. Accepts full asset paths or mount point prefixes (e.g. /PluginName/ or /Game/Path/To/Asset).

epic_get_plugin_info.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Gets metadata for a discovered plugin, including description, version, base directory, content directory, descriptor path, and mounted asset path.

epic_get_plugin_template_descriptions.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the list of available plugin templates. Pass one of the results to CreatePlugin to create a new plugin from that template.

epic_is_enabled.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Checks whether a discovered plugin is currently enabled.

epic_is_game_feature_active.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Checks whether a Game Feature Plugin is active. Raises an error if the subsystem is unavailable or the plugin is not found. Use GetGameFeatureState if you need the current state when the plugin is not active.

epic_is_game_feature_plugin.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Return whether or not a plugin is a Game Feature Plugin. Will error if no plugin of this name can be found by the Plugin Manager.

epic_is_plugin_creation_allowed.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Checks whether the editor settings permit plugin creation from the plugin browser.

epic_is_plugin_modification_allowed.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Checks whether the editor settings permit modifying plugins from the plugin browser.

epic_list_capabilities.summary: [Epic AgentPluginToolset.AgentPluginToolset] Lists available capabilities from the current agent plugin directories and working directory. Discovery fails after 60 seconds. Warnings report rejected sources and discovery limits. Treat capability IDs as opaque values and pass them unchanged to GetCapabilities. Use an agent's Reference, not its ID, when a skill asks for a 'subagent_type'. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_discovered_game_feature_plugin.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Lists all discovered Game Feature Plugins sorted by name. This includes disabled plugins and plugins the Game Features system has not registered, which the other tools cannot resolve. Use the Plugins toolset to do general plugin enable/disable tasks.

epic_list_discovered_plugins.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Lists the names of all discovered plugins (enabled and disabled), sorted alphabetically.

epic_list_enabled_game_feature_plugins.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Lists enabled Game Feature Plugins that the Game Features system has registered, sorted by name. The project's policy can keep an enabled plugin from registering; ListDiscoveredGameFeaturePlugins still includes those. Use the Plugins toolset to do general plugin enable/disable tasks.

epic_list_enabled_plugins.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Lists the names of all enabled plugins, sorted alphabetically.

epic_remove_additional_plugin_directory.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Removes a directory the project searches for plugins, saves the .uproject file, and rescans. Plugins from the directory that are enabled stay loaded until the editor restarts. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_disallowed_plugin.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Removes an entry from a plugin's DisallowedPlugins array in its .uplugin file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_game_feature_plugin_metadata.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Removes one of the configured additional metadata keys from the GFP's .uplugin. After removal the key round-trips through AdditionalMetadata as an empty string -- that is the engine parser's default for missing keys, surfaced honestly. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_remove_plugin_dependency.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Removes a dependency entry from a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file.

epic_request_activate_game_feature.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests activation of a Game Feature Plugin, loading it first if it is not already loaded.

epic_request_deactivate_game_feature.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests deactivation of a Game Feature Plugin, which leaves it loaded.

epic_request_load_game_feature.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests load of a Game Feature Plugin without activating it. Use RequestActivateGameFeature instead to make the plugin's features live. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_request_unload_game_feature.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests unload of a Game Feature Plugin, taking it out of the Loaded state. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_game_feature_plugin_built_in_au.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Sets the BuiltInInitialFeatureState on the GFP's .uplugin descriptor and writes the descriptor back to disk. EPluginToolsetGFPAutoState::Invalid is not accepted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_game_feature_plugin_metadata_va.summary: [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Writes a value for one of the configured additional metadata keys to the GFP's .uplugin. JsonValueLiteral must be a valid JSON literal (e.g. true, 42, "hello", {"Major":1}); booleans and numbers are stored as native JSON types rather than strings. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_plugin_enabled.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Enables or disables a plugin in the project and saves the .uproject file, checking it out via source control if enabled.

epic_update_plugin_dependency.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Changes the settings of an existing dependency entry in a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file. Anything not provided keeps its current value, as do fields the plugin editor doesn't show, such as platform lists. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_update_plugin_descriptor.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Updates a plugin's descriptor fields and writes them to its .uplugin file. Checks out the file via source control if source control is enabled. No-ops if the serialized descriptor is unchanged (file is not touched).

epic_validate_new_plugin_name_and_locati.summary: [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Validates that PluginName and RelativePluginLocation are acceptable for a new plugin.
