action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

set_developer_setting.summary: Set a UPROPERTY(Config) value on a settings class default object (a UDeveloperSettings subclass or any config= class) and save it the way the Project Settings dialog does: PostEditChangeProperty on the default object, then UpdateSinglePropertyInConfigFile into Default<Config>.ini (TryUpdateDefaultConfigFile for a container), or the per-user config with persist=user. The ini is the one the class names, never a caller path. Unlike set_config, the settings object sees the change and the value survives a restart; unlike editor(set_object_property), it is saved. Returns configFile, section, key and the iniLines now on disk. Read the current value with editor(get_property) on the class path.

get_maps_settings.summary: Read Project Settings > Maps & Modes: default GameMode, server GameMode, GameInstance class, game/server/editor startup/transition maps. settings is the live value in the editor, stored is what DefaultEngine.ini holds (null when the file has no entry) (#1566).

set_maps_settings.summary: Write Project Settings > Maps & Modes. Classes accept a /Script path, short name or Blueprint asset path and must derive from GameModeBase or GameInstance; maps must be existing world assets; an empty string clears. Every value is validated before any is written. Updates the live settings object and DefaultEngine.ini, then returns settings, stored (read back from the file) and persisted per write. For any other Project Settings page, editor(set_property) on the settings class path persists a config property the same way (#1566).

resolve_collision_profile.summary: Read one collision profile's resolved per-channel responses: collisionEnabled, objectType, and every channel with Block/Overlap/Ignore. This is the project-side half of blueprint(get_component_collision) (#925): a component's ResponseArray only lists the channels it OVERRIDES, so the profile is where an inherited response actually comes from. Project trace and object channels appear under their configured names, with enumName (ECC_GameTraceChannel1) alongside so a caller can key on something stable. By default the eight engine channels plus every channel the project configured are returned; includeAllChannels=true adds the unused slots. channel narrows it to one. A profile that does not exist lists the ones that do.

create_cpp_class.summary: Create a new native UCLASS in a project module. Uses the same engine template path as File → New C++ Class. Writes .h + .cpp; returns both paths plus needsEditorRestart (true unless Live Coding successfully hot-reloaded).

list_project_modules.summary: List native modules in the current project (name, host type, source path), in the .uproject's own declaration order. Feed moduleName from here into create_cpp_class.

generate_project_files.summary: Generate IDE project files (Visual Studio, Xcode, etc.).

list_available_plugins.summary: List every plugin installed in this engine or project, sorted by name, with its category, version, type, whether it is enabled in THIS editor session, whether it is enabled by default, and the .uproject's current reference to it under projectReference {present, enabled}. Those two disagree after enable_plugin until the editor restarts, which is the point of reporting both.

enable_plugin.summary: Enable a plugin in the .uproject. Plugin enablement is neither a UPROPERTY nor an INI key, it is a JSON array in the .uproject read once at startup, so set_config cannot reach it and without this a plugin-gated capability stays permanently unreachable through the bridge. Idempotent: a plugin already enabled, or enabled by default with no entry, reports existed and writes nothing. The change is a file change, so modules, classes, content and settings appear only after editor(restart_editor), which the result says. Only the plugin's entry in the on-disk .uproject Plugins array is patched; every other field, including a Modules edit made while the editor runs, is left as the file has it (#1248).

disable_plugin.summary: Disable a plugin in the .uproject. removeReference deletes the entry outright instead of writing an explicit disable, which is the difference between handing a default-on plugin back to its default and overriding it, and the two are not the same file. Idempotent against whichever of the two was asked for. Refuses to disable the bridge itself, since that would leave no way to undo it. Patches only that entry of the on-disk .uproject (#1248). Takes effect on the next editor start.

live_coding_compile.summary: Trigger a Live Coding compile (Windows only). Hot-patches method bodies of existing UCLASSes without editor restart - the fast inner loop for UFUNCTION implementations. Does NOT reliably register brand-new UCLASSes; use build_project + editor restart for those.

live_coding_status.summary: Report Live Coding availability/state (available, started, enabledForSession, compiling). Helps choose between live_coding_compile and build_project.

list_localization_cultures.summary: Report the project's cultures: the editor's current culture, language and locale, the game's native culture and the cultures it has compiled localization for, CulturesToStage from the packaging settings, and every project localization target with its native culture and supported cultures.

list_localization_targets.summary: List the project's localization targets (includeEngineTargets adds the engine's): name, guid, cultures with word counts, nativeCulture, what each gathers from (packages with include/exclude paths, source files with search directories, metadata), conflict status, and its files (gather and compile configs, manifest, an archive and a LocRes per culture, each with exists, bytes and modified). Every row is valid set_localization_target input.

set_localization_target.summary: Create or change a project localization target: cultures (replaces the list), nativeCulture, gatherFromPackages with includePaths/excludePaths (wildcards relative to the project root, e.g. Content/UI/*), gatherFromTextFiles with searchDirectories. A new target gathers nothing until told what to. Written to DefaultEditor.ini as Project Settings would. A call that changes nothing reports unchanged; the rollback removes a created target or restores the previous settings.

remove_localization_target.summary: Remove a project localization target; deleteFiles also deletes its configs, manifest, archives and LocRes. The rollback recreates its settings (not deleted files). Removing one that is not there reports alreadyRemoved.

gather_localization_target.summary: Gather text for one localization target: writes its gather config and runs the GatherText commandlet in a separate process, as the Localization Dashboard's Gather Text does, then answers with the exit code, the error lines, a log tail and the target's refreshed files and word counts. A second gather or compile while one runs is refused.

compile_localization_target.summary: Compile one localization target's archives into LocRes files (culture narrows it to one), through the GatherText commandlet as the Localization Dashboard's Compile Text does, then refreshes the editor's loaded localization. Answers with the exit code, error lines, a log tail and the target's files.

epic_compile_live_coding.summary: [Epic LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset] Triggers a Live Coding compile and returns a pending result that resolves once the compile finishes. Live Coding must be enabled in Editor Preferences. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_directory.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Creates a directory and any missing parents. A directory that already exists is a success. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_delete_file.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Deletes one file. Directories are rejected. Recursive deletion is unavailable. Source-controlled files are marked for deletion when source control is available. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_discover_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Initialize automation worker discovery and load the test list. Must be called once before ListTests or RunTests. Takes several seconds as it discovers the local automation worker and enumerates all registered tests. Returns an async result that completes with true when tests are available, or an error if discovery fails.

epic_download_url.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Downloads an HTTPS URL to a file. Redirects are not followed. Responses above 1 GiB are rejected. Local, private, and selected special-use addresses are rejected. Only HTTP 200 responses succeed. Host resolution and the HTTP request each time out after 30 seconds. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_edit_text_by_anchor.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Edits the unique occurrence of a piece of text. Source files and results above 1 MiB are rejected. Big-endian UTF-16 files are rejected. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. AnchorText is matched exactly first. If that fails, LF and CRLF variants are tried. NewText uses the file's existing line ending. Replace changes the anchor text itself. InsertBefore and InsertAfter insert whole lines and preserve the anchor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_edit_text_by_line_range.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Edits an inclusive range of one-based lines. Source files and results above 1 MiB are rejected. Big-endian UTF-16 files are rejected. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. Lines outside the range remain unchanged, including their line endings. NewText uses the file's existing line ending. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_enable_live_coding.summary: [Epic LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset] Call before CompileLiveCoding on a session launched with Live Coding off; starts the Broker/Agent. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_section_property_values.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns the current values of the specified properties as a JSON object.

epic_get_section_schema.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns a JSON Schema describing the user-visible properties of a settings section. The schema maps each property name to its type, description, and constraints. A section that uses a custom widget has no settings object and so no schema.

epic_get_supported_platforms.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns the platforms the project declares support for in its .uproject file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_test_results.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Get detailed results for the current or most recent test run. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed.

epic_get_test_status.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Get a lightweight status snapshot of the automation controller. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed.

epic_is_live_coding_ready.summary: [Epic LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset] Poll before calling CompileLiveCoding to avoid blocking on the Broker's initial module load. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_available_platforms.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the platforms a project can declare support for, the choices in the Project Settings Supported Platforms section. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_categories.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all categories within a settings container, sorted alphabetically.

epic_list_containers.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all known settings containers, sorted alphabetically. Common containers are "Editor" and "Project".

epic_list_directory.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Lists a range from the immediate contents of a directory. Directories with more than 100000 immediate entries are rejected before filtering or range selection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_sections.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all sections within a settings category, sorted alphabetically.

epic_list_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] List available automation tests. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed.

epic_read_text_file.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Reads lines or fragments without line numbers, budgeting the complete JSON response for EDA. Decode Contents once as JSON when ContentsEncoding is "json-string" to recover NUL and U+FFFE/U+FFFF without transport substitution. Oversized lines are returned in character-aligned fragments. Pass NextCursor to continue without losing text. Supports UTF-8 and byte-order-marked UTF-16. Legacy single-byte text is not supported on all platforms. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_reset_section_to_defaults.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Resets the settings in a section to their default values. Project sections saved to a Default*.ini cannot be reset, matching the Settings editor.

epic_resolve_path.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Resolves a native path, Unreal virtual-content path, or plugin path that the plugin manager finds to an absolute native path. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_run_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Run a set of automation tests by name. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Starts executing the specified tests and returns an async result that completes with a summary when all tests finish.

epic_run_tests_by_filter.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Run automation tests selected by a filter expression. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Much faster than RunTests when targeting a large batch because the engine narrows the report tree in a single pass instead of running a per-leaf membership check against the requested name list. Filter syntax (multiple expressions joined by '+'): "StartsWith:System.Engine" prefix match against the full test path "^Foo" prefix anchor (equivalent to StartsWith:) "Bar$" suffix anchor "Substring" bare token matches anywhere in the path "Group:Smoke" expand a named group from AutomationControllerSettings ini Groups Returns an async result that completes with the same summary shape as RunTests.

epic_save_section.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Saves the settings in a section. The default config file is checked out first when source control is enabled.

epic_search_settings.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Finds settings by the label shown in the Settings editor, the property name, the tooltip, or the console variable the property is bound to, across every container. Every word in the query must match, ignoring case. A section whose own name matches is returned with an empty PropertyName. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_set_section_properties.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Sets one or more properties on a settings section from a JSON object and saves. PropertiesJson must be a JSON object mapping property names to new values, in the same format returned by GetSectionPropertyValues. If any value is rejected, none are applied and nothing is saved. The default config file is checked out first when source control is enabled.

epic_set_supported_platforms.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Replaces the platforms the project declares support for and saves the .uproject file, checking it out first when source control is enabled. Packaging, running or cooking for a platform not in the list warns. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_stop_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Stop all currently running tests. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. If a RunTests async result is pending, it will be completed with an error.

epic_write_text_file.summary: [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Writes a complete UTF-8 text file and creates missing parent directories. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

tools.name: reflection
tools.description:
UE reflection: classes, structs, enums, gameplay tags, and SaveGame instances.

Call reflection(action, args={...}). Actions:
reflect_class(className, includeInherited?:b)
reflect_instance(objectPath, propertyPath?, filter?, includeInherited?:b, includeValues?:b, editableOnly?:b, maxDepth?:i, cursor?, limit?:i)
reflect_struct(structName)
reflect_enum(enumName)
list_classes(parentFilter?, cursor?, limit?:i)
list_structs(package?, filter?, cursor?, limit?:i)
list_tags(filter?, cursor?, limit?:i)
create_tag(tag, comment?)
create_enum(name, packagePath?, entries?:[*], onConflict?)
set_enum_entries(assetPath, entries:[*])
is_class_loaded(className|class)
is_module_loaded(moduleName|module)
list_loaded_modules(filter?, loadedOnly?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)
inspect_save_game(slotName, userIndex?:i)
epic_get_class(instance:ref)
epic_get_properties(instance:ref, properties:[s])
epic_get_property_schema(instance:ref, root?, maxDepth?:i)
epic_list_properties(instance:ref)
epic_reset_properties(instance:ref, properties:[s])
epic_search_subclasses(base_class:ref, class_name)
epic_set_properties(instance:ref, values)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

reflect_class.summary: Reflect UClass properties and functions. To call a static BlueprintCallable editor function with arguments and return values, use editor(invoke_static_function) with className, functionName and args. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix (UMyConfig and MyConfig both resolve), a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a Blueprint class path; a failed lookup lists the spellings tried and the closest matches (#823).

reflect_instance.summary: Per-instance writable schema: what can be written on THIS asset, CDO or subobject right now. reflect_class answers what a class has; this answers what the object in front of you will accept, which is what removes the write-and-see loop. Per property: type and kind, the same tooltip/category/displayName/clamp/UI-range/units metadata reflect_class reports, the UPROPERTY flag names, the current value and valueText, and the constraints a write has to satisfy - enum values, allowed and disallowed classes for an object reference, array/set element type, map key and value types, struct field layout, container element count. Instance state on top of that: 'editable' with a 'notEditableReason' (EditConst, EditDefaultsOnly read on an instance, EditInstanceOnly read on defaults), the EditCondition and whether it is met on THIS object, 'settable' saying whether asset/editor(set_property) can write it at all, and 'valueObjectPath' for an instanced subobject so the next call can aim at it. objectPath takes an asset path, an object path, a class path or a Blueprint path (its generated-class defaults). propertyPath scopes the read to one nested struct or object reference, including one array element picked by key (`Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Presentation`).

reflect_enum.summary: Reflect UEnum by full path, short name, or short name without the E prefix. Resolves native enums in any loaded module and loads unloaded Blueprint (UserDefinedEnum) assets via the asset registry. Returns enumPath, userDefined, and per-value name/value/displayName/tooltip; a failed lookup lists close matches (#762).

list_classes.summary: List classes. parentFilter resolves with or without the C++ A/U/F/E prefix (#823). Rows carry name, path and parent, sorted by path so a page boundary is stable.

list_structs.summary: List UScriptStructs, native and user-defined. Rows carry name (the registered spelling, without the F prefix), cppName (with it), path, package, parent, native and tableRow (derives from FTableRowBase, so usable as a DataTable row struct), sorted by path so a page boundary is stable. package narrows to one package or content folder: /Script/Engine, a bare module name (Engine), or /Game/Data. filter is a case-insensitive substring of name or cppName (#1088).

list_tags.summary: List gameplay tags, optionally only those under a prefix.

create_tag.summary: Create a gameplay tag in Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini. Inserts exactly one +GameplayTagList line, keeping the file's comments, order and existing values, and rebuilds the live tag tree so the tag is usable without a restart (method=ini_append, registeredLive). Only when the file cannot be written does it fall back to the Gameplay Tags editor, which can check the file out but rewrites it whole (method=gameplay_tags_editor) (#1322). Idempotent: a tag the ini already declares reports existed. A failure names the ini path and the cause, including a read-only (checked-in) file.

create_enum.summary: Create UUserDefinedEnum asset, optionally seeded with entries: strings, or {name, displayName?} objects (#274).

set_enum_entries.summary: Replace entries on an existing UUserDefinedEnum. entries takes the create_enum form: strings, or {name, displayName?} (#274).

is_class_loaded.summary: Report whether a UClass is currently loaded in the editor (loaded), whether it exists/is loadable (exists), and its owning module + that module's load state. Distinguishes 'not loaded yet' from 'does not exist'. className takes a short name, /Script/<Module>.<Class>, or a BP class path (#689).

is_module_loaded.summary: Report whether a named module is currently loaded (#689).

list_loaded_modules.summary: Enumerate modules with runtime load state. filter is a case-insensitive substring; loadedOnly defaults to false. Returns modules[{name, loaded, gameModule}] + totalLoaded/totalModules (#689).

inspect_save_game.summary: Load a SaveGame slot read-only and return its reflected UPROPERTY(SaveGame) values. Non-serializable properties are listed in skippedProperties instead of failing the call. userIndex defaults to 0.

epic_get_class.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Returns the class of an Unreal object. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ObjectToolset.GetClass.

epic_get_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Returns the values of one or more properties on an object. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ObjectToolset.GetProperties.

epic_get_property_schema.summary: [Epic EditorToolset.ObjectToolset] Returns a JSON Schema of the properties on an object, with each property's type and description. Much larger than ListProperties, so find the property there and come here only when its type is needed. A schema describes types rather than an instance, so Root cannot carry a subscript. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Returns a list of properties that are on the specified object. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ObjectToolset.ListProperties.

epic_reset_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Resets one or more properties on an object to their default values, removing any per-instance overrides. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ObjectToolset.ResetProperties.

epic_search_subclasses.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Finds all subclasses of a given class. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ObjectToolset.SearchSubclasses.

epic_set_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Sets the values of properties on an object. On UE 5.9 it calls EditorToolset.ObjectToolset.SetProperties.

tools.name: source_control
tools.description:
Source control through the editor's own provider (Perforce, Git, Unity Version Control, Subversion): provider, connection and supported operations, file status, history, the project's pending changes, checkout, add, mark for delete, revert, sync, diff, submit, and whether bridge writes check out read-only files automatically. Provider-specific actions (shelves, streams, branches) come from provider plugins injected here under their own prefix, such as p4_*.

Call source_control(action, args={...}). Actions:
get_provider()
get_status(paths:[s], limit?:i)
list_changes(paths?:[s], limit?:i, includeUntracked?:b)
checkout(paths:[s])
add(paths:[s])
revert(paths:[s], dryRun?:b, discardUnsaved?:b, restoreFrom?:o)
diff(path, revision?, openEditor?:b, contextLines?:i, maxLines?:i)
submit(paths:[s], description)
mark_for_delete(paths:[s])
sync(paths?:[s])
history(path, limit?:i)
connect(password?)
set_checkout_mode(mode:{manual,auto})
epic_add(files:[s])
epic_check_out(files:[s])
epic_create_branch(branchName, repository?)
epic_create_changelist(assetPaths:[s], description)
epic_delete(files:[s])
epic_delete_branch(branch, repository?)
epic_download(file, revision?, destination?)
epic_edit_changelist_description(changelistId, description)
epic_get_asset_source_control_state(assetPath)
epic_get_changelist_files(changelistId)
epic_get_checked_out_assets()
epic_list_asset_revisions(assetPath)
epic_list_branches(repository?)
epic_list_changelists()
epic_list_submitted_changelists(revision?, length?:i, repository?)
epic_load_asset_revision(assetPath, revision?)
epic_merge_branch(branch, repository?)
epic_move_files_to_changelist(changelistId, files:[s])
epic_push_branch(branch, repository?)
epic_query_branch(branch?, repository?)
epic_query_changelist_details(revision, repository?)
epic_query_history(file)
epic_query_provider(repository?)
epic_query_states(files:[s])
epic_resolve(files:[s])
epic_resolve_complete(files:[s])
epic_resolve_mine(files:[s])
epic_resolve_theirs(files:[s])
epic_restore_as_latest(description, repository?)
epic_restore_branch(branch, repository?)
epic_revert(files:[s])
epic_revert_unchanged(files:[s])
epic_submit_changelist(changelistId)
epic_submit_changes(description)
epic_switch_branch(branch, repository?)
epic_sync(revision?, repository?)
epic_validate_changelist(changelistId)
epic_validate_changes()

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

get_provider.summary: The active provider, whether it is enabled and connected, its status fields (port, user, client or workspace, branch, repository, where the provider reports them), what it supports (checkout, changelists, diff against the depot), which source_control actions the provider can run (operations, asked of the provider where the engine supports it) and the bridge's checkout mode. Call this first. With no provider configured it reports enabled=false rather than failing.

get_status.summary: State of named assets, files or folders, refreshed from the provider: checked out, added, deleted, modified, conflicted, out of date, checked out by another user (otherUser), what can be done next (canCheckout, canAdd, canRevert, canSubmit) and unsavedInEditor for a loaded package. A folder reports every file the provider knows under it, up to limit.

list_changes.summary: Every changed, added, deleted, opened or untracked file under the project's Content, Config, Source and Plugins folders (or the paths given), with its state. Where the provider uses changelists (Perforce) each file names its changelist and changelists lists them with descriptions. Capped at limit with total and truncated; a failed refresh is reported as a warning over the cached list rather than an error.

checkout.summary: Check out (open for edit) files so they can be saved. Reports checkedOut, alreadyCheckedOut and failed with a reason per file (locked by another user, out of date, not under source control). On a provider without checkout (Git) the files are reported as checkoutNotRequired. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call checked out.

add.summary: Mark new files for add. A file must exist on disk, so save a new asset first. Reports added, alreadyControlled and failed per file. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call added.

revert.summary: Revert files to the repository revision, discarding local edits. dryRun=true lists what would be reverted (wouldRevert) and changes nothing. Unsaved editor edits to a named package are reported (unsavedInEditor) and refuse the call unless discardUnsaved=true. Loaded packages are unloaded and reloaded around the revert; a loaded map must be closed first. No inverse: the discarded edits are gone.

diff.summary: Diff one file against a repository revision: head, or revision (the provider's id, a unique prefix of 7 or more characters, its number, or head, as history lists them). A text file (config, source, .uproject) returns a unified diff with addedLines and removedLines, capped at maxLines. A package returns its status and the revision it would be compared with; openEditor=true opens the editor's asset diff window against that revision, with the revision loaded into a /Temp package that is unloaded when the window closes (unloadsOnClose).

submit.summary: Submit (Perforce, Subversion, Unity Version Control) or commit (Git) the named files with a description. Only the named files are submitted, never implicitly. Files with unsaved editor edits refuse the call. Reports submitted and failed per file. No inverse: a submit is in the repository history, and undoing it is a new change.

mark_for_delete.summary: Mark files for delete in the repository. Where the provider removes the file from disk on delete (Git, Perforce) it is gone locally too. Reports markedForDelete, alreadyDeleted and failed per file (marked for add, not under source control, locked). Files with unsaved editor edits refuse the call; a clean loaded package is listed under loadedInEditor. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call marked.

sync.summary: Sync (Perforce get latest, Git pull) the named paths, or the project's Content, Config, Source and Plugins folders, to the latest repository revision. Packages under the paths with unsaved editor edits refuse the call. Loaded packages whose file changed are reloaded (reloaded); changedFiles lists the named files and loaded packages the sync rewrote. No inverse: going back is another sync.

history.summary: Revision history of one asset or file, newest first: revision, user, date, action, description, changelist (checkInIdentifier) and file size per revision, capped at limit with total and truncated.

connect.summary: Connect, or reconnect, the editor's configured provider, with an optional password or ticket for providers that log in. Reports wasConnected and connected, and the provider's own error text when it fails. The password is never echoed.

set_checkout_mode.summary: Choose what a bridge write does with a read-only file under source control for the rest of the editor session. manual (the default) refuses and names source_control(checkout); auto checks the file out first and lists it on the result as autoCheckedOut. UE_MCP_CHECKOUT_MODE=auto at editor startup turns it on from the start. Rolls back to the previous mode.

epic_add.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Adds files to source control; they are added on the next submit. Async: await the result. The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that is already tracked, fails the call with its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_check_out.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Checks files out, so they can be edited and submitted. Async: await the result. The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that is not tracked or is checked out exclusively by another user, fails the call with its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Creates a branch off the current branch. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. Providers may refuse while there are pending changes, and may push the new branch to the server. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_create_changelist.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Creates a new pending changelist and moves the specified files into it. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_delete.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Marks files for delete and removes them from disk, discarding any unsaved changes in their loaded packages. Unloads the assets of the deleted files and reloads the open level when its map or external packages change, so a deleted actor of a level that stores its actors in separate files disappears from that level. Blocks until the delete and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not tracked; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_delete_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Deletes a branch for every user. Providers that keep history may archive it instead. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. The provider decides which branches it accepts, for example it may refuse the current branch. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_download.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Downloads a revision of a file to a local path, without changing the workspace. Async: await the result. Refreshes the history of the file first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_edit_changelist_description.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Replaces the description of a pending changelist. Async: await the result. The default changelist's description cannot be edited; to give its files a description, create a changelist with CreateChangelist and move the files into it with MoveFilesToChangelist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_asset_source_control_state.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Returns the source-control state for an asset. Blocks until the provider answers. Does not write to the message log. Raises when the asset does not exist or when the state cannot be read, for example when source control is disabled or unavailable. A file that is not tracked by source control is not an error: bIsSourceControlled is false. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_changelist_files.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists the files in a pending changelist, including files that are not content. Raises when source control is unavailable or the changelist does not exist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_get_checked_out_assets.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Returns the content paths of all assets you currently have open in source control (checked out, marked for add, or marked for delete). Non-content files (source, config, etc.) and anything that doesn't map to a mounted content root are omitted. Files marked for delete are still listed. Raises when source control is not enabled or the status refresh fails. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_asset_revisions.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Returns the source-control revision history for an asset, newest first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_branches.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists the branches of a repository. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_changelists.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists the pending changelists, including the default changelist. Raises when source control is unavailable, the provider does not use changelists or the refresh fails. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_list_submitted_changelists.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists submitted changelists, one page at a time, in the order the provider reports them, typically newest first. Async: await the result. To get the next page, pass the last identifier of a page as Revision. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_load_asset_revision.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Loads a historical revision of an asset alongside the currently loaded one. Async: await the result. Treat the loaded package as read-only. It stays in memory until garbage collection runs. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_merge_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Merges the head of another branch into the current branch and reloads the loaded packages the merge changes, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the merge and the reload complete. Game thread only. Previews the merge first to find the affected files. Files changed on both branches may become conflicted: resolve them before submitting. Providers may push the merge result to the server. Raises when the branch is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises, without merging, when a loaded package the merge changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_move_files_to_changelist.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Moves files into an existing pending changelist. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_push_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Pushes a branch to the server. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_query_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the details of a branch. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_query_changelist_details.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the details of a submitted changelist, such as its description, author and date. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_query_history.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the revision history of any file, such as a Verse file, a project file or an asset, newest first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_query_provider.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the status the provider reports for a repository, for example the current branch, user and workspace. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_query_states.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the current source control states of files, refreshing them from the provider first. Async: await the result. A file that is not tracked is not an error: its state reports bIsSourceControlled as false. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_resolve.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Marks conflicted mergeable files, such as text or Verse files, resolved once their conflict markers have been removed from the files on disk. Edit and save the files first. Async: await the result. Does not change the files. For files that are not mergeable, use ResolveMine or ResolveTheirs instead. The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that still has conflict markers, fails the call with its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_resolve_complete.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Completes the resolution of conflicts, once every conflicted file has been resolved with Resolve, ResolveMine or ResolveTheirs. Async: await the result. Providers may record the resolved files locally, for example by committing them to a personal branch. The provider decides when it accepts this; for example it fails while conflicts remain or when the repository is not resolving conflicts. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_resolve_mine.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Resolves conflicted files by keeping the local version, and reloads their loaded packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the resolve and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises, without resolving, when a loaded package of the files has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not conflicted; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_resolve_theirs.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Resolves conflicted files by taking the incoming version, discarding their local changes, and reloads their loaded packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the resolve and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises, without resolving, when a loaded package of the files has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not conflicted; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_restore_as_latest.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Makes the synced revision the latest revision of the current branch again, by submitting a new revision with its content. Blocks until the provider completes. Game thread only. Raises when the description is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises when the branch moved on since the last sync. Raises when files the restore changes are checked out by other users; the error lists them. Raises when the provider fails the operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_restore_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Restores a branch removed by DeleteBranch. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. The provider decides which branches it can restore. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_revert.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Reverts files, discarding their local changes and any unsaved changes in their loaded packages, and reloads those packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the revert and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not checked out; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_revert_unchanged.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Releases the checkout of the given files that are checked out but not modified, so other users can check them out. Refreshes the modified state of the files first. Does not change the files on disk, so their loaded packages are not reloaded. Files that are not checked out or are modified are left alone. Blocks until the revert completes. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_submit_changelist.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Submits a pending changelist after validating it, and fails with the validation errors if it does not pass. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Invokes the Submit Tool when one is available, as the Submit action in the Changelists window does; the user completes the submit there, so the changelist is not yet submitted when the result completes. Otherwise submits it directly. Async: await the result. Use this rather than submitting by any other route. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_submit_changes.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Submits every pending change under the source control locations, without a changelist. Blocks until the submit completes. Game thread only. Refreshes the status of the source control locations, then submits every file there that can be checked in. Invokes the Submit Tool when one is available, as SubmitChangelist does; the user completes the submit there, so the changes are not yet submitted when this returns. Otherwise checks the files in directly, after virtualizing payloads when virtualization is enabled, which may append tags to the description. Does not save, sync or validate first, and does not add files that are not tracked. Raises when the description is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when there is nothing to submit. Raises when the Submit Tool fails to start. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_switch_branch.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Switches to the head of another branch and reloads the loaded packages the switch changes, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the switch and the reload complete. Game thread only. Previews the switch first to find the affected files. Raises when the branch is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises, without switching, when a loaded package the switch changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_sync.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Syncs to a revision and reloads the loaded packages the sync changes, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the sync and the reload complete. Game thread only. Previews the sync first to find the affected files. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises, without syncing, when a loaded package the sync changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_validate_changelist.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Validates a pending changelist the way the submit check does: the registered validators run on the changelist and on its assets. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_validate_changes.summary: [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Validates every pending change under the source control locations, without a changelist, the way the check-in dialog does. Collects the same files SubmitChanges submits, and runs the registered files validator on them. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

read.summary: Full dump of a StateTree asset: state hierarchy (with description, tag, customTickRate, color), tasks, conditions, transitions, evaluators, global tasks, root params, bindings, and editor data extensions (class + objectPath, editable with editor(set_property)).

list_states.summary: List all states with IDs and paths, depth-first in the tree's authored order, cursor-paginated.

add_state.summary: Add a child state under the parent named by stateId or statePath, or a root state when neither is given.

set_state_property.summary: Set a property on a state (name|type|selectionBehavior|bEnabled|weight|linkedAsset|description|tag|customTickRate|color). For tag: gameplay tag string or empty to clear. For customTickRate: number in seconds or empty to disable. For color: palette color display name, GUID, or empty to clear.

clear_state_nodes.summary: Remove all tasks/conditions/transitions from a state.

add_task.summary: Add a task to a state. structType is a C++ struct name, e.g. FMyStateTreeTask or an engine-shipped task like FStateTreeRunParallelStateTreesTask.

add_enter_condition.summary: Add an enter condition to a state.

remove_enter_condition.summary: Remove an enter condition by index.

set_task_instance_property.summary: Set a property on a task's instance data.

set_task_property.summary: Set a property on the task's node struct (FStateTreeTaskBase-level: bConsideredForCompletion, bTaskEnabled, bShouldStateChangeOnReselect). Distinct from set_task_instance_property which targets instance data. value is string-encoded, e.g. 'true'/'false'.

add_transition.summary: Add a transition to a state.

add_transition_condition.summary: Add a condition to an existing transition.

list_bindings.summary: List all property bindings, optionally filtered to one struct.

list_bindable_sources.summary: Enumerate the context/bindable sources in a StateTree (context objects, parameters, evaluators, global tasks, per-state nodes) with their structId + struct type - what a property can bind FROM, sorted by structId, cursor-paginated (#681).

add_evaluator.summary: Add an evaluator to the StateTree (tree-level).

remove_evaluator.summary: Remove an evaluator by node ID.

set_evaluator_instance_property.summary: Set a property on an evaluator's instance data.

set_evaluator_property.summary: Set a property on the evaluator's node struct (FStateTreeEvaluatorBase-level).

add_global_task.summary: Add a global task to the StateTree (tree-level).

remove_global_task.summary: Remove a global task by node ID.

set_global_task_instance_property.summary: Set a property on a global task's instance data.

set_global_task_property.summary: Set a property on a global task's node struct (FStateTreeTaskBase-level).

list_colors.summary: List all color palette entries for a StateTree. Returns: colors[] with id, displayName, color.

add_color.summary: Add a new color to the StateTree palette.

list_state_parameters.summary: List parameters defined on a state. Returns: parameters[] with name, id, type, value; also bFixedLayout.

add_state_parameter.summary: Add a parameter to a state's property bag. Rejects fixed-layout (linked) states.

remove_state_parameter.summary: Remove a parameter from a state's property bag by name. Rejects fixed-layout (linked) states.

set_state_parameter.summary: Set the value of an existing state parameter. On fixed-layout states, also marks the parameter as overridden.

set_schema.summary: Attach or replace the StateTree schema, then compile. The schema is what makes a tree compilable: without one the compiler logs "does not have a schema" and stops, and everything that loads the asset reports it as failed to link. Repairs a tree that has no editor data at all (what asset(create_asset_by_class) writes) by creating the editor data, the schema and a root state. Omit schema to take StateTreeComponentSchema, then StateTreeAIComponentSchema, then whatever concrete schema this editor has, and read schemaSource / schemaNote to see which was used (#833).

compile.summary: Compile a StateTree asset. Returns success, errors[], warnings[].

validate.summary: Validate a StateTree asset without compiling.

list_node_types.summary: Enumerate every task, condition, evaluator and utility consideration THIS tree's schema allows, with the exact structType string add_task / add_enter_condition / add_transition_condition / add_consideration / add_evaluator / add_global_task take, and the property names their instanceProperties map accepts. Every add_* action takes a C++ struct name and nothing listed them, so authoring meant guessing. Also reports the schema's own capability flags (allowEnterConditions, allowUtilityConsiderations, allowEvaluators, allowMultipleTasks, allowGlobalParameters), which is what decides whether an add would be refused, and the context data a binding can come from. Blueprint-authored nodes are listed separately with the wrapper struct and the two calls that author one, because a Blueprint node needs set_node_class after the wrapper is added.

read_state.summary: Read ONE state whole, including everything the tree-wide read omits: utility considerations, the LinkedSubtree link, RequiredEventToEnter, TasksCompletion, Weight, and every transition's priority, enabled flag, delay variance and reactivation rule. Returns the state's objectPath, which is how the fields with no typed setter are written - editor(set_property) at that path reaches Transitions[0].Priority and the rest. problems[] names the faults a state cannot report about itself: utility selection with no scoring considerations anywhere below it, considerations whose parent never reads them, a Linked type pointing at nothing, and a transition targeting a deleted state. Pass stateId OR statePath.

add_consideration.summary: Add a utility consideration to a state, which is what produces the score a parent uses when its selectionBehavior is TrySelectChildrenWithHighestUtility or TrySelectChildrenAtRandomWeightedByUtility. Those behaviours were already settable and nothing could add the scoring half, so the setting could be written and never did anything. Refuses when the tree's schema does not allow considerations, and warns when the PARENT does not select by utility, because that is the silent failure. Pass stateId OR statePath.

remove_consideration.summary: Remove a utility consideration from a state by index. The rollback captures the struct type, operand and instance values, and says plainly that a replay appends at the end with a new nodeId rather than restoring its position or its bindings. Pass stateId OR statePath.

remove_transition_condition.summary: Remove one condition from a transition by index. add_transition_condition shipped without it, so a mistyped condition could only be undone by deleting the whole transition. Pass stateId OR statePath.

set_state_link.summary: Link a state to a Subtree state in THIS asset, or to another StateTree asset, or clear both. UStateTreeState carries two separate link fields and only the asset one had any route: add_state documented a linkedSubtree parameter and assigned LinkedAsset with it, so in-asset subtree reuse was impossible. Goes through SetLinkedState / SetLinkedStateAsset rather than assigning the field, which is what pulls the linked target's parameters into this state - without that a linked state has an empty fixed-layout parameter list and set_state_parameter has nothing to override. Pass stateId OR statePath; for linkType subtree pass targetStateId OR targetStatePath, for asset pass linkedAsset.

move_state.summary: Reparent or reorder an existing state. add_state takes an insertIndex for a NEW state and nothing could move one afterwards, so wrong order meant delete and rebuild - and order is load-bearing, since TrySelectChildrenInOrder walks it and NextState and NextSelectableState transitions resolve through it. Refuses to move a state under its own descendant, which would detach the branch. insertIndex is the final position among siblings; omit it to append. Reports unchanged when the state is already there, and rolls back to its previous parent and index. Pass stateId OR statePath, and newParentStateId OR newParentStatePath OR toRoot.

set_node_class.summary: Point a Blueprint node wrapper at its Blueprint class AND reallocate its instance data. This is the step with no property-write equivalent: the wrapper reports the Blueprint class AS its instance data type, so a node added before the class is set has no instance data at all, and writing the class afterwards does not go back and allocate it. Works on any task, condition, transition condition, consideration, evaluator or global task, addressed by the nodeId every add_* action returns. Returns instanceObjectPath, where the Blueprint's own variables live for editor(set_property).

read_runtime.summary: Read a RUNNING StateTree in depth: run status, last tick status, the state change count, the active states, the execution frames and the pending event queue. gameplay(get_state_tree_runtime) answers the same question with active state names only, which cannot tell you whether the tree succeeded, failed or stopped, nor whether an event you sent is still waiting to be consumed. Needs a game world, so run it in PIE. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath.

send_event.summary: Send a gameplay event to a running StateTree, which is how an event-driven tree is meant to be driven from outside and had no route at all. The event is QUEUED and consumed on the tree's next tick, so the snapshot returned still shows the state before it is handled; read it again with read_runtime after a tick. Refuses an unregistered tag, since no transition could ever match one. Has no inverse: once queued it is consumed and whatever it triggered has run. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath.

request_transition.summary: Force a running StateTree to transition to a named state, resolved through the COMPILED data - so a state added since the last compile is reported as missing rather than silently ignored. Queued like an event and resolved on the next tick against every other pending request by priority. Refuses when the tree is not Running, naming the status it is in. targetStateTag needs UE 5.8 or later; targetStateId works everywhere. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath, and targetStateId OR targetStateTag.

move_node.summary: Reorder a task, enter condition, consideration, transition condition, evaluator or global task within the list it is in, found by its nodeId. Tasks run in list order and conditions combine in list order through their operand and indent, so order is load-bearing; the node keeps its ID, so bindings into and out of it survive. The rollback moves it back.

read_node.summary: Read ONE node by nodeId wherever it lives: where it is (container, state, transition, index), its node struct properties, instance data (struct or Blueprint object), execution runtime data, the struct ID bindings into it use (instanceStructId), its editor description, and the typed flags taskEnabled, consideredForCompletion, canEditConsideredForCompletion and evaluationMode.

set_node_flags.summary: Set the typed node flags the editor exposes, with the editor's rules: taskEnabled and consideredForCompletion on tasks (state or global; a Blueprint task's completion flag lives on its instance), evaluationMode (Evaluated, ForcedTrue, ForcedFalse) on enter or transition conditions. consideredForCompletion is refused on a disabled task or one that does not allow the edit.

set_node_data.summary: Write a node's data by nodeId: target node (the node struct), instance (default; struct or Blueprint object) or executionRuntime. Pass propertyName to write one property, or omit it to replace the whole struct with value in Unreal text format. Works on conditions and considerations, which the index-addressed set_*_property actions do not reach.

list_bindable_properties.summary: Binding discovery for one bindable struct (structId from list_bindable_sources or read_node's instanceStructId). Without targetPath: every property of it with type, category and current binding. With targetPath: every compatible source in that property's scope, exact matches before numeric promotions (exactOnly drops promotions; maxDepth limits descent into value structs). UE 5.7 and later.

check_binding.summary: Check a proposed binding without writing it: resolve the target (and the source, when given) against the structs' current values, report each end's type, whether the source is in the target's scope, the compatibility (compatible, promotable, incompatible), canBind and the reasons. Omit the source to only resolve a path. UE 5.7 and later.

promote_to_parameter.summary: Promote to Parameter: create a parameter with the target property's type and current value, on the given state (the target's state or an ancestor, not linked) or on the tree parameters when no state is given, and bind the target to it. The name defaults to the property name and is made unique. UE 5.7 and later.

epic_add_evaluator.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based evaluator to the asset. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

epic_add_global_task.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based global task to the asset. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8.

tools.name: widget
tools.description:
UMG Widget Blueprints, Editor Utility Widgets, and Editor Utility Blueprints. One parameter contract across every action (#798): the asset is always `assetPath`, an Unreal package path such as `/Game/UI/WBP_Example`; a widget inside the tree is always `widgetName`; its parent panel is always `parentWidgetName`; arguments for any wrapped `epic_*` action go in `input`, and a top-level `assetPath` is folded into the asset reference of the wrapped tool for you. A `.uasset` suffix, an object suffix (`.WBP_Example`), backslashes, and the legacy `path` / `widgetBlueprintPath` / `widgetBlueprint` spellings are accepted and normalized. Create actions take `assetPath` too; `name` plus `packagePath` remains valid and is composed into it. See [Widget parameter contract](widget-parameters.md).
